Gold prices in Pakistan increased by Rs3,500 per tola on Wednesday, despite a slight decline in international market, as investors awaited the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy decision and comments from its chair for clues about the future path of rates.
In the local market, gold prices rose to Rs425,636 per tola, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). Similarly, the price of 10-gram gold increased by Rs3,001 to reach Rs364,914. On Tuesday, gold prices had declined by Rs1,300 per tola, settling at Rs422,136. Wednesday's increase reversed those losses and pushed domestic bullion prices higher. In the international market, spot gold edged down 0.3% to $4,044.54 per ounce by 11:46 am EDT (1546 GMT), as per Reuters. US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.4% to $4,057.30 per ounce. Higher oil prices weighed on bullion, while concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East added to market uncertainty. Rising energy prices can fuel inflationary pressures, potentially influencing the pace of monetary easing by major central banks.
Investors remained cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy announcement, scheduled for 2 pm EDT (1800 GMT), followed by a press conference by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
Market participants were looking for signals on the central bank's assessment of inflation and economic conditions, as well as indications of whether interest rates could decline further.
Rate expectations are a key driver of gold prices because bullion does not pay any yield. Lower rates generally make gold more attractive relative to interest-bearing assets, while expectations of tighter monetary policy can weigh on bullion demand. Investors were also looking ahead to the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index, due on Thursday. The measure is closely watched by the Federal Reserve as an indicator of inflationary trends. Developments in oil markets and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East were also expected to remain important factors for investors assessing inflation risks and the outlook of monetary policy.
Silver prices in Pakistan increased by Rs61 per tola to reach Rs5,854 on Wednesday. Meanwhile, the Pakistani rupee continued its upward trajectory, gaining Rs0.03 against the US dollar to close at 276.77 in the inter-bank market. On Tuesday, the local currency had settled at 276.80 against the greenback. Internationally, the US dollar held near two-week highs ahead of central bank policy decisions, with the Federal Reserve widely expected to keep rates unchanged while signalling the possibility of a move in December.
Fed holds rate steady
Later on Wednesday, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, as expected, opting to delay any changes to borrowing costs until after next week's US midterm elections and awaiting further data on the path of inflation.

items.author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
items.content:
The State Bank of Pakistan's (SBP) decision to raise its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12% has cast a shadow over the economic recovery, with economists warning that persistent energy and food price pressures could keep monetary policy tight while higher borrowing costs weigh on private investment, employment and growth.
The Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI) economist Dr Abid Qaiyum Suleri said the 50-basis-point increase reflected growing concerns over inflation, particularly rising energy and food prices. With inflation reaching 10.3% in September, the central bank wanted to prevent temporary supply shocks from turning into persistent inflationary pressures.
He expects energy prices to remain elevated in the near future amid fears of another wave of US-Israeli attacks on Iran after the US midterm elections and the possibility of Iranian retaliation against neighbouring Gulf states.
This outlook leaves limited room for monetary easing in the coming months, as persistent external tensions could prolong energy price pressures and complicate the inflation outlook. He expects monetary policy to remain tight, with rate cuts unlikely unless energy prices stabilise and inflation records a sustained decline.
The SBP projects economic growth of 3.5-4.5% in fiscal year 2027, but prolonged high borrowing costs could constrain the recovery, he said.
SDPI Deputy Executive Director and founding head of the Policy Solutions Lab Dr Sajid Amin Javed said the 50-basis-point increase was expected as double-digit inflation, a recent surge in global oil prices and fears of a prolonged US-Iran conflict worsened Pakistan's inflation and economic outlook.
He said the SBP had kept the policy rate unchanged since April 2026 despite rising headline inflation, expecting global oil prices to settle and bring inflation down. However, renewed increases in oil prices and fears of further escalation had changed the outlook, prompting the Monetary Policy Committee to raise the rate.
He considered the increase necessary amid double-digit inflation, saying it was consistent with a cautious approach of making small adjustments to signal the central bank's commitment to price stability. Although higher interest rates might not directly curb supply-side inflation, he said, the increase sent the right signal to the market.
However, he warned that if fears of conflict persisted and oil prices remained elevated, the SBP could introduce a series of gradual rate increases over the next three to four months. This could further slow an already sluggish economy, although the rate would not return to its previous peak.
He projected average headline inflation of 11-13% in fiscal year 2026-27, higher than previously anticipated, while economic growth could fall below 3.5%.
The concerns over growth were echoed by Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE) Professor of Economics and Registrar Dr Nasir Iqbal, who argued that maintaining the policy rate at 11.5% would have been a more balanced response to the prevailing inflationary risks.
Referring to PIDE's Monetary Policy Assessment for October 2026, he said price pressures were largely driven by supply-side constraints rather than excessive domestic demand. Energy prices, food prices and external shocks remained the main sources of inflation, he added. Higher interest rates cannot directly address these constraints. Instead, tighter monetary conditions raise borrowing costs for businesses, discourage private investment and increase the government's debt-servicing burden, potentially weakening an already fragile economic recovery.
With September inflation at 10.3% and growth remaining modest, he said further monetary tightening risked adding to the pressure on businesses without adequately addressing the underlying sources of inflation.
Looking ahead, he expects inflation to remain elevated and volatile if global energy prices and domestic food supply pressures persist. High borrowing costs are also likely to constrain investment, employment generation and economic activity, keeping growth moderate rather than allowing it to accelerate significantly.
He urged the SBP to avoid further rate increases unless there was clear evidence that inflation had become broad-based and persistent.
His assessment highlights the limitations of relying on monetary tightening when inflation is driven primarily by supply-side factors. While higher interest rates can restrain demand, they cannot directly lower international energy prices or resolve domestic food supply disruptions.
The three economists' assessments underline the difficult choices facing monetary policymakers. Persistent inflation and uncertainty over global energy prices could keep the policy rate elevated, but the cost of credit may restrict business investment and weigh on economic activity. The outlook will depend partly on whether geopolitical tensions ease and energy prices stabilise enough to allow inflation to decline.
While Suleri sees limited scope for rate cuts without a sustained improvement in inflation, Javed warns that prolonged oil price pressures could lead to further gradual increases. Meanwhile, the PIDE economist cautions that additional tightening could deepen the economic costs without resolving the supply-side pressures driving inflation. The challenge for the SBP will be to contain inflation while avoiding further constraints on investment, employment and the broader economic recovery.

items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) put on an impressive show on Wednesday as the benchmark KSE-100 index staged a strong rally, driven by accelerating purchases in the final hours despite lingering concerns over monetary tightening and rising international oil prices.
The market opened on a steady note and quickly advanced, reaching 164,830.55, up 363.35 points, or 0.22%, within minutes of the opening bell. It touched the intra-day high of 166,100.34 and low of 164,355.83. Investors came back and buying gathered pace late in the session, which helped the KSE-100 index close with notable gains of 1,269.55 points, or 0.77%, at 165,736.76.
Similarly, Asian equities rose on optimism surrounding artificial intelligence demand and ahead of earnings announcements by major US companies. The positive tone in regional markets lent support to investor sentiment, although geopolitical risks continued to cloud the outlook. Oil prices, meanwhile, remained a major concern.
Ahmed Sheraz, equity trader at KASB KTrade, noted that the KSE-100 closed with an increase of 1,270 points (+0.77%) in a broadly positive session, with approximately 183 million shares traded. Buying interest remained widespread, led by commercial banks, fertiliser, automobile and power stocks.
Among major contributors, Fauji Fertiliser led the rally following an attractive Rs18.5/share dividend announcement and its results were broadly in line with expectations. National Bank followed by posting decent earnings, while Hub Power supported the index on the back of a Rs5-per-share payout.
Market sentiment continued to improve after the State Bank's 50-basis-point policy rate hike to 12%, which was lower than expectations. This supported banking stocks, while cyclical sectors also witnessed renewed buying interest, allowing the market to consolidate at higher levels. "However, Brent crude hovering around $115 per barrel remains a key concern, alongside geopolitical uncertainty involving Iran, Israel and the US," Sheraz added.
According to JS Global analyst Nawaz Ali, bullish activity continued at the PSX for the third consecutive session, where the benchmark KSE-100 index gained 1,270 points. Buying interest was driven by investor optimism about a potential easing of geopolitical tensions.
Meanwhile, the corporate results season remained in full swing, with earnings-driven activity also contributing to market momentum. National Bank's better-than-expected results triggered stock buying in the banking sector. "Looking ahead, any positive developments regarding the US-Iran situation that lead to a decline in crude oil prices could further improve investor confidence," Ali stated.
Topline Securities observed that the benchmark index maintained a positive trajectory throughout the session, touching the intra-day high of 1,633 points, while the downside remained limited to 111 points, reflecting sustained buying interest and improved investor sentiment. Overall trading volumes increased to 578 million shares from Tuesday's total of 402 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs26 billion.
Shares of 496 companies were traded in the ready market. Of these, 269 stocks closed higher, 180 fell and 47 remained unchanged.
Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs624 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Meta has introduced a new AI-powered app called Waddle World, allowing users to raise a virtual pet, interact with it, and share details about their daily lives.
The app is similar to the classic Tamagotchi virtual pet games but adds artificial intelligence to make interactions more personal.
Waddle World is currently available for iOS and Android users in the Philippines. Meta has not announced when it will launch in other countries.
How Waddle World Works
Waddle World features a 16-bit pixel-style environment where users can hatch and raise their own virtual pets.
Players can feed their pets, play games with them, and interact with them throughout the day.
Unlike traditional virtual pet games, Waddle World uses AI to learn about users through their interactions. The app also allows users to share their thoughts and experiences by speaking or typing.
The virtual pet listens and turns these conversations into journal entries written from its own perspective, complete with small illustrations.
Additionally, users can play short mini-games and receive weekly emails summarizing what their virtual pet has learned about them.
Meta launches AI Tamagotchi!
Meet Waddle World, an AI-powered virtual pet that:
• Remembers your conversations
• Creates illustrated journals
• Sends personalised postcards
• Lets you feed it and play games
Currently available in the Philippines. pic.twitter.com/S8WJJFNE9R
— Matt Navarra (@MattNavarra) October 27, 2026
No Daily Tasks or Rewards to Maintain
Meta says Waddle World is designed to be a relaxing experience rather than an app that pressures users to return every day.
Unlike many mobile games, it does not require players to maintain daily login streaks or chase high scores.
Users can spend a few minutes or longer with their pets without worrying about losing progress.
Meta also describes Waddle World as a virtual pet experience rather than a traditional AI chatbot, assistant, or productivity tool.
The app is intended for adults aged 18 and older.
Meta Continues Testing New AI Apps
Waddle World is part of Meta’s ongoing efforts to explore new uses for artificial intelligence beyond traditional chatbots.
The company has previously introduced Pocket, which allows users to create games using AI, and Vibes, an app for generating AI videos.
Meta has also been developing a Tamagotchi-style physical device powered by its Muse AI technology.
The new virtual pet app could be an early experiment related to that project, although Meta has not confirmed a connection.
Availability
Waddle World is currently available for free on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store in the Philippines.
Social media consultant Matt Navarra highlighted the app on October 27, drawing attention to Meta’s latest AI experiment.
For now, it remains unclear whether Meta plans to release Waddle World worldwide.
The launch also comes as AI companion services face increasing scrutiny. Companies including Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits alleging that their products harmed teenagers.
Meta has not said whether those concerns influenced Waddle World’s design or its adults-only availability.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman took a swipe at Defence Minister Khawaja Asif in the National Assembly on Wednesday, saying defence agreements were being negotiated in Iran while Pakistan’s defence minister was at home.
“Khawaja Asif sahib is also present here. A defence agreement is being made in Iran, and the defence minister is sitting here,” Fazlur Rehman said, before turning Asif’s own famous line against him: “Koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai” (Have some shame, have some decency).
The remark drew laughter in the House, and a video of the exchange shared by JUI-F Senator Kamran Murtaza has since gone viral on social media.
Remark Linked to Tehran Talks
Fazlur Rehman’s comment referred to the high-level talks held in Tehran on Monday, where Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other senior Iranian officials.
The three envoys represented the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the military alliance signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye in August.
It was the first meeting between representatives of the pact and Iranian leaders, and focused on regional security and preventing a fresh military escalation.
Khawaja Asif said a day later that Pakistan would defend Saudi Arabia with full force under the pact.
Asif’s Own Words Come Back to Haunt Him
“Koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai” is one of the most quoted lines in Pakistani politics. Khawaja Asif famously used it in the National Assembly years ago to criticise PTI lawmakers, and it has since become a popular meme.
Social media users were quick to point out that this may be the first time the line has been used against Asif himself, with him sitting in the House.
During the same speech, Fazlur Rehman also called on the government and opposition to sit together and draw up a new Charter of Democracy.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
The Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF26) will be held on November 12–13 at the Jinnah Convention Centre in Islamabad, bringing together policymakers, local and international mining executives, investors, financial institutions and technical experts to explore investment opportunities in Pakistan’s minerals sector.
Organised by the Government of Pakistan and endorsed by the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), the forum is Pakistan’s flagship platform for connecting the country’s mineral potential with global investment, expertise and technology. Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDC) is the founding partner. Building on the momentum of PMIF25, this year’s forum will focus on translating dialogue into investment, partnerships and projects across mineral exploration, processing and sustainable mining.
PMIF26’s strategic partners include PPL, Mari Energies, GHPL, Reko Diq Mining Company, PMPL and Frontier Works Organization (FWO). Wood Mackenzie is the lead conference producer, while Milbank, White & Case and Lazard are knowledge partners. Academic partners include NAVTTC, NUST, the University of Peshawar and the engineering universities of Peshawar and Lahore, among others.
“PMIF26 provides an important platform to connect Pakistan’s mineral potential with global investment, expertise and technology. Our country has a vast mineral resource base and a harmonised regulatory framework with investment-friendly policies. OGDC is already a joint venture partner in the Reko Diq project, and we want to expand our footprint in the minerals and mining sector through our cooperation with global partners. We look forward to welcoming policymakers and industry leaders from across the world to Islamabad to exchange ideas, build partnerships and explore new ventures,” said Ahmed Hayat Lak, MD/CEO OGDC and President PMIF.
The forum comes as critical minerals gain strategic importance for the global energy transition, advanced manufacturing and emerging technologies. It will showcase Pakistan’s mineral potential, highlight policy reforms and explore opportunities across the mineral value chain.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar and Chief of the Army Staff & Chief of Defence Forces (COAS & CDF) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir are among the key speakers. Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik will deliver the welcome address on the opening day of PMIF26. International speakers include John L. Thornton, Chairman of Barrick Mining Corporation; Robert Friedland, Founder and Executive Co-Chairman of Ivanhoe Mines; Patrick Barnes and Wael Jaber of Wood Mackenzie; Isabel Chatterton and Claire Alidenes of the Asian Development Bank; and Mustafa Aksoy, Chief Executive Officer of Çalık Group.
Other speakers include representatives of the World Bank Group, Reko Diq Mining Company, Lazard, Weir, Milbank and the Federal Institute for Geosciences and Natural Resources, alongside Pakistani government officials and industry leaders. The forum will provide a platform for local and international participants to discuss investment, technical cooperation, policy development and the future of the mining industry.
The two-day strategic conference will cover investor-ready mining jurisdictions, critical minerals and Pakistan’s role in the energy transition, financing early-stage exploration, workforce development, women’s participation in mining and the development of next-generation mining projects. Sessions will also address geological survey collaboration, infrastructure, export corridors, environmental and social considerations, and national capability development. Ahmed Hayat Lak, MD/CEO of OGDC and President of PMIF, will deliver the closing remarks.
A technical conference will feature more than 50 peer-reviewed technical papers, geological survey data, technology benchmarking and a workshop on Pakistan’s innovation potential in critical minerals mining. Similarly, an international exhibition will connect project developers, investors, equipment manufacturers, technology providers and other industry stakeholders. The exhibition will offer opportunities to showcase solutions, establish partnerships and explore business prospects. It will include a Mineral Expo of rare mineral specimens, project showcases and procurement briefings.
The PMIF26 exhibition will provide a marketplace for the minerals ecosystem, bringing together local and international companies to showcase their capabilities and explore opportunities for collaboration, investment and innovation. Exhibitors include the Pakistan Mineral Development Corporation (PMDC), Allied Engineering & Services (Pvt.) Ltd., National Resources (Private) Limited (NRL), Bore and Bore Private Limited, Globacore Minerals Limited, Frontier Works Organization (FWO), Mari Energies, Barrick Mining Corporation, Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL), Government Holdings (Private) Limited (GHPL), Reko Diq Mining Company and Pakistan Minerals Private Limited (PMPL), among others. The exhibition will also feature a European Pavilion, offering a platform to explore international partnerships and investment opportunities.
The 2025 edition of PMIF brought together 5,000 delegates from more than 50 countries and featured 16 memoranda of understanding and agreements, alongside 18 panel discussions. Building on that international engagement, PMIF26 aims to strengthen Pakistan’s links with global mining and investment networks.
The post Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF26) Set for November 12–13 in Islamabad appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.title: Islamabad Eases Motorcycle License Rules for Students
items.summary:
Islamabad Traffic Police has introduced a special facility to help college and university students obtain motorcycle driving licenses more quickly.
Under the initiative, students can obtain their motorcycle licenses on the same day without completing the usual 42-day learning period, Islamabad Traffic Police spokesperson said.
The facility will remain available from November 1 through November 30, 2026. Students who want to use the service must visit the Islamabad Traffic Police Headquarters to complete the licensing process.
Chief Traffic Officer Kainat Azhar Khan said the initiative aims to help young people obtain motorcycle licenses in line with legal requirements and encourage them to follow traffic rules.
Islamabad Traffic Police hopes the initiative will make the licensing process easier for students while promoting lawful driving and road safety.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
foodpanda, Pakistan’s leading food delivery and quick-commerce platform, hosted a delegation of journalists and media representatives for an exclusive tour of its cloud kitchen (dark kitchen) infrastructure. The media briefing aimed to demonstrate the operational framework of dark kitchens, demonstrating how delivery-only facilities are expanding culinary access, lowering entry barriers for food entrepreneurs, and supporting local business growth across Pakistan.
During the tour, journalists observed the end-to-end operational journey, from order receiving and real time inventory tracking to food preparation, packaging, and rider dispatch. Members of the media were given full access to inspect food safety standards, hygienic kitchen layouts, temperature control systems, and rider pickup management protocols designed to ensure fast, efficient, and consistent food delivery.
Moeen Qureshi, Head of Kitchen, foodpanda Pakistan commented, “Cloud kitchens represent an important pillar in the evolution of Pakistan’s urban food landscape. By hosting our media partners for an open, transparent look at our kitchen operations, we hope to highlight how digital infrastructure empowers small food businesses, creates sustainable livelihoods for local chefs, and ensures reliable food access for consumers. Our focus remains on combining culinary innovation with operational excellence to support an inclusive food ecosystem across the country.”
Cloud kitchens operating on the foodpanda ecosystem act as plug-and-play culinary hubs, enabling established restaurant brands, unique food concepts, and home chefs to expand their footprint into new neighbourhoods without the high capital required for traditional physical dining spaces. By providing fully equipped kitchen infrastructure and data-driven demand insights, foodpanda allows vendors to focus on quality while the platform manages logistics, tech integration, and delivery infrastructure.
The walkthrough also highlighted foodpanda’s adherence to local food authority guidelines, staff safety training, and hygiene audits, addressing common industry misconceptions around delivery-only kitchens.

items.title: Austria to launch parliamentary inquiry into use of smart glasses amid privacy concerns
items.summary:
Austria is set to launch a parliamentary inquiry into the use of smart glasses amid growing privacy concerns, the country's secretary of state for digitalisation said on Wednesday.
Alexander Proll presented a three-stage model aimed at regulating smart glasses, which can feature built-in cameras, microphones and artificial intelligence functions, public broadcaster ORF reported.
Under the proposed model, recordings would be prohibited in sensitive areas, including schools, kindergartens, changing rooms, toilets, courts, prisons, and police and military facilities.

items.content:
Austria is set to launch a parliamentary inquiry into the use of smart glasses amid growing privacy concerns, the country's secretary of state for digitalisation said on Wednesday.
Alexander Proll presented a three-stage model aimed at regulating smart glasses, which can feature built-in cameras, microphones and artificial intelligence functions, public broadcaster ORF reported.
Under the proposed model, recordings would be prohibited in sensitive areas, including schools, kindergartens, changing rooms, toilets, courts, prisons, and police and military facilities.
Read: From smart glasses to AI pins, privacy fears challenge tech's next big bet
KI-Staatssekretär Alexander Pröll (ÖVP) sagt im oe24-Interview, wo er Smartglasses in Österreich verbieten möchte, wo sie nützlich sind und wie sich der öffentliche Raum ändert. https://t.co/hsUS7DLAwx
— oe24.at (@oe24at) October 28, 2026
Recordings in public spaces would also have to be clearly visible to others, according to the proposal.
Proll said a parliamentary inquiry would be the next step, bringing together experts in science, data protection and technology, as well as representatives of people affected by the use of smart glasses.
He ruled out a total ban on the technology, saying the government aims to allow technological progress while ensuring that people cannot be secretly filmed.
Proll also said manufacturers should be required to make recordings clearly identifiable through measures such as visible recording lights and acoustic signals.
Meanwhile, nearly 25,000 people have signed a petition calling for a ban on smart glasses, according to ORF.
The Vienna city government also urged federal authorities last week to examine a possible ban on the devices in public transportation, government offices and schools, the broadcaster reported.

items.content:
Google announced its latest artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini 4 Carbon, on Wednesday, claiming significant gains in coding, autonomous agent tasks and cybersecurity defence.
Unveiled just two weeks after launching its Gemini 4 Argon model, the company described Carbon in a blog post as its strongest frontier model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.
Google attributed the rapid release timeline to its researchers and AI models "working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster."
Read: Google announces Gemini 4 flagship AI model after months of delays
Introducing Gemini 4 Carbon, our latest frontier model.
Carbon delivers improved performance across domains — ranking #1 on v5.0 of the @ArtificialAnlys Intelligence Index and sets a new state-of-the-art in cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.
It’s rolling out starting… pic.twitter.com/oQrHzxvMSo
— Google (@Google) October 28, 2026
The company claimed that Gemini 4 Carbon ranks first on the updated version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59.
Based on user feedback from its previous release, Google said it improved the model across full-stack web development, scientific tasks and multimodal understanding, claiming an 89-point jump to fourth place on the WebDev Arena leaderboard.
In cybersecurity benchmarks, the tech giant claimed the model holds a "firm lead," scoring 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities, 54.8% on ExploitGym for exploitation and 71% on CWE-bench for patching.
I did say we'd be releasing our models periodically...introducing Gemini 4 Carbon, our next frontier model.
Following Argon's release just two weeks ago, Carbon shows the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier, it ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of @ArtificialAnlys… pic.twitter.com/GN9LqZ7Zcf
— Sundar Pichai (@sundarpichai) October 28, 2026
"On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates," the company said.
Addressing safety and alignment, Google claimed that internal testing showed Carbon cuts unsupported claims by approximately half compared to Argon, stating methodological caveats directly rather than fabricating missing evidence.
The company also claimed the model retrieves relevant sources and surfaces discrepancies to users when facing ambiguity, while reducing task overreach by 26% and under-service by 29% during multi-step workflows.
Google said Gemini 4 Carbon will first become available to cybersecurity defenders this week before rolling out more broadly to developers, businesses and consumers.
The company plans to offer introductory pricing of $2 per 1 million input tokens and $10 per 1 million output tokens, with cached input tokens discounted by 95%, before standard pricing rises to $4 per 1 million input tokens and $20 per 1 million output tokens.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Traveltech startup Holiday Tribe is in talks to raise around ₹50 Cr (about $5.2 Mn) in a fresh funding round, with RPSG Capital Ventures among the prospective investors, sources told Inc42.
The startup is actively engaging with the investment firm, the sources said. However, the round is yet to be finalised, and its size and investor participation could change as discussions progress.
Queries sent to Holiday Tribe and RPSG Capital Ventures did not elicit a response by the time of publication.
Founded in 2022 by Anshu Sharma and Chirag Goyal, both former MakeMyTrip executives, Holiday Tribe offers customised holiday packages. The startup combines AI-powered planning with travel experts to provide itinerary recommendations, bookings, and support for family holidays, honeymoons, luxury trips, and group travel.
Its platform features a planning tool called Avni and lists domestic and international destinations, including Kerala, Bali, Dubai, Japan, Vietnam, and several European markets. Customers can also seek customised quotes through its travel advisors.
Holiday Tribe previously raised ₹25 Cr in a pre-Series A round last year. The round comprised equity and debt. Powerhouse Ventures led the fundraise, with participation from GSF and undisclosed angel investors. Before that, the startup raised ₹5.4 Cr in seed funding in 2024.
At the time of the pre-Series A fundraise, Holiday Tribe said it would invest in AI capabilities for personalisation, itinerary optimisation, and customer assistance, while expanding its supplier base in emerging destinations. Its deployment plans for the proposed fresh round are not yet known.
RPSG Capital Ventures, part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, is an early-stage consumer investment firm focused on businesses across food and beverages, personal care, and lifestyle goods and services.
Investors Back Customised Holiday Platforms
Holiday Tribe’s funding talks come amid investments in startups building customised holiday planning and booking services.
In July, Gurugram-based 30 Sundays raised ₹61 Cr in a Series A round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Info Edge Ventures and Eximius Ventures.
30 Sundays offers itinerary planning, bookings, and on-trip support for outbound Indian travellers, primarily targeting couples. It said the capital would help strengthen its AI capabilities, expand its engineering team, and enter markets including Georgia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and the Philippines.
The startup uses AI across lead qualification, itinerary creation, follow-ups, and reservations. At the time of the fundraise, it claimed an annualised gross booking value run rate of about ₹200 Cr across Bali, Vietnam, the Maldives, and Thailand.
Established travel platforms are also expanding their holiday offerings. Earlier this month, TravClan raised $5 Mn through a mix of equity and debt, with Flipkart and August One investing in equity and Trifecta Capital providing debt.
The partnership is intended to help Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel expand their curated international holiday packages and on-ground support. TravClan works with more than 15,000 travel agents to customise and book packages, hotels, and activities.
The post Exclusive: Holiday Tribe In Talks To Raise ₹50 Cr From RPSG Capital Ventures, Others appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
When AI-powered sales intelligence startup Reo.Dev raised $11.3 Mn in July 2026, its priorities reflected a growing reality for Indian startups building for global markets.
The company planned to deploy fresh capital towards expanding sales and marketing operations in the US, which already accounted for nearly two-thirds of its revenue. Yet most of its approximately 75-member workforce remained in India.
Reo.Dev is not alone in operating across these two markets. Bengaluru- and San Francisco-based Coreworks AI raised $5 Mn earlier this year to develop its enterprise AI platform. More recently, RapidCanvas secured $29 Mn to expand its go-to-market and field AI engineering teams across India, the US and Brazil.
These companies illustrate the increasingly international nature of India’s AI startup ecosystem, where the markets founders sell into, the teams they build and the locations from which they operate do not necessarily overlap.
The momentum is backed by capital.
According to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026, Indian AI startups raised $438 Mn during the July–September quarter, a 265% year-on-year increase. With $676 Mn raised in the first half, cumulative funding for the first nine months of 2026 crossed $1.1 Bn.
As more startups pursue global AI opportunities, however, an important question is emerging. Does getting closer to Silicon Valley necessarily make an Indian AI startup more competitive?
For Suhas Motwani, cofounder of The Product Folks, a global community of product professionals and builders, the answer is more complicated than a change of address.
“The corridor is real, and for a lot of founders it is useful,” says Motwani. “The harder question is what gets built on each side of it, and what gets lost when the move happens too early.”
Why Silicon Valley Is Becoming Harder To Ignore
The attraction of Silicon Valley extends well beyond fundraising, which was the case even at the height of the Indian SaaS boom.
For AI startups, just like SaaS startups before them, proximity to potential enterprise customers, experienced operators, specialised talent and the wider AI ecosystem can shorten the distance between product development and commercial validation.
That matters particularly for startups building enterprise AI products, where customer discovery often requires understanding complex workflows, procurement processes, security requirements and the commercial value of automation.
As Inc42 previously explored in its analysis of enterprise AI sales, winning enterprise customers is no longer simply about demonstrating technical capabilities. Startups must identify decision-makers, prove measurable returns and navigate the operational risks associated with deploying AI in live business environments.
For companies whose largest potential customers are American enterprises, building those relationships from thousands of kilometres away can introduce additional challenges.
Physical presence can create opportunities for more frequent customer interactions, closer feedback loops and a better understanding of how enterprise buying decisions are made.
Motwani believes this proximity can be particularly useful in a sector where product capabilities, customer expectations and competitive positioning are evolving rapidly. But there is an important distinction between using Silicon Valley to accelerate learning and treating relocation itself as a competitive advantage.
“A low barrier to raising in the Bay is very different from a low barrier to building a durable company,” he says. “The move itself is cheap. The compounding effects are not.”
The challenge for founders is to determine whether their company genuinely needs a physical presence in the US, and what business outcomes that presence is expected to deliver.
How AI Is Changing The India–US Equation
The India–US technology corridor is not new. Indian SaaS companies have spent years building products and engineering teams at home while selling to enterprise customers abroad.
However, AI is changing the economics of that relationship.
The cost and complexity of developing frontier AI models continue to demand enormous capital, computing infrastructure and specialised talent. At the same time, access to increasingly capable models is making it possible for smaller teams to build AI-powered applications without developing the underlying technology themselves.
The distinction is becoming more visible as the global AI industry enters a new phase.
On 26 October, Anthropic publicly filed its registration statement for a proposed US initial public offering. The Claude maker reported approximately $16.3 Bn in revenue during the first half of 2026, compared with about $1.2 Bn in the corresponding period last year, illustrating the rapid commercial expansion of the frontier AI industry. Its proposed listing also comes amid questions over the enormous capital requirements and long-term economics of building advanced AI models.
For Indian founders, the implications extend beyond the public market performance of companies such as Anthropic.
While frontier AI development remains heavily capital-intensive, application-layer startups can increasingly build on models developed elsewhere, allowing them to direct more resources towards solving specific customer problems.
This distinction is particularly relevant to India. According to the Google × Inc42 Bharat AI Startups Report, 2026, 90% of funded Indian AI startups covered in its analysis operate at the application layer.
However, access to powerful models also means that technological capabilities can become easier for competing startups to replicate. A sophisticated AI feature, by itself, may no longer constitute a lasting competitive advantage.
What becomes harder to replicate is a startup’s understanding of its customers, its integration into their workflows, its distribution network and the trust it builds through repeated use.
This is where the India–US corridor takes on a different significance.
For application-layer startups, being close to Silicon Valley can offer access to frontier AI developments, customers and distribution networks. But the ability to build quickly, experiment cost-effectively and develop products for demanding users can remain rooted in India.
The opportunity is no longer just about exporting Indian engineering capabilities to the US. It is about determining which parts of an AI business need to operate closer to the technology frontier, which need to be closer to customers, and where the startup can build its strongest competitive advantage.
Knowing The Risks
For much of the past decade, Indian technology startups have competed globally by combining engineering talent, leaner operating structures and access to international markets.
AI is changing the economics of building software, but it has not eliminated the importance of these advantages.
Moving an entire founding or engineering team to San Francisco can significantly increase operating costs, particularly when the startup is still experimenting with products, pricing and its target customer segment.
More importantly, an early relocation can affect the company’s product development process.
Founders who move away from their engineering teams may find themselves managing critical product decisions across time zones. The resulting separation can make experimentation, communication and decision-making more complex at precisely the stage when startups need to move quickly.
There is also the question of which users influence the product roadmap.
A startup developing AI products for American enterprises may benefit enormously from spending more time with US customers. But the same approach could prove counterproductive for a company building for Indian consumers, small businesses or enterprises with distinctly local requirements.
Motwani argues that the environment in which a startup develops its earliest products can influence the capabilities it prioritises and the problems it learns to solve.
India, for instance, exposes AI products to considerable variation in languages, devices, connectivity, user behaviour and willingness to pay.
A product designed around affluent, English-speaking users with reliable connectivity may not necessarily work as effectively for consumers using regional languages, shared devices or less predictable networks.
These constraints can force teams to improve reliability, usability and cost efficiency much earlier in the product development cycle.
The risk is not that an Indian founder builds for the US. It is that the founder changes markets without deliberately reassessing which customers, capabilities and advantages should shape the business.
An Opportunity Too Large To Overlook
The case for maintaining a strong presence in India is also increasingly supported by the size of the domestic opportunity.
According to the Google × Inc42 Bharat AI Startups Report, 2026, India’s AI market is projected to reach $126 Bn by 2030.
Enterprise AI expenditure is estimated to grow from $11 Bn in 2025 to $71 Bn by 2030, while consumer AI expenditure is projected to rise from $13 Bn to $55 Bn over the same period.
For application-layer startups, this represents a significant opportunity to build products that address specific customer problems, integrate into existing workflows and earn sustained adoption.
There are, however, important differences between market opportunity and commercial readiness.
India was already the world’s second-largest market for AI application downloads in 2024, accounting for 177 Mn downloads. Yet the Bharat AI report estimated consumer AI monetisation at just $12 Mn during that period.
In other words, significant user adoption does not automatically translate into strong monetisation.
For Indian AI founders, this creates two different opportunities. The US offers access to enterprise customers with established software budgets, while India offers a large and diverse market in which startups can build products around local workflows and underserved customer segments.
Choosing between them should depend on the problem being solved, rather than the assumption that one market is inherently superior.
There are also alternative routes to global customers that do not require startups to abandon their Indian operating base.
An earlier analysis published on Inc42 examined how India’s Global Capability Centres (GCCs) could become an important route to multinational enterprise buyers, offering Indian AI startups access to global workflows and potential decision-makers within the country itself.
The major implication is that access to international customers does not always require shifting the entire centre of product development overseas.
The Case For Building Across Two Markets
Rather than viewing Bengaluru and Silicon Valley as competing destinations, Motwani sees merit in founders using the two ecosystems for different purposes.
Through his work with The Product Folks, he has observed differences in the priorities that dominate conversations among founders and product professionals in the two markets.
In San Francisco or the Valley, discussions tend to centre on distribution, pricing and category creation. In Bengaluru, they are often more focused on engineering teams, product positioning, capital efficiency and the immediate challenges of building a sustainable business.
Both perspectives matter.
A startup can build a technically capable AI product in India and still struggle to reach the right international customers. Equally, access to American buyers and investors does not guarantee that the company will develop a defensible product or sustainable business model.
This is where a two-market operating strategy becomes relevant.
For founders serving US enterprises, customer-facing functions may need to be closer to those customers, while product and engineering teams can continue operating from India.
Reo.Dev offers one illustration. As Inc42 reported in July, the startup was expanding its American sales and marketing operations while retaining most of its workforce in India.
But operating across two markets brings its own challenges.
Founders must establish clear ownership of product decisions, maintain communication between customer-facing and engineering teams, and ensure that feedback from international customers translates into improvements rather than endless customisation.
There is also a less visible challenge: access to the right relationships.
Entering a new market requires more than understanding its customers. Founders often need introductions to experienced operators, potential partners, investors, early hires and advisors who understand the practical challenges of building across borders.
Motwani has been working to address some of these gaps through The Founder Folks, an invite-only founder initiative emerging from The Product Folks network.
Built around the India–US corridor, the initiative seeks to connect founders with experienced operators, potential customers and advisors, alongside offering practical guidance on US market entry, fundraising and managing cross-border teams.
Its emphasis reflects a broader challenge in the ecosystem: founders looking to build global businesses need more than access to capital. They also need access to relevant experience, networks and market-specific knowledge.
Ultimately, a US presence can accelerate customer discovery, but whether that learning becomes a competitive advantage depends on how effectively it informs the product being built.
The Real Test Is Product-Market Fit
The debate over where Indian AI startups should operate ultimately connects to a larger challenge facing the sector.
AI has made it easier for startups to develop prototypes, experiment with new capabilities and launch products. But these improvements do not automatically make it easier to build businesses that customers depend on.
Motwani believes founders must distinguish between what an AI product can demonstrate and what users will actually trust it to do.
“The shift from demo to daily use is not about adding features,” he says. “It is about deciding what work a user will actually trust the system to do.”
This distinction becomes particularly relevant when founders enter new markets.
Customer expectations around product reliability, workflow integration, support, pricing and accountability can vary considerably between India and the US.
A product that performs well during a demonstration may still struggle when deployed within an enterprise workflow that requires multiple approvals, integration with legacy systems or verification of AI-generated outputs.
These challenges are becoming more consequential as investor expectations mature.
Inc42’s Q3 2026 investor survey found that 63% of institutional investors surveyed saw some degree of froth in Indian AI startup valuations. At the same time, 39% believed vertical AI applications would capture the greatest value over the next five years.
The findings suggest that while investor interest in AI remains strong, the ability to build commercially viable, differentiated applications will increasingly matter.
For founders, the priority is not simply to reach a larger market. It is to understand which problems customers will pay to solve, how the product fits into their existing processes and whether the business can deliver value consistently.
A startup may need to be in San Francisco to understand those requirements. Another may discover its strongest opportunities by working more closely with Indian enterprises and consumers.
Neither outcome can be determined by geography alone.
Where Will India’s Next Global AI Companies Be Built?
India’s AI startup ecosystem is entering a phase in which global ambitions are becoming more closely intertwined with domestic capabilities.
As frontier AI companies prepare to face greater public market scrutiny, the application layer offers Indian startups an opportunity to participate in the global AI economy without necessarily matching the capital or infrastructure investments of the largest model developers.
But it also raises the competitive bar.
Building products is becoming faster. Access to underlying AI capabilities is expanding. What will distinguish companies is their ability to identify valuable problems, reach the right customers and develop products that become indispensable to their workflows.
Access to US capital, customers and talent can help startups accelerate their growth. At the same time, India’s engineering ecosystem, domestic demand and operating advantages continue to offer meaningful opportunities.
The challenge is to combine those strengths without assuming that a particular operating model will work for every company.
For some founders, relocating to the US will be commercially necessary. For others, maintaining customer-facing teams abroad while building from India may offer a more effective structure. And for startups addressing domestic problems, staying close to Indian users could be fundamental to product-market fit.
The decisions will also evolve as companies grow. What makes sense during initial customer discovery may not be the right structure after a startup finds product-market fit or begins scaling internationally.
Motwani’s argument is that founders should approach these choices as deliberate business decisions rather than signals of ambition.
“The corridor is a tool,” he says. “Like any tool, it rewards the founders who are clear about what they are using it for and punishes the ones who confuse motion for progress.”
As Indian AI companies compete for opportunities on both sides of the Pacific, the differentiator may ultimately be neither their headquarters nor their ability to access Silicon Valley.
It will be whether they can use the strengths of both markets to build products customers value, businesses that endure and competitive advantages that are difficult to replicate.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has facilitated overseas Pakistanis with a temporary, tax-free mobile phone registration facility for up to 120 days during each visit to Pakistan, enabling them to use their mobile devices without paying applicable Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) taxes under the prescribed policy.
The facility is available through the PTA’s fully automated Temporary Mobile Registration System, accessible through the Device Identification Registration and Blocking System (DIRBS) portal.
PTA Offers Overseas Pakistanis tax-free Mobile Registration for 120 Days Per Visit
According to the PTA, overseas Pakistanis can apply online to temporarily register their mobile devices for use during their stay in the country. The registration is valid for up to 120 days per visit, in line with the FBR policy.
Applicants are required to visit the portal at https://dirbs.pta.gov.pk/drs/login and select the option titled “Temporary Registration for Overseas Pakistanis and Foreign Nationals” after signing up.
The application process requires applicants to provide their Computerised National Identity Card (CNIC) or National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOP) details, along with passport information matching the details provided to immigration authorities. Foreign nationals are required to submit their passport details.
Applicants must also enter the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number or numbers of their devices and specify whether they use a single-SIM or dual-SIM handset. The IMEI number can be checked by dialling *#06# on the mobile phone.
The system also requires applicants to provide a Pakistani mobile phone number registered in their own name and select their mobile network operator. After submitting the application, users must complete verification through a one-time password (OTP).
See Also: Mobile Phones on Installments in Pakistan: IT Minister Reveals Latest Update on Proposed Policy
The PTA said devices would be registered temporarily following successful verification of the submitted information.
The facility is intended to facilitate overseas Pakistanis visiting the country by allowing them to use their personal mobile phones without going through the regular tax-paid registration process, subject to the applicable conditions.
Applicants are advised to ensure that their identity, passport, mobile number and device details are accurate to avoid delays in completing the registration process.

items.title: 'Nobody heard us' – why Gen Z are leading protests across Europe
items.summary:
Maya Gourdel, a 19-year-old student in Brussels, sits at a desk writing slogans against those running her country: “If we burn, you burn with us!” The slogan, taken from the 2012 film "The Hunger Games" that has been adopted as a symbol by many youth movements globally, reflects the anger, frustration and desire for change driving Gen Z-led protests around Europe.
From the suburbs of Paris to the squares of Belgrade, thousands have taken to the streets.
The demands are various but often overlapping: frustrations with shabby schooling facilities, perceived lack of economic opportunity, cost of living, corruption, housing and a sense of not being listened to. At times, those protests triggered violence, with thousands of shops in France alone being damaged or looted in recent weeks and police firing stun grenades and water cannons.
Read More: The model that fuels Europe's protests
This weekend, they also brought real change: student-led protests culmi
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Maya Gourdel, a 19-year-old student in Brussels, sits at a desk writing slogans against those running her country: “If we burn, you burn with us!” The slogan, taken from the 2012 film "The Hunger Games" that has been adopted as a symbol by many youth movements globally, reflects the anger, frustration and desire for change driving Gen Z-led protests around Europe.
From the suburbs of Paris to the squares of Belgrade, thousands have taken to the streets.
The demands are various but often overlapping: frustrations with shabby schooling facilities, perceived lack of economic opportunity, cost of living, corruption, housing and a sense of not being listened to. At times, those protests triggered violence, with thousands of shops in France alone being damaged or looted in recent weeks and police firing stun grenades and water cannons.
Read More: The model that fuels Europe's protests
This weekend, they also brought real change: student-led protests culminated in the toppling of Serbia’s long-time leader, Aleksandar Vucic, after nearly two years of demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism.
After a leaderless student-led protest movement swept Serbia's former President Aleksandar Vucic from power in a historic snap election, the country is waiting to hear who it will appoint as prime minister and to other key ministerial positions as it forms a government…
— Reuters (@Reuters) October 28, 2026
“Waking up, the first thing we felt was certainly a sense of relief and freedom," said student protester Stasa Piletic. "Personally, I feel a sense of victory. I feel that we finally moved from protests to responsibility."
‘An explosion of rage’
Chiara, a 21-year-old student in protest-hit Milan, believes “it's vital to take part in people's spontaneous movements born from an explosion of rage that made collective action possible.”
"I think the worst damage this ruling class has done to my generation is stealing even the ability to imagine a future, to dream," she said.
She said Italian students were confronting a reality of schools without enough teachers and crumbling buildings.
Thousands of young people marched through the streets of several Italian cities, including Milan and Rome.
The protests encompassed a broad range of issues from education and corruption to anti-war movements and rising costs.
Read more: https://t.co/wymlhvQV7W pic.twitter.com/HGA35lyYjq
— The Washington Post (@washingtonpost) October 26, 2026
“And all of this with the prospect of an underpaid job which we didn't qualify for and the prospect of living in a tiny, overpriced house, probably away from our city, which we didn't want to live in."
Protests led by Gen Z have caused unrest worldwide as the generation born roughly between 1997 and 2012 found its voice, from Bangladesh in 2024 and Nepal in 2025, to India this year. Now Europe has become a focal point.
Read More: Teenager's hand blown off as French school protests enter third week
Rising prices and the cost of living are a concern for 40% of 16-30-year-olds, according to a European Union survey published in 2025.
Among the 92.7 million people in the EU who faced the risk of poverty or social exclusion in 2025, the highest risk was recorded for young adults aged 18-24 years, at 26.3%, while the lowest was recorded for adults aged 65 years or over, at 18.8%.
Younger people are also wary of shouldering the financial burden of an older generation that tends to vote in greater numbers. People over 60 in France make up a quarter of the population but own 60% of France's wealth, according to the OFCE think tank.
French pensions are by far the biggest public expense, on track to reach 14% of economic output, as the population ages and voters resist raising the retirement age or reducing benefits. That is still less than Greece or Italy, which spend the largest proportion of national income on public pensions among OECD countries, at around 16% of GDP, according to OECD figures in 2025. But it is much more than Australia, Chile, Iceland, Ireland or South Korea, which spent less than 4% of GDP on public pensions, according to the OECD.
📈 El gasto en pensiones sube un 6,3% en octubre, hasta un nuevo máximo de 14.540 millones de euros https://t.co/1sHndCQzit
— Europa Press (@europapress) October 27, 2026
‘Young people in Europe are united’
Bilal Narjissi, a 17-year-old high school student in a suburb north of Paris, has been protesting against “deplorable” conditions and staff shortages at his school. “There used to be rats,” he said. Students were evacuated last year when a roof collapsed on the courtyard, though no one was hurt, he said.
Protests showed “that young people in Europe are united”, he said, adding, "we all agree on one point: that young people are treated like children, far too much, and that they aren't listened to enough.”
Also Read: ‘Threat exists’: Paris police warn of possible unrest ahead of protests
A French government report in October said pension spending had risen by 2.5 percentage points of GDP between 2000 and 2023 while that for education had declined by 0.5. It also showed 32% of the education ⁠ministry’s budget went towards pensions, crowding out money for other areas.
Gourdel, too, has been protesting for better conditions in schools in Belgium.
“We tried to do it passively. Nobody heard us. It's only when people started to burn trash or that kind of stuff that the media and cameras started showing us,” she said.
The protests are still spreading, with a demonstration planned in Germany this weekend over the cost of living, inequality, war and the state of schools.
Die Jugend begehrt auf. Am Wochenende will sie mit Demonstrationen auf ihre Probleme aufmerksam machen. Woher kommt die große Unzufriedenheit und kann daraus eine Massenbewegung entstehen? https://t.co/nPChUfLrlY
— Frankfurter Allgemeine (@faznet) October 28, 2026
Unrest has also hit Albania, where student-led demonstrations against Prime Minister Edi Rama's government, fuelled by anger over perceived corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards, engulfed Tirana and spread to other cities.
“Our Prime Minister spent 130 days not listening to us,” said Xyke Kurti, a 19-year-old architecture student.
“If you ask a student in Albania, 'where do you see your future?' Everyone says "outside this country", she said, arguing that at home, even if you have talent, someone with "connections is always going to beat you".
Serbia’s student movement did what demonstrators in other European capitals can only dream of.
Now, though, comes the gritty business of governing, something neither the students nor their candidates have any experience of. Luka Stojakovic, another protester, brushes that aside. "We have seen where people with political experience have brought us."

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Wednesday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.85 and Rs1.75 per litre, respectively, for October 29.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs377.91 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs399.82 per litre on Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs3.19 per litre while increasing the price of HSD by Rs2.25 per litre for October 28.
Read: Govt cuts petrol by Rs3.19, increases diesel by Rs2.25 for Oct 28
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices climbed about 2% on ‌Wednesday as continued fighting in Yemen and an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia renewed concerns about additional supply disruptions from the Middle East.
Brent futures rose $1.81, or 1.6%, to $115.69 per barrel at 10:42 am EDT (1442 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose $2.52, or 2.5%, to $102.42.
"Crude ​futures once again pricing in nearer term tighter supplies on news the US is likely to re-start military operations soon, which could be more intense than in ​the past given the latest attacks on Saudi Arabia and other Middle East allies," Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at US financial services firm BOK Financial, said in a note.

El-Sayed has disavowed the group and denied any connection with it. Pollsters and political strategists say the attacks are aimed at ⁠dissuading Jewish and Black voters in the Detroit area who backed his primary opponent, Representative Haley Stevens, from voting for him.
"He's a Muslim-American, and so Rogers is attempting to do his best to portray El-Sayed ​as an outsider who's dangerous," said Jonathan Hanson, a political scientist and public policy lecturer at the University of Michigan.
Read More: Republican ‘Muslim Brotherhood’ attacks on El-Sayed seek to exploit Democratic divisions
Michigan's Senate seat is critical to both parties' efforts to control the chamber. Republicans hold a 53-47 ​Senate majority heading into Tuesday's election.
Independent analysts rate the race a toss-up. The RealClearPolitics average shows El-Sayed ahead by 2.5 percentage points in a state Trump carried by 1.4 points in 2024.
El-Sayed leads by 2.5% statewide in the latest RealClearPolitics Poll Average, up from 1.9% this weekendhttps://t.co/crdWT2R7rF
— RealClearPolitics (@RCPolitics) October 27, 2026
El-Sayed campaign spokesperson Cole Wozniak accused Rogers of resorting to "desperate, bad faith attacks" and said the Democrat was focused on "his plans to bring down costs and stand up to the chaos and corruption in Washington".
Abby Ronson, a spokesperson for the Rogers campaign, pointed to Rogers' appearance on Sunday on NBC News' "Meet the ​Press," where he said he was not criticising Islam but what he described as El-Sayed's adherence to a "radical Islamic agenda".
Identity attacks
Advocating policies to curb corporate influence and expand the social safety net, El-Sayed, 41, has ​emerged as one of the Democratic Party's most prominent progressives. He describes himself as a capitalist and rejects the socialist label, but a victory on Tuesday would likely be seen as a boost for the party's left wing as it ‌seeks greater ⁠influence ahead of the 2028 presidential election.
But the margin of any victory will matter, said Michigan State University political scientist Matt Grossmann.
"If El-Sayed wins by a couple of points but trails Democratic gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson by a wide margin, that won't be a very convincing argument," Grossmann said. "And if El-Sayed were to lose, then it would be a mark against that faction of the party."
Rogers, 63, has cast himself as a pragmatic conservative focused on lowering costs, boosting manufacturing and strengthening border security. With Trump's popularity sagging, he recently called for an end to the war in Iran and the trade dispute with Canada, while avoiding direct criticism of the ​president.
"I have an opponent who wants to represent Palestine. I want to represent Michigan."
With the midterms just around the corner, Republican U.S. Senate nominee Mike Rogers makes his case to Michigan voters, promising to lower prices, improve children's reading skills, bring… pic.twitter.com/We0ODSXs2p
— Fox News (@FoxNews) October 27, 2026
But portraying El-Sayed as a national security threat has ​also become a central feature of Rogers' closing ⁠message. Rogers has based that claim in part on a 2012 group letter signed by El-Sayed and other Egyptian Americans in support of then-newly elected Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi, who was backed by the Muslim Brotherhood. The letter called on Morsi to purge the media and security services of holdovers from the dictatorship toppled during ​the Arab Spring.
The El-Sayed campaign did not immediately respond to a query about the letter.
Earlier this month Rogers agreed with a social media post calling El-Sayed ​a terrorist. He also appeared ⁠with Trump at a rally on Sunday where the president likened El-Sayed to the September 11 attackers and said his goal was to keep a "jihadist" out of the Senate.
The rhetoric prompted a rare rebuke from the NAACP, the nonpartisan civil rights organisation, which does not typically intervene in political races.
"The blatantly racist attacks surrounding the Michigan Senate race are unacceptable and disgusting," NAACP President Derrick Johnson said in a statement. "It’s the same ugly, divisive tactics we’ve seen used ⁠during the darkest ​chapters of the South’s history."
A poll by Michigan State University's Institute for Public Policy and Social Research found that 38% of ​Michigan voters were less likely to support a Muslim candidate.
Also Read: Anti-Muslim hate targeting Michigan Senate nominee El-Sayed surged after primary win: study
John Clark, a political science professor at Western Michigan University, said the attacks on El-Sayed were aimed in part at depressing Democratic turnout but could work against Rogers by angering and boosting turnout among Michigan's ​sizable Arab American communities in Dearborn and elsewhere.
"Maybe this helps with some voters, but it has the potential of backfiring with others," Clark said.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Ecommerce major Meesho reported a 68% decline in its consolidated net loss to ₹132.5 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27) from ₹411.4 Cr in the year-ago period as its revenue growth outpaced increase in expenses.However, net loss remained largely unchanged from ₹132.8 Cr in the June quarter.
Operating revenue rose 34% YoY and 11% QoQ to ₹4,131.6 Cr. Including other income of ₹127.4 Cr, Meesho’s total income stood at ₹4,259 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 31% from ₹3,254.9 Cr a year ago.
Meesho incurred exceptional expenses in the last year quarter which it didn’t incur this year, leading to the sharp annual reduction in loss. In Q2 FY26, Meesho incurred exceptional expenses of ₹45 Cr towards a business combination and a vendor dispute settlement, besides a ₹64.4 Cr tax charge related to the business combination. Neither charge recurred in the quarter under review.
Before exceptional items and tax, its loss narrowed by 57% to ₹123.3 Cr from ₹285.5 Cr a year earlier.
“Our Q2 performance reflects the strength of Meesho’s operating model, with NMV growing 23% YoY to ₹12,911 Cr and Annual Transacting Users reaching 284 Mn. More consumers are shopping on Meesho, and they are shopping more frequently, even as first-time buyers grew 16% QoQ,” Meesho’s CEO Vidit Aatrey said.
Meanwhile, Meesho’s total expenses increased 24% to ₹4,382.3 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹3,540.4 Cr. Other expenses, the company’s largest cost bucket, increased to ₹4,079.9 Cr from ₹3,292.1 Cr a year ago. The results did not provide a further breakdown of this expense head.
Employee benefit expenses rose 18% YoY to ₹280.9 Cr, while depreciation and amortisation expenses more than doubled to ₹20.1 Cr.
Marketplace Loss Narrows, New Initiatives’ Loss Widens
Meesho’s marketplace segment, which includes its ecommerce marketplace, advertising, logistics and content commerce businesses, accounts for nearly all its operating revenue.
The segment’s revenue rose 34% YoY to ₹4,119.9 Cr, while its loss narrowed to ₹130.5 Cr from ₹370.7 Cr. Contribution margin of the marketplace vertical also grew to 6.0% of NMV compared to 3.3% in the year-ago period and 4.6% in the previous quarter.
Notably, with the festive season falling 19 days later, sales driven by this demand surge shifted more towards Q3 this year. Festive-aligned NMV – measuring the sales for 90 days before Dussehra – grew 33% YoY.
“As we flagged last quarter, our Mega Blockbuster Sale (MBS) moved from Q2 last year to Q3 this year, so Q2 will look softer than the underlying trend and Q3 stronger. The two are best read together,” the management said.
Meanwhile, revenue from new initiatives increased more than fivefold to ₹11.7 Cr from ₹2.3 Cr in Q2 FY26. However, the segment’s loss widened to ₹41.6 Cr from ₹13.5 Cr a year earlier and ₹39.3 Cr in the preceding quarter.
Meesho groups its low-cost local logistics network for daily essentials, digital financial services and AI services under new initiatives.
In particular, logistics efficiencies enabled deliveries that were 15% faster YoY, helping to increase the contribution margin, said the management.
During the September quarter, the parent company invested an additional ₹75 Cr in Meesho Grocery to support its growth and financial requirements.
It further cited its increasing adoption of AI as driving a 171% jump in engineering productivity between March and September 2026 and slashing code approval times by 41%.
Separately, Meesho said its proposed ₹202.1 Cr acquisition of Singapore-based Kirana Club and a direct 0.41% stake in its Indian subsidiary, Retail Pulse Labs, is expected to close within Q3.
Alongside the results, its board approved the appointment of Sudhir Ganesh Sitapati as an additional independent director for five years, effective October 28, subject to shareholder approval.
Shares of Meesho ended today’s trading 1.77% higher at ₹227.60 apiece on the BSE.

items.title: Imran Khan’s sister Noreen taken to Punjab Institute of Cardiology after health issue in jail: lawyer
items.summary:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s sister Noreen Niazi, 70, was admitted to Lahore's Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) on Wednesday following a deterioration in her health while in custody, according to her legal counsel.
Imran’s sisters were detained in September under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, 1960, as the PTI prepared for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody on September 21.
Their initial detention orders were issued for 30 days. The detention at Kot Lakhpat Jail was later extended on October 7 for another 30 days.
“Noreen Niazi Sahiba has been transferred to Punjab Institute of Cardiology due to deteriorating health in jail,” her legal counsel, Rana Mudassar Umer, said on X.
He alleged that no family member was informed of her transfer to the hospital

Their initial detention orders were issued for 30 days. The detention at Kot Lakhpat Jail was later extended on October 7 for another 30 days.
“Noreen Niazi Sahiba has been transferred to Punjab Institute of Cardiology due to deteriorating health in jail,” her legal counsel, Rana Mudassar Umer, said on X.
He alleged that no family member was informed of her transfer to the hospital
نورین نیازی صاحبہ کی جیل میں طبعیت خراب ہونے پر پنجاب کارڈیالوجی منتقل کیا گیا ہے۔ ان کی صحت کیلئے دعاؤں کی درخواست ہے۔ 70 سالہ نورین نیازی غیر قانونی نظر بند ہیں اور ان کی ہسپتال منتقلی پر کسی خاندان کے شخص کو اطلاع نہیں دی گئی۔ pic.twitter.com/IRXs29TcWV

The PTI expressed serious concern over the reported deterioration in Noreen’s health in detention and her transfer to the PIC in Lahore, in what the party described as an "extremely alarming condition".
In a statement shared on X, the party criticised the authorities over the treatment of the 70-year-old, alleging that she was being held in illegal and unconstitutional detention. The PTI described the situation as an example of state oppression and raised concerns about the risks to her health.
"The most shameful thing is that, despite such a grave situation, not even a single family member was informed about her transfer to the hospital," the party said, while questioning the legal and administrative basis for transferring an elderly woman to the hospital without informing her loved ones.

— PTI (@PTIofficial) October 28, 2026
The PTI also accused the government of subjecting former prime minister’s sister and other members of his family to harassment and mistreatment for political reasons.
"If anything happens to her, the entire responsibility will lie directly with the current rulers and the relevant administration," the statement read further.
Two days earlier on October 26, the Lahore High Court disposed of a petition for the release of Imran’s three sisters after the Punjab government confirmed that their detention had been extended by another 30 days.
