— Insist on leadership rotation to Abia, urge massive voter turnout
By Steve Oko
The South-East Traditional Rulers Council has renewed its demand for the unconditional release of detained Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, lamenting that previous appeals to the Federal Government have failed to yield the desired outcome.
The monarchs also reaffirmed their position that the council’s leadership should rotate to Abia State, with HRM Eze Sir Dr Linus Nto Mbah assuming the chairmanship in accordance with the council’s constitution.
These resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued after the council’s quarterly delegates meeting held on October 23, 2026, at the Parliament of Ndi Eze, Owerri, Imo State.
On the political front, the traditional rulers expressed concern over the scheduled dates for the forthcoming national elections, which they said could pose challenges for the South-East.
They nevertheless urged eligible voters across the region to return to their respective registration areas and participate massively in the elections.
The council also called on traditional rulers and community leaders to suspend festivals and ceremonies during the election period to enable eligible voters to exercise their civic responsibilities.
On traditional leadership in the South, the monarchs reaffirmed their support for the rotational chairmanship of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council among the South-East, South-West and South-South geopolitical zones.
They rejected any arrangement that would confer permanent chairmanship on one zone, insisting that the position should rotate among the three zones for two-year terms, in line with the decision of the Southern Governors Forum reached in Ogun State in 2025.
The council further called for the reconstitution of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council’s leadership to reflect recognised traditional rulers from member states and conform to the leadership template of the Southern Governors Forum.
The communiqué was signed by the chairman of the South-East Traditional Rulers Council and chairman of the Abia State Council of Traditional Rulers, HRM Eze Dr Linus Nto Mbah; the Obi of Onitsha, HRM Igwe Nnaemeka Achebe; and other traditional rulers from the five South-East states.
The monarchs expressed appreciation to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, for hosting the meeting, as well as the Imo State Council of Traditional Rulers and the people of the state for their hospitality.
They also acknowledged the support and encouragement of governors across the South-East.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
.Vows to hunt down anyone who threatens ad-hoc staff, corps members
.Set to hold National Election Security Confab
By Omeiza Ajayi
ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has unveiled an intelligence-led security framework to curb violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, vowing to hunt down anyone who threatens its ad-hoc staff, National Youth Service Corps NYSC members or permanent personnel.
INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this in Gombe on Tuesday while declaring open the North-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election.
The Commission in its daily bulletin said it was shifting from reactive, election-day deployments to a framework designed to protect voters, personnel and electoral materials before any ballot paper is moved.
INEC said its collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC, the Department of State Services DSS, the Armed Forces and other paramilitary agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES has, according to him, been fundamentally restructured.
The new framework, which the Commission terms the “ICCES Tentacle,” extends inter-agency security coordination from national and state headquarters directly down to the most remote Local Government Areas and Registration Area Centres.
Amupitan told the gathering that no election, however well planned administratively, could be deemed credible if voters, election personnel and observers operate under physical threat or fear of violence.
He explained that the framework rests on three pillars, the first being “Map and Mitigate.” Under it, the Commission will use Electoral Risk Management (ERM) tools to identify security flashpoints, seasonal threat factors and local vulnerabilities early, so that security agencies can deploy proactive measures long before ballot papers arrive.
The second pillar, “Ensure Safety,” provides a protective umbrella over all electoral personnel, technological assets, including Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and server infrastructure, and, most importantly, the voter.
The third pillar, “Guarantee Access,” is aimed at ensuring that each of the 176,846 polling units nationwide remains a safe, peaceful and dignified space for the exercise of democratic rights, regardless of geographical remoteness or historical security challenges.
According to him, the collaboration among the agencies had already produced concrete results. He disclosed that joint operations led by the DSS recently uncovered a covert plot by criminal kingpins targeting the Commission’s ad-hoc staff and Youth Corps members.
Amupitan said swift, intelligence-led intervention neutralised the threat, and the principal orchestrators were arrested and are currently undergoing prosecution.
“Let me send a clear message from Gombe,” Amupitan said, warning that anyone who attempts to threaten, intimidate or harm ad-hoc staff, NYSC members or permanent personnel of the Commission would be hunted down and brought to justice under the full weight of the law.
He disclosed that the Commission would shortly convene a National Election Security Conference in Abuja, where state-specific security protocols for high-risk zones would be finalised.
Amupitan acknowledged that the North-East presents distinct operational challenges, including vast desert terrains, riverine stretches along the Benue trough, remote agrarian communities and expansive landmasses. He noted, however, that the zone had demonstrated remarkable resilience and civic determination.
The zone has 13,965,475 registered voters, representing 13.51 per cent of the national register of over 103 million. Bauchi State has the highest number with 3,012,547 voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671.
The Chairman said the 2027 General Election would be a simultaneous national undertaking across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The Presidential and National Assembly Elections are scheduled for Saturday, 16th January 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly Elections will hold on Saturday, 6th February 2027.
Earlier, the host Resident Electoral Commissioner REC for Gombe State, Alhaji Umar Muktar Gajiram, speaking on behalf of all North-East RECs, assured the Chairman that the zone was fully prepared, loyal and committed to ensuring that not a single voter out of the 13.96 million in the zone is disenfranchised.
Gajiram said all directives on voter register display, logistics audit and technological testing would be executed to the letter.
Amupitan assured staff and stakeholders across the North-East that INEC was not working in isolation, describing security as “the bedrock of electoral integrity.”
“Insecurity may pose a challenge, but our collective constitutional resolve is far stronger,” he said.
The post 2027: How we will curb election violence – INEC appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja
Diplomats from MIKTA member countries and the Federal government have called for improved access to climate finance, stronger international partnerships and increased investment in practical solutions to help developing countries address climate change.
The call was made at a MIKTA roundtable on Climate Finance and Implementation Partnerships in Africa, held on Tuesday in Abuja, ahead of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP31, scheduled to hold in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20.
The discussions brought together representatives of Australia, Türkiye, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Mexico, Ethiopia and relevant stakeholders from the climate change sector to examine ways of translating climate commitments into projects that support economic growth, energy access, agriculture and community resilience.
Speaking at the meeting, the Australian High Commissioner to Nigeria, Ms Leilani Bin-Juda PSM, said climate action must deliver practical outcomes, particularly for developing countries and communities most vulnerable to its effects.
Bin-Juda said many developing countries continued to face difficulties accessing climate finance because of complex applications, fragmented funding systems, reporting requirements and delays.
She said Australia was working with Türkiye towards COP31 and with Pacific partners to ensure their priorities were reflected in the global climate discussions.
The High Commissioner also highlighted a Pacific-led Action Plan on access to climate finance for Small Island Developing States and Least Developed Countries, launched at Pre-COP in Fiji on October 8.
She said the initiative sought to simplify funding applications, approvals and disbursement, mobilise private investment and strengthen countries’ capacity to develop investment-ready projects.
Bin-Juda urged Nigeria to support the initiative, noting that broader international backing would strengthen efforts to make climate finance more accessible and responsive to the needs of vulnerable countries.
“For Australia, COP31 is about turning climate ambition into practical outcomes,” she said.
The Turkish Ambassador to Nigeria, Mehmet Poroy, said COP31 should focus on implementing existing commitments and ensuring that climate ambitions translated into measurable results.
Poroy said African countries needed adequate financial resources, technology, institutional capacity and support for project preparation to implement their national climate plans.
He said climate finance should also support development priorities, including energy systems, sustainable agriculture, food security, green industries and climate-resilient cities.
The ambassador highlighted Türkiye’s Climate Implementation Bridge initiative, being developed with the United Nations Development Programme, to help developing countries bridge the gap between climate commitments and investment-ready projects.
He explained that the initiative was not designed to establish a new fund or replace existing climate finance mechanisms, but to help countries connect their climate priorities with appropriate financing and private capital.
Poroy said cooperation between MIKTA countries and African partners could help strengthen implementation as the international community prepares for COP31 and COP32, expected to be hosted by Ethiopia in 2027.
Meanwhile, the Indonesian Ambassador to Nigeria, Bambang Suharto, said the scale of investment required to achieve climate targets in developing countries highlighted the need to combine public resources, private investment and international support.
He said Indonesia estimated that it would require about $472.6bn to achieve its climate targets, with annual financing needs of approximately $14.5bn through 2030, compared with an annual state budget allocation of about $4.42bn.
Suharto said Indonesia was exploring different financing instruments, including green sukuk, blended finance, thematic bonds and concessional funding, to support climate action.
He called for existing international climate finance commitments to be delivered and for greater support for project preparation to help countries develop proposals capable of attracting investment.
The envoy also highlighted the importance of ocean conservation and coastal resilience, including mangrove restoration, early-warning systems and sustainable fisheries.
He expressed Indonesia’s readiness to consult with Nigeria and interested partners on a possible Indonesia-Nigeria Climate Finance and Resilience Partnership, with potential areas of cooperation including climate-resilient agriculture, land restoration, coastal protection, clean energy and green industrialisation.
Similarly, South Korea’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yoan, outlined opportunities to deepen climate cooperation with Nigeria through renewable energy, agricultural technology, infrastructure and green investment.
Jeong said South Korea was committed to achieving carbon neutrality by 2050 and had set a 2035 target to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by 53 to 61 per cent compared with 2018 levels.
He said Korea’s cooperation with Nigeria included a planned 2026 to 2030 project involving the Korea International Cooperation Agency, KOICA, and the Food and Agriculture Organisation, FAO, aimed at creating green jobs for young people in agriculture and food systems.
According to him, the project is expected to support practical training in climate-smart agriculture and digital technology, with the broader objective of improving food security and strengthening resilience.
Jeong also identified private investment and a stable investment environment as important factors in mobilising climate finance, noting that clear regulations, transparent procedures and reliable infrastructure could encourage long-term investment.
He noted, Nigeria estimated that it would require about $337bn between 2026 and 2035 to meet its climate commitments, underscoring the need for domestic resources, international financing and private-sector participation.
The Mexican Charge d’Affaires in Nigeria, Jose Manuel Briseno Flores, also stressed the need to ensure that climate resources translated into practical outcomes, including renewable energy products.
He said climate finance should support solutions that could be deployed to address the needs of communities while advancing the transition towards cleaner energy.
In her remarks, the Director-General of the National Council on Climate Change, NCCC, Mrs Omotenioye Majekodunmi, said the country was committed to moving from climate pledges to implementation.
Majekodunmi who was represented by the council’s Department of Energy, Transportation and Infrastructure, NCCC, Mrs Jummai Vandu said Nigeria supported efforts to turn its Nationally Determined Contributions into bankable, investment-ready projects that could attract financing and deliver measurable results.
She identified adaptation finance, decentralised climate action, gender inclusion and a just transition as key priorities for the country.
According to her, climate finance must be predictable and accessible to communities facing environmental challenges, while international partnerships should create pathways for states, cities and local governments to implement projects at the subnational level.
She also said women and young people should be empowered as decision-makers and direct beneficiaries of climate investments, adding that the transition to clean energy must protect energy security, job creation and economic equity.
Majekodunmi said Nigeria was ready to work with MIKTA, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and other international partners to ensure that COP31 produced practical outcomes.
Also speaking, the Ambassador of Ethiopia to Nigeria, Legesse Geremew Haile, said Africa faced disproportionate climate vulnerabilities despite contributing marginally to global emissions.
He called for direct access to predictable, grant-based financing and technology transfers, noting that African countries needed support to implement their climate priorities.
The Ethiopian envoy highlighted his country’s Climate Resilient Green Economy Strategy and Green Legacy Initiative as examples of efforts to combine environmental protection, employment and sustainable development.
He said Ethiopia was looking forward to hosting COP32 in 2027, adding that the conference would provide an opportunity to place African development priorities, just energy transitions and loss-and-damage delivery at the centre of the global climate agenda.
MIKTA is a cross-regional partnership comprising Mexico, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Türkiye and Australia.

items.content:
By Clare Nnabuike, Minna
Five person, four male students and a young lady have died in a fatal accident involving the Niger state governor Mohammed Umaru Bago’s convoy in Minna, the state capital.
The incident happened on Monday at Gidan Mangoro community along the Minna–Bida Road. It followed a head-on collision between a high speeding Hilux van in the convoy of Bago, and a private Peugeot 206 car.
The lady identified as Mrs Nafisa was driving the car and died at the spot of the accident. She was said to be a staff of an NGO, and Programme Manager at Labspace, and the Founder of Wosh Mart Service Ltd.
A resident of Gidan Mangoro, Abdullahi Musa, told Vanguard that the accident occurred at about 11:35am when the governor was returning from Bida. He and his team paid a condolence visit on the Etsu Nupe and chairman of the Niger state council of traditional rulers Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar over the passage of the Sagi Nupe Hajia Aisha.
He said the occupants of the private car driven by Nafisa were suspected to be postgraduate students of the Federal University of Technology, Minna.
His words, “The people in the private car died instantly, while those in the government Hilux sustained serious injuries with the driver dying on the spot.
Nafisa
“The accident was caused by wrongful overtaking by the Hilux in the governor’s convoy. The other car was in its lane when the Hilux rammed into it.”
A member of staff of Minna General Hospital, where the victims were rushed to told Vanguard that three people died on the spot while two other people died due to high level of injuries sustain from the crash.
“Some of the injured victims were subsequently referred to IBB Specialist Hospital for advanced medical care,” he said.
Vanguard gathered that one of the occupants of the Hilux van was a former Niger state local government council chairman who sustained fractures to his legs but was still alive at the time of this report.
The Niger State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC Aishat Sa’adu, confirmed the road crash but said that by the time her officers arrived at the scene, the victims had already been evacuated to the hospital.
The Police Public Relations Officer of the Niger state command Superintendent of Police Wasiu Abiodun confirmed the incident and said the accident was under investigation. He did not however give the names or numbers of the deceased.
“The accident occured this morning and we are investigating it,” Abiodun said.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
…19-month health workers’ arrears
By Victor Ahiuma-Young
The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) have reached an agreement on a series of measures aimed at easing the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and the payment of 19 months’ arrears owed to health workers.
The resolutions were reached at a conciliation meeting held at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, following an earlier meeting convened on 22 October.
The meetings were organised to address concerns raised by the NLC over the rising cost of living, the implementation of the National Minimum Wage, petroleum pump prices, workers’ welfare and outstanding allowances.
Under the agreement, the Federal Government will provide a transport intervention of ₦70,000 across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026.
The government also approved the peculiar allowance with effect from 1 May 2026. Payment of the arrears is expected to begin in November and will be made in three equal monthly instalments.
In addition, the 19 months’ outstanding allowances owed to health workers will be paid within three months, beginning in December 2026.
The meeting also agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and commence work immediately. However, the parties remained divided over the effective date for implementing the new minimum wage.
On the issue of tax relief for workers, the meeting resolved that the matter would be referred to the National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory issue.
The Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications of the proposed hazard allowance for agricultural officers to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission for verification.
The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template.
Similarly, the NSIWC is expected to complete an updated assessment of the cost implications of the proposed CONHESS adjustment within three weeks. The assessment will enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to take a decision on the matter.
The Federal Government and the NLC urged state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and implement the agreed measures.
The parties also agreed to reconvene after one month to review the level of implementation of the resolutions.
The agreement was signed on behalf of the federal government by Dr. Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, Honourable Minister of Labour and Employment, Timi Yakubu, Director-General, Budget, Dr. Garba Abdul S. U., Permanent Secretary (SWO), Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation. For the NLC , its president, Comrade Joe Ajaero; For the Joint National Public Service Negotiation Council (JNPSNC), National Secretary, JNPSNC, Olowoyo Gbenga

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎ABUJA– THE National Credit Guarantee Company Limited (NCGC) on Tuesday said its guarantees have already unlocked ₦64.13 billion in loans for 174,495 borrowers nationwide, as it intensifies efforts to dismantle the collateral barriers that have long shut viable Nigerian businesses out of formal credit.
It said it is supporting an estimated 914,791 direct and indirect jobs within its first 14 months of operation.
‎‎Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Bonaventure Okhaimo, disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents at the presidential villa, Abuja, on the company’s achievements, challenges and expansion plans.
‎‎The company, which was established by President Bola Tinubu to dismantle longstanding barriers to credit access, has also disclosed that 22,616 Nigerians who had never accessed formal bank credit have secured loans through its intervention, while women now account for 42.7 per cent of beneficiaries.
‎‎Okhaimo, who was accompanied by the Executive Director, Risk Management, Professor Ezekiel Oseni, and Executive Director, Strategy and Operations, Mrs. Tinuola Aigwedo, among others, explained that the company had deployed N30.19 billion in credit guarantees to unlock the N64.13 billion in loans as of October 21, 2026.
‎‎He said the intervention had enabled participating financial institutions to extend loans to previously excluded businesses and individuals, particularly those unable to meet conventional collateral requirements.
‎‎According to him, the initiative has already reached more than 170,000 beneficiaries through 19 participating financial institutions, including commercial and microfinance banks.
‎‎”For every one naira that we give as a credit guarantee to a bank, it creates two naira in loans. That’s the additionality”, Okhaimo explained.
‎‎He stressed that President Tinubu established the company to address a fundamental weakness in Nigeria’s financial system, where otherwise viable businesses were routinely denied credit because they lacked acceptable collateral.
‎‎”The President has said, don’t let a viable Nigerian business suffer because it doesn’t have collateral. He has taken the collateral and given it to the bank. So that’s what we are doing”, he said.
‎‎Explaining the operational model, Okhaimo said NCGC does not lend directly to businesses or individuals but provides guarantees that encourage financial institutions to extend credit to borrowers they would ordinarily consider too risky.
‎‎He said the company currently assumes up to 60 per cent of the credit risk on eligible loans, allowing lenders to relax collateral requirements while retaining responsibility for credit assessment, loan monitoring and recovery.
‎‎According to him, some banks traditionally demand collateral worth more than 150 per cent of the amount being borrowed, a practice that excludes many small businesses despite their commercial viability.
‎‎”What we are saying is, forget about collateral. Do the other due diligence. As long as the customer’s business is viable and the customer has good character, we are willing to support by giving you a credit guarantee that will enable you to give loans to your customers”, he stated.
‎‎On employment generation, the NCGC boss said the company’s interventions had supported 914,791 jobs, comprising direct employment reported by participating banks and indirect employment estimated through recognised development finance multipliers.
‎‎He explained that the indirect employment calculations were based on sector-specific multipliers, including those used by the African Development Bank, with NCGC attributing employment impact according to its share of guaranteed credit risk.
‎‎Speaking on the initiative, Aigwedo said women entrepreneurs remained disproportionately excluded from formal credit because of their limited ownership of assets acceptable as collateral.

Internet users in Pakistan may face slower speeds during peak hours until November 2, 2026, due to emergency maintenance on the AAE-1 international submarine cable, Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) has announced.
According to PTCL, the maintenance began today, October 27, on the section of the cable between Italy and France. The company said users in Pakistan may experience “minor service degradation” during peak hours while the work continues.
PTCL thanked its customers for their patience and understanding during the maintenance period.
Why AAE-1 Matters for Pakistan
The Asia-Africa-Europe 1 (AAE-1) cable is one of the main routes carrying Pakistan’s international internet traffic. The roughly 25,000-kilometer system links South East Asia to Europe through Egypt and lands in Pakistan at Karachi.
PTCL commissioned its Pakistan operations in 2017. The cable connects the country to Europe through landing points in Greece, Italy, and France.
Because the maintenance is on the European end of the cable, users are most likely to notice slower speeds when accessing services hosted in Europe, especially during busy evening hours.
Previous Disruptions
This is not the first time issues with AAE-1 have affected internet users in Pakistan. In January 2025, a fault on the cable near Qatar caused slow internet speeds across the country for nearly two weeks before PTCL announced that it had been fixed.
PTCL has not said whether it will add backup bandwidth during the current maintenance window.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
…Says past loans failed to ease hardship
…2026 capital budget yet to be implemented
…Rising fuel prices show loans haven’t eased hardship
…No work on Eastern Rail Line despite $3bn loan approval
By Juliet Umeh
Senator Victor Umeh has questioned the Federal Government’s request for fresh loans, saying there is no justification for further borrowing when the government says it has surpassed its revenue targets.
Umeh, who represents Anambra Central, spoke on Channels Television’s programme, where he reacted to the President’s request for approval of additional external borrowing. He said the government should account for previous loans and show their impact on Nigerians’ lives.
“From what they have told us, there is no justification for the borrowing. Since you have surpassed your revenue expectations, there is no need taking the country into a circus around borrowing all the time,” he said.
Umeh said previous loans had been presented as funding for infrastructure, but Nigerians were yet to see the results.
“All the borrowing plans we have approved before have been hinged on the development of infrastructure. When you ask where the money is going, you are told the government needs money for emergencies,” he said.
He added: “What we want to see is how these monies you have borrowed have impacted positively on the lives of the Nigerian people.”
He said the country was in distress, with living costs rising while many people lacked money.
“The cost of living has become unacceptable. People don’t have money. They don’t have purchasing power in the midst of soaring costs,” he said.
Citing fuel prices, he said he had bought petrol at N1,410 per litre, while diesel was selling for about N1,889 per litre.
“When will these things come down? When can people buy petrol or diesel without complaints?” he asked.
Umeh criticised budget implementation, saying the 2026 capital budget had yet to be implemented as October drew to a close.
“In the 2026 budget, there is no implementation of the capital budget yet. This is the end of October. We have barely one month until the end of the year,” he said.
He cited a previously approved loan for the eastern rail line, saying no work was under way.
“Part of that $21 billion was $3 billion for the reconstruction of the Eastern Rail Line. No work is going on there,” he said.
He said the government should explain whether the funds had been accessed and how they had been used before seeking more loans.
Asked whether opposition lawmakers could block the request, Umeh said the governing majority had the numbers to secure its approval.
“We are not rubber stamps, but you don’t have the number to say no to it,” he said.

Akanbi Elizabeth, the widow of late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, broke down in tears while paying tribute to her husband at a memorial event in Ibadan, Oyo State.
In a video from the tribute night held at Jogor Centre on Tuesday, Elizabeth struggled to complete her speech as she became overwhelmed with emotion while remembering her late husband.
“Toluwanisings, my dear husband. I will forever miss you. Please do not forget your children and I,” she said.
Several gospel artistes attended the event to honour the late singer, including Adeyinka Alaseyori, Esther Igbekele, Laolu Gbenjo, Akintayo Akinwande, SB Live, Bidemi Olaoba, Mr Gbera, Peterson Okopi and Sarah Apekeola.
Nollywood actress Bimbo Oshin was also among the celebrities present at the memorial.
Toluwanisings died in Ibadan on October 14, 2026, after reportedly slumping. His death has since generated controversy over allegations that efforts to obtain emergency medical care for him were unsuccessful, disagreements over his burial arrangements
and calls for an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death.
Following his death, the singer’s personal assistant, Babadunni Gbolabo, alleged that efforts to secure emergency medical treatment took him to between seven and eight hospitals in Ibadan.
The allegations sparked public concern about access to emergency medical services and the circumstances surrounding the singer’s death.
The controversy surrounding his death has also extended to his burial arrangements, with disagreements emerging between his widow and members of his paternal family over where he should be laid to rest.
Meanwhile, the singer’s grandmother, Sabitiyu Olayemi, alleged that he neglected her for years, adding to the family-related controversies that emerged after his death.

By Peter Duru, Makurdi
The Benue State Police Command has arrested a 60-year-old man over the alleged defilement of a 10-year-old girl in Igumale, Ado Local Government Area, LGA, of the state.
The Commissioner of Police, CP, Cletus Nwadiogbu, disclosed this on Tuesday while briefing journalists on the security situation and operational achievements recorded by the command in October 2026.
According to him, the incident was reported to the police on October 13, prompting the arrest of the suspect, while the victim was taken for medical examination and necessary treatment.
Nwadiogbu said, “the Command recorded an arrest in an alleged defilement case reported on 13th October 2026 in Igumale, Ado Local Government Area, involving a 10-year-old girl.
“A 60-year-old suspect was arrested, while the victim was taken for medical examination and necessary treatment. Investigation is ongoing, and the Command will ensure that the matter is handled in accordance with the law, with the privacy and welfare of the victim protected.”
The Police Commissioner added that the case was among several serious offences being investigated by the command as part of efforts to protect vulnerable persons and bring suspected offenders to justice.
He also disclosed that “the Command rescued 29 kidnapped victims during the period under review through intelligence-led operations and collaboration with other security agencies and community-based security groups.”
According to him, “four passengers abducted after a commercial vehicle was attacked along Uzer Village axis of Ayilamo-Tse-Abi Road in Logo LGA on October 5 were rescued following a joint operation involving the police, Operation Whirl Stroke, Benue State Civil Protection Guards and local hunters.”
The Commissioner said “17 farmers were also rescued from Tse-Acha and Tse-Wuam communities in Bamun Village, Tombo District, Logo LGA, on October 7, while eight kidnapped victims, including a Reverend Father, were rescued in Ohimini LGA following their abduction along the Ugbokolo-Ajegbe-Awume Road on October 13.”
He disclosed that “the Command also arrested 34 foreign nationals during separate operations, comprising 16 Cameroonians apprehended in Otukpo LGA on October 9 and 18 Nigeriens intercepted at Orokam on October 22.”
He said investigations were ongoing to establish their immigration status and circumstances of movement.
Nwadiogbu further reported the arrest of suspects in separate operations against cultism, unlawful possession of firearms and violent crimes, with seven locally fabricated firearms and 16 rounds of ammunition and cartridges recovered during the period under review.
The Commissioner also disclosed that one suspected bandit was neutralised during an encounter involving personnel of Operation Zenda Joint Task Force along Amaafu-Abaji Road in Katsina-Ala LGA on October 2, while a locally fabricated firearm was recovered.
He urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible information to security agencies, stressing that public cooperation was essential to preventing crime and protecting lives and property across the state.
CP Nwadiogbu expressed gratitude to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, for his continued support and commitment to strengthening policing operations and ensuring the safety of lives and property across the country.
He also appreciated the Benue State Governor, Rev. Fr. Hyacinth Alia, for his constant support to the command and commitment to peace, security and stability in the state, while acknowledging the contributions of other security agencies, community leaders, local vigilantes and members of the public whose cooperation continues to support efforts to maintain law and order.

items.content:
A High Court of Imo State, on Tuesday, resumed trial of five persons accused of kidnapping 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps members on Independence Day, admitted the evidence tendered against them by the Department of State Services (DSS).
At the resumed sitting, the Court heard a continuation of the evidence of Ikem Emmanuel, the first principal witness, who testified that the defendants made confessional statements admitting to the crime of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms.
The witness tendered an audio visual recording of the confessions of the defendants.
He also tendered their written statements, the recovered firearms and money in cash, recovered recovered from them.
The Presiding Judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, in admitting the exhibits, ruled that the arms and money be kept in the custody of the DSS.
The principal witness maintained that the defendants statements were obtained in the presence of their legal representatives and DSS legal officers.
In a related matter involving two other kidnap suspects, the DSS officer also gave evidence on the investigation, stating that their confessional statements were taken under caution in the presence of their lawyers and DSS legal officers.
He also tendered the audio visual recording of their statements, written statements money recovered in Naira, but for want of time, could not tender his report.
At the conclusion of proceedings, the trial judge, Justice Orafu adjourned both matters to October 28th, 29th and 30th for continuation of hearing. He ordered that all the five defendants remain in custody of the DSS.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi
ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC on Tuesday said it flagged a number of questionable registration records during the physical display of the preliminary register of voters, and has begun reviewing them.
It added that currently investigating reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs in the register published on its website.
In a statement issued on Tuesday night, the Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Malam Mohammed Kudu Haruna, said the Commission “has noted public concerns and reports circulating on social media regarding suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters recently published on its website.”
The Commission said the online register was not a new or altered document. “The register published online on 26 October 2026 is the same preliminary register physically displayed at Registration Areas (RAs) nationwide from 9th to 15th October 2026 as part of the Display, Claims and Objections exercise,” the statement said.
It explained that the questionable records had already been picked up at that stage.
“During the physical display, a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination. The Commission commenced the process of reviewing these records and taking appropriate corrective action in accordance with established procedures,” it stated.
INEC added that what Nigerians can see online is the version before any of those corrections. “The online publication represents the original preliminary register and does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities,” the Commission said.
It stressed that the document was never meant to be the final word on who is eligible to vote.
“It is important to emphasize that the preliminary register is not the final certified register. The Display, Claims and Objections exercise is specifically intended to facilitate public scrutiny, identify inaccuracies and irregularities, and enable appropriate corrections before certification,” the statement said.
On the suspicious photographs, the Commission said it was looking into how they got into the register in the first place. “The Commission is also examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and will take appropriate action based on verified findings,” it said.
INEC also acknowledged the citizens and stakeholders who raised the alarm. “The Commission appreciates the vigilance of citizens and stakeholders who have brought these concerns to public attention. Such scrutiny contributes to the process of improving the accuracy and integrity of the register,” the statement read.
It assured the public that proven irregularities would not be swept aside. “The Commission assures Nigerians that verified irregularities will be addressed through the applicable procedures,” it said.
The Commission said the work would be completed before the final register is certified. “INEC remains committed to completing the necessary verification, adjudication, and data-cleanup processes ahead of the scheduled certification of the final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026,” Haruna said.

items.content:
By Henry Umoru, ABUJA
THE Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters has cleared the President, Nigeria Guild of Editors, NGE, and Editor, Vanguard Newspapers, Eze Anaba, and 15 other nominees for appointment to the governing board of the National Human Rights Commission, NHRC.
The committee, chaired by Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central) screened the nominees as part of the legislative process for reconstituting the commission’s governing board following President Bola Tinubu’s request for Senate confirmation.
The Committee will, thereafter, forward its report to the Senate for consideration at plenary, where the upper chamber will take a final position on the nominations.
Speaking with journalists after the screening exercise, Anaba explained that his nomination would provide an opportunity to sustain his longstanding commitment to human rights protection, which he described as an integral part of his journalism career.
The NGE President, who expressed confidence that his diverse professional backgrounds would strengthen the commission’s capacity to promote and protect the rights of Nigerians, however cautioned against making definitive commitments before the completion of the process by the Senate.
“We’ve just been screened. We’ve just been confirmed. So don’t let us jump the gun. That’s number one,” he said.
Anaba expressed satisfaction with the committee’s decision, adding that the Senate’s final position would determine the next stage of the process.
Explaining his background in human rights advocacy, the Vanguard Editor said his professional experience had consistently brought him into contact with issues relating to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms.
“I’ve done this human rights thing all my life. It has gone together with my journalism job. So it’s going to be a continuation of what I’ve been doing,” he said.
Anaba also disclosed that he had been associated with the activities of the NHRC before his nomination to its governing board, just as he expressed optimism that the incoming board, with its blend of professional expertise, would improve the commission’s performance and strengthen its contribution to human rights protection in the country.
Earlier in his remarks after the screening, Adegbonmire explained that the screening exercise had been completed and that the committee’s recommendations would be presented to the Senate for consideration.
He said the Senate would communicate its decision to the President through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation after deliberating on the report.
Adegbonmire clarified that the NHRC’s governing board comprises 16 members, including representatives of the Federal Ministries of Justice, Interior and Foreign Affairs.
He explained that the three ministries’ representatives were not subjected to individual screening because the law specifies the offices or ranks to be represented rather than the names of particular nominees.

By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo
Suspected kidnappers have abducted six persons during an attack on Nuru Suraj Estate in the Millennium City area of Kaduna metropolis on Tuesday morning.
The attackers were said to have invaded the estate early in the morning, shooting sporadically and throwing residents into panic as they scrambled for safety.
Sources in the area disclosed that the suspected kidnappers gained access to the estate through its second gate before carrying out the abduction.
A resident, who identified herself as Maman Hamid, said her house was close to those of the victims, adding that the attackers arrived at the estate and began shooting, causing fear among residents.
According to her, the assailants exploited the second entrance to gain access to the estate before whisking away the victims to an unknown destination.
The circumstances surrounding the abduction, including the identities of the victims and whether any contact had been established with their families, were not immediately clear as of the time of filing this report.
The incident has renewed concerns over the security situation in Millennium City, an area of Kaduna metropolis that has witnessed previous attacks by suspected kidnappers.
A few weeks ago, suspected kidnappers reportedly invaded another part of Millennium City and abducted several persons, raising fresh concerns among residents over the recurrence of such attacks in the area.
Efforts to obtain a reaction from the Kaduna State Police Command were unsuccessful as the command had yet to react to the latest incident as of the time of filing this report.

“Those who don’t have people following them are collecting cards in the hands of women; they are buying so as to stop them from coming out to vote,” he said.
He urged anyone whose PVC had been collected to retrieve it and encouraged eligible voters to turn out on election day with their cards.
“Everyone should not agree to sell their card, and everyone should come out on election day with their card,” the former police chief said.
The endorsement was announced at a rally organised by the Alago Support Group for Adamu, who is seeking to govern Nasarawa State in 2027.
He expressed appreciation to the group for its support, saying the endorsement had strengthened his confidence in his political ambition.
Adamu also thanked God for what he described as progress in his political journey, adding that the support from the Alago community was encouraging.
He said his ambition was driven by the need to improve the welfare of ordinary residents, particularly vulnerable people who, according to him, had been neglected under the present situation.
“Our coming out for this election is for the common people. We came out for the common man, to see that the common man does not suffer the way they are suffering now,” he said.
Adamu pledged to prioritise education, healthcare and security if elected governor, promising to pursue improvements in public services and create safer communities.
“We will put people’s lives first, to see that education with quality is given to our people, health with quality our people have obtained, and the issue of security, we will see that everyone will find peace, so that people can return to their homes to sleep without any fear,” he said.
He also expressed gratitude to the Alago Support Group and other supporters for their commitment to his aspiration, saying he hoped to secure victory in the 2027 election.
The former IGP’s allegation of PVC collection and vote-buying was not accompanied by specific details of those allegedly involved.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The federal government has agreed in principle to consider expanding its targeted subsidy on petroleum products, including diesel and up to five million more beneficiaries, sources told ProPakistani.
The development follows talks between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeem ur Rehman at the Prime Minister’s House.
If the technical committees of both sides build on the emerging consensus, petroleum products could become Rs. 30 to Rs. 40 per litre cheaper for eligible beneficiaries, sources said.
Targeted vs Blanket Subsidy
The type of subsidy remained the main point of disagreement during the negotiations. The government argued that targeted relief was necessary under the International Monetary Fund (IMF) program.
It said a blanket subsidy could put the programme at risk and would benefit wealthy and low-income consumers alike.
Instead, the government has offered to add up to five million more consumers to the existing petrol subsidy scheme. It is also considering bringing more older models of motorcycles and vehicles under the programme.
JI Pushes for Diesel Relief
JI insisted that diesel must also be covered, as agriculture and other key sectors rely heavily on it. The party said excluding diesel hurts farmers and raises costs across the economy.
In response, the government indicated that diesel could also be included in the targeted programme to an appropriate extent.
Sources added that the government has already cut the price of locally produced diesel by Rs. 32 per litre by delinking it from international prices, following pressure and negotiations by JI.
Both technical committees will continue working on the framework. The final scope, eligibility criteria, and subsidy amounts will depend on the outcome of these talks.
Earlier, Hafiz Naeem said the prime minister had asked for 7 to 10 more days to address JI’s demand to abolish the petroleum levy.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has confirmed that Pakistan is preparing to send its first astronaut into space in the near future.
Speaking at an international conference organized in collaboration with the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs in Islamabad on October 27, Iqbal said Pakistan had successfully launched five satellites over the past 18 months.
He said space technology was essential for protecting vulnerable communities from climate change and natural disasters, including floods, cyclones and glacial melting.
Planning Minister said satellite data and early warning systems could help reduce casualties and economic losses by improving disaster preparedness.
Referring to the devastating floods of 2022 and 2025, the minister said Pakistan had suffered economic losses exceeding $30 billion despite contributing less than one percent of global greenhouse gas emissions.
He criticized international partners and financial institutions for failing to provide adequate new grant financing for reconstruction, saying that repurposing previously approved loans for education and health was inconsistent with climate justice.
Iqbal called for reforms to the international financial system and urged developed countries and financial institutions to provide grant-based assistance to vulnerable nations rather than adding to their debt.
He also stressed the need to incorporate satellite data into development planning, particularly for infrastructure projects such as roads, bridges and hospitals.
The minister called for better information-sharing among government institutions, investment in space-related skills and more opportunities for young people, especially women, in space science and geospatial technologies.
He also urged regional cooperation to improve disaster preparedness and the exchange of information on shared rivers, mountain systems and climate risks.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Modders have discovered a way to unlock previously restricted AI processing performance on Nvidia’s GeForce RTX 20, 30, and 40-series graphics cards.
The modification removes a performance limit that Nvidia placed on certain AI calculations, allowing supported GPUs to complete some operations up to twice as fast.
According to VideoCardz, the RTX 4090 can achieve double its previous peak performance in specific AI tests, while the RTX 3090 Ti has shown improvements of up to 80% in certain calculations.
However, the improvements mainly apply to AI-related tasks rather than gaming.
How Modders Unlocked the Performance
Nvidia’s GeForce RTX graphics cards contain specialized hardware called Tensor Cores, which helps process artificial intelligence workloads.
However, Nvidia has limited the speed of certain calculations on its consumer graphics cards. Specifically, calculations that use FP32 accumulation run at half the speed of similar operations using FP16 accumulation.
These restrictions do not apply in the same way to some of Nvidia’s professional graphics cards. Modders have now discovered a way to bypass the restrictions by changing low-level GPU settings before Nvidia’s graphics driver starts.
The modification does not require replacing the GPU hardware or permanently changing its firmware. The changes are temporary and are cleared when the GPU loses power.
RTX 4090 and RTX 3090 Ti See Major Improvements
Early testing shows significant improvements in certain AI calculations.
The RTX 4090’s peak processing performance increased from approximately 165.6 trillion operations per second to 331.6 trillion operations per second in a specific Tensor Core test.
Meanwhile, the RTX 3090 Ti recorded an improvement of approximately 80% in BF16 calculations used for AI processing.

These figures represent specific AI computing tests rather than overall GPU performance.
Other supported graphics cards have also shown improvements, although the results vary depending on the model and workload.
What This Means for AI and Gaming
The unlocked performance could benefit people who use Nvidia graphics cards to run AI applications on their computers.
Tasks involving complex mathematical calculations, including AI image generation and processing prompts for local chatbots, could become faster.
However, the performance improvements are generally smaller in real-world applications than in the benchmark results.
For example, some RTX 3090 tests showed improvements of roughly 14% to 36% in AI prompt processing.
The speed at which chatbots generate text remains largely unchanged because that process often depends more on memory bandwidth than raw processing power.
Importantly, the modification does not provide a similar performance boost in video games.
Not All Nvidia Graphics Cards Are Supported
The modifications currently target selected models from Nvidia’s RTX 20, 30, and 40-series graphics cards.
Most of the available tools are designed for Linux, although experimental Windows versions are also being developed.
Support varies between different GPU models, and the modifications have not been confirmed to work across every graphics card in these generations.
Nvidia’s newer RTX 50-series cards are not currently covered by the confirmed working methods.
The tools are also experimental and carry risks, including system crashes, startup failures, and possible hardware problems.
For now, the discovery shows that some older Nvidia graphics cards can deliver significantly higher AI processing performance without requiring new hardware, although the actual benefits depend on the software and tasks being used.

items.title: Decision Final on New Provinces
items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has called for a “full stop” to the debate on creating new provinces, saying the people of Sindh have already given their decision.
Speaking to the media at Spencer Eye Hospital in Karachi’s Lyari on Tuesday, alongside Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah, Bilawal said the Sindh Assembly had made its stance clear “at least seven to eight times now.”
“The people here can determine the fate of this province and the city. I think we should close this topic because the people themselves have closed it,” he said.
He was responding to a question about the “pressure” on the PPP over new administrative units and a possible rollback of the 18th Amendment. When asked whether the government had spoken to him about a 28th constitutional amendment, he simply replied, “No.”
Karachi Needs Federal Attention
Commenting on the dispute between the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) and Pakistan Railways, Bilawal said the federal government should pay attention to Karachi, which he called the country’s economic hub.
The debate on new provinces began in July after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi proposed dialogue among political parties on governance reforms.
MQM-P has since demanded a separate province for Karachi, while the PPP has strongly opposed the idea. In September, the Sindh Assembly passed a resolution rejecting any attempt to divide the province.

The D-8 Organisation for Economic Cooperation is pursuing a target of $500 billion in intra-member trade by 2030, Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan said in Doha, where he discussed measures to strengthen economic integration and accelerate trade among member countries and pressed for implementation of the bloc's Preferential Trade Agreement following its ratification by Egypt.
The D-8 secretary-general appreciated Pakistan's continued support for the organisation and highlighted the importance of implementing the agreement, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of Commerce on Tuesday.
Both sides emphasised the need to translate existing economic cooperation frameworks into practical commercial opportunities through greater private-sector participation, improved market access and stronger trade linkages among member states, in discussions that also focused on advancing the organisation's trade target.
Khan reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to strengthening cooperation within the D-8 framework and supporting initiatives aimed at facilitating trade, encouraging investment and promoting sustainable economic growth among member economies.
The meeting on October 25 was one of a series of high-level engagements during the World Investment Forum 2026 in which the minister met senior officials, international economic leadership and prominent business representatives, focusing on strengthening Pakistan's international trade relations, attracting foreign investment, enhancing regional connectivity and expanding economic cooperation across key sectors.
During the engagements held on October 25 and 26, Khan met Qatar's Minister of Municipality, the chairman of the Qatar Chamber of Commerce and Industries and representatives of Retaj Group, with the meetings exploring opportunities for expanding bilateral and multilateral trade, strengthening private-sector linkages and promoting investment in agriculture, food security, industrial development, hospitality and tourism.
In a separate bilateral meeting on October 26, Khan met Qatar's Minister of Municipality to discuss expanding cooperation in agriculture, food security and bilateral trade, with both sides exchanging views on opportunities to strengthen commercial relations and promote greater institutional and business-level engagement in agricultural development and food supply chains.
The discussions highlighted the potential for closer collaboration between relevant government institutions and private-sector stakeholders to identify practical areas of cooperation and facilitate mutually beneficial commercial partnerships, and reaffirmed the shared commitment of both countries to further strengthening longstanding bilateral relations through enhanced economic engagement in sectors of common interest.
In another engagement, Khan met the chairman of the Qatar Chamber of Commerce and Industries to explore new avenues for strengthening bilateral trade, investment and private-sector cooperation, and invited Qatari investors to explore opportunities in Pakistan's Special Economic Zones (SEZs), particularly in the Karachi industrial area, where export-oriented manufacturing and industrial partnerships could provide access to domestic and international markets.
He encouraged the Qatari business community to expand business-to-business interactions with Pakistani counterparts and develop stronger people-to-people connections to translate the longstanding friendship between the two countries into tangible economic and commercial opportunities, and highlighted Pakistan's strategic geographical position and the potential for investors to access wider regional markets, including Africa, through improved trade connectivity and supply-chain networks.
The Qatar Chamber chairman highlighted changing global supply-chain dynamics and expressed interest in proposed regional transit routes and connectivity initiatives.
Both sides recognised that improved logistics infrastructure, diversified supply chains and stronger regional transport connections could play a significant role in facilitating trade, reducing commercial barriers and opening new markets for businesses in both countries.
As part of his engagements with Qatar's private sector, Khan also met representatives of Retaj Group to discuss potential cooperation in the hospitality and tourism industries, during which the group expressed interest in exploring joint ventures with Pakistani business partners and examining opportunities to expand its hospitality brands into Pakistan and other Islamic countries.
The discussions focused on potential investment partnerships, hospitality-sector development and opportunities for greater collaboration between businesses of the two countries, with both sides recognising the potential of hospitality and tourism cooperation to encourage private investment, create new commercial opportunities and strengthen economic relations.
The series of meetings reflected Pakistan's continued efforts to diversify its international economic partnerships, attract foreign investment and strengthen its position in regional and global trade networks, and highlighted the growing importance of private-sector cooperation, regional connectivity, agricultural development, food security, industrial investment and hospitality in expanding economic relations.
Khan reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to maintaining close engagement with international institutions, government counterparts and business communities to translate economic dialogue into practical trade and investment opportunities, and the meetings concluded with a shared understanding of the importance of continued institutional coordination, stronger business linkages and mutually beneficial partnerships to advance economic cooperation and sustainable growth.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its winning streak on Tuesday, holding firmly in positive territory throughout the session, as broad-based buying in heavyweight sectors lifted market mood. Investors seemed to have moved past the State Bank of Pakistan's (SBP) latest rate hike as softer international oil prices and hopes of progress in resolving the US-Israel conflict with Iran sparked interest.
The benchmark KSE-100 index maintained its upward trajectory after a strong opening, where stock buying gathered pace in cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration and oil marketing sectors. The market's advance reflected investors' willingness to keep their exposure to equities despite a tighter monetary policy.
The index added 1,428.73 points, or 0.88%, to settle at 164,467.20. During the session, it touched the high of 164,787.67 and low of 163,545.70, remaining in the green throughout the day.
Meanwhile, international oil prices fell amid expectations of easing of hostilities in the Middle East, but persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia and maritime shipping kept investors wary and prices near six-month highs. The combination of positive factors allowed the benchmark index to extend gains despite worries about implications of the higher policy rate for businesses and economic activity.
"The market witnessed a positive session, primarily supported by buying interest in commercial banks, cement, fertiliser and automobile sectors," remarked Ahmed Sheraz, equity trader at KASB KTrade. MCB Bank, Fauji Fertiliser, UBL, Pakistan Petroleum and NBP were among the key contributors to the market's performance.
"Additionally, with the ongoing corporate results season, stock-specific activity continues to drive investor flows, leading to selective buying despite broader macroeconomic concerns," he said. "However, there is a cautious outlook amid geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East, Israeli elections and the upcoming US midterm polls."
Brent crude traded around $115-116 a barrel, which sparked fears about imported inflation, while domestic price pressures and the increase in the SBP policy rate to 12% may continue to weigh on investor sentiment. "Going forward, the market is expected to maintain a mixed-to-cautious stance, with corporate earnings, oil prices, geopolitical developments and macro indicators dictating direction. Selective, stock-specific activity may lend support to the index, although volatility is expected to stay elevated," Sheraz said.
According to Ali Najib of Arif Habib Limited (AHL), the market opened on a strong note, remained in positive territory throughout the session and closed near its intra-day highs. The rally was primarily driven by investor relief following the SBP's moderate 50-basis-point rate hike, which was lower than an aggressive 100bps increase anticipated by some market participants while considering the geopolitical situation, global oil prices and their impact on domestic inflation.
Sentiment was further supported by easing geopolitical concerns amid diplomatic efforts by the Makkah alliance countries, including Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, as officials held high-level talks in Iran to explore a peaceful resolution to the ongoing US-Iran conflict. On the macroeconomic front, the SBP reported cumulative net foreign exchange interventions of $17.2 billion between Jun'24 and Jul'26, including $863 million in Jul'26, highlighting its continued management of forex market liquidity and reserve accumulation.
Cumulatively, trading volumes increased to 402 million shares versus Monday's total of 376 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs18 billion.
Shares of 497 companies were traded in the ready market. Of these, 282 stocks closed higher, 170 fell and 45 remained unchanged.

items.content:
Oil futures fell by more than $2 a barrel on Tuesday as traders focused on Middle East peace talks, though prices remained near the highest in six months as the Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict raged on and investors worried about the potential for more fighting in the US-Israeli war with Iran.
Brent crude futures were down $2.09, or 1.8%, at $113.72 a barrel by 1744 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude was down $1.93, or 1.9%, at $99.83.
Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei met Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on Tuesday, a day after holding talks with representatives of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan. State media said Khamenei had emphasised the importance of pursuing Iran's interests and maintaining its conditions for ending the war.
The four countries agreed to continue talks with a view to strengthening cooperation in peace and security, Iranian state media said.
Swiss bank UBS said it expects Brent prices to stay elevated near $110 a barrel through to the end of the year, citing volatile Middle East supply and geopolitical uncertainty. It was previously forecasting $100 a barrel at the end of this year.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has risen but the number of vessel attacks has increased, with risks likely to become more acute if US naval support wavers, UBS said.
Investors were also looking for cues from a general election in Israel on Tuesday.
"The outcome of today's parliamentary elections in Israel could also be significant for further developments in the war with Iran, as Israeli Prime Minister (Benjamin) Netanyahu, if re-elected, might attempt to achieve regime change in Iran," Commerzbank analysts wrote.
OPEC+ set to keep output targets steady
OPEC+ oil-producing countries are likely to keep their December oil output targets steady on Sunday, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters, in line with expectations that further output policy adjustments are unlikely until next year.
The online meeting of seven core OPEC+ members - Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman - comes as Gulf members have been boosting exports that have been disrupted for months by the Iran war. Most, however, are still pumping well below their output targets.
All three people declined to be named and said no final decision had been made.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain has emphasised that agricultural research institutions must produce practical results that could directly benefit farmers, increase crop productivity and contribute to Pakistan's economic growth.
He expressed these views while chairing a high-level meeting at the National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC), Islamabad, where he reviewed the research achievements of various institutes during Kharif 2026 and their plans for Rabi 2026-27.
Addressing the scientists, Rana Tanveer Hussain stressed that developing high-yielding, climate-resilient crop varieties, improving water-use efficiency and reducing agricultural production costs must remain central priorities of national research institutions.
The federal minister particularly directed scientists to accelerate the development of indigenous Basmati rice varieties with superior yield and quality to reduce dependence on Indian varieties. He also called for paying greater attention to pulses and oilseeds, adding that increasing their domestic production would help reduce Pakistan's import bill.
Hussain directed the Agricultural Engineering Institute to focus on the commercialisation of locally developed machinery so that farmers could benefit from affordable and efficient agricultural technologies. He also instructed livestock researchers to prioritise the development of vaccines against major animal diseases and promote research-based animal feed products.
Highlighting the country's agricultural export potential, the minister called for the adoption of modern beekeeping practices, improvement in honey quality and compliance with international standards. He also encouraged the promotion of high-value fruit crops, including avocado and blueberry, in areas with suitable climatic conditions.
Hussain emphasised that PARC scientists must strengthen collaboration with provincial governments, international research organisations and the private sector to ensure that scientific innovations reach farmers without unnecessary delays.
Earlier, Pakistan Agricultural Research Council Chairman Dr Syed Murtaza Hassan Andrabi briefed the minister on the council's research programmes and institutional initiatives, including the strengthening of the Agricultural Linkages Programme and revival of the Inter-Provincial Agricultural Research Coordination Committee to improve coordination among research institutions.
During presentations, the federal minister was informed that six crop varieties had been approved during Kharif 2026, while more than 265 tonnes of quality seeds had been produced. Scientists also highlighted progress in livestock breeding, development of a locally produced thermotolerant PPR vaccine, agricultural mechanisation, climate-smart farming and water conservation.
The meeting was further informed about advancements in horticulture, food processing and honeybee research, including the establishment of Pakistan's first hi-tech beeswax sheet production unit. The minister appreciated these initiatives and emphasised their wider adoption and commercial application.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Hackers have started exploiting serious security flaws in PHP, a programming language used by millions of websites worldwide.
The vulnerabilities, known as PHP2Shell, allow attackers to run malicious commands on vulnerable web servers without needing a password.
The two security flaws, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, recently received emergency patches. However, researchers have now confirmed successful attacks just days after the updates were released.
Hackers Successfully Exploit PHP Flaws
Security researcher Adel Karimi, who works at Perplexity, discovered the attacks using special test servers designed to detect hacking attempts.
These systems, known as honeypots, allow researchers to monitor how hackers try to break into websites.
Karimi found that attackers successfully ran commands on test servers using PHP 8.4.26 with Apache.
The attacks also exposed information stored in the servers’ memory, which helped the hackers carry out further commands.
According to the investigation, researchers recorded 35 successful command executions across three test servers on October 24.
The activity came from two IP addresses, although it remains unclear whether the same attackers were responsible.
Researchers Confirm the Security Threat
Karimi explained that the attacks went beyond simply crashing vulnerable servers.
The hackers were able to access approximately 800KB of memory data and use that information to execute commands remotely.
Cybersecurity researcher Marcus Hutchins from Expel also reviewed the findings and confirmed that they provided strong evidence of successful exploitation.
However, the attacks were recorded on servers with a particular configuration.
Researchers have not confirmed whether the same method would work equally well against other PHP versions or server setups.
The available evidence directly confirms an attack method linked to CVE-2026-109618, but does not separately establish successful exploitation of CVE-2026-109619.
Security Updates Available
PHP developers have already released emergency updates to address the vulnerabilities.
The security fixes are available in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
Website owners using affected older versions should update their servers to protect against possible attacks.
If successfully exploited, the flaws could allow hackers to access sensitive information, change website files, or run harmful software, depending on the permissions available on the server.
The confirmed attacks show that PHP2Shell is now a real security threat rather than just a potential weakness.
Although the documented successful attacks targeted test servers, they demonstrate why website administrators need to install the latest PHP security patches.

items.author: Arsalan Khattak
items.content:
The Senate Standing Committee on Science and Technology has passed the Pakistan General Cosmetics Bill, 2026, which aims to strengthen safety standards and improve regulation of the country’s cosmetics market.
Senator Kamil Ali Agha chaired the committee meeting at Parliament House on Monday, where members reviewed the bill’s provisions section by section before approving it.
The proposed legislation seeks to require transparent ingredient labeling, curb misleading marketing, and ensure that personal care products sold in Pakistan undergo scientific safety assessments.
The chairman also questioned officials about the number of cosmetics companies operating in the country and their registration with the Directorate General of Trade Organizations, the Federal Board of Revenue, the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, and sales tax authorities.
The committee emphasized that industry associations should be easy to establish across regions and that regulations should not create unnecessary barriers for emerging businesses. Members also examined the balance between raw materials imported for local manufacturing and finished cosmetic products imported directly.
The meeting was attended by the federal minister for defense production as a special invitee, the minister for science and technology, Senators Husna Bano and Dr. Afnan Ullah Khan, senior officials, and the Law Division’s legal team.

items.content:
The Daily Trust Foundation (DTF) has launched a journalism academy to strengthen ethical reporting, improve digital skills and equip journalists with the knowledge needed to tackle misinformation and hold public institutions accountable.
‎
‎The Chairman of the Foundation, Malam Bilya Bala, stated this on Tuesday at the launch of the DTF Journalism Academy, saying the initiative would address critical gaps in Nigeria’s media industry through structured and accessible professional training.
‎
‎Bala said the academy emerged from lessons the Foundation learned while implementing multi-year grants supported by the MacArthur Foundation, which exposed weaknesses in investigative reporting, specialised knowledge, newsroom collaboration and digital journalism.
‎
‎He also identified misinformation and declining public trust in journalism as challenges that require sustained professional development.
