items.author: APP
items.content:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) proposed 12 amendments to the 2023 codes of conduct for political parties, media organisations and election observers to curb the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) during elections.
According to sources in the ECP, the draft amendments proposed five changes to the code of conduct for media organisations, five for political parties and candidates, and three for election observers.
The commission has sought public and stakeholder feedback on the proposed amendments by Nov 20, with the measures aimed at regulating AI-generated content, prohibiting deceptive deepfakes and ensuring transparency in election-related communication.
Read: AI able to manipulate elections worldwide, expert says
Under the proposed rules for media, outlets would be required to clearly disclose when content generated or modified through AI is broadcast, published or released.
The draft strictly prohibits the use of deepfake technology to create fabricated images, voices or statements of political party leaders, candidates, election officials, members of the judiciary, armed forces personnel and other state officials if the content is false, defamatory or intended to ridicule them.
Media organisations would be permitted to use AI tools for preparing, translating, presenting or analysing election-related content, provided they disclose such use to their audiences and remain responsible for the authenticity and accuracy of the material.
The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA), the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority, and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency would monitor undisclosed or unlabeled AI-generated media content and report violations to the ECP, with appropriate action to be taken in cases of non-compliance.
The proposed amendments also require media houses to promptly remove misleading or undisclosed AI-generated content from their platforms, or correctly relabel it, when directed by a regulatory body or the ECP.
For election observers, three amendments have been proposed, requiring them to remain vigilant for AI-related manipulation during the observation process and immediately report any such instances to the ECP.
The draft also bars observers from using AI to generate, alter or enhance their observations, factual findings, photographs, videos or reports submitted to the commission.
Five amendments have been proposed for political parties and candidates to regulate their use of AI-generated material during election campaigns.
Under the proposed provisions, political parties and candidates would not be allowed to create, publish, broadcast or distribute AI-generated or manipulated content, including deepfake images, videos and audio clips, without clearly labelling it as AI-generated.
The draft prohibits the use of AI-generated material intended to deceive voters by falsely portraying a person’s image, words or actions.
It also bars the creation of fabricated, ridiculing or defamatory images, voices or statements of political leaders, candidates, election officials, members of the judiciary, armed forces personnel and other state officials through deepfake technology.
Political parties and candidates would be required to preserve all AI-generated content produced during the election process.
The proposed rules further prohibit the use of AI-powered bots, automated accounts and similar tools to manipulate online engagement or create fake trends.
The use of AI for voter outreach through robocalls or voice-cloned messages would also be regulated, with a clear disclosure at the beginning of each call or message that the content has been generated through AI.
The proposed amendments aim to strengthen transparency and accountability in election campaigning and media coverage while addressing the risks posed by fabricated digital content and AI-driven voter manipulation.

items.title: Putin says accusations of Russia provoking European protests are ‘clear overkill’
items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin called accusations that Russia was provoking mass protests in major European cities a “clear overkill.”
Speaking in an interview with the VGTRK broadcasting company published on Sunday, Putin said he was surprised that the initial reaction in Europe was not anti-Russian but anti-American.
“Claims immediately began to be thrown out that the events taking place in Europe are the result of the activities of the current American administration and its support for right-wing parties and movements,” he said.
Read: Kremlin dismisses allegations of Russia's involvement in Europe unrest
Putin said that was “strange and completely unexpected” to him, as he did not expect European leaders to attack “their main ally and protector, so to speak, in the military sense of the word, across the ocean.”
“But they quickly came to their senses and switched to their traditional accusations against the Russian Federation,” he said.
Blaming Russia for all mortal sins as is happening now, amidst the mass unrest in European countries, has become a standard practice for the West, Vladimir Putin told Vesti reporter Pavel Zarubin:https://t.co/zJnAK3SlsY pic.twitter.com/BkPionkaiz
— TASS (@tassagency_en) October 25, 2026
The president added: “There is nothing unexpected here. As is known, Russia has always been accused of all mortal sins. But now I am ready to respond.”
Putin said claims that Moscow was provoking mass demonstrations in major European cities are an obvious exaggeration even to ordinary citizens of European countries.
“My first reaction when I saw this was surprise, because to say that we are provoking mass protests in major European cities is a clear overkill, which, in my opinion, is obvious to ordinary citizens of European countries,” he noted.
“Nevertheless, they have now taken this well-trodden and worn-out path, and we see some accusations against Russia,” he added.
Putin said this points to “the weakness and inability of some leaders in European countries to take responsibility for what is happening.”
“This is bad. Why? Because it means they do not analyse the events, do not look for the causes of what is happening, but simply shift the blame onto someone, first the US, now Russia,” he said.
Nationwide student protests have been underway in France for several weeks.
Read More: France deploys 70,000 police to try to contain nationwide protests
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, speaking at an OECD-hosted conference on October 21, accused protesters of using “hostile narratives” from Russia, China, Iran and the MAGA community.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on October 19 that nobody takes such “absurd accusations” seriously. US President Donald Trump had blamed the unrest on mass migration.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, is facing early durability concerns after some buyers reported screen cracks along the hinge just hours after its public launch. Users have shared images online showing screen cracks and lines of dead pixels along the device’s folding area.
The reports have raised questions about the durability of Apple’s hinge mechanism and the long-term reliability of its first foldable phone. However, the number of reported cases remains unclear, and Apple has not issued an official statement about the problem.
iPhone Duo Owners Report Screen Cracks Along Hinge Shortly After Launch
According to complaints shared online, some iPhone Duo owners experienced screen damage after only a short period of use. One buyer in Australia claimed that the display broke after around six hours, despite opening the phone fewer than 20 times.
The user reportedly noticed an unusual movement beneath the screen while unfolding the device. A loud snapping sound followed, and the display developed a split along the crease. The owner said the phone showed no other visible signs of damage that would suggest a drop or physical misuse.
Similar images have also appeared online from users in China. However, it remains uncertain whether all the affected devices were purchased by customers or included store display units that may have experienced heavy handling.
The reported damage mainly appears around the central fold, with some images showing visible cracks while others display thick lines of dead pixels.
Apple Has Yet to Comment on the Reports
Early reviewers did not report similar screen failures during their initial testing. However, the limited number of review devices means these experiences may not reflect how the phone performs across a wider group of users.
Apple has not publicly addressed the complaints or confirmed whether the reported cases point to a manufacturing or design issue.
Some customers who took their damaged phones to Apple retail stores reportedly received replacement devices. The company may also examine returned units to identify the cause of the failures.
If further investigation reveals a widespread hardware defect, Apple could need to review its manufacturing process or make changes to the device’s design.
Screen Repairs Could Cost $999
The reported failures have also drawn attention to the potential cost of repairing the iPhone Duo’s foldable display. According to the report, replacing the internal screen outside the standard warranty could cost $999.
For buyers investing in Apple’s first foldable phone, such a high repair cost makes screen durability an important consideration.
The report states that early screen failures are covered by the standard iPhone warranty. Customers also have a 14-day return window if they decide the device does not meet their expectations, although applicable terms may vary by market.
Owners experiencing unusual sounds or visible changes around the hinge should contact Apple support or visit an authorised service provider rather than continuing to fold the device.
See Also: iPhone Duo Warranty in Pakistan: What Mercantile and GNext Offer
Early Durability Concerns Could Affect Apple’s Foldable Phone
Foldable smartphones place additional stress on their displays and hinges because users repeatedly open and close the devices. Manufacturers have faced durability challenges with these designs, particularly around the folding area.
The latest reports suggest that Apple could face similar challenges with its first foldable smartphone. However, it is too early to determine whether the reported failures are isolated incidents or signs of a broader problem.
How Apple investigates the damaged units and responds to affected customers could play an important role in building confidence in its foldable technology.
For now, prospective buyers may want to monitor further reports and wait for more information about the screen failures before making a purchase decision.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Indian protesters angry over a proposed Himalayan mega-dam, intended to counter an upstream Chinese hydropower project, have clashed with police and torched buildings, officials said.
The violence in northeastern Arunachal Pradesh state erupted late on Friday during protests against the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project of state-run hydropower company NHPC, Chief Minister Pema Khandu told reporters on Saturday.
“The mob destroyed a lot of properties, police station, the NHPC office was vandalised, several elected representatives’ homes were ransacked,” Khandu told reporters.
Around 40 police personnel were injured by stones thrown by protesters, who also vandalised the NHPC’s offices. Police fired tear gas canisters to disperse the crowd.
Read: UN experts urge Indian authorities to cease 'use of excessive force' to curb protests
Khandu urged opponents of the project to engage with the government. “Question us, have dialogue with us, instead of violence,” Khandu said.
India says the proposed dam is needed to counter China’s $167-billion Yaxia project, a likely record-breaking hydropower scheme upstream in Tibet.
New Delhi fears the Chinese project could affect water flows downstream, and says the proposed Indian dam would create a vast reservoir to store water and help maintain flows into the Brahmaputra river. Beijing has said its project will have no “negative impact” downstream.
China claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of southern Tibet. India says the state is an integral part of its territory.
India’s proposed dam, which would be by far its largest hydropower project, has drawn fierce opposition from local communities who fear the loss of their homes and land.
Read More: Injuries in China's Tibet rise to 76 after earthquake, death toll remains at 16
The project underscores tensions between the two most populous countries, which share a disputed Himalayan border patrolled by tens of thousands of troops.
India’s foreign ministry said on Friday the two sides remained in regular contact to manage border tensions, after a top Indian border police official Shatrujeet Kapur reported “face offs” between Indian and Chinese forces.
“The situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns,” foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters in New Delhi. “Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation.”

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
The trial in the knife attack on Bollywood actor Saif Ali Khan began in Mumbai, with the first witness telling the court that the intruder had demanded INR10 million during a break-in at the actor’s Bandra residence in January 2025.
The nurse, who cared for Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan’s younger son, Jeh, identified the accused, 31-year-old Mohammad Shariful Islam, during her testimony on Friday, according to Gulf News.
The nurse, who is the complainant in the case, has worked with the family for more than five years and was the first witness called to testify, the report said.
According to the The Indian Express, the nurse told the court a noise had woken her at around 2am on January 16, 2025. She initially noticed that the bathroom light was on and assumed Kareena was inside.
After waking again, she saw a man wearing a cap moving towards Jeh’s bed. The child was four years old at the time.
The nurse said she rushed towards the bed and attempted to pick up the child when the intruder attacked her with a hacksaw blade and told her to remain silent. When she asked what he wanted, the man allegedly demanded INR10 million.
The commotion alerted another nanny, who raised the alarm. Khan and Kapoor Khan then emerged from their rooms, and the actor confronted the intruder, asking who he was and what he wanted.
According to the witness, the man subsequently attacked Khan and another member of the household staff. Khan managed to overpower the intruder, while others took refuge in a room and locked themselves inside.
The accused had fled by the time additional staff members arrived, according to Gulf News. The nurse sustained cuts to two fingers during the incident.
Khan was taken to Mumbai’s Lilavati Hospital following the attack, where he underwent emergency surgery for multiple injuries. Doctors reported six wounds, including two deep injuries to his left hand and neck. A fragment of a knife was lodged near his spine, and surgeons removed a piece of the blade measuring approximately 2.5 inches.
The actor was discharged from hospital several days later.
Mumbai Police arrested the accused near Hiranandani Estate in Thane on January 19, 2025, three days after the incident. Police said he had used several aliases, including Vijay Das and Bijoy Das, according to Gulf News.
Described in the report as a Bangladeshi national, the accused remains in judicial custody. He faces charges under India’s Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including robbery with a deadly weapon, causing grievous hurt and house trespass. He has also been charged under the Foreigners Act and the Passport (Entry into India) Rules.
The trial followed two unsuccessful attempts by the accused to plead guilty. According to Gulf News, his lawyer, Vipul Dushing, submitted an application in late August stating that his client was willing to plead guilty and seeking leniency. The court rejected the request on September 11 and ordered the trial to proceed.
The accused again indicated on October 8 that he intended to plead guilty to all charges. Hindustan Times reported that the court rejected this second attempt as well, paving the way for witness testimony to begin.
Khan has previously spoken about the ordeal in an interview with journalist Barkha Dutt on Mojo Story, recalling that he feared he might die as he lay injured on the floor.
The actor also said he had considered forgiving the intruder, although he struggled to move past the possibility that the man had tried to kill him. 
As proceedings continue, the defence is expected to cross-examine the nurse. Other members of the household staff are also expected to testify, while Khan himself could be called as a witness.
The report did not specify a date for the next hearing.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
An Istanbul court ordered prosecutors to investigate Turkish nationals allegedly involved in the mistreatment of participants in the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla while they were held in Israel, during the first hearing of a case against 35 defendants, including Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The Istanbul 11th High Criminal Court ruled that individuals identified by complainants as Turkish citizens who participated in alleged abuses against them in Israeli custody should be identified and referred to prosecutors for necessary legal action.
The court also ordered that existing arrest warrants and Interpol Red Notice requests against all 35 defendants remain in effect.
The case concerns Israel's armed interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla, which was carrying humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip.
Flotilla participants describe alleged mistreatment
During the hearing, complainant Osman Cetinkaya said he had joined the flotilla as a doctor to deliver medical supplies to Palestinians in Gaza. He said Israeli soldiers confiscated five or six boxes of medical supplies from their vessel and that participants were subjected to mistreatment at Israel's Ashdod port.
Cetinkaya said he wished to pursue his complaint against the defendants.
Another complainant, Zeynep Tekocak, said she had been subjected to two strip searches and had an altercation with Israeli soldiers after refusing to remove her headscarf. "They recorded me wearing the clothes they gave me instead of my headscarf and mocked me," she told the court.
Read: Three years of genocide: Israel’s traditional Asian allies shift stance on Gaza
Tekocak said one of the soldiers who detained her had told her he was from Turkiye's central province of Yozgat. "They took our personal belongings, and I have not been able to recover any of them. Our privacy was seriously violated. I am filing a complaint," she said.
Turkish lawmaker Sema Silkin Un also testified, saying she and approximately 80 other participants were held in a poorly ventilated room after being detained. She said that an Israeli soldier insulted Islam while they were reading the Quran.
Un said detainees were not allowed to sleep and were subjected to verbal abuse and psychological mistreatment. "We were not even allowed to close our eyes where we were held. Sleeping was forbidden," she said.
She added that police officers who arrived the following day insulted Turkiye and the detainees in Hebrew.
Lawyers call for broader investigation into Gaza
Riza Saka, president of the Istanbul No 2 Bar Association, described the proceedings as historic and called for further international evidence to be included in the case. He referred to provisional measures ordered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in proceedings concerning allegations of genocide in Gaza.
Saka requested copies of relevant ICJ documents and a UN report concerning allegations of genocide in Gaza. He also referred to the arrest warrants and Red Notice requests issued against Netanyahu and the other defendants.
Lawyer Yasin Samli argued that the case involved allegations of genocide, crimes against humanity and attacks against civilians. Samli said lawyers had submitted eight volumes of evidence, including five concerning alleged crimes against women and children in Gaza.
Court seeks separate indictment over alleged crimes against Gaza civilians
In its interim ruling, the court noted that the existing indictment primarily described actions taken against the Global Sumud Flotilla, while allegations concerning crimes committed against civilians in Gaza were presented only indirectly and in general terms.
The panel said investigations into genocide and crimes against humanity could be conducted upon a request from Turkiye's justice minister.
Read More: Israel committed 'brutal violations' against aid flotilla activists: ICBSG
Taking into account the principle that courts are bound by the factual allegations set out in an indictment, the panel ordered a formal request to prosecutors concerning a possible new indictment.
The request calls for alleged crimes against civilians in Gaza, separate from the actions involving the flotilla, to be described in concrete terms and linked to supporting evidence.
The court said evidence submitted by the Istanbul No 2 Bar Association and the International Jurists Union should be considered in that process.
Court orders asset inquiries, requests ICC documents
The panel also ordered inquiries into whether any of the 35 defendants hold movable or immovable assets in Turkiye.
It directed that a request be sent through the Justice Ministry for documents from proceedings involving the defendants before the International Criminal Court (ICC). The court additionally ordered that a UN report submitted concerning allegations of genocide in Gaza be requested through the Justice Ministry.
The panel accepted applications to participate in the proceedings from complainants and several organisations, including the Istanbul No 2 Bar Association, MAZLUMDER, the International Jurists Union and the Association of Lawyers of the Earth.
The hearing was adjourned until March 30, 2027.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone is facing early durability concerns after owners reported cracks in the inner display near the hinge, in some cases within hours of purchase.
Photographs shared on Reddit and technology forums show cracks along the screen’s central fold, with some damaged displays developing bright lines of pixels. However, the cause remains unclear, and the reports do not establish how widespread the problem is.
One Australian customer said their iPhone Duo’s display cracked after approximately six hours of ownership and fewer than 20 openings.
According to MacRumors, the owner felt something beneath the screen near the hinge while opening the phone to show a friend, followed by an audible crack. The customer reported no visible external damage.
Apple initially offered an express replacement, but the owner instead visited an Apple Store and received a replacement device on the spot.
Similar images have circulated online, with Tom’s Guide and Digital Trends reporting complaints involving devices in several markets. However, social media posts alone cannot establish a failure rate or confirm that all reported cases share the same cause.
The complaints have also drawn attention to the phone’s hinge mechanism and dust resistance.
Tom’s Guide covered a durability test by YouTuber JerryRigEverything, which reportedly found dust entering the hinge area. During a subsequent bend test, a green line appeared on the inner display before it stopped responding.
The test involved deliberate physical stress and does not establish that the same damage occurs during normal use.
The location of the reported cracks has prompted speculation about possible pressure from internal hinge components, manufacturing tolerances or trapped debris. None of these explanations has been confirmed.
Users have also taken to X to share their concerns about the device’s durability.
In a post on Saturday, Sam Kohl warned against taking the iPhone Duo to the beach, highlighting concerns about the device’s potential vulnerability to environmental elements. The post can be viewed here.
Another user, fenibook, reported on Friday that two cases of inner-display failure had already emerged on the phone’s launch day, adding that further reports over the following days would help establish whether the problem was more widespread. The post is available here.
Apple had not publicly identified a cause for the reported failures in the coverage reviewed.
The complaints have emerged as the iPhone Duo attracts strong interest following its launch. A separate report highlighted strong demand during the phone’s initial sales period, while another noted limited store availability at launch.
Supply constraints could complicate replacement arrangements for affected buyers, although there is no evidence linking limited availability to the reported screen damage.
For now, the reported failures remain a developing story rather than proof of a widespread defect. More verified cases, technical inspections and an official response from Apple will be needed to determine whether the incidents point to a broader reliability problem.

items.title: Flipkart’s Summer Of Discontent
items.summary:
Questions over an IPO and ESOPs, huge investments in quick commerce and food delivery and the pressure to deliver profits: Flipkart is juggling one too many hot potatoes for the past year.
In that time, the ecommerce giant has seen 14 senior level exits, including three more VPs who are set to leave the company next.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Questions over an IPO and ESOPs, huge investments in quick commerce and food delivery and the pressure to deliver profits: Flipkart is juggling one too many hot potatoes for the past year.
In that time, the ecommerce giant has seen 14 senior level exits, including three more VPs who are set to leave the company next.
The latest executives to leave are Kanchan Mishra, VP of smartphones; Amit Sachan, VP of product and tech; and Kamal Chopra, VP of corporate, as Moneycontrol reported. While Mishra spent more than a decade at Flipkart, Sachan and Chopra have been with the company for four and five years, respectively.
As their tenure shows these are not employees who had just joined the company one or two years ago in the wake of all the IPO talk. These were executives who had seen much of the restructuring at Flipkart in the post-pandemic years.
Plus, these departures come at a time when the company’s employees have raised concerns over ESOP liquidity and the company’s long-awaited IPO remains without a firm timeline. It has coloured these exits with a darker tint as a result.
Walmart has reportedly asked the company to prioritise profitability before going public, while the expansion of its quick commerce business, Flipkart Minutes, requires significant ongoing investments. Employees holding stock options, meanwhile, are waiting for an opportunity to cash out.
Sources told Inc42 that some of these executives left as they were unable to see a clear opportunity to liquidate their ESOPs, while others moved to new jobs or wanted to start their own ventures. It must be noted that at this middle management level, Flipkart has around 30 executives in VP roles and more than a dozen senior vice presidents, so these departures will not necessarily destabilise the company, but it is a sign of bubbling discontent.
ESOP Liquidity Dispute Widens
In fact, sources told us that the frustration over stock options has moved beyond internal discussions, with former senior executives approaching Walmart’s board to seek a fair opportunity to realise the value of their vested ESOPs.
Earlier this month, former Flipkart executives, including ex-Myntra CEO Mukesh Bansal, former chief business officer Ankit Nagori and former CFO Sanjay Baweja, wrote to Walmart’s board seeking fair treatment and a full cash-out opportunity for their vested options simply because they left the company.
The issue has gained importance because an IPO has long been seen as a potential exit route for employees holding Flipkart shares or options. With the listing pushed back, those employees have little clarity on when they can realise that value.
For senior executives who have spent a year at Flipkart, the delay also affects decisions about whether to stay or pursue opportunities elsewhere. While ESOP liquidity is one reason behind some departures, the company’s leadership churn is also a result of executives moving into new roles or setting up their own ventures.
The founder of a unicorn startup with over 30,000 employees told us that while Flipkart has the responsibility of providing liquidity to employees, listing in a hurry to meet these demands would be a mistake.
“At the end of the day, Flipkart’s management and Walmart have to do the right thing by the company. If they have already done a $50 Mn ESOP buy back last year, then they already provided some liquidity opportunity. If an employee has already made ₹10 Cr – ₹15 Cr through that, then they need to give the company some more time for the next event. But if an employee who has made a few lakhs of rupees via the buyback is upset, then the management needs to address that. What’s the point of listing in a rush, without getting a good market value?” the founder said on the condition of anonymity.
Walmart Wants Profit Before IPO
The fact is that Flipkart’s listing plans have been discussed for years, but the immediate priority appears to be improving its financial performance.
In May 2026, Moneycontrol reported that parent Walmart wanted Flipkart to achieve EBITDA breakeven by the end of FY27 before considering an IPO or another external fundraise. The report said the decision followed Walmart CEO John Furner’s visit to Bengaluru.
The reported directive adds another hurdle for a company that completed its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026, ahead of a potential domestic listing.
There is the looming valuation question. Flipkart currently commands a valuation of $35 Bn – $36 Bn and earlier was eyeing a valuation of $50 Bn.
This valuation expectation complicates finding the right window for the listing. Walmart can afford to wait for improved financial performance which would justify the valuation, but that’s not the case with employees seeking liquidity.
Others believe that Flipkart cannot go into an IPO with the narrative of a growth-at-all-costs tech startup. The company is far too mature for this. “Flipkart will likely face pushback and could be forced into a valuation haircut to land in the $25B–$30 Bn range. This will match global tech-retail multiples,” Rahul Sharma, Head of Research at Equity99 said.
On the other hand, the company can position itself as a disciplined, maturing omnichannel ecosystem. “A concrete roadmap to profitability can successfully defend the $35 Bn mark that Flipkart is said to be seeking,” he added.
The delay is particularly striking because other Indian ecommerce companies have already reached the public markets. Meesho listed on the NSE and BSE on December 10, 2025, following a ₹5,421 Cr IPO. Snapdeal’s parent, AceVector, listed on October 5, 2026, after a ₹420 Cr public issue.
Their listing gives investors a way to set benchmarks for ecommerce, while Flipkart continues to work towards its own debut. However, the comparison also shows that going public does guarantee a strong market reception. AceVector shares listed at an issue price of ₹32 and subsequently traded below that level.
For Flipkart, the question is whether stronger financial performance can support its valuation expectations without forcing the company to slow its growth plans.
Flipkart Minutes Complicates Profitability Push
The push to improve profitability comes amid Flipkart’s aggressive investments in quick commerce.
Flipkart Minutes has expanded its dark store network to compete with Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto. The business gives Flipkart a way to serve customers looking for rapid delivery of groceries, electronics and other everyday products.
However, the expansion requires spending on dark stores, inventory, fulfillment and delivery operations. New stores need time to build order volumes and improve their economics. Until a store reaches sufficient throughput, its operating costs can weigh on the business. Flipkart Minutes has scaled to 1,000 micro fulfillment centers across 130+ cities and 8,000+ pincodes in under two years.
Flipkart Minutes’ business head Kunal Gupta earlier said that profit is a function of scale. “We have grown four times in the last one year. We want a healthy progressive journey. There is a clear line of sight of profit, otherwise we would not have opened so many stores.”
The current scale of Minutes’ spending is not publicly disclosed. However, its expansion presents a challenge for Flipkart as Walmart reportedly seeks EBITDA breakeven before an IPO.
Now, Flipkart is preparing to enter another competitive market with its food delivery service branded eat-in by Minutes. Currently available for its 8,000 employees, will soon be available to the public by the end of this month.
The food delivery business could add to Flipkart’s spending requirements. The company reportedly will use a dedicated delivery fleet through its logistics arm Ekart.
Moreover, it will also require onboard restaurants and attract customers in a market where established players spend on discounts, promotions and customer acquisition. These costs could build before the service reaches sufficient order volumes to support its operations.
The launch puts Flipkart in the position of investing in two businesses that require scale to improve their economics, even as Walmart reportedly wants the group to reach EBITDA breakeven before an IPO. While food delivery could bring more frequent customer visits to Flipkart’s app, it will also require spending to compete with established platforms.
Flipkart’s Silver Lining; Revenue Rises, Losses Narrow
Flipkart’s financial performance will also remain under scrutiny as it works towards a potential IPO.
The Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% YoY increase in consolidated revenue from operation to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in FY26, compared with ₹1.23 Lakh Cr in FY25. Its consolidated net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr from ₹8,646 Cr in the previous year. The financial results cover the wider Flipkart Group, including Myntra, Cleartrip, logistics, and other business, rather than the ecommerce marketplace alone.
The group said its gross margins rose 23% during FY26, while adjusted EBITDA improved by around ₹1,500 Cr. Adjusted operating margin improved by 230 basis points, from -7.7% to -5.4%, while adjusted operating business losses narrowed by 17%, or around ₹1,600 Cr.
However, the improvement in operating performance translated into only a modest reduction in net loss. Higher finance cost, the recognition of deferred tax assets and certain exceptional items weighed on the bottom line.
The ecommerce vertical, Flipkart Internet, reported a 19.3% YoY decline in revenue from operations to ₹16,295 Cr in FY26. Its net loss rose to ₹5,498 Cr from ₹1,694 Cr in FY25. A significant portion of that is likely due to the redomiciling to India which was completed in March 2026.
As Flipkart works on its public market plans, the combination of profitability targets, valuation expectations and employee concerns over stock liquidity is likely to remain in focus. For senior executives weighing their next move, the absence of a firm IPO timeline leaves questions unanswered: when will the equity they have accumulated at Flipkart become liquid wealth?
Edited By Nikhil Subramaniam
Creatives: Abhyam Gusai

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Julian Alvarez apologised to Atletico Madrid fans on Saturday for trying to leave the club during the summer, admitting he understands why supporters were angry with him.
The Argentina international was heavily linked with Barcelona this summer and said during the World Cup he thought it would be best if Atletico sold him.
The Rojiblancos refused to accept an offer from the Catalan giants and Alvarez was whistled and jeered by the club’s own fans at the start of the season.
However, the tension has gradually eased and Alvarez netted his first goals of the season this week, firstly against Stuttgart in the Champions League and then on Saturday helping the club beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0.
“I wanted to apologise to our people for my words during the World Cup,” Alvarez told Movistar.
“The truth is it was a mistake on my part, both in how I expressed myself and the timing. Above all because I understand people’s anger — I would have been angry too, as a fan.
“And also because of how they’ve stuck by me and supported me all these years and in these last few weeks. They’ve been very generous, and I really value that.”
Atletico signed the 26-year-old from Manchester City in 2024 and he has become a key figure for Diego Simeone’s side over the previous two seasons.
Alvarez put in his brightest display of the season against Deportivo and his goal split the teams at the Metropolitano stadium.
“I’m starting to feel good… I’m grateful to all my teammates because they’ve supported me,” continued Alvarez.
“They’ve really stuck by me throughout this whole time… and I’m working to improve.
“I’ve felt better in these last few matches… both physically and with the ball.”
AFP

items.title: One-Year Anniversary Tribute to Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, Chief of Army Staff of the Nigerian Army
items.summary:
Today marks one year since Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu assumed office as the 25th Chief of Army Staff on 30 October 2025. In this short but transformative period, he has steered the Nigerian Army with clarity of purpose, professional vigour, and a soldier-centred vision that is already yielding measurable institutional reforms and tangible security gains across the country.

items.content:
Today marks one year since Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu assumed office as the 25th Chief of Army Staff on 30 October 2025. In this short but transformative period, he has steered the Nigerian Army with clarity of purpose, professional vigour, and a soldier-centred vision that is already yielding measurable institutional reforms and tangible security gains across the country.
Strategic Reforms and Institutional Transformation
Upon assumption of command, Lt Gen Shaibu articulated a clear command philosophy built on five mutually reinforcing pillars known as PROSE:
Professional Excellence, Robust Administration, Operational Readiness, Strategic Cooperation, and Exemplary Leadership. At the heart of this philosophy sits an uncompromising Soldier-First culture that prioritises the welfare, training, dignity, morale, and empowerment of troops as the foundation of combat effectiveness.
This doctrine—now widely referred to as the *Shaibu Doctrine* and examined in the forthcoming book *The Shaibu Doctrine: Mission Command and the Remaking of Nigeria’s Army at War*—has driven a decisive shift from predominantly static defence postures toward more agile, mobile, and offensive operations. Mission Command principles have been emphasised, empowering subordinate commanders with clear intent while granting them the initiative to adapt to fluid battlefield conditions. The result is a more responsive, decentralised, and adaptive force.
Key structural reforms include the historic expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to twelve divisions, approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, alongside the recruitment of approximately 28,000 additional personnel. New formations and units have been established or operationalised to improve territorial coverage, reduce response times, and strengthen command-and-control, particularly in the North-West and other high-threat areas. Parallel investments in technology—drones, unmanned aerial systems, improved intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities, Army Aviation assets, and multi-domain integration—have begun to modernise the force for contemporary threats spanning land, air, cyber, and information domains.
Troop welfare has received sustained attention: better accommodation, medical support (including new helipad facilities for casualty evacuation), timely rotations, modern combat equipment, and logistics improvements have all featured prominently in his agenda.
Visible Security Gains
Under Lt Gen Shaibu’s leadership, the Army has sustained offensive pressure against Boko Haram, ISWAP, bandits, and other criminal networks. Kinetic and non-kinetic operations have neutralised high-value targets, dismantled camps, recovered significant quantities of arms and ammunition, and facilitated the rescue of thousands of civilians. Operations in the North-East (Operation Hadin Kai) and North-West (including Operation Fansan Yamma) have recorded notable successes in degrading terrorist and bandit capabilities, restoring relative stability in previously contested areas, and enabling the return of communities to productive life.
These operational outcomes rest on stronger inter-agency collaboration, improved intelligence sharing, and a renewed emphasis on professionalism, discipline, and adherence to the rule of law—elements repeatedly stressed by the Chief of Army Staff in his engagements with troops and senior commanders.
A Leadership Defined by Purpose
Drawing on extensive operational experience—including service as Theatre Commander of Operation Hadin Kai, General Officer Commanding 7 Division, and earlier command appointments in the North-East—Lt Gen Shaibu has brought both battlefield credibility and intellectual depth to the highest levels of Army leadership. His approach combines strategic foresight with genuine concern for the men and women who bear the brunt of Nigeria’s security challenges.
As the Nigerian Army marks this first anniversary of his command, the progress is evident: a larger, better-structured, more technologically aware, and soldier-focused force; a doctrinal pivot toward initiative and offensive action; and concrete gains against the threats that have long challenged national security.
The journey of transformation continues. Yet the foundation laid in this first year—professional excellence, robust administration, operational readiness, strategic cooperation, and exemplary leadership—offers a clear pathway toward a more resilient and combat-ready Nigerian Army capable of safeguarding the nation’s sovereignty and enabling lasting peace and development.
Congratulations, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, on a remarkable first year as Chief of Army Staff.
The nation acknowledges the dedication of the officers and soldiers of the Nigerian Army under your command. May the coming years consolidate these gains for the greater security and prosperity of Nigeria.

By Ozioruva Aliu, BENIN CITY
Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State has said he would not hesitate to sign the death of the four convicted Vegetable Market kidnappers if they did not appeal against the judgment within the stipulated time.
Read Also: Court orders speedy trial of 5 suspected kidnappers of NYSC members in Imo State
He said even if they appealed they were just postponing what would still come on them.
Speaking during a fellowship at God’s People Worldwide Prayer Ministry, while reviewing his administration’s efforts to curb kidnapping, cultism and other violent crimes in Edo State, said insecurity was one of the biggest worries he met on assuming office.
Okpebholo said that he raised the state of the roads and the security situation with President Bola Tinubu at their meeting who he said give him the approval to resolve the issues.
The governor said that when the gunmen struck at the Vegetable Market in Benin City, he called the President, who asked if he could handle it, and he said he could.
“I called the Commissioner of Police and told him I wanted these guys arrested, because I already have an approval from God, and they were caught within that time.
“They are already sentenced to death, and I pray they don’t appeal the judgment. Even when they appeal the judgment, they are only delaying time. If within the days stipulated, they don’t appeal, I will execute,” he said.
An Edo State Special Criminal Court on September 29 2026 sentenced four defendants to death for the abduction of a woman at the Vegetable Market along Airport Road, Benin City.
The governor said that before he began the campaign against kidnapping and cultism, he met prominent traditional rulers across the state to warn them against interceding for anyone involved in the crimes.
He recalled many strange incidents linked to spiritual forces after his administration pulled down a building associated with a cult group: “A black bird died in my office when I demolished their building. A vulture also died in my bed while contesting for governorship,” he said.
Founder of God’s People Worldwide Prayer Ministry, Apostle Ehijele Umuahia, during the event urged church members to vote for the governor and his preferred candidates in the 2027 elections.
Citing Proverbs 29:2, he told the congregation that prayer for the governor should go together with active participation in the electoral process. Christians, he said, should come out in large numbers to vote.
Umuahia described Governor Okpebholo as a humble man whose commitment to the things of God predates his time as governor. He said he has known him for over 15 years, from the days of the late Chief Tony Anenih.
“Whenever Chief Tony Anenih came to visit me, he was one of those who accompanied him. That was how we came to know each other,” he said.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The Archdiocese of New York said Saturday it had agreed to a settlement in which the church would pay more than $800 million to hundreds of victims of sexual abuse by clergy.
The agreement, to be formally signed in early November, marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the American Catholic Church has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s.
“We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks wrote in an email sent to his priests and forwarded to AFP by the archdiocese.
According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 victims will receive at least $250,000, and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered.
The Archdiocese of New York, which covers Manhattan, Staten Island, the Bronx and several counties north of the city, will now be able to “turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children,” Hicks’ email said.
Hicks was appointed bishop last year by Pope Leo XIV, replacing the influential conservative Cardinal Timothy Dolan. Before his departure, Dolan had announced the creation of a $300 million fund to compensate sexual abuse victims.
In the 2000s, press investigations revealed that Catholic priests in the United States had committed sexual abuse against thousands of children over several decades, and that church leaders had often covered up these cases or transferred the offending priests instead of reporting them to civil authorities.
Dioceses across the country have had to pay hundreds of millions of dollars in damages, and programs have been created to compensate victims without going to trial.
Last June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco announced it had reached an agreement to pay $395 million to about 530 victims of sexual abuse committed by its clergy in order to settle their lawsuits.
AFP

Gunmen swarmed a rural Nigerian village on motorcycles and killed at least 20 people, survivors told AFP on Saturday, in the latest attack in the country’s northeast.
Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally
The attackers opened fire just after Friday prayers in the rural village of Binnari, in Taraba state, residents said.
Northeastern Nigeria is home to a long-running jihadist insurgency, though Taraba, located toward the centre of the country, also faces non-ideological “bandit” gangs.
Bandits raid villages, kidnap people for ransom and levy “taxes” on farmers or miners in rural areas of Nigeria with little state presence.
“People were running in different directions to escape the attack. Nobody knew where it was safe to go,” said Binnari resident Isiyaku Musa.
He and Sa’idu Nuhu both gave a death toll of at least 20.
“After the attackers left, we counted more than 20 bodies, and some people were still missing,” Nuhu told AFP.
Police say 10
Police gave a lower toll, saying 10 bodies had been recovered as of Friday evening.
“The Nigerian authorities continue to leave rural communities in some parts of the north at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity,” Amnesty International Nigeria said.
“Consistent failure of the authorities to bring the suspected perpetrators to justice is clearly emboldening impunity,” the rights group said on social media.
Malam Abubakar Saifullahi, a community leader, said the attackers arrived on about 50 motorcycles, two men apiece, before raiding the village.
“They looted shops and took cash, foodstuffs and other provisions. They also took motorcycles abandoned by people fleeing the attack,” Saifullahi said.
Banditry has become a growing issue in northwest and central Nigeria, with powerful gangs – motivated by money rather than ideology – battling overstretched police and military across hard-to-reach, rural locations.
Separately on Saturday, the Nigerian military said it had killed 15 “terrorists” in northeastern Borno state in an air strike.
Nigeria has been fighting a jihadist insurgency since Boko Haram’s 2009 uprising.

items.content:
Julian Alvarez continued on his road to redemption by scoring the only goal as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 on Saturday to close the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona to two points.
Diego Simeone’s side are second, with champions Barca hosting Real Madrid, third, in the Clasico at Camp Nou on Sunday.
Alvarez netted for the second consecutive game, having grabbed his first of the season in Atletico’s 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart in midweek.
Atletico supporters hounded Alvarez during his first appearances this season after he tried to force his way out of the club in the summer, but the tension has gradually cooled.
Home fans at the Metropolitano stadium directed a few whistles at the team in general after a slow start, with Deportivo having the best chance of the first half.
Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved well from Lorenzo Amatucci, while at the other end Diego Simeone’s side lacked spark.
Early in the second half Alvarez found the breakthrough. Alejandro Grimaldo fired in a dangerous low pass towards the far post, where the Argentina international turned it over the line.
Alvarez came close to a second after a slick team move, with Alex Baena slipping him in, but Depor goalkeeper Leo Roman saved the striker’s attempted lob with his face.
The former Manchester City striker looked much closer to his best form in this outing after struggling with some fitness problems earlier in the campaign.
Alexander Sorloth lashed narrowly over from a tight angle as Atletico sought to kill off the game, unsuccessfully.
Deportivo might have levelled in stoppage time with Kevin Sanchez volleying well wide from Adama Traore’s cross when well placed to trouble Oblak.
The Galicians’ best chance came with virtually the last kick of the game, with Oblak saving from Sanchez on his line, when the forward seemed destined to score.
Earlier, Georges Mikautadze snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in a derby clash against Valencia, who had midfielder Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men.
The Yellow Submarine came from behind to triumph, climbing into mid-table and leaving Javier Aguirre’s Los Che 19th, in the relegation zone.
Pepelu sent Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level at Mestalla stadium after 69 minutes.
Inigo Perez’s Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit Jose Gaya in the face with his elbow.
However, English midfielder Elliott, on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent.
Villarreal striker Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points.
AFP

items.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Former US president Barack Obama delivered a scathing critique of his successor, Donald Trump, at a rally Saturday in Ohio to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
“After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,'” Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.”
The 65-year-old Democrat blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices.
“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said. “Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.”
Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in this northern industrial state.
“Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said.
The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his party’s candidates in the upcoming crucial elections that will decide control of Congress.
In Ohio, former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024.
Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close.
Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate.
After Cleveland, Obama will head north to Michigan this evening for a rally in Detroit alongside Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate candidate.
While both of Michigan’s Senate seats are currently held by Democrats, El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers.
AFP

He or his staff could also face numerous congressional investigations by Democrats, who have said they want to examine business dealings conducted by the president and those close to him through the family’s holding company since his return to the White House.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Clashes broke out Saturday in Paris and other French cities amid demonstrations held a week after others that degenerated into street violence and prompted a robust security backlash as President Emmanuel Macron seeks to restore order.
Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers were confronted with “an extremely elevated level of violence” from black-clad “ultra-left” extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.
Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.
Two people were “seriously” injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case.
Authorities had deployed 70,000 security forces across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living.
The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over a country that goes to the polls in six months to choose a successor to Macron after 10 years.
Nunez said Saturday’s outcome was more “positive” than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses.
There was nevertheless widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest.
– Police battle ‘rioters’ –
Saturday’s demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union.
The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources.
Macron’s government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones. The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as “illegitimate”.
In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully.
The march had been pushed to the capital’s southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities.
Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing. Nunez said the confrontations lasted two hours and involved “500 rioters” at the back of the march.
AFP journalists saw police charge several times and vigorously use tear gas and batons against some, mostly young, protesters.
“The police started moving towards everyone, telling them to get down and back off. They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters,” one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP.
– Ultra-right vs ultra-left –
In the western city of Nantes, thousands of protesters broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water cannon to reach the city centre, an AFP journalist there witnessed.
Emma, 23, marching in the northwest city of Rennes, said she was angry at “everything happening at the moment”, denouncing the bans on demonstrations and the “repression” of the high schools student protests.
Marching in the rain at the head of the protest in the northern city of Lille, 47-year-old Delphine insisted: “Neither the president, nor the weather will stop me from demonstrating.”
In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse around 1,000 people gathered in the south of the city.
“If they prohibit protests then that means we are heading more and more towards a regime that is fascist, that is dictatorial,” said one 20-year-old protester in Lyon, who gave only his first name, Silem.
In the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, far-right activists came out onto the streets seeking confrontations with “ultra-left militants”, in what authorities said was an unprecedented development.
There was looting on the sidelines of the marches in Marseille and Grenoble, said police.
Meanwhile, the Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, called for more demonstrations on October 31 for “the freedom to protest”.
Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who marched in the Paris rally, said Macron “is going to understand that this is going to repeat itself every week”.
– Protest against Le Pen’s party –
Tensions were heightened by a rally in the city of Orleans by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally party to kick off her campaign for the presidential election.
Thousands of counter-protesters chanting anti-fascist slogans marched in the city. Police put their number at 13,000 while organisers said twice as many participated.
The unrest across France highlighted the febrile political atmosphere ahead of the vote, in which Le Pen leads in surveys.
Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February.
Protests have also been taking place in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems. Italy has mobilised 500 troops to Milan after street violence there.

items.title: Ronaldinho returns to football with Italian third tier
items.summary:
Brazil legend Ronaldinho will make his playing return aged 46 next month for Ravenna, the third-division Italian club announced on Saturday.
The 2002 World Cup winner’s move to Ravenna was announced in June.
He is aiming to score his 300th career goal.
The former Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker retired in 2015, 10 years on from claiming the Ballon d’Or and has become a shareholder in Ravenna, situated between Venice and San Marino.
“The wait now has a date: Sunday, November 15,” Ravenna said in a statement.
“The Brazilian legend will wear the Ravenna FC shirt in the derby against Forli.
“An event that will turn the eyes of the world toward the Bruno Benelli Stadium.”
Ravenna are second in Group B of the Italian third tier, six points below leaders Spezia and are aiming for a return to Serie B for the first time since 2008.

items.content:
Southampton ended West Ham’s nine-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 win at the London Stadium to surge into the Championship top six despite starting the season with a four-point deduction.
Saints began the campaign with the points penalty after spying on opposition training sessions, which also cost them the chance of promotion in the play-off final last season.
Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin all struck before half-time for the visitors, who are now within three points of the automatic promotion places.
Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers, but there were swathes of empty seats and boos by full-time as they missed the chance to go top.
“This is a tough place to come, against a quality team, and we knew we needed to start strongly, so we worked on that all week,” said Saints boss Tonda Eckert after his side went 2-0 up inside the opening 10 minutes.
“They made it tough for us in the second half, so it was important that we stayed brave to bring the result over the line.”
Burnley sacked manager Nicky Hayen after just 14 games in charge following his side’s 4-1 defeat at Lincoln, which left the Clarets in the relegation zone.
Relegated from the Premier League last season, former Club Brugge boss Hayen won just one of his 12 league matches in charge.
“Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect,” the club said in just a two-sentence statement.
“The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.”
Swansea’s missed the chance to retake top spot after they were thrashed 5-0 by QPR at Loftus Road.
Richard Kone scored a hat-trick inside the first 15 minutes before Jimmy Dunne’s double rounded off a remarkable scoreline that nudges Rangers into the play-off places.
Adam Armstrong scored the only goal as fourth-placed Wolves beat struggling Watford 1-0 to move within two points of the automatic promotion places.
AFP

items.title: Woman killed, two injured on Plateau farm
items.summary:
By Golok Nanmwa, Jos
A woman has been killed, while two others sustained injuries while harvesting groundnuts on a farm at Gwom-Ajang, Foron District, in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State.
The incident occurred at about 4pm on Saturday, according to a member of the community, Silas Bitrus, who confirmed the incident to our correspondent.
Bitrus said, “The incident occurred around 4pm while they were harvesting groundnuts on the farm.”
He added, “A woman was killed, while two others sustained injuries.”
Also confirming the incident, the National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, condemned the attacks and urged security operatives to go after the attackers.
Also in a related development, the Coalition of Plateau State Indigenous Youth Bodies has alleged a plot by some groups to launch a counter-propaganda campaign against the Department of State Services, DSS, and other security agencies operating in the state.

Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for just the second time in 36 years and the first since 2018.

“It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players also. They deserved this win, they prepared very well,” De Zerbi said.

Tottenham started the season on a dismal run
items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Roberto De Zerbi said Tottenham’s historic 2-0 victory against London rivals Chelsea proved his side have a winning mentality as they banished their dismal start to the season.
Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for just the second time in 36 years and the first since 2018.
Trips across the capital to west London have largely been fruitless experiences for Tottenham over the last four decades.
But De Zerbi’s men enjoyed a memorable visit to the Bridge on Saturday thanks to a comical own goal from Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders and a late wonder-goal from Mathys Tel after Blues star Cole Palmer was sent off.
“It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players also. They deserved this win, they prepared very well,” De Zerbi said.
“We are improving a lot, we are improving in the mentality, in the group and the relationships with the players and then we are improving on the pitch.”
Tottenham started the season on a dismal run of six league games without a win, raising the spectre of another relegation battle after they narrowly avoided dropping into the Championship on the final day of last season.
With the pressure mounting on De Zerbi, the Italian has drawn his players closer together thanks to meals together and a trip to Marbella.
– ‘The spirit, the belief’ –
A win against promoted Coventry on Monday lifted the tension around the north London club and vanquishing Chelsea was another reward for De Zerbi’s team-building ethos.
“Now it is a complete team. When we stay for dinner and stay together in the dressing room I see a different group, a different relationship and different atmosphere among the players,” he said.
“The character was today great but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here last season, two or three seasons ago, they suffered the last results, two times 17th position, we are working to change the last part of the history of the club.”
Tottenham were beginning to lose the faith of their long-suffering fans after another miserable start to the season.
But De Zerbi was adamant he never doubted they would get back on track.
“I have to believe for sure in this group. I never lost the confidence in my players,” he said.
“The week in Marbella, to speak better face to face, to open ourselves and remove the mask it is important.
“It is important for the spirit, the belief. The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more important than the tactics.”
For Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso, it was a painful setback as the optimism engendered by successive victories over Bournemouth and Everton was washed away on a rain-lashed evening.
Alonso’s expensively assembled team sit in fourth place but remain very much a work in progress after the third league loss of his first season in charge.
“We are all disappointed with the result, with the performance collectively and individually we were not at our best level,” he said.
“It was about the first goal and it went their way and with 10 men it was difficult but we can do better.”
Alonso refused to blame Penders and Palmer for their roles in the defeat.
“We feel for everyone, it is a team thing, a collective. We have to move on,” he said before adding he “hadn’t seen” Palmer’s two bookings.

ABUJA: Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the power brokers of Northern Nigeria, traditional rulers and Islamic clerics are solidly behind his return to office in 2027.
He spoke at the flag-off of the party’s presidential campaign in Kaduna, in the presence of the President and all the governors of Northern Nigeria.
“We have been engaging all and sundry, our traditional rulers, our ulama and our imams, to understand the importance of your return in 2027 for continuity, for the peace of this country and for Nigeria,” Yari said.
He told the President that the northern establishment had turned out in full.
“We believe in you, and those people believe in us. All the shakers and movers of this part of the country are here. In the northern part of the country, anybody who is not here today, Mr President, then there is nobody there. We are here.
“By God’s grace, Your Excellency, Mr President, we resolve, by God’s grace, that as far as Northern Nigeria is concerned, Mr President, I need your ears. Mr President, I want you to listen to us carefully. Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent for you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, by God’s grace, Insha Allah. And the promise we have made, you are going to see it on January 16, 2027,” Yari said.
Yari described Kaduna as “the spiritual centre of politics in Northern Nigeria”, adding that the venue had drawn “all the governors of Northern Nigeria”.
On the economy, he said the President’s reforms had changed the country’s fortunes. “If we talk about the economy, we know the state of the economy when you stepped into the leadership of this country. Today, the total indices have changed completely to the advantage of Nigeria and other countries of the world.
“Mr President, I can enumerate at least a few: from the exchange rate, to the subsidy removal and many more,” Yari added.
The APC-PCC boss said the party would take its case to voters on the strength of the administration’s achievements.
“We Nigerians, at the head of this campaign, are going to campaign with our records. Our records are there. The infrastructure is there. What you did in health, education and human capital development is there. The students are there. The transparent cash and conditional cash transfers are also there for men and women,” he said.
Turning to the 2023 election, Yari said: “I would like to be a student again, to be told how you did it, because we want the country.”
He said the party was committed to justice and urged the President to listen closely to the North’s message.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja
Nigeria and South Korea have called for stronger bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, technology transfer, agriculture and skills development to promote economic growth and create opportunities for their citizens.
The two countries renewed the call at a reception to mark South Korea’s National Day in Abuja on Friday, with both sides expressing commitment to expanding their longstanding diplomatic relations.
Speaking at the event, South Korea’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yoan, said the two countries, which established diplomatic relations in 1980, had opportunities to deepen economic cooperation through partnerships that support local businesses, entrepreneurship and human capital development.
Jeong said South Korea was willing to share its development experience with Nigeria while respecting the country’s priorities and working with it as an equal partner.
He recalled that South Korea’s economy was devastated by the Korean War, with its annual per capita income below $100 in 1953, but said investment in education, hard work and international cooperation had helped the country rebuild.
The ambassador said the experience demonstrated the importance of investing in people, developing local industries and sustaining partnerships that deliver long-term benefits.
Highlighting ongoing cooperation, he said the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), in partnership with Nigeria’s Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency (SMEDAN) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), broke ground on an entrepreneurship centre in Abuja in September.
According to him, the centre is expected to support young entrepreneurs and start-ups by helping them develop business ideas and build sustainable enterprises.
He also said South Korea’s Smart School project, implemented in collaboration with the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC), had reached about 8,000 children and provided training for more than 300 teachers and school leaders.
Jeong added that KOICA and the Food and Agriculture Organisation were collaborating on an initiative to create green jobs for young Nigerians through agriculture.
He said about 2,000 Nigerian officials had also received training in South Korea through KOICA programmes, describing capacity development as a key component of the bilateral relationship.
On private sector cooperation, the ambassador identified opportunities for Korean companies to expand their engagement with Nigerian businesses in energy, manufacturing, clean water and digital technology.
He listed Daewoo E&C, LG, Samsung, Hyundai and Solpia among Korean companies working with Nigerian partners, adding that the South Korean Embassy and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) would continue to promote investment, technology sharing and local employment.
Beyond economic and technical cooperation, Jeong highlighted the growing cultural relationship between the two countries, noting that Korean pop music, television dramas, films and beauty products had gained popularity among Nigerians.
He said South Koreans had also shown interest in Nigeria’s Afrobeats music and Nollywood films, describing cultural exchanges as an important way of bringing the people of both countries closer.
The ambassador said the theme of the celebration, “One Heaven. One Earth. One Humanity,” reflected the importance of peace, human dignity, mutual respect and international cooperation.
He explained that South Korea’s National Foundation Day, known as Gaecheonjeol, is celebrated on October 3 and commemorates the country’s traditional founding story associated with Dangun and the principle of Hongik Ingan, commonly interpreted as “to benefit all humanity.”
In her remarks, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, represented by the Chief of Protocol of the Ministry, Ambassador Babagana Wakil, commended South Korea’s achievements in technology, engineering, manufacturing and social development.
She called for stronger cooperation in agriculture, industrial manufacturing, automobile assembly, shipbuilding and technology transfer, noting that closer collaboration could support Nigeria’s development priorities.
The minister also identified education, digital technology, scholarships, technical training, academic exchanges and research as areas for expanded partnership between the two countries.
She stressed the need to strengthen maritime cooperation in areas including maritime safety, transportation, fisheries and technical capacity development.
Odumegwu-Ojukwu further called for renewed engagement under the Nigeria-South Korea Joint Commission framework to identify practical measures for increasing bilateral trade and investment.
She said closer cooperation would enable both countries to address shared development challenges while creating more opportunities for their businesses and citizens.
The reception featured a Taekwondo performance and Korean cuisine, showcasing aspects of South Korea’s cultural heritage.
The event underscored the commitment of both countries to building on more than four decades of diplomatic relations through stronger economic partnerships, capacity development and cultural exchanges.
