items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Luminous Jannamike
Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain what his administration has done to end hunger and poverty, following the President’s claim that the opposition created the problems.
Atiku said Nigerians were more concerned about the government’s record than its attempts to shift responsibility, insisting that the 2027 presidential election would put Tinubu’s handling of the economy and security under scrutiny.
In a statement on Saturday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku accused the President of blaming his political opponents for hardship that had worsened under his watch.
“Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record,” Atiku said.
On the economy, the ADC candidate challenged Tinubu to account for the consequences of petrol subsidy removal, the naira’s depreciation and rising poverty.
“Which administration removed the petrol subsidy and watched the naira fall from about ₦471 to ₦1,329 to the dollar?” he asked.
Atiku also questioned the government’s handling of public finances and the country’s poverty levels.
“Which administration has presided over a rise in poverty that led the World Bank to estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians will be below the national poverty line in 2026? Which administration extended the 2024 budget into 2025 while also operating a separate 2025 budget?” he asked.
He further demanded explanations for what he described as questionable public spending, citing energy security expenditure, NNPC pipeline-related spending and charges associated with an Abu Dhabi financing facility.
“Which administration recorded ₦7.13 trillion under ‘energy security’ in 2024 and faces questions over ₦11.2 trillion in NNPC pipeline related spending? Nigerians deserve to know who received these sums and what was delivered,” Atiku said.
He also questioned the country’s external accounts and the charges associated with the financing facility.
“Which administration must explain the $12.4 billion gap flagged in Nigeria’s external accounts for the first half of 2026? Which administration paid $22.5 million in ‘other charges’ on the Abu Dhabi financing facility?” he asked.
On security, Atiku faulted the administration over persistent killings, kidnappings and displacement, demanding answers from the government.
“Which administration is responsible for the killings, kidnappings and displacement that continue to terrorise communities? These are the questions Nigerians are asking while your government blames the opposition,” he said.
Atiku also criticised Tinubu’s commissioning of the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium, arguing that the ceremony did not establish that the project had been completed.
“Your decision to commission the unfinished Abuja to Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium shows how far removed you are from the daily reality of Nigerians. A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon-cutting ceremony,” he said.
Returning to the central issue, Atiku said the government could not avoid accountability by blaming political opponents for describing the hardship Nigerians were experiencing.
“You cannot govern for three years, make life harder, and then blame others for describing the hardship. You asked who created the hunger. Nigerians are asking what you have done to end it,” he said.
He said the 2027 presidential election would test Tinubu’s record against the experiences of Nigerians.
“The people will judge your government by the lives they are living, not by the excuses you offer at campaign rallies.
“The 2027 presidential election will be a referendum on your record. Nigerians have felt the cost of your leadership in their homes, markets and communities. Their verdict is already clear: they have rejected your administration,” he added.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Bestway Group officially introduced Chinese automotive giant Geely Auto to Pakistan at a launch ceremony at Park View City, Islamabad, attended by the Group founder Sir M. Anwar Pervez, the Group Chairman Lord Zameer Choudrey and the senior executives from both organisations, industry leaders, distinguished guests and members of the media. The launch marks Bestway Group’s expansion into the automotive sector, bringing Geely’s engineering expertise, technological innovation and vehicle range to the Pakistani market.
Bestway Automotive, Geely’s sole authorised distributor in Pakistan, will oversee Geely’sintroduction and development, including vehicle sales and after-sales support. The partnership also paves the way for local assembly, with Bestway preparing its facility in Karachi for the next phase of Geely’s operations in Pakistan.
At the heart of the launch is Geely Auto’s global brand philosophy, “See the World in Full”, which reflects the belief that mobility is about more than getting from one place to another. It is about creating better experiences and enabling people to explore new horizons, possibilities and perspectives. This vision shapes Geely’s approach to inclusive mobility, bringing together engineering, technology and design to help people experience more of the world around them.
Irfan Sheikh, Group Managing Director, for Non-Banking Businesses at Bestway Group, Pakistan, said, “Tonight is a proud moment for everyone at Bestway. This partnership brings together two organisations with complementary strengths, with Bestway drawing on decades of experience in investing in and building businesses in Pakistan, and Geely bringing its global expertise in the automotive industry. We are delighted to introduce three Geely models to the Pakistani market – the EX2, EX5 and Starray EM-R. Their unveiling marks an exciting first step in this journey. Our aim is to have locally assembled Geely vehicles on Pakistan’s roads within the next few months. We see tremendous potential in this partnership and are committed to establishing Geely as a recognised and trusted name in Pakistan.”
The three models cater to different mobility needs. The Geely EX2 is a compact, fully electric hatchback designed for urban driving, while the EX5 is a fully electric SUV. The Starray EM-R features range-extended electric vehicle (REEV) powertrain technology, combining electric driving with the flexibility of an onboard petrol engine.
Haider Choudrey, Group Chief Executive Officer, Bestway Group, said, “Geely’s arrival marks an important milestone in Bestway’s longstanding commitment to Pakistan. Through its investments in sectors such as cement manufacturing and banking, Bestway has invested more than $350 million in Pakistan, creating over 20,000 jobs and supporting livelihoods in the last three years alone. With Bestway Automotive, we are extending this commitment to the automotive sector. Our partnership with Geely will open up opportunities for local manufacturing, employment generation, skills development and a stronger automotive supply chain, while offering Pakistani consumers greater choice and access to global automotive technology.”
Evin Ye, Vice President of GAIC and Managing Director of Geely Auto ASEAN said, “Pakistan is our first market in South Asia, and we see significant potential here. We are delighted to begin this journey with Bestway, a partner that understands the market and shares our commitment to customers. This is much more than a business arrangement; it is a long-term commitment to grow together, strengthen customer support and bring safe, intelligent and high-quality mobility to Pakistani families.”
Through this partnership, Bestway and Geely aim to build lasting customer relationships and contribute to the development of Pakistan’s automotive industry.

Wang conveyed Xi's "cordial

The trip fell near the date both countries use to mark the entry of Chinese troops into the Korean War. Kim attended a memorial ceremony to fallen soldiers and visited an automobile factory, Xinhua said.

items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
Former Speaker of the Benue State House of Assembly and Nigeria’s former Ambassador to Namibia, Terhemen Tarzoor, has faulted former Governor Samuel Ortom over his reported remarks against Governor Hyacinth Alia and his administration urging political leaders to exercise restraint in their public engagements.
Tarzoor, who spoke with newsmen in Makurdi, described some of Chief Ortom’s comments during a recent television programme as inappropriate, arguing that political differences should not undermine the dignity of the office of the governor or the people of the state.
The former lawmaker, who is also the Benue State coordinator of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors for President Bola Tinubu 2027, said Ortom whom he described as an elder brother he respects, should be more measured in his public statements about the incumbent governor.
“My take is that the former governor should not call the number one citizen 419. He has no right to call him that,” Tarzoor said, reacting to Ortom’s alleged description of Alia as a “419” and a “fake Reverend Father.”
He also faulted Ortom’s reported comparison of the administration of Benue State to a Catholic parish, where priests allegedly collect offerings and spend the money without being questioned, Tarzoor, a Knight of St. John International, defended the Church’s financial management system, insisting that it operates established structures for accountability.
“As a Knight of St. John International, I want to disabuse his mind and the minds of people who listened to that programme that there is a high level of accountability in the Catholic Church,” he said.
“There is no Catholic priest that can just earn money and spend at ease in the Catholic Church,” he said, adding that political leaders should avoid statements that could be interpreted as questioning the integrity of religious institutions without sufficient knowledge of their operations.
Tarzoor also criticised what he described as an unfair comparison between Ortom’s eight-year administration and Alia’s government, which has been in office for just over three years. He argued that any meaningful assessment of their performances must take into account the period each administration has spent in office and the targets set for them.
“In comparative statistics, you talk about time-frame equality and goal equality before you can compare and contrast,” he said.
The former Speaker further expressed concern over Ortom’s reported reference to some Benue people as “shenanigans,” describing the expression as inappropriate.
“I see that as repugnant. If he has issues, he should apply the right language, apply decorum in the manner to address matters. That is the only legacy we can leave for our children, those yet unborn,” he said.
On the issue of former governors’ entitlements, Tarzoor said he was unaware of any law providing for the benefits Ortom reportedly claimed were denied him, including a house in Abuja or elsewhere in the country and sponsorship of medical check-ups.
“When I was Speaker, we never had such a law anywhere,” he said, while acknowledging that he could not speak definitively on whether such legislation had been enacted after he left office. “Any legitimate concerns over entitlements could be addressed through appropriate channels rather than public exchanges,” he said.
The former Ambassador maintained that the Alia administration was open to scrutiny, urging the media and members of the public to seek accurate information on government revenue and expenditure through established procedures, including the Freedom of Information framework.
“Governor Hyacinth Alia is open to all criticisms. The law is clear on freedom of information. You test it; the records will be there for you to see,” he said, urging political leaders to promote constructive engagement and accountability.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
New-age tech stocks lost over $11 Bn in combined market capitalisation this week, with Swiggy leading a broad sell-off amid weakness in the wider Indian equity market.
Of the 67 stocks under Inc42’s coverage before this week’s listings, 63 declined between 1.03% and 24.5%. Only Yudiz, Capillary, ixigo, and Tracxn ended the week higher.
Swiggy was the biggest loser, falling 24.5% to close at ₹176.70 after its Q2 FY27 results highlighted mounting losses at quick commerce arm Instamart. The stock touched an all-time low during intraday trade yesterday.
Twelve other stocks, including Yatra, Turtlemint, FirstCry, Unicommerce, and IndiaMART InterMESH, hit fresh 52-week lows during the holiday-shortened week.
The selling extended to Eternal, Ola Electric, Paytm, and Lenskart, dragging the combined market capitalisation of the 67 companies to $149.2 Bn.
Meanwhile, B2B manufacturing company Zetwerk and defence tech company Tonbo Imaging made their public market debuts at a premium yesterday. Both came under pressure after listing, closing 13.02% and 2.44% below their respective BSE listing prices.
The two additions took the combined market capitalisation of the 69 new-age tech stocks tracked by Inc42 to $152.32 Bn, equivalent to about 3.2% of the total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies.
Here are some of the key developments at listed new-age tech companies during the week.
Eternal Reports Profit Jump
Eternal reported a nearly 92% YoY jump in Q2 FY27 net profit and unveiled Dark, an end-to-end encrypted AI platform for advanced AI users. Founder Deepinder Goyal said a global launch is planned before the end of 2026.
Eternal also announced a proposed merger between portfolio company AdOnMo and gated-community management platform Mygate. It expects to hold a 4.4% stake in the merged entity.
Ecommerce Platforms Face Action
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) took action against seven ecommerce platforms, including IndiaMART and Justdial, over listings and sales of unauthorised hazardous explosives.
The action led to the removal of 3,940 sellers and product listings across the platforms.
ideaForge Terminates US Agreement
Drone maker ideaForge’s wholly owned US subsidiary terminated its joint venture agreement with US-based First Breach Inc, citing the failure to complete the transaction within the agreed deadline and discussions between the parties.
Signed on September 23, 2025, the agreement envisaged a joint venture to license, source, design, engineer, manufacture, and distribute unmanned aerial vehicles in the US.
Unicommerce Logs Profit Growth
Ecommerce SaaS company Unicommerce’s consolidated net profit rose 11% YoY to ₹6.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue grew 15% to ₹59.1 Cr. Expenses increased 19%, outpacing revenue growth, with a lower tax expense supporting profit growth. The company expects profitability to improve in H2 as incremental investments moderate.
With that, here’s a look at the broader market trend this week.
Markets End Winning Streak
The Sensex declined 2.15% to 73,123.83, while the Nifty 50 fell 2.63% to 22,600 during the week.
Both indices declined across all four trading sessions, with markets closed on Tuesday for Dussehra. Rising crude prices, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, and sustained FII outflows weighed on sentiment.
Broader markets saw steeper falls. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 declined 5.6% and 7.3%, respectively, while the Nifty Bank lost 2.8%.
Brent crude approaching $115 per barrel heightened concerns over inflation, rupee depreciation, and corporate margins. Investors also scrutinised Q2 earnings, valuations, and management guidance. IT stocks remained relatively resilient, while metals, realty, and consumer durables faced selling pressure.
Foreign investors sold equities worth ₹2,697 Cr, their tenth consecutive week of net selling, although outflows moderated from ₹8,991 Cr. Domestic institutional investors bought ₹10,942 Cr.
“Going ahead, the steady moderation in FII selling offers some comfort, though elevated crude and sharp broader-market weakness keep the downside risk alive,” said Vinod Nair, head of research at Geojit Investments.
Next week, investors will track Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan rate decisions, US GDP, India’s industrial production, and corporate earnings. West Asia developments, crude prices, US treasury yields, and India-US trade negotiations will also remain in focus.
Now, let’s take a look at the performance of Swiggy and ixigo.
ixigo Defies Market Sell-Off
ixigo rose 1.45% during the week following its Q2 results on October 17.
The online travel aggregator swung to a consolidated net profit of ₹63.4 Cr from a ₹3.5 Cr loss a year earlier. This included a ₹40.7 Cr exceptional gain from the partial sale of its Freshbus stake and remeasurement of its remaining investment.
Operating revenue grew 12.9% YoY to ₹321 Cr, while gross transaction value (GTV) rose 22% to ₹5,304.5 Cr. However, adjusted EBITDA fell 17.2% to ₹23.6 Cr, with the margin narrowing to 7.3% from 10%.
Hotel GTV surged 158.7% to ₹111.3 Cr, while revenue increased to ₹8.1 Cr from ₹1.3 Cr. Room nights exceeded 4.7 Lakh, and inventory topped 70,000 properties. However, the segment’s contribution loss widened to ₹1.2 Cr from ₹71 Lakh.
Train revenue increased 16.4% to ₹149.1 Cr, while bus revenue rose 23.8% to ₹81 Cr. Flight revenue fell 7.5% to ₹82.7 Cr despite 37.2% GTV growth, with the gross take rate declining to 7% from 9.38%.
Choice Equity retained its ‘ADD’ rating and ₹190 target, citing hotel growth but flagging margin pressure from planned investments of ₹10-12 Cr over the next couple of quarters.
Swiggy Hits Record Low
Swiggy’s 24.5% weekly fall left it 54.7% below its ₹390 IPO price, with widening Instamart losses weighing on sentiment.
Its consolidated Q2 FY27 loss narrowed 16% YoY to ₹922 Cr but widened 17% sequentially from ₹791 Cr. Operating revenue rose 36% YoY to ₹7,571 Cr, while consumer-facing businesses’ gross order value (GOV) increased 25% to ₹20,793 Cr.
Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹895 Cr from ₹849 Cr a year earlier and ₹778 Cr in Q1, despite GOV rising 31% YoY to ₹9,230 Cr.
Swiggy cited pricing investments, customer and category mix changes, and new dark-store costs for contribution-margin pressure. It expects Q2 to mark peak adjusted EBITDA losses and anticipates around 100 basis points of margin improvement in Q3.
Food delivery’s adjusted EBITDA rose to a record ₹341 Cr from ₹240 Cr, while revenue grew 22% to ₹2,338 Cr. Segment profit increased 39% to ₹349 Cr.
Swiggy plans to shift Instamart to an inventory-led model over two to three quarters, targeting an 80-basis-point contribution-margin improvement.
Brokerages largely retained ratings but cut targets over quick commerce losses and execution concerns. HSBC lowered its target to ₹240 from ₹315, while CLSA cut its target to ₹262.
Edited by Vinaykumar Rai
Creatives by Varshita Srivastava

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by Cole Palmer’s red card in Saturday’s 2-0 victory.
Roberto De Zerbi’s side clinched their second successive league win thanks to Penders’s howler in the second half at a rain-lashed Stamford Bridge.
Chelsea forward Palmer was sent off for a second booking moments later before Mathys Tel produced a superb solo effort to condemn the Blues to their first home defeat against Tottenham since 2018.
Since 1990, Tottenham had won just once in 41 previous away matches against London rivals Chelsea in all competitions.
Ending that miserable run gave Tottenham only their second win in their last 16 league games against Chelsea, both home and away, and their first since 2023.
After a dismal start to the season, Tottenham have climbed to 12th place after building on Monday’s win against Coventry, which ended their wait for a first league win this season.
It was a bitter blow for fourth-placed Chelsea, who had beaten Bournemouth and Everton in their previous two league games.
They were booed off at full-time and remain very much a work in progress under Xabi Alonso in the Spaniard’s first season in charge.
With Joao Pedro sidelined by a late injury, Morgan Rogers was Chelsea’s central striker, but their revamped attack was short of bite.
Teed up by Rogers after Pedro Neto stole possession from Mateus Fernandes, Palmer went close to an early opener with a curler that Antonin Kinsky tipped over at full stretch.
Tottenham responded with a spell of probing pressure as Omar Marmoush met Andy Robertson’s cross with a shot that was repelled by Penders.
Alonso’s men pieced together the best move of the half with a flurry of one-touch passes to reach Jordan Henderson on the edge of the area, but the midfielder’s low drive was palmed away by Kinsky.
– Spurs spring a surprise –
Neto tested Kinsky with a fierce blast but the Tottenham keeper was up to the task with a save at his near post.
Tottenham suffered a blow when often-injured midfielder James Maddison limped off in a premature end to only his second start since May 2025.
Maddison had already missed training sessions since his long-awaited start against Coventry and his latest fitness setback suggested it was a failed gamble to start him at the Bridge.
In keeping with the sloppy fare, Neto fired straight at Kinsky from a dangerous position after Palmer pounced on Sandro Tonali’s wayward pass.
When Palmer’s run was halted by Fernandes’s handball, the Chelsea star escaped with a yellow card after barging into his rival with such aggression that the Tottenham midfielder was sent crashing to the sodden turf.
Tottenham exacted swift revenge in the 77th minute.
Fernandes’s in-swinging corner should have been caught by Penders, but he opted for a punch that was completely mistimed as he diverted the ball into his net for a comical own goal.
It was a horrible moment for the 21-year-old Penders, who was making his first league start in the absence of Emiliano Martinez following jaw surgery.
Rubbing salt into Chelsea’s wounds, Palmer was dismissed three minutes later for an ugly stamp on Conor Gallagher.
Tel wrapped up Tottenham’s memorable triumph in fitting style in the 87th minute, skipping away from Chelsea’s flat-footed defence to drill a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the area.

.As APM launches reset movement in Lagos
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
Oyo State Governor and Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has accused President Bola Tinubu of using reported growth in foreign reserves to create impression of economic recovery which is untrue.
Makinde accused Tinubu’s administration, of using rising foreign reserve figures as a “political gimmick” to obscure widespread hunger and economic distress across the nation.
​Speaking via online video message on Saturday at the launch of the Makinde and Daura for Better Nigeria (MAD) Resetter Movement in Lagos, Makinde maintained that boasting about macroeconomic growth means nothing to millions of citizens struggling daily to afford basic necessities.
“I am with you 101 per cent towards the reset agenda for Nigeria. We need to reset our economy, our security architecture, our educational system and the socio-political environment,” he said.
Makinde likened the situation to a household where the head boasts of savings while family members go hungry.
“We have heard stories that Nigeria’s foreign reserves are going up. I liken it to a household where the head is telling the people that we have a lot of money in our savings accounts, but everyone in that household is hungry,” he said.
Makinde said economic progress should be measured by citizens’ prosperity and ability to pursue opportunities, and called for return to federalism and multiparty democracy.
“Nigeria was negotiated on the basis of a federalism arrangement. Nigeria was negotiated on the basis of multiparty democracy,” he said.
​Comparing the government’s stance to a flawed household dynamic, Makinde stated; “We have heard stories that Nigeria’s foreign reserves are going up. I liken it to a household where the head is telling the people that we have a lot of money in our savings accounts, but everyone in that household is hungry.”
​APM Presidential candidate, stressed that true economic progress must be judged by tangible improvements in living standards, job opportunities for young people, and financial independence, rather than official statistics.
​Calling for a comprehensive national reset, Makinde urged Nigerians to look beyond propaganda and demand a return to genuine federalism and multiparty democracy.
He called on citizens across all geopolitical zones to join the movement to reshape the country’s economic, educational, security, and socio-political frameworks ahead of the 2027 general elections.
​Also, Director-General of the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, Hassan Felix, questioned the government’s claims of economic recovery.
Citing rising unemployment, worsening insecurity, and the departure of foreign companies from Nigeria, Felix stated that the “time of deceit is over” and demanded an immediate change in direction.
​Similarly, Director of Volunteers and Support Groups for the campaign, Dr. Emmanuel Dennis, stressed that the movement intends to break away from traditional political rallies focused merely on entertainment.
​”We want to make our campaign issue-based,” Dennis said, pointing to soaring petrol prices, stagnant salaries, and erosion of electoral integrity through judicial outcomes rather than voter choice,” Dennis stated.
He therefore, urged supporters to back the movement in resetting governance both in Lagos State and at the federal level.
​APM pledges inclusive governance in Lagos
​The launch also featured the endorsement of APM’s Lagos State governorship candidate, Adelaja Adeoye, along with the party’s senatorial and legislative flagbearers, by local government party chairmen represented by Isiaka Sodeinde.
​Pledging an inclusive, gender-sensitive administration free from the influence of political godfathers, Adeoye urged voters to resist vote-buying ahead of the polls.
​”Your PVC is the instrument in your hands; that is your power,” Adeoye told supporters.
“If truly you are tired of bad governance, don’t collect money from them. Don’t let them bribe you because what they give you won’t last you a day,” Adeoye stated.

items.content:
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Saturday said Pakistan's crude oil and other energy supplies remained satisfactory despite escalating regional conflicts, seeking to allay concerns over a possible fuel crisis after lawmakers raised questions in the Senate about petroleum availability through December and the country's preparedness for further disruptions.
However, he acknowledged that additional measures would be needed to meet domestic gas and liquefied natural gas (LNG) requirements.
Addressing a ceremony at a private university in Lahore, Aurangzeb said Pakistan had so far avoided energy shortages, queues at petrol pumps and law-and-order problems arising from an energy crisis.
He said arrangements were in place to meet energy requirements until November, while preparations for the winter were continuing amid uncertainty over regional supplies.
His remarks followed Friday's Senate debate, during which Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Senator Sherry Rehman questioned whether petrol would remain available through December as the conflict in the Middle East intensified.
She called on the petroleum and energy ministers to brief parliament on contingency plans, including the possibility of rationing, and warned that disruptions to energy supply routes could have serious implications for Pakistan's energy security and economic stability.
Rehman also highlighted the country's dependence on imported liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), saying around 70 per cent of its requirements were met through imports and 30 per cent through domestic production.
Pakistan had received five LPG cargoes last year, while only two were expected this year, she told the Senate, demanding that the government present a clear supply plan.
Opposition leader Raja Nasir Abbas also warned that the widening regional conflict, stretching from Iran to Yemen, threatened key maritime chokepoints and could aggravate Pakistan's energy difficulties.
He pointed to an existing LPG shortage and flour shortages in Punjab, criticising political leaders for focusing on power struggles instead of public concerns. He also called on Pakistan to mediate between Yemen and Saudi Arabia.
Responding to concerns over fuel affordability in the Senate, Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani had maintained that there was no fuel supply problem and said more than 10 million people were benefiting from targeted fuel subsidies.
He said motorcyclists were receiving Rs500 worth of free petrol per week, while owners of vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc were receiving Rs1,000 in relief on 10 litres of petrol. Assistance was also being provided to rickshaw and loader operators and users of small cars.
Aurangzeb said the government had taken effective measures to secure energy purchases and supplies despite regional conflicts. While the arrangements currently in place were sufficient to meet requirements until November, he acknowledged that further steps were necessary to address gas and LNG needs, with planning for the winter still under way.
 
Targeted relief reaches millions
The finance minister said the government had opted for targeted subsidies instead of general subsidies to ensure that relief reached those who needed it most.
Under the scheme, assistance had been extended to motorcyclists, users of three-wheelers and owners of vehicles with engine capacities below 800cc.
Aurangzeb said 12 million unique individuals had benefited from the scheme so far, while the total number of people benefiting from the relief was estimated at 40 million to 50 million.
Aurangzeb also highlighted improvements in Pakistan's economic indicators, saying information technology (IT) export services had grown from $1 billion to $4.6 billion. IT exports were expected to reach $5.5 billion during the current fiscal year, he added.
He said Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves had reached a record high and were sufficient to cover more than three months of imports. In contrast, he recalled, reserves in the past had fallen to a level sufficient to finance just two weeks of imports.
Aurangzeb said Pakistan's credit rating had improved three times since April last year, while significant steps had been taken to restore access to international financial markets.
The minister said Pakistan had undertaken a private placement in April this year, accessed international markets through the issuance of a Panda bond and issued bonds worth three billion euros in the first week of September.
He said orders received from investors for Pakistan's Eurobonds were twice the amount issued, reflecting interest from investors in Asia, the Middle East, Europe and the United States.
Aurangzeb said international investors were increasingly assessing Pakistan's economic outlook beyond its current programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which is scheduled to conclude in October next year.
He maintained that Pakistan's economic stabilisation was being accompanied by structural reforms and that the process had moved beyond planning into implementation.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Advocate Amjad Hussain Azar has maintained that mines and minerals are a provincial subject and should not be treated as the exclusive domain of the federal government, calling for stronger enforcement and monitoring of the region's mineral resources.
He also backed the creation of new provinces wherever consensus exists, saying the Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly had already passed a resolution demanding provincial status for the region.
Speaking to the media in Karachi on Saturday, Azar said his government had completed its first 100 days and begun implementing the Pakistan Peoples Party's (PPP) manifesto.
He highlighted efforts to ensure transparent recruitment and promote livestock, commerce, tourism and border trade, while disclosing that a public-private partnership unit had been established in Gilgit-Baltistan and that the United States had shown interest in investing in the region's energy sector.
On the question of provincial autonomy, Azar argued that the federal government could not handle every matter itself and that provinces should be allowed to discharge their respective responsibilities.
He said the mining and minerals sector particularly required effective enforcement and monitoring.
The chief minister said the Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly had passed a resolution seeking provincial status for the region and that the PPP supported this demand.
He maintained that new provinces should be created wherever there was consensus, while the issue should not be pursued in areas where agreement had yet to emerge.
Azar said his government had started fulfilling its promises and assuming the responsibilities of a democratic political administration. He added that work was underway to improve higher education, healthcare and education in Gilgit-Baltistan.
Commenting on the country's economic difficulties, Azar said industrial activity had stalled and that industries could not operate sustainably on the basis of expensive thermal electricity.
Hydropower, he said, was the cheapest source of electricity and offered considerable potential to support industrial growth.
He said a public-private partnership unit had been established in Gilgit-Baltistan and disclosed that the United States had shown interest in investing in the region's energy sector.
The chief minister also highlighted Gilgit-Baltistan's vast tourism potential, saying the region's economic opportunities should be developed so its people did not remain poor. He stressed the need to harness local resources to improve livelihoods and create better economic prospects.
Azar also pledged to work towards ending load-shedding in Gilgit-Baltistan, asking residents to allow the government some time to address the problem.
He said his government remained in contact with Gilgit-Baltistan residents living in Karachi and was attentive to their concerns.
Taking aim at the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) performance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Azar urged people to assess the province's 13 years under PTI-led governments by examining conditions across its different regions.
He alleged that the party had failed to focus on governance and instead remained engaged in confrontations with political parties and state institutions.
He said such an approach was bound to produce adverse consequences, arguing that the PTI had relied on popular slogans and political disputes rather than effective governance.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has taken a swipe at UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband over the way he sat during an official meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Istanbul.
“Etiquette dictates that the soles of your shoes should not be visible to the people sitting around you, especially when you are in a formal setting,” Asif wrote on X on Saturday.
He was quoting a photo from the meeting showing Miliband sitting with one leg crossed over the other, with the sole of his shoe facing Dar.
The Defence Minister’s post drew big traffic within hours. The minister is known for blunt social media remarks and has targeted foreign leaders before.
Some X posters said if a Pakistani official had sat like this, body language and diplomatic etiquette experts would have rushed to school him. He added that the British get a free pass from the same behavior.
What the Meeting Was About
Dar met Miliband on Friday on the sidelines of the R4 and E3 foreign ministers’ meeting hosted by Türkiye. According to an official statement, the two sides agreed to further strengthen bilateral cooperation and discussed regional and international developments.
UK Foreign Secretary also praised Pakistan’s role in promoting regional peace.
The Istanbul meeting brought together the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, the UK, France, Germany, and Italy. Talks focused on the US/Israel-Iran conflict and tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.
Dar also held separate meetings with his German, French, Saudi, Turkish, and Egyptian counterparts during the visit.

Speaking on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign launch in Kaduna, Shettima said Tinubu had consistently supported politicians from the north, including former President Muhammadu Buhari.
He said it was only fair for the region to reciprocate the support by re-electing the President and other candidates contesting different positions under the APC.

He said Tinubu had at a time supported and provided a platform for former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to contest the presidency in 2007 after his exit from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).
Shettima also recalled how Tinubu canvassed support for late President Buhari during his presidential campaigns in 2015 and 2019.

items.content:
The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari, has assured President Bola Tinubu of overwhelming support from northern Nigeria in the 2027 general election.
Speaking on Saturday at the APC presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna, Yari said the campaign council was committed to mobilising support across the North through engagements with traditional rulers, Islamic scholars, imams and other influential stakeholders.
“Northern Nigeria is 100% yours, insha Allah. This is the promise that we make, and you are going to see it in January 2027,” Yari said.
The former Zamfara State governor said the campaign would focus on the administration’s performance in infrastructure, healthcare, education, human capital development and social welfare.
Tinubu gave you succour when PDP chased you in 2007, Shettima tackles Atiku
Atiku to Tinubu: You can&#8217;t light fire of hardship, then blame your neighbours for the smoke
According to him, the APC intends to use its campaign to communicate the government’s policies and achievements to Nigerians, particularly in the northern region.
Yari said engagements with traditional and religious leaders were part of efforts to explain the administration’s programmes and encourage support for Tinubu’s re-election bid.
He also defended the government’s relationship with farmers, dismissing allegations that the administration had neglected the agricultural sector.
The APC chieftain claimed that about two million farmers had committed to supporting Tinubu in the 2027 election.
“They are lying that the government of Asiwaju Bola Tinubu does not like farmers, that you hate farmers. That is not true,” he said.
Yari argued that such claims did not reflect the administration’s position on agriculture, insisting that the government was committed to addressing the concerns of farmers.
He also accused critics of deploying artificial intelligence (AI) to circulate false information about the Tinubu administration, urging the campaign to counter such claims by presenting what he described as the government’s achievements.
The former governor further cited developments in the foreign exchange market, Nigeria’s foreign reserves and the country’s trade balance as indicators of economic progress under Tinubu.
On the exchange rate, Yari said the naira had improved from a level approaching N1,800 to about N1,300 against the dollar.
He also claimed that Nigeria’s foreign reserves had increased from $3.9 billion to between $54 billion and $57.7 billion.
On trade, Yari said the country’s trade balance had risen from about N44 billion in 2023 to N7.5 trillion.
He presented the figures as evidence of progress under the current administration and said they would form part of the APC’s message to voters ahead of the next general election.
However, the figures cited by Yari were claims made during the campaign address and would require independent verification against official economic data.
Yari also pledged that the APC Presidential Campaign Council would work closely with governors across the country to mobilise voters and strengthen the party’s chances in the 2027 presidential election.
He described the governors as key figures in the party’s mobilisation efforts at the state level, adding that the campaign council would complement their activities.
“The governors, your commanders in the states, are doing a remarkable job. We are going to complement them, and by God’s grace, the victory is ours,” he said.
Yari expressed confidence that coordinated mobilisation and the presentation of the administration’s record would help the APC secure another electoral victory in 2027.

items.content:
Former Chairman of the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON), Professor Abdullahi Saleh Pakistan, has said President Bola Tinubu deserves a second term in office because of projects executed by his administration and what he described as improvements in security.
Pakistan, who is also the leader of the Izala group in Kano State, stated this in an interview with DCL Hausa, saying the federal government had executed projects worth over N9 trillion in Kano State.
He said many residents were unaware that the projects they could see around them were being executed by the federal government.
The cleric said the Kano State Governor had during their meeting told them that several projects were being carried out in the state by the federal government, saying that many people don’t know that they were federal government interventions.
Atiku to Tinubu: You can&#8217;t light fire of hardship, then blame your neighbours for the smoke
2027: Forget about social media news, Nigerians love Tinubu &#8211; Information minister
He cited the provision of solar power systems to Northwest University, Kano, which he said cost N6 billion, despite the institution being owned by the state government.
He also said the federal government provided a solar power system for Radio Kano at a cost of N2 billion.
Pakistan said he would continue to promote Tinubu’s administration because he believed the president had demonstrated the capacity to govern and deserved another term to complete the projects he had started.
He cited the Kaduna-Abuja highway, saying travellers had faced serious security challenges in the past but that the situation had improved under Tinubu.
The cleric also defended his position on insecurity after a video circulated in which he was alleged to have said kidnapping was not a problem in northern Nigeria.
He said the video had been edited, explaining that his argument was that former President Muhammadu Buhari inherited the Boko Haram insurgency, while there was no banditry Katsina, Kaduna, Sokoto and Zamfara at the time.
According to him, Tinubu also inherited the kidnapping crisis and remnants of Boko Haram from the Buhari administration.
He added that kidnapping became a major problem in Zamfara during Buhari’s tenure, when a former defence minister was also from the state.
Pakistan said he believed insecurity had reduced significantly under Tinubu, particularly in the North-East, where he claimed reports of mass killings had become less frequent.
On the 2027 presidential election, he said former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar had yet to convince him that he had a better plan than Tinubu for addressing insecurity.
He said he had not seen a convincing explanation from Atiku on how he intended to tackle the problem.
Pakistan also denied reports that he had threatened Nigeria may fall into violence if Tinubu was not re-elected, saying he had only argued that Tinubu before he became President had made sure that North should be allowed to complete its eight-year presidential tenure under Buhari before power returned to the South.
He said Tinubu had supported Buhari’s bid for a second term despite opposition to the former president’s re-election over concerns about his health and other issues.
According to him, Tinubu’s support for Buhari demonstrated his willingness to stand by the North, adding that the region should acknowledge the role he played.
He recalled that Tinubu had offered Atiku an opportunity to contest under the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN) after the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) denied him its presidential ticket.
Pakistan also said he had previously supported the candidacy of Nuhu Ribadu, a northern Muslim, with a southerner as his running mate.
He said his support for Tinubu was also informed by his assessment of the president’s record in Lagos, where he claimed projects continued despite delays in the release of funds to the state, alongside the payment of salaries.
The cleric, however, said he would not use his religious position to advance his political interests.
He said he kept his religious responsibilities separate from politics and did not use the pulpit to persuade his followers to adopt his political views.
He added that he did not force his children to share his political choices, stressing that every Nigerian had the right to hold and express an independent political opinion.
Pakistan urged Islamic scholars to avoid harsh language when discussing political disagreements, saying people should respect one another’s political choices.
He said even though his name was included in a campaign committee for Tinubu and Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, said that his participation would not conflict with his religious teachings.
The cleric disclosed that he and about nine other people met Tinubu about two weeks ago for roughly two hours, during which they presented issues affecting the North and requested that the president address them if re-elected.
According to him, Tinubu indicated that he was not desperate for power, money or recognition and would be willing to return to private life if Nigerians no longer wanted him in office.
Pakistan said he and other supporters had also recently met the Kano State governor and were surprised by the projects presented to them.
He maintained that he would not stop promoting Tinubu despite what he described as allegations against him.

items.content:
By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has mocked the All Progressives Congress, APC, over what it described as a disappointing Northwest zonal flag-off rally in Kaduna, alleging that rented crowds and empty seats exposed the ruling party’s declining public acceptance.
The council said the rally, which was intended to showcase the APC’s political strength across the Northwest, fell short of expectations despite alleged mobilisation of attendees from the seven states in the zone and beyond.
In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC alleged that attendees were reportedly paid between ₦50,000 and ₦100,000 each, yet the Kaduna Township Stadium, which it put at a capacity of 5,000, remained sparsely occupied.
“For a rally billed as the Northwest zonal flag-off, what we witnessed was a shameful spectacle. Despite the alleged mobilisation of crowds from across the zone and beyond, the stadium remained scantily filled, with empty seats everywhere,” Ologbondiyan said.
He also faulted the reception given to speeches by APC leaders, describing it as unenthusiastic and at odds with the ruling party’s attempt to project political strength in the region.
The ADC-PCC further questioned President Bola Tinubu’s performance claims, criticising his reported commissioning of road projects at the rally.
Ologbondiyan alleged that some attendees expressed dissatisfaction with the APC after leaving the stadium, chanting “Ba mu yi,” a Hausa expression he interpreted as a rejection of the ruling party and its policies.
“You can rent a crowd, but you cannot rent acceptance. Even if people attend a rally, that does not mean they have surrendered their convictions. The real test of public support is what Nigerians will decide at the ballot box,” he said.
The council accused the APC of recycling promises made during the 2015, 2019 and 2023 election cycles without adequately accounting for its years in power.
It also accused Tinubu of shifting responsibility for Nigerians’ economic hardship to opposition leaders instead of addressing the consequences of his administration’s policies, particularly fuel subsidy removal, which it said had intensified the pressure on households struggling with rising living costs.
The ADC-PCC urged the ruling party to abandon what it called wasteful political jamborees, apologise to Nigerians over the prevailing economic difficulties and prepare for an orderly transfer of power in 2027.
The council maintained that the ADC offered a credible alternative to the APC, expressing confidence that voters would use the next general election to reject the ruling party.
“The message from Kaduna is loud and clear: Nigerians are saying ‘Ba mu yi’ to the APC and Tinubu. Come 2027, they will speak even louder with their votes,” Ologbondiyan declared.

items.content:
Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, has commended the 2027 presidential campaign flag-off rally organised by the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council.
The rally was organised for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.
Idris gave the commendation on Saturday at the rally ground in Kaduna State, expressing confidence in Tinubu’s popularity and the support for his administration’s reform agenda.
He described the large turnout at the rally as an indication of the president’s acceptance among Nigerians, particularly supporters who believe in his policies.
Tinubu gave you succour when PDP chased you in 2007, Shettima tackles Atiku
2027: It&#8217;s our turn to repay Tinubu, Shettima tells northerners
He urged Nigerians to look beyond social media reports and opposition criticisms, insisting that the crowd at the rally demonstrated support for Tinubu.
“We have always been saying this: forget about all the social media news, forget about all the talk from the opposition. Asiwaju is loved by Nigerians,” Idris said.
He described Kaduna as a significant location for the campaign flag-off, noting its historical importance as the former capital of Northern Nigeria.
According to him, the presence of supporters from different political backgrounds demonstrated a willingness to unite behind Tinubu and his administration’s reform agenda.
Idris said that Nigerians were increasingly recognising the potential benefits of the government’s policies and the prospects for economic recovery.
He said that the country was facing challenges, but expressed optimism that the administration’s reforms would eventually improve the nation’s economic conditions.
“There may be challenges at this moment, but we are moving away from that. We are consolidating on progress, and Nigeria is going to be better for it,” the minister said.
He said the administration remained committed to moving the country towards economic growth, improved living conditions and sustainable national development.
Idris described the atmosphere at the rally as encouraging for the president’s re-election campaign.
He said that the administration’s vision was to achieve prosperity for Nigerians through policies intended to strengthen the economy and create development opportunities.
“We are excited; everybody is excited. All of us are moving in the direction of progress, in the direction of prosperity, like the President has promised every Nigerian,” he said.
The minister also challenged opposition parties to demonstrate their level of public support, arguing that the gathering reflected strong enthusiasm for Tinubu.
He dismissed criticisms of the president’s popularity, urging supporters to remain focused on the administration’s development agenda.
Idris expressed confidence that Nigerians would vote for Tinubu for a second term in the 2027 presidential election.
He said the president’s re-election would provide an opportunity to consolidate the ongoing reforms and pursue the administration’s promise of national prosperity.
“Nigeria will vote President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for the second time, and Nigeria is going to march towards the prosperity that the president has promised all Nigerians,” he said.
Also speaking at the rally, the spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council and Minister of Solid Minerals, Mr Dele Alake, described the gathering as an encouraging moment for the ruling party.
Alake said the enthusiasm displayed by the crowd indicated the level of mobilisation and support expected to shape the party’s campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections.
“It is a very excited moment for most of us here. And I see the crowd here, lively. That is a pointer to what will happen in the next election,” he said.
He expressed confidence that Nigerians would support Tinubu’s re-election, describing him as a leader with the experience and determination to guide the country towards progress.
Alake said the president had demonstrated courage and vision by taking difficult decisions aimed at addressing longstanding economic challenges.
He said that the reforms were necessary to reposition the country for sustainable development and establish a stronger foundation for future prosperity.
According to him, Tinubu’s commitment to implementing the reforms reflected his determination to leave a lasting legacy and put Nigeria on the right path.
“Now, it is the season for prosperity. Nigerians are beginning to see the results of those reforms, and they have been trickling in, and they will continue to trickle in,” Alake said.
He expressed optimism that the benefits of the reforms would continue to emerge, describing the country’s economic prospects as encouraging.
Alake said the rally provided an opportunity for supporters to unite behind Tinubu’s vision, adding that the administration’s policies are intended to move Nigeria towards greater prosperity and development.(NAN)

items.author: Qaisar Shirazi
items.content:
Rising fuel prices, food costs and transport fares are adding to the financial strain on households in the country, with petrol prices increasing 26.11% and high-speed diesel 26.39% in the first nearly four months of FY2026-27.
Petrol prices rose to Rs377.71 per litre on October 24 from Rs299.50 on July 1, an increase of Rs78.21 per litre, according to available price records. High-speed diesel climbed to Rs393.66 per litre from Rs311.47 over the same period, an increase of Rs82.19.
Higher fuel costs are also increasing expenses for passenger transport, freight operators and the movement of agricultural produce, adding to pressure on household budgets and supply chains.
The price index for 51 essential commodities rose about 5.81% between July 2 and October 22, according to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics' weekly Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI), adding to the pressure on salaried workers, daily-wage earners, pensioners and low-income families.
The fresh surge in food and fuel prices squeezed household budgets across major cities as chicken is being sold for as much as Rs700 per kilogram, beef for Rs1,500 per kilogram in Karachi and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has become Rs150 per kilogram more expensive.
The rising costs have also pushed up transport fares and raised the prospect of a Rs5 to Rs10 increase in the price of roti from next week, while consumers complain that authorities have failed to curb profiteering and provide relief.
In Karachi, soaring food prices have made it increasingly difficult for low- and middle-income households to afford even two meals a day. Chicken prices have risen by as much as Rs200 per kilogram during the current month, taking the price of chicken meat to Rs700 per kilogram.
Consumers say beef and mutton were already beyond their purchasing power, and chicken has now become increasingly unaffordable as well.
Beef is being sold in the open market for Rs1,200 per kilogram with bones and between Rs1,400 and Rs1,500 without bones. Heifer meat is available for Rs1,400 per kilogram with bones and between Rs1,600 and Rs1,700 without bones.
Consumers say meat is not available anywhere at the government-notified rates, while shopkeepers openly violate official price limits with little fear of action.
Flour prices have also added to the pressure on household budgets. 2.5-number flour is selling for Rs150 per kilogram, while flour milled at traditional stone mills, commonly known as 'chakki atta', costs Rs180 per kilogram.
Cooking oil has reached Rs600 per litre, following an increase of Rs40 per litre in the prices of edible oil and ghee over the past month.
Meanwhile, an increase of up to Rs150 per kilogram in LPG prices over the past week has further aggravated the cost-of-living crisis. The higher fuel costs have also led to increases in fares charged by rickshaws, taxis and Qingqi three-wheeled motorcycles.
Tandoor operators have warned that they may raise the price of roti by Rs5 to Rs10 from next week if LPG prices do not come down.
Bakery owners are also preparing to increase prices, citing higher gas costs and rising prices of flour and refined flour. Buns, rusks, sliced bread, biscuits and other bakery products are among the items whose prices are being raised.
Vegetable prices remain high in Karachi. Onions are selling for between Rs160 and Rs180 per kilogram, tomatoes for Rs100, carrots for Rs150, cucumbers for Rs100, peas for Rs400, okra for Rs250, round gourds for Rs300, bottle gourd and ridge gourd for Rs160, and spinach for Rs100 per kilogram.
Consumers complain that there is no effective check on rampant inflation, that official price lists are absent from markets and that profiteers are operating freely. They say the government has failed to provide relief from rising prices.
Similarly, in Lahore, the government-notified price of broiler chicken meat has reached Rs577 per kilogram, but retailers are selling it for Rs600 per kilogram, in violation of the official rate.
The district administration has been unable to prevent the overcharging.
Meanwhile, consumers in Rawalpindi and Islamabad are facing further increases in chicken and egg prices following earlier rises in the cost of vegetables, fruit, pulses, flour and gram flour.
In the open market, live chicken is selling for Rs450 per kilogram, chicken meat for Rs700 per kilogram and boneless chicken for Rs1,000 per kilogram.
Broiler eggs are priced at Rs265 per dozen, while local desi eggs are selling for Rs600 per dozen, adding to the difficulties faced by consumers.

items.content:
Consumers already struggling with exorbitant liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices are now facing a worsening shortage after dealers abruptly shut their shops in protest against "harassment by enforcement agencies" and inaction against LPG companies and alleged profiteers.
The strike has forced people to search for alternative cooking fuels, with coal and firewood sellers also raising their prices.
Around 5,500 to 6,000 LPG shops have been closed in Lahore and several other cities, leaving consumers carrying empty cylinders from one shop to another in search of gas.
The shutdown comes after consumers had been forced to buy LPG at exceptionally high prices for the past week and a half, while dealers say they can no longer bear the losses and penalties imposed on them.
Speaking to The Express News, shopkeeper Kashif Bilal Asghar said personnel from the PERA Force and Civil Defence visited shops and confiscated LPG filling pumps. He said each pump cost between Rs50,000 and Rs60,000, while dealers were also being fined between Rs5,000 and Rs10,000.
Asghar maintained that shopkeepers were not responsible for the high prices, arguing that LPG companies and the alleged profiteering network were supplying gas at inflated rates while retailers bore the consequences.
He alleged that the OGRA had not taken action against a single LPG company or plant, despite profiteering worth billions of rupees. Instead, he said, enforcement agencies were targeting shopkeepers.
The dealers have now shut their businesses in protest, saying they would no longer submit to pressure from the LPG mafia.
The shutdown has compounded consumers' difficulties, particularly those already struggling to afford cooking fuel. Residents questioned what they were expected to do when LPG was unavailable at the price fixed by OGRA and could no longer be obtained even at higher market rates.
With LPG unavailable, many people have turned to shops selling coal and dry firewood.
However, the increased demand has also pushed up the price of coal by Rs10 to Rs20 per kilogram. Coal that was previously sold for Rs40 per kilogram is now being offered at between Rs50 and Rs60 per kilogram.
Small food businesses have been among those worst affected by the shortage, as many tandoors and eateries depend entirely on LPG to operate. The disruption has left vendors struggling to keep their businesses running while the cost of alternative fuels continues to rise.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
With only a week left in the twice-extended deadline for filing income tax returns, the previously non-resident but now resident Pakistanis are facing a unique problem as they are barred from disclosing their wealth in this year's returns.
The restriction on stating the opening wealth position for the tax year seemed a technical glitch on the part of Pakistan Revenue Automation Limited in return documents for the last tax year. The deadline to submit returns with all benefits of being a filer is going to end next Saturday.
The Karachi Tax Bar Association has written to the member operations of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to fix the glitch, which otherwise could create serious legal problems for people who have become resident Pakistanis.
The association stated that a specific restriction in the Wealth Reconciliation Statement was creating difficulties for individuals returning to Pakistan after a period of non-residence. Under the income tax law, if a Pakistani lives abroad for a certain number of days in a year, the person becomes a non-resident Pakistani for tax purposes.
The tax bar stated that the difficulty arose because the Inland Revenue Information System (IRIS) web portal automatically populated the opening wealth balance from the last filed Wealth Statement and did not allow that balance to be edited.
Where an individual resumes resident status after the intervening years of non-residence, the system therefore retains the wealth balance reported before that period, rather than allowing the appropriate opening balance for the relevant tax year to be entered.
"This has created a reconciliation difficulty where no wealth statements are required under Section 116(2) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 during the intervening years," it added.
The individuals who have returned to Pakistan and become residents are now required to furnish the Wealth Statement and Wealth Reconciliation Statement for tax year 2026.
However, the IRIS automatically carries forward the wealth balance for the last period of being the resident Pakistani into the non-editable opening balance field. This prevents the individual from entering the appropriate opening wealth balance for tax year 2026 and reconciling the movement in wealth for that year, as contemplated by Section 116(2).
The Karachi tax bar stated that under the self-assessment and declaration framework of income tax laws, a taxpayer should have the liberty to declare the opening wealth balance on the basis of relevant information and records, subject to applicable provisions of the law.
It asked the FBR, that without prejudice to this broader position, to resolve the matter by modifying the relevant validation on IRIS to permit returning individuals to enter the appropriate opening wealth balance for the relevant tax year. This will enable them to reconcile the movement in wealth for that year without requiring a reconciliation spanning the intervening years of non-residence.
The FBR is currently undergoing a period of uncertainty after a proposal to either establish a new tax agency or outsource some of the functions was shot down by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The Inland Revenue Service officers had threatened to observe a pen-down strike against any such move.
The association had taken back the deadline following assurance from the FBR member operations that no adverse action would be taken. However, subsequently, the FBR suspended two officers and posted another seven in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan on suspicion of being behind the pen-down strike move.
This has created uncertainty in the organisation and could also undermine its work, according to multiple taxmen who spoke to The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity.

The National Biosafety Committee (NBC) deferred consideration of pending Food, Feed and Processing applications for soybean meal imports, renewal of genetically modified (GM) corn biosafety licences and several cotton-related applications at its 38th meeting, holding that the recommendations forwarded by its technical arm did not provide sufficiently clear conclusions for decision-making.

A representative of the Ministry of National Food Security and Research explained that in 2019 the government had decided to place commercialisation of biotech food crops on hold until a comprehensive policy framework was developed.
That gap has now been addressed through the approval and notification of the National Agricultural Biotechnology Policy (NABP) 2025, which provides a regulatory framework for the evaluation and commercialisation of agricultural biotechnology products, he said.
The reservations that led to the 2019 decision have therefore been resolved, and relevant authorities have been informed to proceed under the approved framework, according to the explanation given to the committee.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange's (PSX) benchmark KSE-100 index fell 2.4% during the outgoing week, shedding 4,045 points to close at 162,375, as escalating geopolitical tensions, rising oil prices and domestic economic uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The index declined for the fifth consecutive week, slipping below the key psychological levels of 166,000, 164,000 and 163,000 amid broad-based selling pressure.
On a day-on-day basis, the PSX commenced the trading week with a lacklustre session, where the KSE-100 index declined 454 points (-0.27%) to close at 165,966, slipping below the 166k level. On Tuesday, rising oil prices weighed on the PSX, which registered a negative trading session, losing 814 points (-0.49%) to 165,152.
Nevertheless, the bourse witnessed a positive session on Wednesday, finding support around 165,000, with the benchmark index gaining 779 points (+0.47%) to end trading at 165,931. However, the market lost even 164k on the second last session as geopolitical risks escalated. The KSE-100 dived 2,007 points (-1.21%) to 163,924. Geopolitical headwinds pushed the index below the 163,000 mark on the final trading day on Friday, when the market fell 1,550 points (-0.95%) to close at 162,375.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL) noted that the KSE-100 index declined 2.4% week-on-week to 162,375, shedding 4,045 points, primarily due to persistent geopolitical uncertainty. At the start of the week, Pakistan's FY26 GDP growth was revised down to 3.65% from 3.70% (FY25 revised to 3.11% from 3.18%), with quarterly growth of 3.89%, 4.31%, 4.42% and 2.0% from Q1 to Q4. Agriculture, industry and services grew 3.50%, 3.34% and 3.81%, respectively, while the economy's size reached Rs126.4 trillion ($450.4 billion), with per capita income at $1,896.
AHL mentioned that power generation in Sept'26 increased 5% year-on-year to 13,217 gigawatt hours (GWh), driven by higher hydel, local coal, imported coal and wind generation. The cost of generation rose 32% YoY to Rs9.35/kilowatt-hour due to a higher share of RLNG, high-speed diesel and furnace oil, along with elevated oil prices. Consequently, distribution companies sought a positive fuel cost adjustment of Rs2.56/kWh for Sept'26.
A committee reviewing Automotive and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-31 proposed reforms to boost exports, accelerate New Energy Vehicle (NEV) adoption and enhance competition. Key measures included lower sales tax on NEVs, reduced import tariffs, mandatory export targets for original equipment manufacturers, localisation requirements and incentives for incremental exports.
Cotton arrivals increased 8% YoY to 4,081k bales as of October 15, 2026, led by Sindh (+7% YoY to 2,443k bales) and Punjab (+8% YoY to 1,638k bales). Sowing reached 1.79 million hectares, 82.8% of the 2.16-million-hectare target, while the government had set an FY27 production target of 9.64 million bales, compared to 7.05 million bales in FY26. Petroleum prices recorded a 3.2% WoW decline in motor spirit to Rs377.71/litre and a 1.3% WoW decline in HSD to Rs391.75/litre, driven by lower ex-refinery prices (MS: -4.5% WoW, HSD: -1.8% WoW), while the levy and margins remained unchanged, AHL said.
JS Research Head Muhammad Waqas Ghani commented that the KSE-100 index declined for the fifth consecutive week, shedding 4,045 points (-2.4% WoW) to close at 162,375, amid persistent domestic and geopolitical uncertainty. Average volumes dropped 13% to 393 million shares, while traded value inched up 7% WoW to $69.7 million. Brent crude rose further, closing the week above $114/barrel, compared with last week's average of $106.
On the macro front, Pakistan's trade deficit widened 21.1% to $9.33 billion during 1QFY27 as imports grew nearly twice as fast as exports, highlighting pressure on the external account. Large-Scale Manufacturing (LSM) posted a 0.67% growth in Aug'26, signalling a slowdown in the industrial sector. The government revised the GDP growth for FY26 slightly downwards to 3.65%. The size of the economy now stands at $450.4 billion, while per capita income hovers around $1,896.
In other news, PM Sharif approved a 1% sales tax on EVs and major import tax cuts under a five-year auto policy, subject to IMF and cabinet approval, potentially lowering vehicle prices. National Savings' profit rates were increased by an average of around 24-40 basis points across major schemes. State Bank's reserves remained stable at $21.5 billion, Ghani said.

items.author: APP
items.content:
Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Establishment Division Senator Ahad Cheema has directed the National Highway Authority (NHA) to prepare a practical business plan with clear timelines and an assessment of its own capacity, calling for realistic project appraisals and sound financing decisions to strengthen the authority's financial sustainability.
He issued the direction while chairing a meeting to review measures for developing the authority's business plan, the ongoing assessment with an Asian Development Bank (ADB) consultant and ways to achieve financial viability, according to a press release issued by the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
Officials briefed the meeting on the initial findings of the study with the ADB consultant, and different models and options were presented to improve the authority's performance, strengthen its operations and support financial sustainability.
The minister called for a thorough review of projects under consideration, with the planning commission proforma, or PC-I, setting out their commercial viability through more realistic indicators to facilitate appraisal by the Central Development Working Party (CDWP).
He asked the authority to classify projects according to their viability and financing requirements, including those requiring government or foreign funding, and said initial project studies should clearly assess viability and be shared at an early stage with the Central Monitoring Unit (CMU) of the Ministry of Finance for comments.
The minister underscored that government or external financing for NHA projects should not lead to a reduction in the authority's Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) allocation, saying the government was not in favour of cutting the allocation, as PSDP funding remained essential to the development programme.
He stressed that commercially, economically and socially viable projects should be prioritised to strengthen financial sustainability and help the authority avoid an unsustainable debt-servicing burden, while projects that are not commercially viable should undergo a thorough study and review before any decision is made.
He also urged the authority to expedite its work with the ADB consultant, whose input is expected to strengthen project mapping, feasibility assessments and financial analysis. Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal, Communications Secretary Ali Sher Mehsud, NHA Chief Executive Officer and other senior officials attended the meeting.

Work on the Charsadda Road Flyover is also underway, with 25 percent of construction completed so far.
The NHA has accelerated work across the project, with different sections currently at various stages of completion.

items.author: Arsalan Khattak
items.content:
The Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Administration and the Capital Development Authority (CDA) took control of five commercial plazas in Mouza Malpur along Murree Road on Friday evening as part of a campaign to recover allegedly encroached state land.
The operation, which involved the CDA Enforcement Directorate and Islamabad Police, targets 108 kanals of government land that officials say people have occupied over the past two decades. A survey identified two fuel stations, nine commercial plazas, 25 houses and two warehouses on the disputed land.
Officials launched the drive after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi directed Islamabad’s chief commissioner and CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf to enforce anti-encroachment laws uniformly.
A revenue review found suspected discrepancies in ownership documents. According to officials, some people used records linked to different khasra numbers in neighboring Mouza Kot Hathial to claim properties in Mouza Malpur.
A document verification camp found cases in which sale deeds reportedly described land about 1.5 kilometers from the occupied properties. Authorities are preparing legal proceedings, including FIRs over alleged fraudulent land transactions.
Officials also reported that someone sold one plaza for Rs. 5 crore just five months ago. CDA Deputy Director General Enforcement Dr. Anum Fatima said the authority would take action against all unlawful occupants.
She added that officials would challenge court-issued stay orders through the relevant legal process while respecting judicial directions. The ICT Administration and CDA said the recovery campaign would continue based on verified revenue records and legal procedures.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Fashion ecommerce platform Myntra reported a net loss of ₹581.8 Cr in the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26), reversing a net profit of ₹546.3 Cr in the previous fiscal.
Myntra’s operating revenue fell 13.5% to ₹5,242.5 Cr in the fiscal under review, compared to ₹6,063.8 Cr in FY25. Myntra earns revenue from three streams – marketplace services, logistics services and advertisement services.
Breaking down the top line, marketplace and collection services contributed to 50.7%. It stood at ₹2,657.3 Cr in FY26, marking a 3% increase from ₹2,580.2 Cr in the previous year. Advertisement Services rose 35.2% to ₹1,236.4 Cr in the year under review, from ₹914.5 Cr in FY25.
Meanwhile, logistics and shipping services fell 53.2% to ₹1,119.2 Cr in FY2025-26, from ₹2,390.5 Cr a year ago. Besides these, other operating revenue contributed ₹229.6 Cr, taking the overall topline to ₹5,242.5 Cr in the reported year.
Including other income of ₹73.3 Cr, the total income for the fiscal year FY26 stood at ₹5,315.8 Cr, a 13.4% fall from ₹6,137 Cr.
The company’s EBITDA loss stood at ₹435 Cr in FY26, from ₹535.9 Cr in FY25.
Founded in 2007 by Mukesh Bansal, Ashutosh Lawania and Vineet Saxena, Myntra is an online marketplace which allows third-party sellers to sell their fashion products. The Bengaluru-based startup was acquired by Flipkart for $240 Mn in 2014.
“Flipkart Group is made up of various business verticals, including Flipkart, Myntra, and Cleartrip. Stakeholders should refer to the consolidated financials of Flipkart Internet Private Limited (Consolidated) when assessing the Flipkart Group’s overall financial performance over the reporting period,” Flipkart said in a statement.
Earlier this year, Flipkart Fashion’s Sharon Pais was elevated to the role of the head of fashion marketplace arm Myntra, replacing Nandita Sinha. Additionally, Myntra also appointed Instacart executive Pramod Adiddam as its chief technology officer (CTO).
Myntra’s parent, Flipkart Group, also released its consolidated FY26 financials following its reverse flip to India. The Walmart-backed ecommerce group saw an 18.2% jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr while loss narrowed 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr.
“At the PAT level, net loss reduced by approximately ₹180 Cr year over year. The improvement was moderated by higher finance costs, the derecognition of deferred tax assets recognised in earlier periods and certain one-off exceptional items,” the company said in a blog post.
Zooming Into Myntra’s FY26 Expenses
Total expenses for the year 2025-26 remained nearly flat, with a 0.6% increase to ₹5,757.7 Cr, from ₹5,726 Cr in the previous year. Here is a closer look at where the ecommerce platform spent the most:
Employee Benefit Expenses: Expenses towards salaries, wages, bonus, staff welfare, gratuity and provident fund, Myntra spent ₹776.9 Cr in the year under review, up 3.8% from ₹748.8 Cr in FY25.
Direct Expenses: Constituting 32% of the total expenses, this includes payment gateway charges and logistic charges. Direct expenses stood at ₹1,841 Cr, marking a 13.9% decline from ₹2,139.4 Cr.
Advertisement And Promotion Expenses: Spending under this head rose 10.5% to ₹2,326.5 Cr, compared to ₹2,105.3 Cr, contributing 40.4% of the overall expenditure.

items.title: KP Bans New Hiring in Health Department
items.summary:
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Health Department has suspended all recruitment activities at health institutions and offices in selected districts until further orders.
According to an official notification, District Health Officers (DHOs) and Tehsil Headquarters (THQ) hospitals have been directed to immediately halt ongoing and planned recruitments.
The restrictions cover all stages of the hiring process, including job advertisements, recruitment tests, interviews, and the preparation of merit lists.
The department has also prohibited the issuance of appointment letters, joining of selected candidates, and new postings until further notice.
The notification warns that concerned officers will be held responsible for any violation of the directives.
