items.author: ​ Our Correspondents
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday approved an indicative wheat price of Rs4,500 per maund for 2027, up Rs1,000 from last year's Rs3,500.
However, the proposed price of Rs4,500 is still Rs500 less than the price demanded by farmers.
The prime minister said the increase was meant to provide relief to growers facing higher production costs, rising petrol prices and inflationary pressure.
He said giving farmers an effective incentive to sow wheat was among the main objectives of the decision, a Prime Minister's Office news release said.
The prime minister said the decision would be an important step towards strengthening national food security, encouraging local production and bringing stability to the agriculture sector.
The new price is expected to help farmers recover their input costs and earn a reasonable profit, he said.
The prime minister acknowledged the guidance of President Asif Ali Zardari and Mian Muhammad Nawaz Sharif in the matter, as well as the consultation and cooperation of the chief ministers of Punjab and Sindh.
He expressed special thanks to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz for her cooperation and valuable suggestions during the consultative process, and appreciated her role in it.
He also thanked Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah for his cooperation.
Separately, National Food Security Minister Rana Tanveer Hussain has promised a better support price for wheat farmers this season, saying Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will coordinate with the provinces to establish a uniform rate as the government seeks to stabilise the market.
Speaking to the media on Friday after inaugurating the upgraded Central Plant Quarantine Laboratory (CPQL), the minister said farmers had received low prices for their wheat. He expressed hope that market prices would decline within a few days, adding that bringing wheat to the market was the responsibility of provincial governments.
"Ensuring food supplies for a population of 260 million is a challenge," he said. "The federal government has reserved one million metric tonnes of wheat and issued directives to preserve the stocks. Pakistan has a surplus of rice and tomatoes," he added.
Turning to the sugar sector, the minister said farmers often struggled to secure an appropriate price for sugarcane in the following season when sugar production exceeded domestic demand. He attributed some of the difficulties to inaccurate data and said the prime minister had directed the development of a mechanism to ensure 100% accuracy.
"The country currently has a surplus of sugar that could be exported to benefit farmers," he said, adding that the ex-mill price was below production cost. He told reporters that sugarcane crushing was scheduled to begin on November 15.
Tanveer also acknowledged that farmers lacked adequate information and awareness. "The government has undertaken awareness initiatives in coordination with provincial administrations," he said, adding that efforts were under way to reduce palm oil imports by developing alternatives.
Speaking about the CPQL, he said the laboratory had been upgraded at a cost of Rs400 million. The facility had previously been in disrepair, its machinery was non-functional and the grant allocated for it had been wasted, he added.
"Importers and exporters had lodged numerous complaints about testing standards, and bribery had become widespread. I cannot say that angels have been working here, but we have broken the mafia. Today, all the mafias have been eliminated," the minister said.
He said the Ministry of National Food Security had partnered with the International Centre for Chemical and Biological Sciences, operating under the University of Karachi's HEJ Research Institute of Chemistry, to upgrade the laboratory. Trained and experienced HEJ staff had been deployed at the facility, he added.
The upgraded laboratory will enhance testing capacity, strengthen export capabilities and enable commercial testing of pesticide residues, he said. The number of interceptions in the plant quarantine sector had already fallen from 376 to 23, and the new facility was expected to bring further improvement.
 
Livestock
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved the restructuring of the Livestock and Dairy Development Board and directed that the selection of its chairman and members be carried out transparently and strictly on merit.
The prime minister chairing a review meeting on reforms in the livestock sector, said the board should be made an effective and active institution by inducting capable and experienced professionals from the private sector, a Prime Minister's Office news release said.
The prime minister directed the authorities concerned to present a comprehensive action plan for the complete eradication of foot-and-mouth disease, with clear targets, measurable results and a fixed timeframe.
He announced that the federal government was establishing a plant in Islamabad for the production of modern and effective livestock vaccines, using its own resources.
The prime minister also directed that world-class consultants be engaged for the development of the livestock and dairy sector, and that the experiences of countries with expertise in the field be drawn upon. He called for partnerships with such countries to be promoted.
Noting that Pakistan possessed vast potential in the livestock sector, the prime minister stressed that it should be harnessed for exports and economic growth. He said improvements in animal health, breeding, production and the value chain would help the country fully realise its export potential, while also boosting the rural economy and creating employment opportunities.
The meeting was given a briefing on the restructuring of the board, animal disease surveillance, vaccination, animal identification and traceability, and measures to increase exports of meat and dairy products.
Alvarez & Marsal
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reiterated Pakistan's willingness to open its economy to promising international markets and consult globally recognised economic experts to advance the country's economic growth and prosperity.
The prime minister expressed these views during a meeting with Peter Briggs, Managing Director of North American Operations at international consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal (A&M).
Shehbaz said that after achieving economic and fiscal stability, the government was taking effective measures to introduce deep-rooted structural reforms and promote export-led growth and a productive economy.
He highlighted the government's focus on improving the performance and efficiency of the domestic manufacturing sector while taking measures to attract foreign direct investment (FDI).
The prime minister said the government was pursuing a strategy to assess the economic viability of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and subsequently move towards privatisation to support the national economy and promote growth.
Emphasising the importance of expertise and professional capacity, Shehbaz Sharif said Pakistan recognised the need for qualified professionals and expert teams to strengthen its economic growth engine.
He added that Pakistan was ready to establish productive partnerships with international consulting firms to support economic growth while ensuring tangible results and accountability.
Briggs thanked the prime minister for the meeting and appreciated the government's commitment to attracting foreign investment and engaging with international economic experts.
He also expressed A&M's eagerness to cooperate with Pakistan to promote a progressive business environment and a productive economy.

The meeting brought together Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty.
In a joint statement issued after the talks, the four countries underlined the "urgent need" to address the US-Israel conflict with Iran only through dialogue and diplomacy and to prevent attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, including vessels.
Significantly for Islamabad, the ministers "expressed support for the Islamabad MoU and welcomed continued diplomatic efforts to prevent further escalation," while reaffirming their commitment to a lasting negotiated settlement.
The reference was seen as recognition of Pakistan's continuing diplomatic role in efforts to prevent the resumption of the Iran conflict. Dar briefed his counterparts on Islamabad's mediation efforts during the subsequent expanded meeting with European foreign ministers.
The Istanbul gathering assumed greater significance because the R4 also sat with the major European powers for the first time. France, Germany and the United Kingdom - traditionally known as the E3 - were joined by Italy, effectively turning Friday's gathering into an eight-country consultation between four regional and four European states.
The discussions covered Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen, Palestine and wider threats to maritime security.
The urgency surrounding the meeting was underscored by Turkish Foreign Minister Fidan, who warned after the talks that renewed military action against Iran would only deepen instability.
"Military intervention in Iran is by no means a solution. No one supports this at the moment," Fidan told reporters.
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani similarly warned ahead of the meeting that there were signs hostilities in the Gulf could resume after the US elections, arguing that preventing another war should be the immediate priority.
The R4 statement also reflected growing concern over disruption to one of the world's most important maritime arteries.
The ministers stressed the importance of freedom of navigation and called for the "swift and full resumption of safe, secure and unimpeded passage" through the Strait of Hormuz. They rejected restrictions affecting lawful navigation, warning that disruption of sea lanes threatened energy, food and fertiliser supplies as well as global supply chains.
On Yemen, the four countries adopted an equally firm position, strongly condemning Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, including strikes targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, as well as attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb.
They expressed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognised Yemeni government and urged the Houthis to halt military operations and return to the political process.
The statement is significant for Pakistan since Islamabad, Ankara and Riyadh are also partners in the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed in August. Dar and Fidan, during their bilateral meeting in Istanbul, condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia and agreed to maintain close coordination under the defence arrangement.
Palestine remained another major focus. The R4 described Israeli occupation as a fundamental source of regional instability, called for an end to violence and settlement activity and reiterated support for an independent Palestinian state based on the June 4, 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
The ministers also demanded uninterrupted humanitarian assistance and reconstruction in Gaza.
Following the ministerial consultations, the participating foreign ministers called on Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. Dar conveyed greetings from President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir.
According to the Foreign Office, the meeting with Erdogan involved "candid exchanges" on regional and global developments and emphasised continued dialogue and diplomatic engagement.
Earlier in Islamabad, Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said the R4 had emerged as a mechanism to deal with regional instability and was now being broadened through engagement with European powers.
"The discussions will cover issues affecting the entire region, including the safe passage of maritime sea lanes, the situation in Yemen, the Houthis, and the Strait of Hormuz," Khan told his weekly briefing.
He said the primary objective was to explore ways of promoting peace and stability and de-escalating the overall situation.
The spokesperson also confirmed that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had completed their ratification procedures for the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, while Türkiye was undertaking the required domestic legal process.
He stressed that the agreement was defensive in nature and consistent with the UN Charter, adding that any decision to invoke its collective-defence provisions in response to attacks would have to be taken by the three partner countries in accordance with the agreement.

items.author: Naeem Asghar
items.content:
Concerns over Pakistan's petroleum supplies amid escalating tensions in the Middle East dominated the Senate proceedings on Friday, with lawmakers demanding clarity on the government's contingency plans even as the finance minister maintained that there was no fuel shortage.
The house, met here with acting Chairman Syedal Khan Nasir in the chair, also debated the use of the carbon levy, relief in the super tax and compensation for civilians affected by operations in South Waziristan, while complaints against Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) officials were referred to the relevant standing committee.
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Senator Sherry Rehman questioned whether the country would have sufficient petroleum supplies in December and urged the government to brief parliament on its contingency and possible rationing plans.
She said renewed attacks on Iran and the escalating conflict in West Asia had heightened uncertainty over energy supplies, with implications for economic stability and ordinary citizens. "What is the government's plan for the availability of petroleum products? Will there be rationing? Members of Parliament have concerns whether petrol will be available till December," she said, insisting that the government must address these concerns.
Rehman said Pakistan relied on imports for nearly 70% of its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) requirements, while domestic production accounted for the remaining 30%. She said the country had received five LPG cargoes last year, compared with only two expected this year, and called for a clear supply plan to be presented before parliament.
However, Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kiani said there were no fuel supply problems. He told the house that more than 10 million people were benefiting from the government's targeted fuel subsidy scheme, while Rs1,676 billion had been budgeted under the petroleum levy for the current fiscal year.
He said the government was providing targeted relief to motorcyclists, rickshaw and loader operators, and users of small cars to mitigate the impact of regional tensions on petroleum prices.
Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas also warned that conflict threatening key energy routes could aggravate Pakistan's energy difficulties. Linking the external crisis to domestic shortages, he said Punjab was already facing a flour shortage while the country was experiencing an LPG shortage. He also called on Pakistan to mediate between Yemen's Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia.
Rehman also questioned the utilisation of the carbon levy imposed on petroleum products, alleging that the proceeds were being absorbed into general federal revenues rather than spent on environmental protection and climate resilience projects.
Citing a meeting of the Senate Standing Committee on Climate Change, which she chairs, she said the finance ministry had acknowledged that the levy was not being spent on environmental projects. She argued that the money was transferred to the Federal Consolidated Fund without being earmarked for climate action.
Referring to water shortages in Balochistan and the absence of resilience schools in Sindh, Rehman questioned how the levy's proceeds were being distributed among the provinces. She said the levy should not continue in its existing form unless it was restructured to ensure that the money was ring-fenced for climate mitigation and resilience measures.
Separately, Minister of State Kiani informed the Senate that the super tax had been abolished for businesses with annual incomes ranging from Rs150 million to Rs500 million, while the rate for those earning Rs500 million or more had been reduced from 10% to 8%.
The house also took up a calling-attention notice regarding compensation for civilians affected by security operations in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas in 2008 and 2009.
Responding to the notice, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said Rs117 billion had been distributed among affectees in South Waziristan. The release of another Rs65 billion in outstanding payments was awaiting completion of an audit and proceedings before the relevant committee, he added.
During the Question Hour, lawmakers expressed dissatisfaction with the government's response to complaints against FBR and Pakistan Customs personnel. The matter was referred to the relevant standing committee for further consideration.
The proceedings ended after Senator Falak Naz Chitrali pointed out a lack of quorum. A headcount confirmed that the required number of members was not present, prompting the chair to adjourn the session until 4pm on Monday.

items.title: Turkey says Libya will unify soon
items.summary:
Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Friday that the time had come to reunify Libya's rival eastern and western administrations, indicating that the militaries of both sides could come under a unified command and expressing hope that an announcement on the issue would be made in the near future.
Turkey backed the UN-recognised government in Tripoli, but ties with authorities in eastern Libya have warmed significantly in recent years. On Tuesday, Libya's eastern-based parliament approved a maritime demarcation deal with Turkey.
"We have now reached a stage where the conditions are ripe to permanently secure the reunification of the east and the west," Fidan told journalists. "Both sides have military structures. These structures need to be brought together under a national army," he added.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Electricity consumers could end up paying more for power generation as Independent Power Producers (IPPs) continue procuring imported coal under existing contracts despite substantially better discounts secured through fresh competitive bidding.
The situation has brought the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) into focus, with concerns that prolonged extensions of existing coal supply agreements could unnecessarily increase fuel procurement costs and ultimately burden electricity consumers.
According to publicly available procurement details, an IPP initially purchased imported coal at no discount against the international API-4 coal price index. Subsequent interim supply arrangements with two suppliers offered a discount of $1.08 per metric ton. Following NEPRA’s directions to conduct fresh competitive bidding, the financial bidding process concluded with an improved discount of $2.10 per metric ton, reflecting an additional discount of $1.02 per ton over the interim arrangements. However, despite the availability of more competitive offers, the IPP continues to procure coal under its previous arrangements while the onboarding of suppliers through the new bidding process remains pending.
The IPP has also sought additional time from NEPRA for the continuation of its existing coal supply contracts, raising questions over how long consumers should continue bearing the cost of procurement at less competitive rates.
The difference of $1.02 per metric ton represents potential savings that could translate into lower fuel costs, provided other contractual and supply conditions are comparable. Given the volume of coal consumed by large power plants, even relatively small differences in per-ton procurement costs can have significant financial implications.
The matter now requires closer regulatory scrutiny to ensure that contract extensions do not become a means of prolonging procurement at higher costs when more competitive alternatives are available.
While temporary extensions may be necessary to maintain uninterrupted coal supplies, the regulator must ensure that any such arrangements are restricted to the minimum period genuinely required for completing the transition to new suppliers.
At a time when electricity affordability remains a major concern for households and businesses, the issue goes beyond contractual formalities. It raises a fundamental question of regulatory oversight and consumer protection.

Pakistan has deferred decisions on several genetically modified (GM) crop applications, including soybean imports, corn biosafety licences and cotton-related cases, after the National Biosafety Committee sought clearer recommendations from its technical panel.
The decision was taken during the 38th meeting of the National Biosafety Committee (NBC) at the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination.
The committee found that recommendations submitted by the 45th meeting of the Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) did not provide clear enough conclusions for final decisions.
It sent the pending cases back to the TAC for further review and directed it to submit clear recommendations.
The agenda included approvals for soybean meal imports for food, feed and processing, renewal of biosafety licences for genetically modified corn, and several cotton-related applications.
The committee also discussed the hold on the commercialization of genetically modified corn and other biotech food crops.
A representative of the Ministry of National Food Security and Research said the government had suspended commercialization activities for biotech food crops in 2019 until a comprehensive policy framework was developed.
The representative said the policy gap had since been addressed through the approval and notification of the National Agricultural Biotechnology Policy 2025, which establishes a regulatory framework for assessing and commercializing agricultural biotechnology products.
Authorities have been informed to proceed under the approved policy, according to the briefing.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) found that artificial intelligence agents left alone on a virtual island began creating their own challenges and learning new skills without being given specific tasks.
The researchers placed 13 AI agents, called Eko, in a simulated desert island environment for 30 hours. Each agent was powered by Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.7 model and could explore the environment independently.
According to the research paper published on arXiv, the agents began experimenting with objects, solving problems, and inventing activities that resembled human play.
More importantly, the agents generally performed better in later challenges than identical AI agents that had not previously explored the island.
AI Agents Invent Their Own Challenges
During the experiment, the researchers allowed the agents to explore the island without assigning specific objectives.
One agent attempted to climb the island’s tallest rock spire but initially failed. It later found another route, using a nearby summit and stacked blocks to reach the top.
Another agent experimented with throwing a golden ring but accidentally launched it into the ocean.
After losing the ring, it decided to build a heart-shaped memorial using stones.
When the environment reset and the ring returned, the agent began using it for different activities, including a basketball hoop and a target.
It eventually discovered that falling off a cliff and respawning could allow it to pass through the ring and appear to wear it.
AI Learns Unexpected Skills
Six of the 13 agents independently discovered that they could throw blocks farther by releasing them in mid-air while jumping.
The researchers had not intentionally designed this technique into the environment, suggesting that the agents could discover new ways to interact with their surroundings through experimentation.
After 30 hours of exploration, the agents were given specific tasks, including placing as many objects as possible on the island’s tallest spire.
The agents with previous experience generally outperformed identical agents that had not explored the island. Researchers also found that the agents’ stored memories helped them apply previously learned techniques.
Could AI Learn Through Play?
The researchers believe that allowing AI agents to explore environments without predefined objectives could offer a new approach to developing artificial intelligence.
Currently, developers typically train AI systems using specific tasks, rewards, and performance targets.
The experiment suggests that independent exploration could help agents develop practical skills that may eventually prove useful in robotics and other applications.
However, the findings do not establish that AI agents experience curiosity or play in the same way humans do.
The agents were also given instructions describing them as naturally curious, which may have influenced their behavior.
Eunice Yiu, a cognitive scientist at the University of California, Berkeley, said more research is needed to determine whether the agents were genuinely playing or simply producing behavior that resembled play.
The study was published on arXiv on October 5, 2026, and has not yet undergone peer review.
The researchers concluded that while some AI capabilities may be learned through assigned tasks, others could benefit from extended periods of independent exploration.

Drawing on Mashreq’s international banking expertise, the proposition aims to simplify financial management for Pakistani businesses while supporting greater participation in the formal digital economy.
Fernando Morillo, Group Head of Retail Banking, Mashreq, added: “Across our international markets, we have seen how digital-first banking models can transform the way businesses operate, improving efficiency, transparency and access to financial services. NEO BIZ builds on this global experience, combining strong commercial capabilities with a scalable platform designed to meet the needs of SMEs. Pakistan represents a high-potential market and NEO BIZ is an important step in extending our global business banking proposition into a rapidly evolving digital economy.”
Designed as a comprehensive solution, NEO BIZ brings together digital business banking, payments, collections and an expanding range of value-added services within an integrated ecosystem. The proposition enables eligible businesses to open and manage accounts digitally, reducing reliance on branch visits and simplifying routine financial transactions. Its broader roadmap encompasses business debit and virtual cards, payroll solutions, invoice-based payments, transaction analytics and bookkeeping capabilities, supporting businesses as their operational and financial needs evolve.
Commenting on the local opportunity, Muhammad Hamayun Sajjad, CEO, Mashreq Bank Pakistan, said: “Pakistan’s SME sector is both dynamic and under-served, with significant gaps in access, awareness and digital capability. With NEO BIZ, we are introducing a platform that is built specifically for the realities of this market, one that simplifies banking, reduces dependency on physical channels and supports businesses as they grow. This launch is a natural extension of our commitment to Pakistan and aligns with our broader vision of enabling financial inclusion and supporting the country’s economic transformation through digital innovation.”
Beyond core banking, NEO BIZ is designed to progressively evolve into a connected business ecosystem through Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) capabilities and strategic partnerships, with plans to integrate bookkeeping, supply chain solutions, tax facilitation, analytics, invoicing and cash flow-based financing. Through a phased approach, Mashreq aims to simplify operational complexities, enhance business efficiency and deliver solutions that respond to the evolving needs of entrepreneurs at different stages of growth.
Providing further detail on the proposition, Syed Jaffar Abbas Shirazi, Head of NEO BIZ, Mashreq Bank Pakistan, said: “NEO BIZ has been designed with a clear understanding of the challenges SMEs face today, from fragmented financial tools and limited product visibility to barriers in accessing financing. Our approach is to bring everything into a single, integrated platform that allows businesses to manage their financial operations seamlessly. From instant account opening and payments to advanced tools such as analytics, invoicing and bookkeeping, NEO BIZ is built to move beyond traditional banking and become a true business enabler.”
NEO BIZ will be distributed through a combination of digital channels, strategic partnerships and phygital touchpoints, ensuring accessibility across a diverse SME base and enabling Mashreq to scale its reach across Pakistan’s business ecosystem.
With this launch, Mashreq aims to accelerate the adoption of digital financial services among SMEs, strengthen digital payment acceptance, support entrepreneurs and self-employed professionals, and contribute to Pakistan’s transition toward a more inclusive, transparent and digitally connected economy.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
Pakistan has reassessed the cost of the under-construction Mohmand Dam at a staggering Rs666 billion, an increase of 115% in the past eight years, which authorities largely attributed to rupee devaluation after 2018.
Mohmand is one of the three largest reservoirs Islamabad is building to deal with Indian water aggression.
The revised project cost was presented before the Central Development Working Party (CDWP) meeting this week, which did not take up the matter for a decision due to paucity of time, according to federal government officials. The CDWP is the first stage for approval of mega projects, which are then sent for final endorsement of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council.
The Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda), the agency responsible for execution of the mega scheme, has assessed the cost at Rs666 billion, according to officials who have seen the documents.
In 2018, the then government had approved the project at a cost of Rs310 billion with a deadline to finish work by September 2025. Since then, the cost has been estimated to escalate by Rs356 billion or 115%, according to the authorities.
The project was planned for completion by 2025, but due to various reasons, mainly dollar exchange parity, cost escalation, design changes that translated into a price hike, the 2022 floods and security issues added to the delay, according to an explanation given by the project management to the Planning Commission during the cost review assessment.
A joint venture of China Gezhouba Group Company Limited (CGGC) and Pakistan's Descon Engineering Limited is constructing the dam.
Planning Commission officials said Wapda had informed that 51% of the overall cost increase was due to dollar parity. They said a detailed discussion was held regarding the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations on the project cost. It was explained that the project contains both local and foreign currency components and that fluctuations in the dollar exchange rate have resulted in a significant increase in the rupee equivalent of the foreign component.
The rupee devaluation impacts everything from a household kitchen to mega projects due to the country's heavy dependence on foreign resources and imports. The rupee-dollar parity has again come under the spotlight after the World Bank said this week that Pakistan's currency was not freely responding to market developments.
It has assessed the difference between the market price and the daily price as of June this year at 10%, slightly higher than the 8% difference being worked out by the central bank under its Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER).
The Planning Commission had asked Wapda to provide details of dollar-denominated contractual payments and the extent to which exchange-rate variation could be passed on to the project cost.
It was observed that the foreign component of a contract cannot simply be converted at the latest exchange rate without establishing the contractual basis and the actual payment obligations. It was pointed out that, for contracts containing foreign currency payments, the actual contractual arrangements and the applicable exchange-rate provisions need to be examined.
According to project documents, as of last month, about 57% physical work had been completed, with Rs275 billion spent on the project.
The project was approved by ECNEC in its meeting held in April 2018 at a cost of Rs310 billion, with rupee cover of Rs71.5 billion.
Out of the total proposed upward revision, the dam cost will be Rs267 billion, an increase of Rs153 billion or 134% over the old estimates. Likewise, the power generation cost went up to Rs399 billion, a surge of Rs204 billion or 105%.
On completion, the project will increase Pakistan's overall water storage capacity by 1.29 million acres and add 2.9 billion units of generation to the national grid. It will also provide 300 million gallons of drinking water annually to Peshawar.
The Mohmand Dam Hydropower Project is of strategic national importance to Pakistan as it directly addresses the country's chronic water storage deficit, energy insecurity and vulnerability to climate-induced floods.
The project faced huge setbacks in the 2022 floods, when heavy flooding in the Swat river damaged diversion tunnels. As a result, work was halted for a significant period, according to the project management's explanation to the Planning Commission.
But the Planning Commission was of the view that the project was a classic example of delays and other issues among various flagship projects being implemented under Wapda.
The Planning Commission is of the view that the project should be recommended for third-party validation for financial and physical resource utilisation, scope of works, variation orders, escalation cost, gestation period, financial closure and other matters.
It has also recommended that the revised financial plan needed updating, including the federal government's share through the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) for dam funding, any provincial share and loans from foreign lenders.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Adviser to Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan has said that the government is undertaking reforms to simplify business environment, remove unnecessary regulatory hurdles and promote domestic and foreign investment in Pakistan.
Addressing a press conference alongside Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister and members of his cabinet, the adviser said that complexity of the regulatory framework and difficulties in doing business had been among the major factors discouraging foreign investment in Pakistan.
"Over the past 78 years, laws and regulations have been introduced to meet different needs. However, with the passage of time, unnecessary complexities and overlapping requirements have accumulated, making it tough for businesses to run efficiently," Khan said.
He explained that the government was conducting a comprehensive review of regulators, laws and regulations affecting businesses across the country. The reform process has made substantial progress, with approximately 60-70% of the overall work completed. Reform proposals submitted by various institutions recommend eliminating, on average, 70-75% of unnecessary or duplicating regulations.
The adviser said review meetings were being held every two weeks to ensure progress and implementation of several proposed reforms had already begun, while further measures were being developed to improve the ease of doing business and strengthen investor confidence.
Highlighting the proposed Asaan Karobar Act, Khan said the government was working to establish a business environment aligned with international best practices. The initiative aims to simplify regulatory procedures, reduce compliance costs and create a more predictable and investor-friendly framework for businesses.
He stated that 170 amendments to the Companies Act, 2017 had been approved by the federal cabinet and the relevant bill was forwarded to parliament. The proposed amendments will facilitate company registrations and business operations while modernising Pakistan's corporate regulatory framework.
The PM aide mentioned that international regulatory systems, particularly those of Delaware in the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, had been studied as benchmarks for the proposed reforms. The government had also engaged a senior international consultant with experience in regulatory reforms across 135 countries to support the process.
Khan said that regulatory reviews were underway in several sectors, including dairy, maritime, beverages, oil refineries, pharmaceuticals and restaurants.

items.author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
items.content:
Small-scale manufacturers are increasingly squeezed by rising raw material, scrap, transport and energy costs, leaving them with slimmer profits per unit. For small businesses, expanding production can mean higher operating expenses and greater financial risk.
Some owners may therefore prefer to keep operations small to maintain control over costs, manage cash flow and protect their limited margins. For businesses with narrow profit margins, these requirements can make expansion financially difficult, encouraging owners to remain small, scale back operations or return to informal status.
Across the industrial areas of Sher Shah, SITE, Korangi, Landhi, Federal B Area and SITE Super Highway, small manufacturers producing essential packaging and high-demand domestic plastic goods are making a deliberate choice to remain small.
Despite massive nationwide consumer demand for affordable daily-use items, ranging from kitchenware such as bowls, jugs and serving plates to essential retail packaging, micro-manufacturers report that escalating raw material scrap costs, local trucking charges and fixed space overheads have squeezed profit margins to razor-thin levels.
For many, expanding operations or adding workforce capacity brings disproportionate operational friction, prompting owners to maintain lean, low-profile workshop operations.
Corrugated box manufacturing
The packaging industry, comprising producers of corrugated boxes that supply master packaging for local wholesale trade, food delivery and retail goods, is feeling the pinch of fluctuating paper scrap prices and rising local transport rates. This ecosystem relies on a vast network of big, small and micro-manufacturers, spanning suppliers of raw paper rolls and fluting sheets to small box-making units across the city.
"Our biggest challenge is the rising cost of doing business," says Sadaqat Shah, a corrugated box unit operator in the Shershah Industrial Area. "When production cost rises, our profit on a standard master carton shrinks to just a few rupees. Moving raw paper bales from warehouses to our unit adds heavy load and transport cost. If we try to scale up or install larger machinery, our electricity and rental overheads double immediately. We deliberately keep our output modest with four workers to stay steady rather than taking on unsustainable debt."
Injection moulding
A similar dynamic is playing out across the heavy recycling and plastic processing units in the SITE industrial area as well as Korangi. Here, small workshops melt down reprocessed plastic scrap and granules to manufacture essential kitchenware and storage items, products with a huge and resilient consumer base across low- and middle-income households throughout Pakistan.
By feeding discarded plastic back into the production loop, these recycling facilities drive a vital localised circular economy that reduces landfill waste while supplying low-cost daily necessities to millions of households.
"The consumer market for basic plastic items such as plates, bowls, jugs and storage containers is huge," explains Mohammad Nadeem, a small-scale plastic moulding and recycling operator. "Every household buys them because they are affordable. But even with steady sales, electricity tariffs and machine maintenance hit small moulding units very hard. We rely on recycled granules to keep costs down, but when utility rates spike, our profit per piece drops to pennies. Keeping our operation small lets us manage daily production without taking on heavy overheads."
Polythene bags
A parallel network of micro-manufacturers produces polypropylene bags for bulk grain, flour and industrial packaging, struggling under the same volatile material costs and high power tariffs that squeeze local moulders.
Producers of polythene retail packaging also operate under tight constraints, as micro-producers find it difficult to pass cost increases down to wholesale traders in Jodia Bazaar and local neighbourhood retail markets.
"The demand for ultra-thin shoppers for retail is huge, but we operate on very thin margins," notes Saqib Ali. "When polymer prices jump, we cannot easily raise our wholesale rates for small shopkeepers overnight. Operating a compact unit allows us to manage inventory tightly and avoid long credit lines in the market."

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Bilateral trade between Pakistan and Bangladesh stands at around $1 billion against a potential worth several billion dollars, Bangladesh High Commissioner Md Iqbal Hussain Khan said, calling for stronger cooperation, improved connectivity, the removal of trade barriers and closer engagement between the business communities to unlock it.
Speaking at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry, he identified agriculture, textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering, food processing, chemicals, minerals, education, healthcare and tourism as promising areas of collaboration, according to a statement on Friday. Honorary Consul of Bangladesh Qazi Humayun Fareed also attended.
He said Bangladeshi imports could expand in maize, rice and basmati rice, textile raw materials, chemicals, minerals and manufactured goods, along with sugar, wheat, cereals and spices. Bangladeshi pineapples had begun reaching Pakistan after clearances, and seasonal fruits, agricultural products and jaggery could further expand trade.
He called for easier business visas, improved e-visa procedures and stronger direct air connectivity, noting Pakistan could serve as a gateway to Central Asia while Bangladesh offered access to Southeast Asia. More than 100 Bangladeshi students study at private universities in Pakistan, and he identified opportunities in scholarships, medical tourism and tourism.
LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar proposed a dedicated Bangladesh trade cell under the senior vice president to coordinate bilateral business activities, suggesting the identification of five priority export sectors, a link with a leading chamber in Dhaka or Chittagong and two to three virtual business-to-business meetings, followed by sector-specific meetings, trade delegations and reciprocal business visits.
He invited Bangladeshi entrepreneurs to explore partnerships in Lahore and said both countries must move beyond discussions and adopt a result-oriented strategy with measurable results.
Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani called for reversing the downward trend in bilateral trade and raising it to at least $2 billion, citing pharmaceuticals, textiles, textile machinery, rice, cement, agriculture, food processing, information technology, engineering, light manufacturing and services.
He urged joint ventures and investment partnerships alongside improvements in shipping, customs procedures, documentation and the exchange of market intelligence.

items.content:
Huawei has opened pre-orders for the Pura 90 Plus in China and released the smartphone’s first official teaser ahead of its launch next week.
The device joins the Pura 90 lineup, which debuted in April 2026 with the Pura 90, Pura 90 Pro, and Pura 90 Pro Max.
Pre-orders opened at 10:08 AM China time through Huawei’s VMall online store, Experience Stores, and authorized retailers. Early buyers will also receive exclusive benefits.
Huawei plans to officially launch the phone next week, with deliveries expected to begin before November 8.
Design and Display
The official teaser shows the Pura 90 Plus in Sunset Purple, a gradient finish combining purple and orange. The same color option is available on the Pura 90 Pro Max.
The phone retains the series’ inverted triangular camera module in the upper-right corner of the rear panel.
However, unlike the flat-edged Pura 90, Pura 90 Pro, and Pura 90 Pro Max, the Plus model features a curved frame and rounded rear panel, similar to the Pura 80 Pro.
According to leaks, the device will feature a 6.8-inch display with 1.5K resolution.
Performance and Hardware
The Huawei Pura 90 Plus, reportedly codenamed Lucia, is expected to feature the Kirin 9020 chipset.
The processor reportedly includes eight CPU cores running at frequencies of 2.5GHz, 2.15GHz, and 1.6GHz, alongside a Maleoon 920 GPU.
However, Huawei has not officially confirmed the chipset or other hardware specifications.
Camera Setup
According to leaks, the Pura 90 Plus could feature a 50MP main camera with a 1-inch RYYB sensor and a physical variable aperture.
The RYYB sensor uses yellow pixels instead of some green pixels to capture more light, while the variable aperture allows users to control light intake and depth of field.
The rumored camera setup includes:

Huawei is also reportedly preparing an improved version of its XMAGE image-processing technology.
Price and Availability
Huawei has not announced the Pura 90 Plus’s official price.
The device is expected to sit between the standard Pura 90 and Pura 90 Pro in the lineup. The standard Pura 90 starts at approximately $704, while the Pura 90 Pro starts at around $823.
Huawei will reveal the phone’s complete specifications, pricing, and availability at its launch event next week.
For now, its rumored hardware specifications remain unconfirmed.

items.title: Mohsin Naqvi Issues Another Shocking Warning
items.summary:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has warned Pakistanis against online scammers who impersonate family members and pretend to be sick to trick people into transferring money.
Speaking alongside NCCIA Additional Director Atif Ameer, the minister shared info about astonishing cases in which fraudsters pose as nephews or relatives and ask for money.
Some scammers also claim to be ill to make their requests appear genuine.
Minister said numerous cases of this kind had been reported and urged cybercrime police to launch public awareness campaigns to help people identify and avoid such scams.
He stressed the need to educate the public about these basic fraud tactics, which can be prevented if people verify the identity of anyone requesting money online.
People should confirm the identity of the person making the request, particularly when the caller’s voice is unfamiliar, before transferring any money, he added.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bukhari said on Friday that the provincial government would pursue the case involving the alleged gang rape of an Azerbaijani woman despite a video statement circulating on social media in which the victim said she had forgiven the suspect and did not want to pursue the case.
The minister’s statement came after a video of the victim, Diana, who was allegedly raped in Lahore earlier this year, circulated on social media in which she said her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) had already been recorded before a judicial magistrate.
A video of the victim, apparently recorded on Oct 9, surfaced in which she could be seen saying that a suspect had neither assaulted her nor taken her mobile phone and belongings.
“I gave my earlier statement under pressure, and I do not want to pursue this case,” she said, requesting that the case be closed.
Later, in another video, Diana reiterated her statement, giving a clean chit to the suspect. She said she wanted to appear before the court to record her statement but was told that her life was in danger.
She further claimed that she had been forcibly sent out of Pakistan and was not allowed to express her view. She also said she wanted to forgive the other suspects and did not want to pursue the matter any further.
Speaking to a private television programme, Aaj Shahzaib Khanzada Kay Sath, Bukhari said Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz was particularly concerned about rape cases and would not allow anyone to relax until all the suspects were arrested and due process was followed.
Read: Azeri woman tells court she was 'threatened, sexually assaulted and pushed out of car'
Asked whether the Punjab government would pursue the case since the state could also pursue rape cases, she replied in the affirmative, saying the chief minister had categorically asked her to convey that she believed the state should be the complainant in cases involving crimes against women and children.
“The chief minister, as chief executive, stands with every victim and with the poor and vulnerable. Until and unless these powerful people are made an example of, such crimes cannot be eliminated,” she said.
Bukhari said the chief minister was prepared to approach the chief justice of Pakistan and the chief justice of the Lahore High Court with the information available to her.
“Whether it is a speedy trial, improving the laws or whatever is needed, she is ready to work on that,” she said, adding that CM Maryam would not allow “this hooliganism and culture of bullying” against women, children or vulnerable sections of society in Punjab.
The minister said the woman, the victim in the case, had, for one reason or another, changed her position, and the possibility of money being involved had also arisen.
However, she said the state would pursue the case because a co-suspect had already recorded a statement saying all the suspects were involved with him.
“Even if they retract this statement, it is not possible for them to get away,” she said, adding that the government would not allow anyone to take the law into their own hands.
Maryam alleges bribe offer
Earlier today, CM Maryam alleged that the family of a suspect in the case had offered Rs15 million to Rs20m to the victim to withdraw her allegations, while the judge who granted bail to the suspect had also allegedly been bribed.
“It was revealed that the accused’s wealthy family allegedly offered Rs15m to Rs20m to the victim in exchange for withdrawing her allegations, despite her statement already having been recorded under Section 164,” Maryam said in a post on X.
In a recent rape case, it was revealed that the accused’s wealthy family allegedly offered 1.5–2 crore to the victim in exchange for withdrawing her allegations, despite her statement already having been recorded under Section 164. It was further alleged that the judge who…
— Maryam Nawaz Sharif (@MaryamNSharif) October 23, 2026
She further alleged that the judge who granted bail to the accused had also been bribed.
“If these allegations are true, they raise deeply disturbing questions about the integrity of the justice system and the vulnerability of rape survivors to financial pressure and the misuse of power,” she said.
Maryam said she would continue to keep a close eye on such cases to ensure that “no rapist or perpetrator escapes justice simply because he has money, influence, or connections”.
“Justice must never be for sale, and no one should be above the law,” she said.
Police warn against influencing probe
As the statements surfaced, Lahore police warned against attempts to influence the investigation into the alleged gang rape through videos circulating on social media, saying the woman’s statement under Section 164 of the CrPC had already been recorded before a judicial magistrate.
Lahore Deputy Inspector General (Investigation) Syed Zeeshan Raza said the woman had named three suspects in her judicial statement and that two arrested suspects had also acknowledged the alleged involvement of the third suspect.
He said the video statement appeared to be an attempt to influence the investigation, adding that the third suspect would be included in the investigation and the case would be completed on merit.
Also Read: Azeri woman in alleged Lahore gang-rape case returns home under police escort
The case was registered at Defence C Police Station in September after the woman alleged that three men had sexually assaulted her at an apartment in a private housing society near Raiwind during the night between Sept 25 and 26.
According to the first information report, the woman had arrived in Lahore on a business trip and was allegedly taken to a cafe by two women, where three men joined them. She alleged that she was subsequently taken to an apartment, given an intoxicating drink and sexually assaulted.
The suspects allegedly left her near the airport and took her mobile phones and other belongings.
On Sept 28, the woman recorded her statement before a judicial magistrate at the Cantonment Courts. Police subsequently identified the suspects and pursued the investigation, with several people arrested in connection with the case.
The latest developments have also raised questions about the primary suspect’s legal status. A sessions court had extended his interim pre-arrest bail until Oct 27, but police subsequently arrested him outside the court premises.
His counsel reportedly challenged the arrest, maintaining that it had taken place despite the extension of bail.
The conflicting accounts are likely to remain central to the investigation.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
The festive season, usually a time to splurge, is telling a different story this year. A smaller number of card transactions and weaker smartphone sales are hinting at consumers tightening their purse strings amid mounting pressure on household budgets.
Early data from Redseer estimated that India’s online festive sales clocked $7-8 Bn in gross merchandise value (GMV) during the first leg, from October 8 to 18. Nearly 100 Mn shoppers placed more than 350 Mn orders, with consumption running at around three times the everyday rate.
However, the data also pointed to a more cautious spending environment. According to Datum Intelligence, a market intelligence and consumer data analytics company, the online festive sales amounted to ₹29,800-₹30,900 Cr this year, down 7-10% from ₹33,200 Cr during the corresponding four-day period last year. Card spending, too, declined 12-15% YoY.
The broader consumer picture was also subdued. LocalCircles’ ‘Mood for the Consumer 2026’ survey estimated that urban households would spend ₹1.97 Lakh Cr on festive discretionary purchases this year, down 6% from ₹2.10 Lakh Cr in 2025. The survey received more than 67,000 responses from urban consumers across 307 districts.
The trends pointed to a central challenge for retailers: consumers continued to browse and buy, but rising expenses, uncertainty over earnings and jobs, and less compelling discounts made them more cautious about committing to expensive purchases.
Shoppers Tune In But Spending Remains Muted
Flipkart’s ‘Big Billion Days’ sale, which opened on October 8 and closed on October 19, recorded 6.3 Mn concurrent users in a minute during its opening hour.
Listed Meesho’s ‘Mega Blockbuster Sale’, which went live on October 9 and wrapped up on October 18, also reported a 75% YoY rise in day-one orders and 60% growth in transacting customers.
Over at Amazon, the ecommerce major said that its nearly two-week long ‘Great Indian Festival’ sale (stretching between October 8 and October 20) saw the number of products ordered during the first twenty four hours more than double YoY.
Redseer’s assessment also highlighted the expanding reach of online festive shopping beyond major cities. Tier II and smaller towns accounted for around two-thirds of shoppers during the first leg, while the number of first-time shoppers from these regions doubled in 2026.
Gen Z made up more than 35-40% of festive shoppers, with demand across gaming devices, creator cameras,wearables, sports footwear, grooming and beauty.
Around 60% of Flipkart’s festive demand came from non-metro customers, while more than 72% of Amazon’s visits came from outside the top nine metros. Meesho also reported strong growth in orders through its Meesho Mall offering.
However, traffic, visitors and orders measured different aspects of shopping activity. They did not, by themselves, establish how much consumers spent or whether the average purchase value increased.
Datum’s card payment data offered another view. On October 9, the first day Amazon and Flipkart opened their sales to all shoppers, card transactions stood at 83.5 Lakh against 82 Lakh on the corresponding day last year. Yet, the value of those payments fell 18% to ₹6,594 Cr from ₹8,067 Cr.
The figures point to lower spending despite a similar number of card transactions. Meesho’s order growth, much of which came through cash on delivery, also illustrated why order counts alone could not establish the value of sales.
The year-on-year comparison, however, comes with an important caveat. The major online sales in 2025 coincided with the September 22 GST rate cuts, which reduced prices on several consumer products. The opening of this year’s sales did not have a comparable tax-led trigger.
Fashion And Select Categories Find Buyers
Category-level disclosures showed that consumers spent on fashion and certain premium products, even as electronics faced pressure.
A Bank of America research note (dated October 20) found that Myntra’s daily active users rose around 40% during the first six days of its ‘Big Fashion Festival’, which ran between October 8 and October 25, compared with its September average.
Myntra’s monthly active users stood at around 93 Mn (up 8% YoY), while Nykaa Fashion’s monthly active users grew 24% to around 17 Mn.
Flipkart also reported a 42% YoY rise in beauty sales during the first hour of its sale, while its lifestyle category grew 12.5%, according to the company’s disclosures. Meesho also reported demand for festive décor and other lower-priced products.
Redseer’s category-level estimates showed that large and small appliances recorded more than 20 times their average daily GMV during the festive period. Electronics ran over seven times the everyday level, while mobiles exceeded five times. These multiple compared festive daily GMV with the January – August 2026 daily average, rather than with the previous year.
Amazon’s disclosures show that some premium categories performed well. Televisions measuring 55 inches and above accounted for 65% of its TV sales, while premium Android smartphones’ sales rose 70% YoY. The company also reported that high-end home theatre sold at 100X its regular day levels, while front-load washing machines with capacities of 9 kg and above sold at 80X.
Fashion and beauty also recorded strong festive demand. Redseer estimated that fashion grew 20-25% and accounted for nearly a fifth of festive GMV, making it the second largest category.
However, these numbers reflected performance in specific categories and do not establish a broad recovery in big ticket demand.
LocalCircles’ survey provided another indication of household priorities. Among respondents who planned festive discretionary spending, 72% intended to buy clothing, footwear or accessories. Home appliances and furniture and travel and holidays were each cited by 45%. Only 22% planned to buy mobile phones, consumer electronics or gadgets.
The findings suggested that expensive electronics were not a priority for most households planning festive purchases.
Household Budget Under Pressure
LocalCircles estimated that urban households would spend around ₹20,000 on festive discretionary purchases in 2026. While 57% of respondents said they intended to spend, 31% planned no discretionary festive purchases.
The survey’s findings on how households planned to fund their purchases were equally telling. Around 83% of households intending to spend expected to use savings to some extent. About 34% expected savings to cover at least a quarter of their festive expenditure, including 16% who said they would fund the entire amount from savings.
This came as retail inflation stood at 5.54% in September and food inflation at 7.74%, according to figures cited by LocalCircles. Higher everyday expenses left households with less room for purchases.
LocalCircles founder Sachin Taparia said, “Household earnings are not rising, and inflation continues to rise.” He also pointed to concerns over AI and its potential effect on white-collar jobs, along with a lack of attractive deals on online commerce platforms.
Discounts may also have done less to persuade shoppers to buy. The Economic Times reported that festive discounts were 35-40% lower than last year. The report also cited price increases of 30-40% for premium electronics in recent months.
Smartphone Sales Exposed The Limits of Online Traffic
Smartphones provided one of the clearest indications of the pressure on high-value purchases. Counterpoint Research’s early assessment found that smartphone sales fell 16% YoY during the first three days of Amazon’s and Flipkart’s festive sales, despite strong traffic on both platforms.
The research firm had initially forecast a 12% decline in festive smartphone volumes. Its early assessment suggested that the fall could be steeper, although the figures available in the supporting documents did not establish the final full-season outcome.
Counterpoint’s report identified higher device prices and fewer direct discounts as factors weighing on demand. Brands relied more on no-cost EMIs, bank cashback and exchange offers to make upgrades affordable without cutting listed prices sharply.
Premium Samsung models, including the Galaxy S25 Ultra and the S25 FE, found buyers, but their performance did not prevent the overall decline in smartphone sales during the opening days. Entry-level devices faced greater pressure because even discounted models were generally more expensive than a year ago.
“We had projected a 12% decline in smartphone sales, but based on the first wave of festive sales, we would not be surprised if the decline deepens to around 16%. Platforms have seen strong traffic, but conversions have been weak. Premium smartphones, however, continue to sell well, which could support revenue despite pressure on volumes,” Tarun Pathak, Research Director at Counterpoint Research.
Counterpoint also noted that the opening days fell during Pitru Pakha, when some consumers in North India traditionally defer purchases. Navratri began on October 11, after the initial sales period, leaving the full festive effect on offline demand to pay out later.
With the online sales campaigns now over, the early figures underline the difficulty retailers faced in converting strong digital engagement into higher-value purchases.
Overall, with household budgets under pressure, rising product prices and fewer compelling discounts, shoppers appear to be prioritising essentials and selective purchases over expensive upgrades this festive season.
Edited By Shishir Parasher

Update | October 23, 2026, 19:45 IST
Reliance Industries’ digital services arm Jio Platforms’ ₹30,213 Cr IPO was subscribed 22.19X on the third and final day of bidding, with investors bidding for 438.26 Cr shares against 19.75 Cr shares on offer, according to BSE data.
Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led demand, subscribing their allotted portion 70.55X, with bids for 345.76 Cr shares against 4.90 Cr shares reserved for the category.
The non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 14X, receiving bids for 51.04 Cr shares against 3.64 Cr shares on offer.
Within the NII category, the portion for bids exceeding ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 15.89X, while the segment for bids above ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was booked 10.22X.

Original | October 23, 2026, 12:14 IST
Reliance Industries’ digital services arm Jio Platforms’ IPO was subscribed 6.76X as of 11:48 IST on the third and final day of bidding, with institutional investors continuing to drive demand.
Investors bid for 133.51 Cr shares against 19.75 Cr shares on offer, according to BSE subscription data. The overall subscription rose from 5.57X at the end of the second day.
Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) subscribed their allotted portion 14.18X, placing bids for 69.49 Cr shares against 4.90 Cr shares reserved for the category.
Within the institutional segment, domestic financial institutions, including banks and insurance companies, bid for 34.51 Cr shares, followed by foreign institutional investors at 26.19 Cr shares and mutual funds at 4.36 Cr shares.
The non-institutional investors’ (NIIs) portion was subscribed 9.17X, receiving bids for 33.44 Cr shares against an allocation of 3.64 Cr shares. Within this category, the portion for bids exceeding ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 10.50X, while that for bids above ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was booked 6.52X.
Retail investors bid for 16.96 Cr shares against 8.50 Cr shares reserved, translating into 1.99X subscription. Meanwhile, the employee and shareholder portions were subscribed 2.46X and 5.59X, respectively.
Inside Jio’s Mega IPO
Jio Platforms has set a price band of ₹1,065–₹1,119 per share for the IPO, which opened on October 21 and closes today. At the upper end, the ₹30,213 Cr (about $3.2 Bn) offering surpasses Hyundai Motor India’s ₹27,870 Cr issue to become India’s largest IPO and values Jio Platforms at around ₹10.3 Lakh Cr (about $108 Bn).
Ahead of the public issue, Jio Platforms raised ₹8,109.8 Cr from anchor investors by allotting about 7.25 Cr shares at ₹1,119 apiece. Participants included HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, BlackRock, the Government of Singapore, and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component. Jio plans to use ₹27,500 Cr to prepay certain borrowings of its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm (RJIL), with the remaining proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes.
The debt repayment makes the offering partly a balance sheet exercise, while its growth prospects depend on expanding beyond telecom connectivity into broadband, cloud services, enterprise solutions, and AI.
RJIL had 533.3 Mn customers as of June 30, 2026, while Jio’s network carried around 60% of India’s wireless data traffic in FY26. Jio Platforms’ operating revenue rose nearly 15% YoY to ₹1.47 Lakh Cr in FY26, while net profit increased 15.1% to ₹30,049 Cr.

items.author: Imran Asghar
items.content:
Investigators probing the high-profile murder of Hina Javed gathered additional photographs allegedly showing brutal torture before her death. The initial post-mortem report also revealed serious injuries to the victim’s body.
Hina, a 45-year-old digital designer, was allegedly tortured and murdered at a residence in Rawalpindi's Lalkurti on August 20.
According to the autopsy report, Hina’s neck was broken, and a deep, 27-centimetre-long wound was found on the back of her head. Multiple marks of violence and bruising were also found on her face, neck, arms and hands. The report further stated that her lips were torn and both arms bore visible signs of violence. Her elbows were allegedly pierced with a screwdriver.
The report also recorded blood in her lungs and an accumulation of blood in the pericardium, the membrane surrounding the heart. The broken neck and unusually long wound on the back of her head have raised further questions about the severity of the alleged torture before her death.
راولپنڈی میں خاتون حنا جاوید کے قتل کیس میں لرزہ خیز انکشافات کا سلسلہ جاری ہے، ابتدائی پوسٹ مارٹم رپورٹ سامنے آگئی
مزید پڑھیں: https://t.co/3WFwptOBtv#HinaJavedMurderCase #PoliceInvestigation #AdialaJail #Expressnews pic.twitter.com/i8fVQFxko7
— Express News (@ExpressNewsPK) October 23, 2026
Hina was allegedly murdered on August 20 in Rawalpindi after being subjected to violence at her in-laws’ home. It was also alleged that her body was subsequently hung in a bathroom from a shower fitting.
Her husband, Faisal Asghar, and domestic worker Zeeshan Arshad, both nominated in the murder case registered at the Civil Lines Police Station, remain in Adiala jail on judicial remand.
Meanwhile, the victim’s family has expressed a lack of confidence in the police investigation and demanded the formation of a judicial commission to ensure an impartial inquiry into the murder.
Read: Hina Javed's family rejects CCD probe
The case has also reached Parliament’s Standing Committee on Interior, which has included it in the formal agenda of its October 29 meeting and sought a briefing from senior Punjab police officials on the investigation and progress made so far.
The committee has summoned Punjab Inspector General of Police and Crime Control Department (CCD) Additional Inspector General Sohail Zafar Chattha. Rawalpindi Regional Police Officer Babar Sarfraz Alpa and Senior Superintendent of Police (Operations) Malik Tariq Mehboob have also been asked to brief the committee on the case.
The parliamentary committee has invited Hina’s family to attend the October 29 meeting, where they can present their concerns and position on the investigation.
In view of the latest medical findings, the family’s reservations about the investigation and the case’s referral to the parliamentary committee, the October 29 meeting has assumed considerable significance, sources said.
Case developments
Hina was allegedly killed by her husband in connivance with his father and an employee. A preliminary post-mortem report found a fracture to a neck bone and injuries to Hina's ribs and hip. Samples, including those required for DNA analysis, were sent to a forensic laboratory.
Police said the precise cause of death remained unestablished until the issuance of complete post-mortem and forensic reports.
A special investigation team took Asghar and Arshad to Lahore under tight security on August 25. Their samples were submitted to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency for DNA and polygraph examinations.
Meanwhile, police sources drew attention to old YouTube lectures by Asghar, who reportedly taught corporate communication at several universities. In one lecture, he asked a student why a husband might shoot his wife and discussed hypothetical scenarios involving marital relationships, infidelity and financial motives.
According to police sources, domestic worker Arshad gave three different statements from the time he was taken into custody until the formal investigation. In his first statement, Arshad claimed that Hina was killed according to a plan in collaboration with Asghar.
Read More: Hina Javed murder: Domestic worker confesses to crime, police say
In his second statement, he claimed responsibility for the murder. However, during the formal police investigation, Arshad allegedly recorded a third statement, saying he had been called during a quarrel between the husband and wife.
According to police sources, Arshad also revealed that Hina resisted and tried to run away to save her life, after which both men caught her. During her resistance, she was allegedly strangled.
According to police sources, the investigation into Hina's murder was not limited to her husband and domestic worker, and inquiries were being conducted from various angles. Police were also examining whether domestic worker Arshad killed Hina after she allegedly saw him stealing money or other items from the house.
According to sources, Arshad used to sleep in a portion of the house occupied by Hina and other family members. He had also been accused of stealing Hina's purse, cash and other items from the house.
Police were investigating whether Arshad killed Hina out of fear that his alleged theft would be discovered. However, according to police sources, another question being examined was whether, if only one person was involved in the murder, he could have moved the body alone to the bathroom and hung it from the shower.
On September 1, the investigation team recovered the alleged murder weapon, a screwdriver, from the possession of suspect and employee Arshad during a 10-day inquiry.
The team also recovered the nikahnamas of both wives of the main suspect along with the divorce deed of his first wife, Iram Zaib.
On September 3, Civil Judge Adil Sarwar Sial sent Asghar and Arshad to Adiala Jail on a 14-day judicial remand in the murder case.
Also Read: Hina Javed murder probe expands
The court ordered that the challan be completed within two weeks and both suspects, along with the challan, be produced before the court on September 16.
On September 6, Arshad, who remained in police custody on a 10-day physical remand, was sent on judicial remand.
Sources said the special investigation team had started recording separate statements of police officers, personnel and others.
On September 11, Arshad filed a bail application before an Islamabad sessions court on Thursday, declaring himself innocent.
In his bail petition, the suspect denied involvement in the murder and contended that the allegations levelled against him in the FIR were completely false and that he had nothing to do with the incident.
He said that he was mentally incapable of committing such a serious crime and requested that he be granted bail.
On September 30, the Punjab government constituted a high-powered committee to review the investigation into Hina's murder case.
On October 1, Additional District and Sessions Judge Naseer Ahmed dismissed both bail applications of accused Arshad and extended the judicial remand of both accused until October 14.
On October 10, a high-level investigation team launched a fresh probe into Hina's murder, visiting the crime scene in Lalkurti and reviewing key evidence, including the victim's DNA report.
On October 17, Hina's family expressed complete distrust in both the CCD and the local police and decided to file a private complaint, also described as a judicial FIR, before a local magistrate next week.
On October 19, Arshad's father alleged that his son was forced at gunpoint to restrain the victim and was subsequently tortured in custody to make him confess to the crime.

items.author: editorial
items.content:
As Americans gear up for the November 3 mid-term polls to elect Representatives and Senators, an uneasy peace prevails in the Middle East. President Trump's wish list for a deal with Iran - under which the Islamic Republic would give up its enriched uranium and provide safe passage for the superpower to exit the volatile region - remains unrealised. Hectic diplomatic efforts by Qatar and Pakistan have yet to bear fruit. Iran remains adamant that the US must exit the region, as the latter stands badly bruised by the losses it incurred in the war.
American military assets stand depleted in the Middle East, with many key military bases heavily degraded by recent conflict. Coupled with this is the reality of Israel being unable to unilaterally defend itself, as its Iron Dome air defence system has been severely overwhelmed. Last but not least is the reluctance of Doha and Riyadh to back any new military adventurism by Washington against Tehran.
This paints a paradoxical security dilemma wherein the Gulf Arab states that once depended on US military muscle are now on their own. On a positive note, a trans-regional security nexus is in the making. The trilateral Makkah Agreement and the recently-signed four-nation Badr Pact - comprising Pakistan, Türkiye, Qatar and Indonesia - are spontaneous responses to this shift. By focusing on joint military production and technical R&D, these nations have emerged as a formidable deterrent force.
Yet, Washington's jingoism and lack of a consistent policy remain a major point of concern. All signs indicate the region is heading back toward a major conflagration. Reports from across the Atlantic that the US wants to nail down Iran as a point-scoring exercise before the midterms are deeply unnerving. The body language and rhetoric emerging from Iran's power corridors is one of defiance, and the IRGC has vowed "surprises" that could prove disastrous for American allies in the region. No such misadventure will bring an end to the war; instead, it would trigger a new geo-economic crisis and leave the region devastated to the core.

items.author: editorial
items.content:
Pakistani journalists continue to work in one of the world's most dangerous media environments, according to several local and international press-related NGOs and monitoring groups. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) regularly ranks Pakistan among the deadliest countries for reporters, with dozens killed in the past two decades, but barely any prosecutions or convictions to show. Reporters Without Borders (RSF) similarly documents persistent physical attacks, death threats, harassment and digital surveillance. The Pakistan Press Foundation (PPF) records dozens of cases each year - from beatings and abductions to pressure on media owners to silence critical coverage. These threats are not just dangers for journalists, but also detrimental to all Pakistanis, as the public's right to know is being eroded.
The threats themselves range from non-state armed groups targeting journalists to political and economic pressures - including advertising boycotts, licensing leverage and legal harassment - which have forced newsrooms to self-censor. Digital intimidation, including hacking and online smear campaigns, increasingly follows reporters home. The common thread is impunity, because when attacks go uninvestigated and unpunished, they embolden further violence. CPJ's impunity index has repeatedly highlighted Pakistan's failure to bring the killers of journalists to justice.
Safety requires more than condemnations. The federal and provincial governments should establish independent, adequately funded protection mechanisms that are approved by journalist unions. The police must treat attacks on journalists as attacks on democratic accountability, with transparent investigations and witness protection. The judiciary should also expedite hearings of cases involving violence against journalists.
Journalists are the public's eyes and ears. A free press is not a threat to stability, but rather a precondition for good governance in a democracy.
