items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) announced its financial results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, at a Board of Directors meeting in Islamabad. According to the company’s press release, PTCL Group recorded 62% year-on-year consolidated revenue growth and maintained momentum across fixed, enterprise and mobile businesses during the third quarter of 2026.
Key Financial Highlights
Consolidated revenue grew by 62% year-on-year, primarily driven by sustained growth in the fixed broadband, enterprise and wholesale segments, alongside strong mobile performance following the successful amalgamation of Ufone and Telenor under PTML.
Consolidated operating profit grew by 181% year-on-year, while net profit reached Rs. 4.7 billion, reflecting benefits from the amalgamation, operational efficiencies and revenue growth.
PTCL revenue grew by 9% year-on-year, with Flash Fiber revenue up 26%, Business Solutions up 15%, Carrier & Wholesale services up 13%, and international business revenue up 11%.
PTCL reported operating profit of Rs. 11 billion and net profit of Rs. 3 billion, a 343% year-on-year improvement.
PTML mobile business revenue increased by 139% year-on-year, driven by consolidation of Telenor Pakistan following the amalgamation and growth in Corporate and Retail segments.
PTML posted operating profit of Rs. 33.5 billion, up 181% year-on-year, reflecting the amalgamation, higher revenue and improved operating performance.
Ubank generated revenue of Rs. 18.3 billion and reported an operating profit, compared with an operating loss in the corresponding period last year. Its bottom line improved by 84% year-on-year.
Strengthening Fixed-Line and Enterprise Leadership
PTCL continued to enhance consumer offerings and its position in fixed broadband. It launched a limited-period Azadi Offer bundling 100 Mbps Flash Fiber with an IPTV set-top box, and partnered with Apple-authorized distributor Mercantile to introduce the iPhone 18 in Pakistan alongside an exclusive Flash Fiber bundle.
The Business Solutions segment maintained momentum amid demand for ICT services, cloud solutions, on-premises AI infrastructure, cybersecurity, managed services, data centre offerings and connectivity.
PTCL said it retained leadership in submarine connectivity, IP bandwidth and domestic bandwidth services for carrier customers.
The addition of 1.5 million subscribers in Q3 increased PTML’s subscriber base to more than 76 million. The company said average revenue per user (ARPU) expanded, supported by portfolio harmonization, usage growth and network integration.
PTML expanded its 5G footprint across major cities, and network integration progressed across 25 districts by quarter-end.
Going forward, PTML plans to prioritize nationwide network consolidation, 5G expansion, network quality, digital capabilities and customer experience. Digital offerings included family-sharing bundles for all subscribers and new self-service features.
Driving Sustainable Social Progress & Digital Inclusion
Under the Ba-Ikhtiar programme, 2,100 women in 22 districts completed digital marketing, e-commerce and digital financial literacy training delivered by U Bank. Beneficiaries received Ufone 5G SIMs with free connectivity and UPaisa wallets. Women entrepreneurs also showcased their achievements at a provincial conference on women’s inclusion in Balochistan.
PTCL signed an MoU with ConnectHear to deploy SILA, an AI-powered sign language solution, at selected customer service centres in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad, with potential expansion.
PTML partnered with the United Nations’ Polio Eradication Initiative, operated by UNICEF through the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC), to provide GSM connectivity to frontline healthcare workers nationwide.
PTCL’s Pakistan Jitna Jawan Independence Day campaign marked the company’s evolution alongside Pakistan over 79 years. At Dragons of Pakistan 2026, PTCL won five awards: one Silver, one Bronze and three Black Dragons.
PTML continued campaigns highlighting expanded coverage and faster speeds, with consumer engagement supported by the iPhone 18 launch. Ufone and Telenor Pakistan won nine Dragons of Pakistan 2026 awards: two Gold, two Silver and five Black Dragons, spanning marketing, PR, media, digital, and content creation.

items.content:
Un organisme chargé de promouvoir les développements liés à la 6G dans l’Union européenne (UE) a sélectionné cinq projets qui se partageront 22 millions d’euros dans le cadre de sa dernière attribution de financements, dont des travaux sur les appareils connectés et sur l’amélioration des données pour les réseaux natifs de l’IA.
L’entreprise commune « Réseaux et services intelligents » (Smart Networks and Services Joint Undertaking, ou SNS JU) explique que les initiatives retenues visent à répondre à des besoins clés de la prochaine phase de développement de la 6G.
L’objectif des projets soutenus est d’aider les chercheurs et les entreprises de la région à faire passer des technologies prometteuses à une phase d’essais à grande échelle avant leur adoption concrète.
L’organisation, financée en partie par l’UE, estime que le moment est « crucial pour les ambitions européennes en matière de 6G », compte tenu de l’intensification de la concurrence mondiale dans les communications de nouvelle génération.
Les projets retenus cette fois sont 6G-AID, Hemes-6G, EUnicon-6G, EU-India-6G-Bridge et SNS Impact.
6G-AID vise à bâtir un socle européen de données pour les réseaux 6G natifs de l’IA ; Hemes-6G réunira huit bancs d’essai à travers l’UE sur une plateforme commune pour des travaux à plus grande échelle. EUnicon-6G cherche à identifier des opportunités pour les appareils connectés autres que les smartphones. Comme son nom l’indique, EU-India-6G-Bridge approfondit la collaboration avec l’Inde et SNS Impact doit soutenir la collaboration entre projets.
Erzsébet Fitori, directrice exécutive de la SNS JU, affirme que ces projets signifient pour l’industrie « un meilleur accès aux données, aux bancs d’essai, aux technologies et aux partenariats nécessaires pour transformer la recherche sur la 6G en produits et services ».Pour les citoyens, ils contribuent à poser « les bases d’une connectivité plus sûre, plus fiable et plus performante dans les années à venir ».
« Ces propositions visent à garantir que l’Europe contribue à façonner les technologies et les normes qui définiront l’avenir », ajoute Erzsébet Fitori.
Les cinq projets retenus sont issus du sixième appel à propositions de l’organisation, clos plus tôt cette année.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday ​to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed.
The push came ‌after governments in Europe and elsewhere took websites offline as a precaution on Wednesday while website operators scrambled to secure systems running the software.
The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand.
Read: Government websites in Europe, elsewhere go dark as software flaw sparks security scramble
"I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella ​said at an event in Germany on Thursday, saying the incident showed the importance of building software that can be maintained securely as systems grow more complex.
"It was a long day ​and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks."
PHP key to internet's foundations like html, python
The developers of PHP - a key ⁠computing language like HTML and Python - released fixes on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI, urging users to "update immediately".
Madeline Lawrence, co-founder of Belgian cybersecurity ​firm Aikido Security, said that details of the flaws had become public before fixes were ready, with attacks reported since. "Companies are racing to update against attackers who can use AI to exploit them. That's the ​whole race," she said.
As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare.
"In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it," Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wednesday. "That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post-announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now."
Impact from ​Japan to Finland
Japanese companies including brokerage Nomura, lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, airline ANA and East Japan Railway said on Thursday they were temporarily suspending some internet services as part of emergency measures.
Brewer Asahi ​Group Holdings temporarily suspended certain websites and systems and was conducting a security impact assessment. Insurer Tokio Marine Holdings said it had suspended its group website.
Japan's Ministry of Finance and Meteorological Agency partially suspended online services to implement ‌safety measures, ⁠while Japan's National Tax Agency temporarily took down its service.
The precautionary shutdowns show Japan's growing concerns over cybersecurity, as the country recorded more cyber incidents in the first nine months of the year than in all of last year, according to data from TrendAI.
Read More: How one hacker used AI agents and a few thousand dollars to break into scores of sites
French telecoms group Orange said it had temporarily suspended access to certain PHP-based websites and applications across several subsidiaries as a precaution.
Tencent Cloud, one of China's largest cloud-computing providers, urged customers to install updated PHP versions but stopped short of calling for widespread website shutdowns.
Finland's state IT services provider Valtori said it had continued installing PHP security patches overnight and was gradually lifting precautionary ​service blocks after shutting down government public web services ​a day earlier.
"Restoring services can take days or ⁠even weeks, as in addition to updates, the systems need to be carefully tested," Valtori Director General Hannu Naumanen said in a statement.
Valtori said the outages were not caused by exploitation of the vulnerabilities or by a cyber breach, and that it was not aware of any active exploitation of the flaws.
Some ​fixes may take weeks to implement
Several Asian governments ordered cybersecurity inspections related to the PHP vulnerabilities on Thursday.
China's industry ministry urged organisations and users ​to inspect systems and upgrade ⁠to the latest secure version of PHP. It also recommended strengthening cybersecurity monitoring and changing accounts, passwords and keys where necessary.
South Korea raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency response measures, citing concerns over an increased risk of hacking attacks.
Felix Kuhlenkamp, head of security at German digital industry association Bitkom, said that many larger operators had already carried out updates, but that for complex IT systems and smaller organisations it could take ⁠longer.
"They may run ​a website using PHP but don't really keep a close eye on it," he said. "If a website is based on ​an old version of PHP for which there is no security update, the entire system must be updated."

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Foodtech major Swiggy reported a consolidated net loss of ₹922 Cr in the September quarter of FY27, narrowing 16% from ₹1,092 Cr in the year-ago quarter. However, its loss widened 17% from ₹791 Cr in the preceding quarter.
Operating revenue increased 36% YoY and 11% QoQ to ₹7,571 Cr. Including other income of ₹212 Cr, total income stood at ₹7,783 Cr.
Swiggy’s consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹760 Cr from ₹695 Cr a year earlier and ₹651 Cr in Q1 FY27, with higher losses at Instamart and its newer businesses weighing on profitability.
Across its consumer-facing businesses, gross order value (GOV) increased 25% YoY to ₹20,793 Cr. Average monthly transacting users rose 21% to 27.8 Mn.
Total expenses increased 30% YoY to ₹8,703 Cr.
Swiggy’s consolidated cash balance stood at ₹13,662 Cr at the end of September, down ₹705 Cr from the preceding quarter.
Instamart Steps Up Investments Ahead Of IOCC Conversion
Swiggy’s quick commerce arm Instamart reported operating revenue of ₹1,306 Cr, up 33% YoY and 6% QoQ. Its segment loss widened to ₹764 Cr from ₹739 Cr a year earlier and ₹651 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Adjusted EBITDA loss increased to ₹895 Cr from ₹849 Cr a year earlier and ₹778 Cr in the preceding quarter. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved marginally to -9.7% of GOV from -9.8% in Q1 FY27.
Swiggy said it believes Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA losses peaked in Q2 FY27. It expects another quarter of double-digit sequential net order value (NOV) growth in Q3 FY27, alongside an improvement of around 100 basis points in adjusted EBITDA margin.
Instamart’s GOV increased 31% YoY and 17% QoQ to ₹9,230 Cr during the September quarter. NOV, which excludes discounts from GOV, rose 35% YoY and 13% QoQ to ₹6,594 Cr.
However, its contribution margin deteriorated 82 basis points sequentially to -1% of GOV. Swiggy attributed the decline to targeted pricing investments to reactivate dormant users and encourage repeat purchases, changes in customer and category mix, and the initial costs of new dark stores.
The renewed spending follows Instamart’s achievement of contribution breakeven in Q1 FY27, after which Swiggy stepped up investments to accelerate growth.
Instamart added 1.3 Mn average monthly transacting users sequentially, taking the total to 14.8 Mn. Orders increased 29% YoY to 130.3 Mn, while net average order value rose 4% to ₹506.
It also added 69 dark stores during the quarter, taking its network to 1,240 stores across 133 cities.
Alongside these investments, Swiggy said Instamart’s transition to an inventory-led model will begin in mid-Q3 FY27 and take two to three quarters to complete.
The update follows the earlier shareholder approval to cap foreign ownership at 49.5% on a fully diluted basis, enabling Swiggy’s transition to an Indian-owned and controlled structure.
Swiggy said inventory ownership could improve Instamart’s contribution margin by around 80 basis points once fully implemented, while giving it greater control over assortment, pricing, and availability.
The company also expects its working capital cycle to improve by eight to 10 days, offsetting the additional investment required to hold inventory on its balance sheet.
Food Delivery Posts Records
Swiggy’s food delivery business reported operating revenue of ₹2,338 Cr, up 22% YoY. Segment profit increased 39% YoY to ₹349 Cr.
“Our food delivery business delivered its highest ever profits and margins while we continue to unlock new category growth through Toing, our standalone offering for affordable meals,” Swiggy cofounder, MD, and group CEO Sriharsha Majety said.
Food delivery GOV increased 18% YoY and 6% QoQ to ₹10,054 Cr. The business posted record adjusted EBITDA of ₹341 Cr, compared with ₹240 Cr a year earlier and ₹292 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Its adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 3.4% of GOV from 2.8% a year earlier. Swiggy attributed the improvement to advertising-led monetisation, delivery efficiencies, and operating leverage.
Bolt and its ₹99 Store together accounted for more than 25% of food delivery volumes.
The company retained its full-year food delivery GOV growth guidance of 18–20%, excluding Toing, after growth exceeded 20% YoY in September.
Meanwhile, its affordable meals app Toing, now present in more than 50 cities, continued to attract new and dormant users. Swiggy said two in three new Toing users were either first-time Swiggy users or users who had been inactive for a long time.
The company said Toing could help lift combined food delivery marketplace growth to 25-30%. In some cities, Toing’s order volumes have already reached 20-30% of core food delivery volumes.
Swiggy said repeat-user unit economics had turned positive in Toing’s earliest launch cities. However, the offering still requires improvements in monetisation and costs to make it sustainable.
It expects Toing’s investment outlay to remain within a limited range in the near term, with spending primarily directed towards customer acquisition and supported by its existing technology and execution infrastructure. Swiggy expects greater clarity on the model’s scalability over the next one to two quarters.
Toing remains part of the platform innovations segment, whose adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹162 Cr from ₹131 Cr in the preceding quarter.
Meanwhile, Swiggy’s out-of-home consumption business, which includes Dineout and Scenes, reported GOV of ₹1,508 Cr, up 35% YoY. It posted adjusted EBITDA of ₹8 Cr, marking its seventh consecutive profitable quarter on this metric.
Shares of Swiggy ended today’s trading session 5.01% lower at ₹211.30 apiece on the BSE.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Artificial intelligence could significantly change the nature of jobs in Pakistan, with 61% of workers in the services sector employed in occupations with above-median AI exposure, according to a World Bank assessment.
The findings, outlined in the Pakistan Development Update’s analysis titled Job Opportunities and AI in Pakistan, show that the potential impact of AI varies sharply across the economy. Services face the greatest exposure, while agriculture is relatively insulated from the technology’s immediate effects.
Importantly, high exposure does not mean that 61% of service-sector workers are expected to lose their jobs. It means their occupations involve tasks that AI could potentially perform or assist with.
The report estimates Pakistan’s average occupational AI exposure score in 2024 at 0.48 standard deviations below the median occupation, broadly in line with other emerging markets and developing economies.
Which Jobs in Pakistan Are Most Exposed to AI?
The World Bank found that 61% of service-sector workers hold jobs with above-median AI exposure. The corresponding figures are much lower in other sectors: 7% in manufacturing, 5% in other industries, and less than 1% in agriculture.
Within services, wholesale and retail trade, financial and insurance activities, real estate, and education stand out. In each of these subsectors, more than 80% of workers are employed in occupations classified as highly exposed to AI.
Jobs involving information processing, administrative duties, and knowledge-intensive tasks are particularly likely to change as organizations adopt AI tools. However, the report distinguishes between AI replacing certain tasks and helping employees perform them more efficiently.
In 2024, approximately 18% of employed workers in Pakistan were in occupations with both high AI exposure and high potential for human-AI complementarity. By comparison, 8% worked in highly exposed occupations with low complementarity, where the potential for substitution may be greater.
Real estate and education are identified mainly as sectors where AI may complement workers, offering opportunities to improve productivity rather than simply replace people.
AI Skills and Workforce Preparation Will Be Critical
Wholesale and retail trade deserves particular attention because it employs a substantial number of workers and includes both AI-complementary and potentially substitutable roles. The sector’s overall employment size means changes in how businesses adopt AI could have wider implications for Pakistan’s labour market.
Agriculture, despite employing a large share of the workforce, remains concentrated in occupations with low measured AI exposure. That does not rule out productivity gains from agricultural technology but suggests fewer immediate changes to the tasks performed in many agricultural jobs.
The World Bank cautions that the actual employment impact will depend on the pace of AI adoption, access to relevant skills, and investment in technologies that support workers. High occupational exposure alone cannot predict job losses.
For Pakistan, the findings highlight a growing need for practical AI training and upskilling, particularly in services. Helping employees work alongside AI could allow businesses to improve productivity while preparing workers for changing job requirements.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Ufone & Telenor Pakistan, in collaboration with the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), hosted an executive knowledge-sharing workshop, titled “Zero Trust in a Hyperconnected Telecom Environment” at their Headquarters to discuss practical approaches to strengthening cybersecurity across increasingly interconnected telecom networks. The workshop brought together regulator representatives, telecom industry leaders, cybersecurity professionals, academia, and technical stakeholders from related sectors.
The workshop focused on the evolving cybersecurity challenges facing telecom networks, where users, systems, services and third parties are increasingly interconnected. Experts highlighted the importance of moving beyond reliance on traditional perimeter-based security controls towards approaches that verify access, strengthen access governance, manage privileged access and support the resilience of critical telecom infrastructure.
The workshop featured openings remarks by Mr. Mukarram Khan, DG PTA Cyber Vigilance followed by technical sessions on evolving telecom threats, Zero Trust implementation and sustaining Zero Trust as an ongoing security approach. The event showcased the strong cybersecurity expertise and delivery capabilities of the Ufone & Telenor Pakistan Cybersecurity Team through engaging knowledge-sharing sessions, complemented by insightful keynote addresses from industry and security expert Tauseef Aslam and participation from other industry leaders and cybersecurity professionals.
The sessions were followed by an audience question-and-answer session and an interactive knowledge quiz, which provided participants the opportunity to exchange perspectives and share practical experience.
The workshop highlighted the fact that cybersecurity in telecommunications is a shared responsibility requiring collaboration among regulators, operators and the wider industry. It further highlighted that Zero Trust is not a one-time technology deployment or a standalone product, but a continuous journey involving access verification, appropriate security controls and adaptation as networks, technologies and threats evolve.
Commenting on the initiative, Chief Corporate Affairs Officers, Ufone & Telenor Pakistan – Shan ul Haq said,
“As telecom networks become more interconnected, building trust into how users, devices and systems access services is increasingly important. Through this workshop, Ufone & Telenor Pakistan and PTA brought industry stakeholders together to exchange practical experience and strengthen our collective understanding of Zero Trust. Collaboration and continuous improvement are essential to building a more secure and resilient telecom ecosystem.”
Through the initiative, Ufone & Telenor Pakistan reaffirmed their commitment to cybersecurity, secure and resilient telecom services, and constructive engagement with the regulator and industry stakeholders, in order to ensure uninterrupted connectivity and digital services. The exchange was intended to contribute to greater cybersecurity awareness and informed industry dialogue to support efforts towards stronger security practices, improved access governance and more resilient interconnected telecom infrastructure.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Huawei may be preparing to expand its Pura 90 lineup with a new model called the Huawei Pura 90 Plus. A recent leak has revealed some expected specs of Huawei Pura 90 Plus, including a large main camera sensor with variable aperture, which could make the phone an interesting option for photography enthusiasts.
According to tipster Digital Chat Station, the upcoming smartphone carries the internal codename “Lucia.” The device is expected to feature a 6.8-inch display with a 1.5K resolution. However, Huawei has not officially confirmed the phone or its specifications.
Huawei Pura 90 Plus Tipped to Feature 50MP 1-Inch RYYB Camera
The biggest highlight of the Huawei Pura 90 Plus is its rumored 50MP main camera. The sensor is said to measure one inch and use Huawei’s RYYB filter technology. It is also expected to support variable aperture, allowing the camera to adjust the amount of light entering the lens according to shooting conditions.
Huawei has used RYYB sensors in several of its flagship smartphones. Unlike conventional RGB sensors, which use red, green, and blue filters, RYYB sensors use red, yellow, yellow, and blue filters. This design can help the camera capture more light, potentially improving low-light photography.
The tipster described this camera combination as a unique setup expected to appear in a smartphone this year. If the information proves accurate, the Pura 90 Plus could offer a notable camera upgrade within Huawei’s existing lineup.
The leaked information also suggests that the phone will feature a triangular rear camera module positioned in the upper-left corner. This design would follow the visual style of the existing Pura 90 series.
Expected Design and Color Options
The Huawei Pura 90 Plus is rumored to arrive in four color options: Obsidian Black, Snow White, Dawn Gold, and Sunset Purple. These finishes could give buyers several choices, although the final colors have not been confirmed.
The reported 6.8-inch display would place the phone among the larger devices in the series. Its 1.5K resolution could also provide a sharp viewing experience for videos, games, and everyday use.
The leak does not provide details about the processor, battery capacity, charging speeds, or other camera sensors. These specifications remain unknown for now.
Huawei Pura 90 Plus Could Expand the Existing Lineup
Huawei launched the Pura 90 series in April 2026. The standard Pura 90 features a Kirin 9010S processor and a triple-camera system with a 50MP main sensor, a 50MP periscope telephoto camera offering 3.7x optical zoom, and a 12.5MP ultrawide camera.
The standard model also offers a 6,500mAh battery and a relatively thin design compared with the Pro and Pro Max versions. Huawei currently offers different configurations across the series, with variations in displays, processors, and camera hardware.
The rumored Pura 90 Plus could join the existing models rather than replace them. Its reported one-inch main camera sensor and variable aperture may help distinguish it from the other devices in the family.
The tipster also suggested that a smaller model with a display measuring around 6.1 inches could arrive in the second half of 2027.
For now, the Huawei Pura 90 Plus remains an unconfirmed device based on early leaks. More details about its hardware, pricing, and launch timeline may emerge in the coming months.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s National Computer Emergency Response Team (National CERT) has issued a cybersecurity advisory warning public and private organizations about growing security risks associated with third-party vendors, suppliers, and external service providers.
According to the advisory, businesses and government institutions could face serious cyber threats if their external partners fail to maintain adequate security measures. Even organizations with strong internal cybersecurity systems may remain vulnerable if attackers exploit weaknesses in a trusted vendor’s network or software.
National CERT warned that third-party service providers often have access to an organization’s systems, sensitive information, and security credentials. If these access points are not properly secured, cybercriminals could use them to infiltrate internal networks, steal confidential data, or compromise digital operations.
The advisory identifies potential sources of risk including cloud service providers, software vendors, third-party applications, plugins, contractors, consultants, manufacturers, distributors, and supply chain partners.
These external relationships have become increasingly important as organizations rely on cloud platforms, outsourced IT services, and integrated software solutions. However, vulnerabilities in any connected system could create security risks for an entire organization.
How Third-Party Vendors Can Become a Cybersecurity Threat
National CERT highlighted that attackers may target smaller vendors or business partners with weaker cybersecurity controls rather than attempting to breach a heavily protected organization directly.
Once a third-party provider is compromised, attackers could potentially exploit existing access privileges to reach the systems or information of the organization it serves.
The advisory also raised concerns about sensitive information being shared with external companies without adequate safeguards. Such practices could expose confidential business records, personal information, or security credentials to unauthorized individuals.
Software applications, plugins, and cloud-based tools were identified as additional areas of concern, particularly when vulnerabilities remain unaddressed or access permissions are not properly managed.
According to National CERT, an organization’s cybersecurity depends not only on its internal security infrastructure but also on the protection measures adopted by vendors and business partners.
National CERT Recommends Five Security Measures
To reduce the risk of third-party cyberattacks, National CERT advised public and private organizations to strengthen their vendor security practices:
Enforce security requirements: Ensure third-party service providers follow appropriate cybersecurity requirements and controls.
Assess vendors before engagement: Evaluate vendors’ cybersecurity measures before granting access to systems or sensitive information.
Limit third-party access: Give external providers only the permissions needed for their assigned work.
Monitor vendor activities: Regularly review third-party activities and access to detect suspicious behaviour or security violations.
Review incident response procedures: Regularly review cyber incident reporting and response plans to ensure timely communication and coordinated action following a breach.
National CERT emphasized that weaknesses in a single external service provider could undermine the cybersecurity defences of an otherwise well-protected organization.
The advisory highlights the need for Pakistani businesses and government departments to assess external technology partners, control access to sensitive systems, and maintain oversight of third-party cybersecurity practices.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Japanese-themed dining chain Harajuku Tokyo Cafe has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a pre-Series A funding round led by ZeroW, with participation from existing investors Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC.
The round also saw participation from new investors, including Blume Founders Fund, Brijesh Parekh Family Office, Epigamia cofounder Rahul Jain, among others.
The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its outlet network by opening 10 outlets in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chandigarh, over the next two quarters.
It also plans to operationalise central kitchens in Mumbai and Bengaluru by December 2026.
Founded in 2021 by London School Of Economics (LSE) alum Gaurav Kanwar, Harajuku operates Japanese-themed dining outlets in Delhi NCR and Mumbai. It operates a casual dine-in chain, Harajuku Tokyo Cafe, and QSR-chain Harajuku Bakehouse.
Harajuku Bakehouse contributes about a third to the startup’s top line. It claims to have sold more than 1,000 loaves of bread per week on Blinkit in Delhi NCR.
Since raising its seed round of ₹19 Cr in August 2025, Harajuku claims to have doubled both its outlet count and overall revenue.
“Our focus has been to build the operational infrastructure required to support consistent quality as we expand. We have invested in centralised kitchens and systems that provide daily visibility into outlet performance, ingredients and costs. This foundation will support our next phase of growth. We aim to achieve ₹100 Cr in revenue this financial year and build on that momentum in the years ahead,” Kanwar said.
The fundraise comes amid the growing popularity of café culture in India, driven by increasing consumer interest in niche and international food offerings.
According to the Swiggy-Kearney ‘How India Eats 2025’ report, the country’s food services market is projected to grow from $78 Bn in 2025 to $120-125 Bn by 2030, with the organised segment expected to expand at roughly twice the pace of the unorganised market.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Google hosted Think Apps 2026 in Lahore, bringing together Pakistan’s top developers, alongside global and regional industry leaders and experts. As the biggest app and gaming event of the year for the industry, it focused on how AI can help Pakistani studios achieve sustainable growth on the world stage.
Pakistani app and gaming studios have increasingly made their mark globally, reaching millions of users beyond the country’s borders. Over the past 12 months alone, products built by local developers generated an extraordinary 4.6 billion downloads worldwide. This expanding international presence provides a strong foundation for boosting Pakistan’s digital exports, especially as rapid advancements in AI create unprecedented opportunities for local developers to scale, innovate, and compete globally.
During the event, experts highlighted actionable AI tools, growth strategies, and monetization frameworks tailored to help studios streamline production, enhance user engagement, and tap into high-value markets.
Pakistan’s next digital export chapter
From its humble beginnings with fewer than 30 people, the industry now supports over 30,000 professionals—reflecting the immense depth of local talent building products for global audiences. Pioneering studios such as Game District and Funsol exemplify an ambitious ecosystem whose reach and vision extend far beyond Pakistan’s domestic market.
Farhan Qureshi, Google Cluster Director for Pakistan, the Philippines, Thailand and Frontier Markets, addresses Think Apps 2026 in Lahore, highlighting how AI can help Pakistani developers build globally competitive businesses and a lasting digital legacy.
“The global impact of Pakistan’s developers reflects the world-class talent and ambition driving the local ecosystem,” said Farhan Qureshi, Google Cluster Director for Pakistan, the Philippines, Thailand, and Frontier Markets. “By empowering developers with cutting-edge AI capabilities, our goal is to accelerate this momentum and enable studios to build high-value products that resonate globally, foster sustainable business growth, and elevate Pakistan’s position in the global digital economy.”
AI opens the next growth opportunity
The opportunity comes as rising competition and user acquisition costs put a new level of challenge on developers. AI offers ways to accelerate coding, improve creative production and build applications around new user needs. Success will depend on combining these capabilities with product quality and experiences that keep users engaged.
Through the Build, Yield and Scale roadmap, Google outlined support across that journey. Google Cloud AI can help studios develop products, while Google Ads and AdMob support user acquisition and monetisation. Expansion into new categories and audiences offers routes to international growth. Google Play’s reach of more than three billion monthly active users underscores the scale of the audience available to developers.
Investing in Pakistan’s next generation
Google’s commitment extends to preparing the next generation of Pakistani developers to compete globally. Its pledge to train 100,000 developers in AI by 2028 will support the creation of next-generation apps and games, while enabling local production of 500,000 Chromebooks will broaden access to technology for digital education. Alongside online safety training delivered to 200,000 families through its Digital Pasban program, these efforts support the skills, access and confidence young Pakistanis need to participate in the digital economy here and abroad.

items.author: Albert Cuesta
items.content:
El organismo que impulsa la 6G en la Unión Europea ha seleccionado cinco proyectos que se repartirán 22 millones de euros en su última convocatoria de ayudas. Entre ellos hay iniciativas sobre dispositivos conectados y sobre la mejora de los datos para redes nativas de inteligencia artificial.
La Empresa Común Europea de Redes y Servicios Inteligentes (SNS JU) ha explicado que los proyectos elegidos buscan responder a las principales necesidades de la siguiente fase de desarrollo de la 6G.
Las ayudas pretenden que investigadores y empresas de la región puedan llevar sus desarrollos hasta pruebas a gran escala y a su adopción en el mundo real.
La organización, financiada en parte por la UE, ha señalado que este es un «momento crucial para las ambiciones de Europa en materia de 6G», en un contexto de creciente competencia mundial en las comunicaciones de nueva generación.
Los proyectos seleccionados son 6G-AID, Hemes-6G, EUnicon-6G, EU-India-6G-Bridge y SNS Impact. El primero se centra en crear una base de datos europea para redes 6G nativas de IA, mientras que Hemes-6G reunirá ocho bancos de pruebas de toda la UE en una plataforma compartida para trabajos a mayor escala.
EUnicon-6G busca identificar oportunidades para dispositivos conectados más allá de los smartphones. EU-India-6G-Bridge, como su nombre indica, refuerza la colaboración con la India, y SNS Impact está concebido para apoyar la cooperación entre proyectos.
La directora de SNS JU, Erzsebet Fitori, ha afirmado que, para la industria, los proyectos supondrán «un mejor acceso a los datos, los bancos de pruebas, las tecnologías y las asociaciones necesarios para convertir la investigación en 6G en productos y servicios».
Para los ciudadanos, ha añadido, ayudarán a sentar «las bases para una conectividad más segura, fiable y capaz en los próximos años».
«Estas propuestas tienen como objetivo garantizar que Europa contribuya a dar forma a las tecnologías y los estándares que definirán el futuro».
Los cinco proyectos proceden de la sexta convocatoria de propuestas de la organización, que se cerró a principios de año.
Con información de Chris Donkin.

items.title: Opposition leaders criticise govt over stalled talks, restrictions on parliamentarians
items.summary:

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Opposition leaders Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Thursday criticised the government over stalled political negotiations and restrictions on parliamentarians, calling for meaningful dialogue and the protection of elected representatives’ rights.
Speaking at a press conference outside Parliament House alongside opposition leaders, Gohar said the opposition had repeatedly engaged in negotiations with the government in good faith and without preconditions, but the process had failed to produce the desired results.
“Our government went away while we kept negotiating with the government,” he said, referring to the opposition’s attempts to pursue political dialogue.
Gohar also questioned the criteria used to assess political leaders’ loyalty to the state, saying that despite nearly three years of the current parliament, he still did not understand the formula used to determine such allegiance. “We have always said that Pakistan comes first and the state comes first,” he said.
“We are treated as though we are not loyal to the state. This perception must end,” he added, calling for an end to questions about opposition politicians’ commitment to Pakistan.
He also called for parliamentarians to be protected so they could represent their constituents freely and without fear. Recalling an incident in September 2024, when opposition lawmakers were allegedly picked up, Gohar said the opposition leader had moved a resolution in the National Assembly in response.
He added that a special committee had also been constituted to address the issue of parliamentarians’ protection.
Achakzai calls for complete recording of parliamentary speeches
Speaking at the same press conference, Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai stressed that parliamentary speeches should be recorded in their entirety, arguing that the official record was essential to preserving the country’s political history and allowing the public to assess the statements of elected representatives.
“The complete speech of a member speaking in the National Assembly being recorded is a constitutional requirement,” he said.
Achakzai said parliamentarians had to struggle even for rights that should ordinarily be guaranteed under parliamentary rules. He maintained that the speaker’s authority should be exercised in accordance with the rules and regulations governing the assembly.
Referring to his speech in the National Assembly a day earlier, he said he had made no inappropriate remarks. He alleged that his four-and-a-half-minute speech had been presented as a nine-minute address.
He also rejected suggestions that his remarks had been directed against the country, saying not a single word in his speech had been against Pakistan.
The opposition leader said the time allotted to opposition lawmakers to speak in parliament had been curtailed, describing the restriction as another obstacle to democratic debate.
Achakzai questioned what he described as the inconsistent issuance of production orders for lawmakers, saying such orders had been issued for some members but not others. He argued that parliamentary proceedings and the rights of elected representatives should be protected without discrimination.
He also criticised the government’s approach to political negotiations, questioning how the opposition could trust a process that, in his view, had been ridiculed by those in power.
He said political dialogue required a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan. He also recalled that Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had met the prime minister in connection with the issue.
The opposition had asked the government to ensure that the prime minister personally extended an invitation for negotiations, he said. “Negotiations cannot take place in an atmosphere where the process itself is being mocked,” he said.
Achakzai called for a committee to investigate allegations of corruption against the incumbent government, proposing that Defence Minister Khawaja Asif head it.
He maintained that the opposition would resist what it considered an undemocratic system through democratic means. “It is the duty of every citizen who wants to save Pakistan to stand up for democracy,” he said, adding that the country needed a strong parliament and state institutions operating within their respective constitutional jurisdictions.
“We will not hand Pakistan over to an undemocratic system,” he said, warning that such an order could threaten the country’s unity.
Raja Nasir Abbas calls for rule of law, constitutional supremacy
Also speaking at the press conference, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas stressed that the rule of law, justice and respect for the Constitution were essential for Pakistan’s progress, saying the country’s political and economic crises could not be resolved without the supremacy of law.
He said the rule of law and access to justice were fundamental to national development. Pakistan could not overcome its ongoing political crisis unless the Constitution was upheld and the rule of law firmly established, he added.
Addressing the country’s economic challenges, Abbas said the economic crisis, too, could not be resolved without ensuring the supremacy of law. He added that justice was necessary to restore public confidence in state institutions and the wider system.
He expressed concern that the trust deficit between the rulers and the people had reached its highest level in the country’s history. He also criticised the continued registration of fabricated cases and first information reports (FIRs), saying such practices further undermined public trust.
Referring to the February 8, 2024, general elections, Abbas alleged that the people’s mandate had been stolen. He said depriving citizens of their right to vote and undermining their electoral choices constituted serious injustices.
He further said tampering with votes amounted to an attack on the Constitution and the rule of law, stressing that protecting the sanctity of the vote was essential to upholding democratic principles and restoring public confidence in the political system.
Abbas reiterated that Pakistan’s sustainable progress, political stability and economic recovery depended on constitutional supremacy, the rule of law and justice for all citizens.
Gohar denies reports of differences within PTI
Meanwhile, Gohar addressed reports concerning internal party affairs, PTI lawmakers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and the provincial organisation, urging party members to verify information before reacting to reports.
He said the news that had prompted a social media post by the party’s secretary general was incorrect and that he had spoken to the relevant leaders and lawmakers.
Describing PTI’s lawmakers from K-P as a valuable asset, Gohar praised their role in supporting Imran over the past two years. He said they had remained steadfast despite difficult circumstances and continued to play a leading role in rallies, public meetings and protest marches.
“All these members are standing even more firmly with Imran Khan, his ideology and his struggle,” he said, adding that they enjoyed the PTI founder’s full confidence.
Gohar said no party lawmaker would consider disregarding Imran’s instructions and assured the provincial leadership that it would be consulted on important party decisions.
On the provincial party presidency, he clarified that Junaid Akbar had been appointed by Imran himself and that he had issued the notification in accordance with the PTI founder’s instructions. Junaid would continue to serve as provincial president, he said.
In Junaid’s absence, senior vice-president Noorul Haq Qadri would chair meetings of the provincial organisation under the party constitution, while provincial secretary general Ali Asghar Khan would oversee other organisational matters.
Gohar said discussions had taken place with the relevant office-bearers and that the provincial organisation had expressed the same preference during its meeting. A formal notification was expected to be issued on the matter.
He added that no changes would be made to the provincial organisation or its existing cabinet until Junaid returned.
Emphasising party unity, the PTI chairman said the party’s focus should remain on Imran’s position, political narrative and struggle rather than internal disagreements or unnecessary public statements.
He reiterated that the party remained united under Imran’s leadership and that his decisions and instructions were final.
Gohar also reaffirmed PTI’s position on the K-P chief minister, saying Sohail Afridi remained the party’s choice and that there was no question of considering anyone else for the position, as the decision rested with Imran.
Salman Akram Raja rejects claims Sohail Afridi derailed talks with govt
Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja has rejected claims that non-functional K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was responsible for the breakdown of negotiations with the federal government, saying the talks collapsed over the denial of access to PTI founder Imran Khan’s personal physicians and concerns over provincial autonomy.
In an interview with a private television channel on Thursday, he said the refusal to allow Khan’s personal doctors to examine him was one of the two principal reasons behind the failure of the negotiations.
He said PTI could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to intervene in the affairs of K-P. “These were the two principal reasons why the talks collapsed,” Raja said, alleging that the government had deliberately undermined the negotiations.
The PTI leader also described the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province as unconstitutional, alleging that the government had introduced the measures to take control of the provincial administration. “They just wanted to take over the province,” he said.
Raja said an all-parties conference (APC) was being planned within the next 10 days, or earlier, to discuss the prevailing political situation. “This is a political issue and therefore all political parties must play their role,” he said.
He disclosed that several political parties were in contact with him over the situation, including Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman.
Asked about the role of Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party chairman Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Raja said the final decision rested with the PTI founder. He described Achakzai and Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Nasir Abbas as a shield for the party, adding that PTI would continue to seek their political advice and support.
Raja also maintained that PTI’s long march had not ended, signalling that the party’s political campaign would continue.
Meanwhile, PTI leader and Senator Syed Ali Zafar denied that negotiations with the government were imminent, saying decisions concerning the party would be made by its parliamentary party.
“We are yet to determine the terms of reference,” Zafar said while speaking to a journalist from the same television channel. He further alleged that the government had decided to impose governor’s rule around one-and-a-half months earlier.
Yousafzai distances party from YouTubers campaigning against state institutions
PTI's K-P information secretary Shaukat Ali Yousafzai on Thursday distanced the party from YouTubers campaigning against state institutions, saying they had no links with PTI and that such campaigns had negatively affected the party.
Speaking in an interview with a private television channel, Yousafzai said PTI founder Imran Khan had always referred to the armed forces as his own institution, adding that no other viewpoint would be entertained on the matter.
He said PTI had always condemned terrorism and described it as unjustified to label the party’s leaders or workers as facilitators of terrorists. He also alleged that the government had used concerns over peace and security as a pretext to impose emergency and governor’s rule in K-P, calling the move unjustified.
He expressed confidence in Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Salman Akram Raja, adding that he would not be “intimidated by a YouTuber” based overseas.
Deadlock on emergency and governor’s rule in K-P
The debate over emergency and governor’s rule in K-P intensified in late September amid worsening security concerns and growing political tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration.
Federal ministers accused the provincial government of failing to address terrorism and governance challenges, while PTI considered the possibility of an in-house change or dissolution of the provincial assembly.
The federal government subsequently stepped up its warnings, with Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and other officials arguing that constitutional provisions allowed the Centre to intervene if circumstances warranted extraordinary measures. The government cited the deteriorating law and order situation and the provincial administration’s handling of security challenges as precursors for governor’s rule and emergency.
Later, on October 11, President Asif Ali Zardari approved the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, following approval by the federal cabinet. The government cited escalating terrorist attacks, threats to lives and property, and what it described as a breakdown of the constitutional system in the province.
The measures invoked Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, while the federal government also authorised the deployment of the army to assist the civil administration.
Read More: PHC takes up challenge to emergency today
The move transferred executive authority from the elected provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and affected 12 districts under the emergency proclamation. PTI rejected the decision, arguing that it undermined provincial autonomy and the party’s electoral mandate.
The intervention also marked the fourth spell of governor’s rule in the province, following earlier instances in 1975, 1994 and 1999.
The issue subsequently moved to Parliament and the courts.
On October 12, a petition challenging the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in K-P was filed in the Peshawar High Court by PTI, a day after President Asif Ali Zardari approved the federal government’s decision on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The opposition argued that the constitutional requirements had not been fulfilled and that the intervention violated provincial autonomy.
Three days later, on October 15, a joint sitting of Parliament approved separate resolutions endorsing the emergency and governor’s rule for two months, despite severe protests from the opposition parties.
So far, the government and the opposition remain at loggerheads regarding the governance of the province.

WhatsApp is rolling out a scheduled messages feature to its iOS app, allowing users to send messages automatically at a selected date and time. The feature is designed to help users plan their messages in advance without having to open the app when the scheduled time arrives.
According to WABetaInfo, the feature is available to some beta testers through WhatsApp beta for iOS version 26.42.10.19, distributed through TestFlight. The company is gradually expanding access, and more beta testers are expected to receive it over the coming weeks.
WhatsApp Rolls Out Scheduled Messages Feature on iOS Beta – Here’s How to Do it
Users can schedule a message directly from an individual or group chat. After typing a message, they need to tap and hold the send button to open the scheduling screen. They can then select the desired date and time using the available controls.
The screen displays the exact delivery time before users confirm their selection. Once the message is scheduled, WhatsApp shows a confirmation in the chat. However, this confirmation is visible only to the person who scheduled the message.
The feature allows users to schedule messages at least 10 minutes in advance and up to two weeks ahead. This gives them enough flexibility to prepare birthday wishes, important announcements, reminders, and other messages without worrying about sending them manually at the right time.
Support for Photos, Videos, and Links
WhatsApp’s scheduled messaging feature supports more than just text. Users can also schedule photos, videos, and links for later delivery.
To schedule a photo or video, users can tap and hold the send button from the drawing editor screen. However, the feature does not currently allow users to schedule multiple items together. They must create a separate scheduled message for each photo or video they want to send.
The feature also supports end-to-end encryption, helping protect scheduled messages in the same way as other WhatsApp communications.
See Also: WhatsApp Tests New Location Request Feature
Users Can Manage Scheduled Messages
WhatsApp has added a dedicated section for scheduled messages in the chat information screen. In group conversations, users can access this section through the group information screen.
This section allows users to review messages before WhatsApp sends them. If they change their mind or need to make adjustments, they can delete a scheduled message at any time before its delivery.
WhatsApp does not notify recipients when a sender deletes a scheduled message before it is sent. This gives users more control over messages they have planned in advance.
Scheduled Messages Also Work in Group Chats
The feature supports both individual and group conversations. However, WhatsApp applies a specific rule to scheduled messages in groups.
A scheduled message will reach only the members who were part of the group when the sender scheduled it. Anyone who joins the group afterward will not receive that message. This approach ensures that the message does not reach people who were not members of the group when it was originally scheduled.
When Will the Feature Be Available to Everyone?
WhatsApp is currently rolling out scheduled messages to a limited number of iOS beta testers. Users running the compatible beta version may not see the feature immediately because availability depends on the gradual rollout.
More beta testers are expected to receive access over the coming weeks. However, WhatsApp has not announced an official release date for the stable version.
The arrival of scheduled messages on iOS follows the feature’s introduction in the Android beta. Once widely available, it could make WhatsApp more convenient for users who want to plan personal messages, group announcements, and important reminders in advance.

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
Actor Zoya Nasir questioned the excitement surrounding Hollywood comedian Sacha Baron Cohen’s recent shoutout to Pakistan, arguing that his history of comedy involving racial and religious stereotypes warranted a closer look at the interaction.
The Bas Tera Saath Ho actor shared her views on Instagram Stories after a video of Cohen’s brief interaction with Pakistani actor Haris Waheed began circulating online.
Waheed, who shared the clip earlier this week, can be seen meeting Cohen, expressing his admiration for the comedian and telling him that he is from Pakistan. Cohen, dressed as his character for the upcoming film Ali G: Who Iz I, responds, “Yo, big up the Pakistan, man,” prompting cheers from people nearby.
The exchange received a warm response on social media, with users appreciating the British star’s acknowledgement of Pakistan. Nasir, however, questioned whether the moment deserved the positive reaction it received.
“I’m sorry but the sheer lack of awareness is staggering. Sacha Baron Cohen has been openly hostile towards Muslims. Majority of his movies back that up,” she wrote.
Criticising the comedian’s approach to comedy, Nasir described his demeanour as marked by “smug, dripping sarcasm” and a “theatrical sense of superiority”.
She challenged the enthusiasm surrounding the exchange, asking: “This was not a positive interaction in anyway, shape or form. Why are we excited about that again?”
Screengrab: zoyanasir/Instagram
 
Cohen is known for creating characters that use exaggerated accents, cultural appropriation and provocative humour to explore prejudice and social attitudes. However, his work has also attracted criticism over whether it challenges stereotypes or risks reinforcing them.
His Borat character, for instance, has sparked debate over the use of ethnic and cultural caricatures, while The Dictator has faced scrutiny over its portrayal of authoritarianism and people from the Middle East. His Ali G persona, meanwhile, has been criticised for appropriating elements of Black culture.
Cohen has consistently defended his work as satire intended to expose ignorance and prejudice rather than endorse them.
In an interview published by Time on October 20, the comedian addressed criticism of Ali G, explaining that the character was designed to expose cultural bias and reveal how readily people in positions of power took him seriously.
“I’ve always designed my characters and comedy as vehicles to expose prejudice, bias and stupidity, though I realise not everyone sees them that way,” he said.
He further described Ali G as a white character who imitates the fashion and lyrics of gangsta rap and dancehall artists, adding that the joke was directed at the character himself and the predominantly white, male establishment that believed him.
Nasir’s comments highlight the divide in how Cohen’s comedy is received, particularly when an interaction involving one of his characters is interpreted as a gesture of goodwill towards a country or community.

items.content:
The federal government has directed all ministries and divisions to submit consolidated details of civil servants’ declarations regarding foreign nationality, travel documents and dependants’ nationality status, according to an official notification issued by the Establishment Division dated October 21.
The notification referred to the Civil Servants (Disclosure and Regulation of Foreign Nationality) Rules, 2026, under which all civil servants were required to submit declarations regarding their own and their dependants’ nationality status within 90 days of the rules’ publication in the official gazette.
Under Rule 3(3), civil servants must declare whether they hold the nationality of any foreign country, possess foreign travel documents or are married to a foreign national. They must also disclose the relevant nationality and travel-document status of their dependants.
The Establishment Division said failure to submit the required declaration or providing false information would constitute misconduct under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020, in accordance with Rule 3(4) of the 2026 rules.
The notification directed all ministries and divisions to provide the information in a consolidated format for officers under their administrative control, excluding those belonging to the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), Police Service of Pakistan (PSP), Secretariat Group (SG) and Office Management Group (OMG).
The prescribed format requires the name, designation and basic pay scale of each officer, confirmation of whether a declaration has been submitted under Rule 3(3), and details of the foreign nationality or travel-document status of both the officer and their dependants.
Earlier this month, the government decided to enforce the Foreign Citizenship Rules 2026, directing civil servants to submit declarations detailing any foreign citizenship held by themselves or their dependants within one week.
The Establishment Division, through an office memorandum, directed civil servants to provide details of foreign citizenship, foreign travel documents and marriages to foreign nationals. The directive applies to officers holding dual nationality and requires them to furnish the relevant information within the stipulated one-week deadline.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Chinese ​AI startup DeepSeek has raised about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion) in its latest funding round from investors including chipmaker ‌GigaDevice, food delivery company Meituan and automaker Geely, according to four people with knowledge of the matter.
Battery maker Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) and WeChat operator Tencent Holdings, both existing shareholders, were among the biggest investors in the round, said two of the people.
Home appliances maker Midea and existing shareholder NetEase also participated, the people ​said.
Other investors include Boyu Capital, CPE and Legend Capital, as well as existing shareholder IDG Capital, three of the people said.
The ​total number of investors in the funding round exceeded 15, one of the people said.
Read: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
DeepSeek, which sources have ⁠said is valued at 500 billion yuan before new capital is injected, will have doubled its original fundraising target of 50 billion ​yuan. The rise underscores strong interest from investors - many backed by the state and big corporations - as China aims to stay competitive in ​the AI race against the US.
"It's encouraging to see such a high valuation for DeepSeek, showing the confidence from investors on the future of its open-source strategies," said Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at research firm Omdia.
"Given that they (the investors) are all Chinese and critical component supply chain vendors, I can see ​DeepSeek itself becoming a key part of these domestic tech supply chains," Su said.
The fundraising is set to be complete in the coming ​days, but financial details and the investor lineup are not ironclad and could still change, a second person said.
DeepSeek could not be immediately reached for comment. ‌Geely declined ⁠to comment. The other firms mentioned in this article did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
On Thursday, Bloomberg first reported, citing sources, that DeepSeek had raised $15 billion in the latest funding round, with CATL and Tencent as its main backers.
DeepSeek's fundraising outcome comes amid growing concerns over massive AI spending that triggered a new selloff in global tech stocks this month.
Read More: China's DeepSeek developing its own AI chip, sources say
The soured sentiment has led to delays or withdrawals ​of data centre IPOs and poor market ​debuts of AI-related companies in South ⁠Korea and Hong Kong, Reuters has reported.
Shares of Z.AI and MiniMax, two large language model developers listed in Hong Kong since January, have fallen sharply from their peaks earlier this year.
After the fundraising, DeepSeek ​is getting closer to tapping public markets. In September, Reuters reported that the company aimed to kick ​off its IPO ⁠process this year and had hired CITIC Securities to prepare for the potential STAR Market float.
Last month, the company released its latest model, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which it said was designed for greater capability, faster inference, higher throughput and scaling to larger models.
The Hangzhou-based firm raised $7.4 billion from its inaugural external funding round ⁠in June, ​Reuters has reported.
Filings by two Chinese investors in July suggested DeepSeek was valued at ​350.88 billion yuan, or around $52 billion, in the June fundraising.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Max Verstappen is set to be a party-pooper this weekend as he seeks to delay Kimi Antonelli's title celebrations by notching a third consecutive win with another triumph at the United States Grand Prix.
Red Bull's four-time world champion won both the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and then the Singapore Grand Prix to emerge as a leading contender for more success just when Mercedes' precocious 20-year-old Italian moved within reach of the title.
The 29-year-old Dutchman, who has acknowledged Antonelli's generational talent, won from pole at the Circuit of the Americas last year and is chasing a fifth win at the Texan track where Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was won five times.
But Verstappen has been reluctant to claim that Red Bull's recovery in form and results will automatically translate to more success. "It's difficult to say – I don't want to say now that I will be in the fight in Austin," he said after his Singapore win.
"But the last few weekends have been great. I just take it race by race and we'll see how it goes there. It's another very different kind of track."
After a run of seven podium finishes in his last eight races, including two wins and three second places, Verstappen, 119 points adrift in fourth, may well scupper hopes that Antonelli can win and, with the stars aligning, become Italy's first champion since 1953 and the youngest in F1 history.
- Title within reach -
To seize the title in Texas, the Italian, who leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 102 points, needs to win the race and see Russell fail to finish in the top nine and Hamilton outside the top four.
Antonelli was only four years old when Sebastian Vettel took the record as youngest champion, with Red Bull, in 2010, and he knows he must stay focused and race to win, as he always does.
"I know it's very close and I know it's there, but I need to make sure I keep doing my best and go out and win and perform in my best way," he said. Italy's last champion was Alberto Ascari for Ferrari.
McLaren's deputy team principal Bradley Lord drew upon tennis when he described Antonelli's position by saying: "We're in that uncomfortable phase where you have to navigate the media with everyone saying 'you can do it – you've got first match point."
Russell's hopes of reining in Antonelli may be aided by Verstappen while Hamilton could also be a threat as he returns to one of his favourite circuits seeking a record sixth win and seventh in the United States GP.
Both Mercedes drivers will run the team's latest updates package as they go into a decisive triple-header of races in Texas, Mexico and Brazil, but it may be that Ferrari and Red Bull can steal the initiative.
These races may be run on bumpy tracks and in hot conditions that deliver unexpected results, a prospect that Verstappen has anticipated.
"From what I saw in the world endurance championship race in Austin, the track is incredibly bumpy and I will probably need to order a new spine after the weekend – or become like Robocop. It's crazy.

items.title: Anthropic Takes On OpenAI, Meta With New Proactive AI Agent Claude Duet
items.summary:
Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent designed to monitor connected apps, prioritise tasks, and carry out work in the background, including when users switch off their devices.
The offering targets professionals and small business owners. Powered by Claude Opus 5.5, it is available as a research preview through a waitlist for Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the US.
Users can access Claude Duet through standalone iOS and Android apps or on Claude’s website. It is included in existing Pro and Max subscriptions but shares usage limits with other Claude products. Background checks count towards these limits, while complex assignments consume more usage, Anthropic said.
Unlike conventional AI chatbots, Claude Duet is designed to identify work that needs attention without waiting for a prompt. It sends users a daily briefing covering important items across connected apps, including emails and calendars, and provides updates when tasks are completed or require a decision.
items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent designed to monitor connected apps, prioritise tasks, and carry out work in the background, including when users switch off their devices.
The offering targets professionals and small business owners. Powered by Claude Opus 5.5, it is available as a research preview through a waitlist for Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the US.
Users can access Claude Duet through standalone iOS and Android apps or on Claude’s website. It is included in existing Pro and Max subscriptions but shares usage limits with other Claude products. Background checks count towards these limits, while complex assignments consume more usage, Anthropic said.
Unlike conventional AI chatbots, Claude Duet is designed to identify work that needs attention without waiting for a prompt. It sends users a daily briefing covering important items across connected apps, including emails and calendars, and provides updates when tasks are completed or require a decision.
Users can assign tasks through text or voice messages, ranging from scheduling meetings and drafting email replies to building dashboards, financial forecasts and web applications. The agent can also search past conversations and use existing Claude memories, skills and connected apps.
Claude Duet connects with more than 6,000 tools and plugins available through the Claude Marketplace, including Gmail, Slack, QuickBooks, Stripe, Gusto, LinkedIn, DocuSign, HubSpot and Shopify.
For instance, it can identify unpaid invoices through QuickBooks or Stripe and draft payment reminders. It can also prepare payroll information, draft job postings, create follow-up emails using customer and deal histories, and help businesses set up and manage online stores.
The agent runs on its own cloud-based virtual machine with a browser, allowing it to continue working even when users close the app or switch off their devices. Anthropic said it checks connected accounts every few hours rather than continuously, partly to limit subscription usage.
Claude Duet can also help users make business purchases through Link, Stripe’s digital wallet, and Shop Pay. Payments require user approval, while Link uses a virtual card to avoid sharing the user’s actual card number. Integration with 1Password for accessing saved website logins is also planned.
Anthropic said the agent requires approval before sending messages, making payments, signing documents or deleting information. Trading securities and transferring money between accounts remain prohibited, even with user approval. Users can disconnect apps, and only they can mark tasks as finished.
Safeguards And Early Limitations
Anthropic said Claude Duet includes safeguards designed to prevent unauthorised actions, prompt injection, and sensitive data leaks. Prompt injection involves malicious instructions hidden in content an agent encounters, such as emails or websites.
The protections include an automated system that assesses proposed actions and controls designed to keep passwords and sign-in tokens out of the agent’s direct view.
A separate message-checking system is designed to block requests to share highly sensitive information, including credit card numbers and government identification. Other sensitive information, such as health and personal finance details, can be shared only on explicit user instructions, Anthropic said.
The company said Claude Duet has undergone adversarial testing and external penetration testing, and is covered by its public bug bounty programme.
However, Anthropic acknowledged that the early version may misinterpret conversations, misjudge urgency, or miss information arriving between checks. It is currently better suited to work assignments than personal errands, such as booking tickets, and users cannot yet view its browser.
The launch adds to the growing competition in always-on AI agents that work across apps with limited human intervention. OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse target similar use cases, while Bengaluru-based Emergent’s Wingman handles tasks across email, calendars, and workplace software through WhatsApp and Telegram.
As agents gain access to more business systems, their permissions and accountability are also coming under scrutiny. Recently, CERT-In warned about unauthorised AI agent access to Indian organisations’ systems, highlighting the risks associated with deploying increasingly autonomous tools.
Anthropic said feedback from early users will inform further development. The research preview does not currently include Team and Enterprise subscribers.

items.content:
Nigerian startup ECS Network is looking to bring long-term structure to competitive gaming in Africa, offering a league system with divisions, promotion and relegation, player statistics and team rankings.
Launched just over a year ago, ECS Network started out as competitive Call of Duty: Mobile (CODM) “scrims” – or practice games – before evolving into a broader e-sports organisation covering multiple games.
“A lot of competitive gaming activity was centred around standalone tournaments, where everything essentially started and ended with one event. We wanted to build something with continuity, where teams and players could compete consistently and have their performances tracked over time,” CEO Larry Channel told Disrupt Africa.
That led the startup to develop a structured league system featuring multiple divisions, promotion and relegation, player statistics, team rankings, MVP recognition and competitive integrity systems.
ECS now has more than 50 staff working across its different titles and operational areas, including event management, competitive integrity, verification, rankings, community management and media.
Channel said there were several tournament organisers and esports communities operating across Africa, but most were primarily focused on individual tournaments or events.
“Our main difference is the long-term structure. ECS is built around an ongoing competitive system where teams can progress through divisions, players can build statistics and rankings, and performances continue to matter beyond a single tournament,” he said.
The approach is resonating. ECS has grown to more than 43,000 players and over 5,000 registered teams across 10 titles, while more than 1,600 teams and 15,000 players have competed in CODM alone since launch. Having started with CODM, the platform has expanded to include Free Fire, PUBG Mobile, eFootball, FC Mobile, Blood Strike, Mobile Legends and Valorant, among others.
“The response has been very strong,” said Channel.
Though its core competitive base is in Africa, ECS has also built an audience in Europe, North America and the Middle East. The startup plans to continue expanding across more games and to strengthen its position as a wider African esports ecosystem.
ECS is self-funded by its management team, and has so far awarded more than NGN75 million (US$56,000) in prize money across its events. It generates revenue primarily through sponsorship and commercial partnerships.
“At this stage, revenue is largely reinvested into the operation and development of the league, including events, prize pools, staffing, infrastructure and community development, rather than being taken as profit,” Channel said.
The journey has not been without its challenges, chief among them changing how players view competitive gaming.
“One of the biggest challenges was changing the mindset around competitive gaming from viewing each tournament as a standalone event to seeing it as part of a longer competitive journey. Building that trust and getting teams and players to buy into a structured system took time, but we’ve seen that improve significantly,” he said.
Sponsorship remains a hurdle too.
“African e-sports is still developing commercially, so securing long-term sponsorship support remains something we’re actively working on,” said Channel.
