items.author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
items.content:
Pakistan's headline inflation is expected to rise to 10% in October 2026, driven by higher electricity charges, petrol prices and food costs, while persistent inflationary pressures could prompt the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to raise its policy rate by 50-100 basis points at its October 26 meeting, according to a Growth Securities report authored by Nasheed Malik, which projects the National Consumer Price Index (NCPI) increasing by 1.5% month-on-month (MoM), compared with 6.2% year-on-year (YoY) and 1.7% MoM in October 2025.
Average inflation during the first four months of FY27 is expected to reach 10.2%, compared with 4.8% in the corresponding period of FY26, and the October projection is above the government's expected average of 8.9% for FY27, the report said.
The transport index is expected to rise by 0.15% to 0.20% MoM following a 5.5% monthly increase in the average petrol price to Rs396.06 per litre, up 48.3% YoY, while the housing index is also expected to increase on a monthly basis due to higher electricity charges and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, which are projected to rise by 6.2% MoM.
The food index is forecast to increase by around 0.25% to 0.30% MoM, mainly due to price increases of 10% in wheat, 14% in chicken, 11% in pulse gram and 5% in garlic, according to the report.
Malik said real interest rates returned to positive territory in June 2026 and are projected to reach 1.5% in October, compared with 1.2% in September, and he expects inflation to remain in the 9% to 10% range until March 2027 if average fuel prices stay between Rs390 and Rs400 per litre, with average inflation for FY27 projected at 9% to 9.5%. He expects the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to raise the policy rate by 50-100 basis points at its October 26, 2026 meeting if fuel prices remain elevated.
A separate assessment by AKD Securities Director Research Mohammed Awais Ashraf holds that Pakistan's improved external and fiscal position is strengthening the case for holding rates steady, with robust remittances, improving exports, record-high foreign exchange reserves and a contained current account position improving macroeconomic buffers and giving the SBP room to hold at its upcoming MPC meeting.
The successful issuance of a $3 billion Eurobond at record-low spreads had further supported external stability, and Ashraf wrote that a slowdown in large-scale manufacturing (LSM), coupled with a decline in fuel prices since the previous MPC meeting, was also expected to support a status quo decision.
He raised his FY27 inflation forecast to 9.1% from an earlier projection, reflecting a higher oil-price assumption of $96.3 per barrel compared with $72.5 previously, maintained the FY28 forecast at 6%, and pushed back the assumed start of monetary easing to April 2027 from October 2026, citing prolonged higher oil prices and a larger-than-expected rise in wheat prices.
Dubai crude declined 15.5% since the previous MPC meeting, from $127 to $107 per barrel, reflecting improved flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the end of seasonal refinery maintenance, though renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Red Sea disruption and declining US oil inventories continue to underpin prices.
Real interest rates are expected to average 3.4% over the next 12 months, assuming normal rupee depreciation and gradual normalisation of oil prices through February 2028, with fiscal discipline improving further.

items.content:
Pakistan is building Buraq, its own large language model trained on Urdu and regional languages, and procuring sovereign compute capacity so that Pakistani data is processed within Pakistan, Federal Minister for IT and Telecom said at the Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in Seoul.
The minister told a World Bank panel on digital government service delivery that the model, and the public compute capacity behind it, form the AI layer of a programme built on four foundations, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of IT on Wednesday.
On digital identity, the National Database and Registration Authority provides verified identity to more than 100 million Pakistanis, now extended into a digital identity that authenticates citizens online and records and enforces consent. On payments, the State Bank's Raast instant payment rail turns an AI model's identification of a qualifying household into delivery.
On data, WASL, the national exchange layer of the Digital Public Infrastructure stack built under the World Bank-supported Digital Economy Enhancement Project, lets institutions share data with every transaction authenticated, encrypted and logged. A citizen Super App and the National Open Data Ecosystem sit on top. On safeguards, the National Data Governance Policy sets a single rulebook for classifying, sharing, protecting and publishing public data.
Governments that skip the foundations get pilots that never scale and systems citizens do not trust, she said. AI is the last layer, not the first.

The session commenced on a relatively healthy note and the KSE-100 index hit 165,845.69, up 694 points by 9.33 am. Adding to the positive tone, a committee reviewing Pakistan's Automotive and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-31 proposed a broad set of reforms to boost exports, including preferential sales tax rates for new energy vehicles (NEVs), covering both locally assembled and imported cars.
The bourse touched the intra-day high of 166,242.43 and low of 164,731.91 while mostly trading in the green. At close, the benchmark KSE-100 index posted gains of 779.34 points, or 0.47%, and settled at 165,930.99.
According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 rose 779 points (+0.5%), a partial recovery with subdued trading volumes of 130 million shares. Activity remained concentrated in refinery, investment companies and securities, and technology and communication sectors, while selective buying in power generation, commercial banks and oil and gas exploration stocks provided support.
Sector-specific performance was positive, where commercial banks, power, cement and autos contributed to the index's gains. However, weakness in Attock Refinery, Fatima Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, Fauji Cement and Millat Tractors partially offset the advance. Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated at $110/barrel, causing macroeconomic uncertainty and tempering the risk appetite.
"We expect the market to remain range bound amid cautious investor sentiment, with near-term direction driven by oil-price movements, geopolitical developments and corporate earnings," KTrade wrote.
"The market gained momentum amid renewed institutional buying, driven by optimism over intensified diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict and expectations of easing geopolitical tensions. Additionally, the prime minister's approval of the draft auto policy for 2026-31 brought auto stocks back into investors' focus," Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib wrote. The proposed auto policy aims to boost automotive exports to $6 billion through tariff rationalisation, localisation and EV incentives. The draft also envisages export-linked incentives and stricter safety standards, subject to requisite approvals. Hub Power, Habib Bank, UBL, OGDC, Mari Energies, PPL, Fauji Fertiliser, Sazgar Engineering, Lucky Cement and NCPL were the major contributors, adding 711 points to the index.
Overall trading volumes decreased to 379.9 million shares from 446.8 million a day ago. The value of traded shares stood at Rs21.3 billion.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Verifiable sales records and digital cash flows could help Pakistani small businesses overcome a major barrier to bank financing: their inability to demonstrate reliable financial performance, as digital banking platforms seek to bring undocumented businesses into the formal financial system.
A large number of Pakistan's micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) operate without formal registration or digitised accounts, making it difficult for banks to assess their creditworthiness. Consequently, lenders often demand collateral, which many small businesses cannot provide. Speaking at the launch of NEO BIZ, a digital banking service for SMEs, Mashreq Bank Pakistan CEO Muhammad Hamayun Sajjad said businesses often maintained bookkeeping records that banks did not consider reliable enough for lending decisions.
Pakistan has approximately 7.14 million MSMEs, contributing nearly 40% to gross domestic product (GDP), 30% to exports and employing more than 80% of the non-agricultural workforce. However, outstanding SME financing stood at around Rs882 billion as of December 2025, according to figures cited at the event.
Digital-first banking models could help bridge this gap by creating verifiable records of business transactions, including sales, payments and collections. Banks could use these records to assess turnover, analyse cash-flow patterns and evaluate repayment capacity, potentially enabling creditworthy businesses without conventional financial statements to access loans.
However, digital records alone would not guarantee financing, as lenders would still need to assess profitability, liabilities and business risks. NEO BIZ like services offer digital business account opening and management, payments and collections. Its broader roadmap includes transaction analytics, invoicing, bookkeeping, payroll solutions and business debit and virtual cards.
The planned development also includes cash-flow-based financing, tax facilitation and supply-chain services. Whether these features translate into increased lending will depend on their implementation and banks' credit policies. "Pakistan's SME sector is both dynamic and under-served, with significant gaps in access, awareness and digital capability," Sajjad said, adding that the platform was intended to simplify banking and reduce reliance on physical channels.
The initiative comes amid a longstanding debate over whether banks' substantial exposure to government borrowing crowds out private-sector lending. Banks have argued that the relationship is not straightforward, maintaining that they can obtain liquidity through the State Bank of Pakistan open market operations (OMOs) while holding government securities and extending credit to businesses.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Electronic Arts (EA) plans to lay off 400 employees, close its BioWare studio and cancel the next "Mass Effect" game, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.
The layoffs will affect 3% of the US video game publisher’s workforce, including 50 employees at BioWare, the studio behind the popular "Mass Effect" and "Dragon Age" franchises.
In an internal letter, EA executives said the company reviewed its operations and decided to cancel several projects to reduce costs.
Read: Saudi-led consortium finalises $55b acquisition of gaming giant EA
“Across our portfolio, we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth,” they wrote.
EA will also cancel a planned game in "The Sims" franchise, code-named "Project Lotus", while reducing the team developing the skateboarding game “skate”.
The company said it would continue investing in its sports games, “Apex Legends”, “Battlefield” and upcoming “Star Wars” and Marvel titles.
Founded in 1995 and acquired by EA in 2007, BioWare struggled in recent years with disappointing game releases and declining sales.
The restructuring follows EA’s $55 billion Saudi-led buyout in August, which took the company private and added $18 billion in debt.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari on Wednesday rejected the criticism surrounding the alleged police encounter in which a man accused of killing a 15-year-old boy was himself killed, categorically denying that Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz had ordered the Punjab Crime Control Department (CCD) to carry out encounters and asserting that the provincial government stood with the oppressed, not the oppressors.
The suspect, Tauqeer Nazir, had allegedly chased Waseem Abbas in his car after a dispute over work and run him over in a private housing society in Multan on Monday. He was arrested and handed over to police on a four-day physical remand by a judicial magistrate the following day. Earlier today, police said the suspect fled custody and was then killed by his accomplices when a police party tried to re-arrest him.
Hours before the incident, the prime suspect in the case involving the death by suicide of former International Islamic University Islamabad student Laiba Ejaz also died after being wounded by gunfire allegedly by his accomplices during an attack on a police team in Islamabad. The developments were met with criticism, with calls for justice through the legal route and the courts.
Read: HRCP calls for independent probe into Waseem Abbas case, expresses concern over alleged extrajudicial killing of prime suspect
In an interview on local television programme Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath about the killing of Multan incident's primary suspect, the minister was asked about hundreds of alleged extrajudicial killings by the CCD, in which the main suspect was reportedly killed while accomplices escaped, rejecting the suggestion that this pattern occurred in every case.
She said that even when a suspect was killed, the remaining suspects were subsequently traced, arrested and brought before the police.
“When a suspect is killed, the investigation slows down a little. When suspects flee, it takes some time to trace them. But this does not mean that this happens in every incident,” she said.
Asked whether the chief minister had directly ordered the CCD to carry out encounters against such suspects, the minister categorically denied it.
“Why would the chief minister order an encounter? It is not as if she has foreknowledge of such incidents,” she said.
“The state has a responsibility to stand with the oppressed. You may consider this a mistake on the part of the state or an allegation against it; you may call it whatever you like, but the Punjab government does not stand with the oppressor. It stands with the oppressed,” she said.
She added that there was no backdoor for the powerful in the province to evade the law or avoid facing legal proceedings.
Also Read: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in CCD encounter
Bokhari said an investigation had revealed that the Multan incident suspect was short-tempered and ill-mannered and had treated Abbas harshly. She said the boy had tried to flee three times but was caught each time.
She said the suspect’s actions demonstrated his mindset, alleging that he chased the teenager and killed him while the latter was attempting to escape through a gate. The minister added that the brutality was such that the victim’s face had become unrecognisable.
Bokhari further alleged that Nazir was a violent person who did not treat his own children properly and subjected them to violence as well.
The minister acknowledged that he had no previous criminal record and that, given the evidence against him, including CCTV footage, a court could have sentenced him. However, she said, he chose to flee rather than face trial.
“These are criminal-minded people. He could have been punished by a court, but if someone tries to escape from the court, or his accomplices help him flee, what can the police do?” she said.
Read: Primary suspect in Laiba Ejaz suicide case dies after being shot by accomplices: police
When asked about a post on X by PML-N MPA and Punjab government official Hina Pervez Butt that was later deleted, Bokhari questioned the seriousness of the former’s statements.
“I do not want to talk about her, but she has posted such things before, perhaps out of a lack of seriousness. She has also made statements that created problems for her and caused embarrassment for the government,” she said.
Earlier in the day, Hina had shared screenshots of a television report about the Multan encounter on X, drawing criticism for her supportive remarks.
“This is Maryam Nawaz sahiba’s government; justice is served immediately here,” she wrote in a post that was later deleted amid criticism over its perceived endorsement of an extrajudicial killing under the provincial government’s watch.
Bokhari said cases involving organised crime were referred to the CCD rather than the regular police to ensure more effective investigation and prosecution and to meet all legal requirements for delivering justice.
She said the CCD had arrested hundreds, possibly thousands, of criminals, adding that public discussion should also focus on those who had been prosecuted and punished rather than only on the few hundred suspects who had allegedly tried to flee.
The minister reiterated that the chief minister had not ordered any encounter, adding that the government stood with the oppressed rather than the oppressors.
On judicial reforms, Bokhari said Pakistan was among the few countries with a large number of judicial laws, but the key issue was their implementation.
She added that the chief minister was also working to revamp the prosecution system and that considerable progress had been made in this regard.
Allegations of extrajudicial killings and increasingly unlawful conduct by Punjab’s CCD have long been a source of concern for human rights organisations, which have repeatedly raised the issue.
According to figures released by the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan in June, the organisation had documented 808 police ‘encounters’ since the CCD was established in April 2025, in which at least 1,100 suspects were killed.
Earlier today, it expressed concern over Abbas's killing and the subsequent death of the primary suspect in an alleged police encounter, calling for an independent and transparent investigation into the case.
The commission said extrajudicial killings violated the right to due process and deprived victims and their families of the opportunity to establish the truth and seek justice.
It added that the perception that such killings were an acceptable means of controlling crime suggested that vengeance without accountability was being prioritised over justice.
The HRCP called for an independent and transparent investigation into the case and urged the authorities to bring an end to extrajudicial killings in all forms.

items.author: APP
items.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Wednesday handed Rs5 million to the family of late student Laiba Ejaz during a visit to her residence to offer condolences and brief the family on progress in the case.
Laiba, who had aspired to study at a top US university, was found hanging from a tree near a road in Islamabad on October 9, after her family allegedly lost around Rs7 million to a consultant who had promised to secure her admission and a scholarship.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the inspector general of Islamabad police and the chief commissioner to take immediate action against the suspect. Naqvi also vowed to look into the case personally. The primary suspect in the case died after being wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices during an exchange of fire with police in Islamabad a day ago.
Laiba's father told The Express Tribune that the interior minister handed him Rs5 million recovered by the police from the primary suspect.
Naqvi was accompanied by Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry during the visit to Laiba's residence in G-10, Islamabad.
Read: PM takes notice of gold medallist's suicide
Naqvi expressed his condolences to the bereaved family and offered prayers.
The interior minister informed Laiba's family about the progress made in the investigation of her case/
“The entire team worked day and night on the Laiba Ejaz case. Fulfilling the promise made to you was our duty,” Naqvi said.
Read More: Primary suspect in Laiba Ejaz suicide case dies after being shot by accomplices: police
Laiba's father expressed his gratitude to PM Shehbaz and the interior minister for their support and efforts in the case.
“We had heard that the state is like a mother. Today, we have come to believe it,” he said.
Suspect killed
According to a police spokesperson, the primary suspect, identified as Muhammad Nauman, was in custody and was being taken to a location for recovery on the basis of information provided by him when the incident occurred.
The spokesperson said four of Nauman’s accomplices, travelling on two motorcycles, had been lying in wait along the route. They opened indiscriminate fire on the police team in an attempt to secure his release.
Nauman was wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices, the spokesperson said, adding that police personnel remained unharmed due to their bulletproof jackets and other precautionary measures.
The injured suspect was taken to a hospital for medical treatment but later succumbed to his injuries, the spokesperson confirmed.
Search operations were under way to arrest the remaining suspects, according to the police.
The Federal Investigation Agency’s (FIA) Anti-Human Trafficking Circle in Islamabad had registered a case against Nauman and Fatima Sarwar under Sections 419 (cheating), 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property) and 109 (abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Sections 18 and 22 of the Emigration Ordinance, 1979.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly acted in connivance to deceive Laiba with promises of a US visa and scholarship. They allegedly received a total of Rs9.3 million from the family.
The FIA said the suspects allegedly prepared fake scholarship award letters, university admission offer letters and fee payment receipts to keep the family under the impression that the process was genuine. Of the total amount, Rs2.9m was transferred through Laiba’s personal bank account, while the remaining sum was received in cash, according to the agency.
Also Read: Islamabad court grants five-day remand of suspect in Laiba suicide case
Laiba's family stated that she had aspired to enrol at Harvard University for further studies and that they had made significant financial sacrifices to secure Laiba’s academic future and fulfil her dream. Laiba’s father sold his plot and pitched in Rs2.1 million from the sale’s proceeds, while her mother sold her gold jewellery.
According to the family, the suspect who reportedly defrauded them claimed to be an accounts officer at the Islamabad High Court and at other times presented himself as an employee of the superior judiciary or an officer of a sensitive institution. The family claimed that despite the substantial payment, the promises regarding admission and the scholarship given to Laiba were never fulfilled.
Laiba’s maternal uncle, Rana Amjad, stated that the Harvard University admission letter, scholarship letter and other documents provided by the suspect turned out to be fake upon verification.
He said that Laiba suffered severe distress and mental anguish after the alleged fraud came to light. Her family demanded a thorough investigation into the matter, the arrest of all individuals involved in the alleged fraud, and the recovery of the money.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima Khawaja has said that Pakistan must establish strong digital infrastructure before expanding the use of artificial intelligence (AI). Shaza Fatima shared these views during a discussion on digital public infrastructure and AI at the Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in South Korea.
Speaking on the third day of the summit, Shaza Fatima explained that AI represents the final layer of digital development. She stressed that countries need reliable digital systems, secure data-sharing mechanisms, and effective public services to make the best use of AI.
Shaza Fatima Highlights Pakistan’s Digital Transformation at Digital Summit 2026 in South Korea
The minister highlighted Pakistan’s ongoing efforts to build its national digital public infrastructure. Under a World Bank initiative to support the development of the digital economy, Pakistan is working to establish its first national digital public infrastructure system.
She said the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) provides verified digital identity services to more than 10 million Pakistanis. This identity system serves as an important foundation for delivering digital public services.
The minister also highlighted Raast, the State Bank of Pakistan’s instant payment system, which enables digital payments across the country. She said such systems are essential for improving access to financial services and supporting the growth of the digital economy.
Shaza Fatima also discussed Wasil, Pakistan’s national data exchange system. The platform enables government institutions to share information securely under clear rules and procedures. It aims to improve coordination between public sector organizations and make digital services more efficient.
According to the minister, work is also underway to develop a central mobile application for citizens and a national open data system on top of Wasil. These initiatives are expected to make public information and government services more accessible.
She further noted that the Pakistan Digital Authority has issued a National Data Governance Policy to establish a clear framework for managing and sharing data. The policy is intended to promote responsible data use and provide clear rules for digital governance.
See Also: Pakistan Highlights Sovereign AI Vision at Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in Seoul
The minister emphasized that Pakistan’s approach to AI would keep human decision-making at the center. She said AI would assist people in making decisions but would not independently determine anyone’s rights or entitlements.
This approach aims to ensure that AI supports public services without replacing human judgment in decisions that directly affect citizens.
Pakistan is also working to develop sovereign AI infrastructure and Buraq, a Pakistani language model designed to support the Urdu language. These efforts could help the country build local AI capabilities and develop technology that better serves its linguistic and digital needs.
The Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 provides a platform for countries to discuss the future of AI, digital governance, and public digital infrastructure. Pakistan’s participation reflects its efforts to strengthen digital public services, improve data management, and build the foundations needed for wider AI adoption.

items.summary:

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.71 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 31 paisas per litre for October 22.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs379.31 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs390.11 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and HSD by 88 paisas and 53 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 21.
Read: Govt increases petrol by 88 paisas, diesel by 53 paisas per litre for Oct 21
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices were little changed on Wednesday ‌as investors weighed possible progress toward Russia-Ukraine talks against declining US oil stocks and a lack of US-Iran dialogue.
Brent crude futures gained 27 cents, or 0.2%, to $109.04 a barrel by 10:50 am ET (1450 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 11 cents, or 0.1%, to $97.72.
"Crude futures are trading both sides of unchanged this morning but well below the overnight highs as attacks in the ​Strait of Hormuz look to be continuing with at least two more ships being struck overnight," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of ​trading at BOK Financial, in a note to clients.

items.title: SBI Reports Suspected Data Exposure Affecting 3,897 Customer Records
items.summary: SBI received alerts about the suspected exposure on October 16 from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In. Its preliminary review covered around 375,000 records available on the dark web, of which 3,897 contained personally identifiable information. The exposed details reportedly included names, contact information, residential addresses and identifiers linked to branches and loan records. SBI activated its cyber incident response procedures and appointed an independent CERT-In-empanelled agency to investigate the incident and assess potential risks.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Global shipments of foldable smartphone displays are expected to increase significantly in 2026, with a growing interest in wide foldable devices. Market research firm Omdia forecasts a 44% rise in foldable display shipments this year, following a 12% decline in 2025.
According to the forecast, manufacturers will ship around 29 million foldable displays in 2026. However, this figure refers specifically to the inner screens used in foldable smartphones, not the final devices. Display shipments and smartphone sales may differ because manufacturers usually ship components before completing and releasing their products.
Despite this difference, the forecast suggests that 2026 could be a strong year for the foldable smartphone market.
Foldable Display Shipments to Increase 44% in 2026 as Wide Foldables Gain Popularity
One of the most notable findings in Omdia’s report is the growing demand for wide foldable displays. These displays are expected to account for 44% of total foldable display shipments in 2026, putting them close to half of the market.
The foldable smartphone market currently includes three main designs: wide foldables, book-style devices with larger and squarer inner screens, and compact flip-style phones.
The increasing popularity of wide foldables is expected to reshape competition among smartphone manufacturers. Devices such as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 and Apple’s reported iPhone Duo are among the products driving interest in this design.
As more companies explore wider foldable phones, manufacturers may place greater emphasis on screen proportions and usability to attract consumers.
Samsung Display Expected to Lead the Market
Samsung Display is expected to benefit considerably from the growing demand for foldable screens. According to Omdia, the company could capture 66% of the foldable display market in 2026.
Samsung Display manufactures panels for both the Galaxy Z Fold8 and Apple’s iPhone Duo, putting it in a strong position as demand for wide foldables increases.
Meanwhile, competing display manufacturers, including BOE, China Star, Tianma and Visionox, are expected to see their market shares decline.
The forecast highlights Samsung Display’s strong position in the foldable screen industry, particularly as more smartphone brands consider adopting wider foldable designs.
Chinese Manufacturers May Increase Competition
Although demand for foldable smartphones remains weak in China, Omdia expects competition to increase as more Chinese manufacturers enter the wide foldable segment.
Huawei was among the early companies to introduce this form factor. However, other manufacturers appear to be taking a more serious interest in the design as its market potential becomes clearer.
Greater participation from Chinese brands could lead to more product choices and increased competition in the coming years.
LTPO Displays Expected to Dominate
Another important trend is the expected dominance of LTPO display technology in foldable smartphones. Omdia forecasts that most foldable displays manufactured in 2026 will use LTPO rather than LTPS technology.
LTPO displays offer more precise refresh-rate control, allowing screens to adjust their refresh rates according to the content being displayed. This can help reduce power consumption while maintaining a smooth viewing experience.
Although LTPO panels generally cost more than LTPS displays, their benefits make them an attractive option for premium foldable smartphones.
Since foldable devices already occupy the higher end of the smartphone market. Manufacturers are likely to continue using advanced display technologies to improve performance and user experience.
Foldable Smartphone Market Outlook
Omdia’s forecast points to renewed growth in the foldable display market during 2026. Rising demand for wide foldables, Samsung Display’s strong position and the wider adoption of LTPO technology are expected to shape the industry.
However, display shipment figures do not directly represent the number of foldable smartphones sold. Actual device sales will depend on product availability, pricing and consumer demand.
If the forecast proves accurate, 2026 could mark an important step forward for foldable smartphones, with wider designs becoming a more significant part of the market.

items.content:
San Francisco-based enterprise AI startup AuxoAI has raised $20.7 Mn (over ₹195 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by NTTVC, a Silicon Valley VC firm backed by Japanese telco NTT.
Industry executives including Norwest Venture Partners’ George Still Jr, ServiceNow CPO and COO Amit Zavery, and Charlesbank Capital Partners’ MD Giacomo Santina also joined the startup’s cap table.
AuxoAI plans to utilise the fresh capital to deepen ecosystem partnerships, expand its talent pool of forward deployed engineers (FDEs), and invest in its proprietary technology and AI-native delivery capabilities, including its Damia platform.
“Our vision is to build a new kind of AI company – one that combines human expertise, enterprise context and engineering to stay with the problem from the first idea through measurable outcomes in production. This investment gives us the opportunity to scale that model globally,” cofounders Arvinder Pal Singh, Amaresh Tripathy and Kabir Singh said in a joint statement.
Founded in 2023, AuxoAI offers an enterprise AI platform that pairs its AI strategists and engineers with enterprise client teams to build custom AI workflows.
It helps enterprises accelerate AI deployment with Damia, a platform it describes as an “AI workbench for enterprise delivery”. It combines a pre-built skill catalogue with tools that capture institutional knowledge to build a context layer.
AuxoAI says that it is an AI-native Google Gemini Enterprise Transformation partner and an AWS advanced-tier partner. The San Francisco-based startup operates engineering and operational hubs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
Over the past three years, the startup claims that it has worked with over 40 clients across manufacturing, healthcare, consumer goods, and telecom sectors to turn AI into measurable business outcomes.
Early adopters, such as marketing firm Athlonearth and restaurant group Fogo de Chao, have deployed AuxoAI’s infrastructure to automate manual tasks, make better informed decisions, and shorten strategy-to-launch timelines.
As enterprises increasingly turn to AI adoption to boost productivity, FDEs are becoming increasingly critical for customising AI deployments to the company’s needs. According to staffing firm TeamLease Digital, demand for FDEs has jumped nearly 800% over the past year.
Startups such as Bolna use FDEs to accelerate enterprise onboarding and shape product development. While better automation could eventually reduce deployment complexity, fragmented enterprise systems make FDEs increasingly important to AI adoption.

items.author: Anirudh Trivedi
items.content:
For India’s D2C brands, quick commerce has opened up another route to millions of consumers. But turning that access into profitable growth remains a challenge. Platform commissions, advertising expenses, inventory requirements and frequent discounting can quickly erode the margins brands earn from the channel.
For Gurugram-based personal hygiene brand Pee Safe, however, quick commerce has become one of its most profitable distribution channels, accounting for nearly 40% of domestic revenue and delivering double-digit contribution margins, compared with single-digit margins on traditional ecommerce.
Getting there was far from straightforward.
Pee Safe spent nearly two years struggling to keep its products consistently available on quick commerce platforms. Its existing distributor network could not meet the channel’s replenishment requirements, while products and pack sizes that performed well on ecommerce did not necessarily find buyers on 10-minute delivery apps.
The company eventually overhauled its supply chain, changed how it managed its product assortment and used the consumer awareness it had built over the years to limit its dependence on paid advertising.
The result is a distribution mix in which quick commerce now contributes 40% of domestic revenue, followed by D2C and ecommerce at 35% and offline retail at 25%.
But the significance of Pee Safe’s experience goes beyond this revenue split. It shows how quick commerce economics can differ considerably depending on whether a brand uses the channel to create consumer demand or fulfil demand that already exists.
In an exclusive conversation for The Quick Commerce Code by Inc42 and Nitro Commerce, Pee Safe cofounder Rithish Kumar discussed how the brand built its quick commerce operations, the changes that improved its margins and the challenges of extending that growth into new markets.
From An Early Bet On Instant Delivery To Fixing A Broken Supply Chain
Pee Safe’s origins predate India’s quick commerce boom.
The idea emerged in 2013 after cofounder Srijana Bagaria developed a urinary tract infection following a road trip. The experience prompted Srijana and Vikas Bagaria to explore products that could address hygiene concerns associated with public washrooms.
After several months of product development, they created a portable, alcohol-based toilet seat sanitiser spray that dried quickly after application. The product became the foundation of Pee Safe, which formally launched in 2017 and subsequently expanded into feminine hygiene, intimate care, personal care and wellness.
The brand was entering categories where consumer education and trust were particularly important. Alongside established multinational companies, newer brands such as Sirona, Nua and Plush were also competing for a share of India’s evolving feminine hygiene market.
For Pee Safe, building distribution was central to taking its products beyond the consumers who were already familiar with the brand.
That also explains why the company began experimenting with faster delivery relatively early.
In 2018, Pee Safe listed its products on Grofers, the grocery delivery platform subsequently rebranded as Blinkit. The proposition was different from conventional ecommerce, where consumers often waited a day or more for delivery.
The pandemic-driven acceleration of doorstep deliveries made the channel increasingly relevant. As Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart expanded, Pee Safe saw an opportunity to make products such as sanitary pads, toilet seat sanitisers and other personal care essentials available closer to the time of purchase.
However, the operating model behind its early quick commerce expansion was not designed for the channel.
Pee Safe initially relied on the same distributors that serviced neighbourhood retailers and modern trade outlets to supply quick-commerce platforms.
For distributors accustomed to servicing established retail relationships, managing a much wider assortment, holding inventory and frequently replenishing platform warehouses presented a different set of demands.
Consequently, Pee Safe frequently struggled with stock availability.
The problem wasn’t necessarily a lack of consumer demand. Products that customers wanted were not always available when they searched for them.
By late 2023 and early 2024, the company began changing its approach.
Instead of depending on traditional distributors to manage quick commerce supplies, Pee Safe moved to a model of supplying platform warehouses through third-party warehousing partners, gaining greater control over inventory planning and replenishment.
According to Kumar, the restructuring materially improved fulfilment.
The company reported fill rates of 97-98% during a recent quarter, while on-shelf availability for its core products exceeded 90%. It targets availability above 80% for products outside its core assortment.
These metrics capture different aspects of fulfilment: fill rate measures how much of a platform’s order a brand supplies, whereas on-shelf availability indicates whether customers can actually purchase the product.
The distinction matters because products that remain unavailable on an app cannot generate sales, regardless of the demand for them.
Pee Safe now has a dedicated team of seven to eight people managing quick commerce operations. Kumar monitors performance dashboards daily and, at times, hourly.
The channel has also changed the company’s working-capital cycle. According to Kumar, quick commerce platforms typically settle payments within 30 days, sometimes sooner, compared with longer cycles in traditional and modern trade.
Faster collections offer an advantage, although they do not eliminate the investment required to maintain inventory across warehouses and fulfilment centres.
The operational improvements are also reflected in third-party availability data.
An analysis by Zodiac AI by Nitro Commerce found that Pee Safe maintained average on-shelf availability of 94.7% on Blinkit during 1-25 August 2026, although availability differed across cities.
For Pee Safe, fixing product availability was only the first part of making quick commerce work. The next challenge was understanding which products consumers wanted to buy through the channel and at what price points.
Why Pee Safe Had To Rethink Its Products For Quick Commerce
When Pee Safe began expanding on quick commerce, it had roughly five to six SKUs on the channel. Today, its assortment has grown to more than 60 products across platforms.
But expanding the catalogue did not mean transferring the same packs and pricing that worked on Amazon or in offline retail.
One of the clearest examples came from acne patches.
Pee Safe initially offered a 60-piece pack priced at ₹499, but the product struggled to gain traction. The company subsequently introduced a smaller 12-piece pack at ₹99, which became one of its leading SKUs in the category.
The smaller pack reduced the upfront commitment and suited consumers looking for a quick solution or trying the product for the first time.
Sanitary pads presented a different pattern.
Rather than gravitating towards smaller packs, customers were frequently purchasing larger quantities. Pee Safe responded by moving from a 12-pad pack priced at approximately ₹199 to a 30-pad pack costing around ₹399.
The contrasting experiences highlighted an important distinction: consumers were not necessarily looking for smaller or cheaper products on quick commerce. Their preferred pack sizes depended on the category and the reason for purchasing.
According to Kumar, the ₹100-₹150 price bracket can work well as an entry point across several categories, but the company uses platform-level demand data to adjust its assortment.
The wider beauty and personal care market shows similar differences in purchasing behaviour.
Redseer’s Quick Commerce BPC Brand Index for January-March 2026 found that 50 gm/ml sunscreen packs accounted for 78% of quick-commerce sales for a leading brand, compared with roughly 50% of its ecommerce sales. Larger 80 gm/ml packs accounted for just 2% of the brand’s quick-commerce sales.
Large FMCG companies, including Parle, ITC and Hindustan Unilever, have also developed channel-specific packs and price points to cater to quick-commerce consumers while differentiating their online and offline assortments.
For Pee Safe, the lesson was to approach quick commerce as a distinct retail channel rather than another outlet for its existing inventory.
The brand uses consumer demand, product movement and regional purchasing patterns to determine which SKUs deserve more inventory and where new products should be introduced.
However, the company did not disclose SKU-level sales uplifts or contribution margins, making it difficult to quantify precisely how much the assortment changes contributed to overall revenue or profitability.
That leaves another important part of the story: why Pee Safe is able to generate stronger margins on quick commerce despite the additional costs associated with the channel.
Why Quick Commerce Is More Profitable For Pee Safe Than Ecommerce
One of the biggest challenges for consumer brands on quick commerce is the cost of getting discovered.
A brand entering Blinkit, Zepto or Swiggy Instamart may need to spend on advertising, discounting and promotional visibility while also absorbing platform and fulfilment costs.
For products priced at ₹150-₹200, those expenses can quickly make the economics unattractive.
Kumar estimates that advertising costs in some categories can reach ₹8,000-₹10,000 per thousand impressions, while additional discounts of 10-15% can further reduce the amount brands retain from each sale.
Pee Safe, however, had an advantage when it expanded on quick commerce: a consumer base that had already discovered the brand elsewhere.
After years of building awareness and repeat consumption through Amazon and other channels, Pee Safe found that many quick commerce customers already knew which products they wanted.
Rather than relying entirely on advertisements to generate discovery, consumers were searching for Pee Safe directly.
That distinction has been central to its profitability.
According to Kumar, a substantial share of the brand’s quick commerce revenue comes from organic demand, helping it limit advertising expenditure and avoid excessive discounting.
The company estimates repeat-purchase rates ranging from 20% to 60%, depending on the product category.
Together, existing brand recognition, repeat purchasing and tighter control over promotions have helped Pee Safe generate double-digit contribution margins on quick commerce, compared with single-digit contribution margins on traditional ecommerce.
There is, however, an important distinction between channel-level contribution margins and company-wide profitability.
Contribution margins measure what remains from sales after the costs included in the company’s calculation. They do not necessarily account for every corporate expense, brand-building investment or other cost incurred by the business.
Pee Safe has not disclosed a detailed like-for-like breakdown of platform commissions, advertising, logistics and warehousing expenses across its sales channels.
Nor has it quantified how much of the demand generated on quick commerce is genuinely incremental, rather than shifting purchases from its existing ecommerce channels.
This matters because the profitability of an individual channel can partly reflect brand-building expenditure incurred elsewhere.
Pee Safe’s experience nevertheless points to a potentially important distinction for emerging D2C businesses: quick commerce may be more effective at profitably fulfilling established demand than at creating demand for an unfamiliar brand from scratch.
For Pee Safe, the next test is whether those economics can hold as the company expands its product portfolio and reaches consumers in markets where brand recognition may be weaker.
Why Expansion Beyond Metros Requires Another Playbook
Pee Safe’s quick commerce footprint now extends to more than 6,500 dark stores across 250 cities through quick commerce platforms, according to Kumar.
But distribution has not translated into uniform demand across markets.
Nearly 50% of the company’s quick commerce sales now come from Tier II cities and smaller markets, while southern and western India together contribute approximately 60% of the channel’s revenue.
The expansion has brought the brand into 25+ markets such as Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Lucknow, Dehradun, Indore, Nagpur, Bhopal, Guwahati and Patna.
These markets have required Pee Safe to rethink which products it launches and how it markets them.
Instead of making its entire catalogue available immediately, the company typically enters newer cities with familiar categories such as sanitary pads, where consumer demand is already established.
Products that require more education, such as menstrual cups, are introduced more selectively. Local purchasing patterns also influence these decisions.
Kumar cited stronger demand for menstrual cups in Kerala and panty liners in Maharashtra and Gujarat, illustrating how category preferences can differ across geographies.
The company uses regional and pin code-level data to identify products underperforming relative to national benchmarks and direct advertising spend toward specific markets.
Content is another part of this approach.
Approximately 80% of Pee Safe’s influencer content is produced in regional languages, allowing the brand to communicate with consumers beyond its initial metropolitan customer base.
The company combines this content with geographically targeted marketing to encourage consumers to purchase its products through quick commerce platforms.
Such spending also highlights the limitations of a purely organic-demand model. While existing brand recognition has supported Pee Safe’s margins, reaching new customers and developing unfamiliar product categories may require additional investment.
Interestingly, Pee Safe is now applying elements of its Indian quick commerce strategy abroad.
Can Pee Safe Sustain Its Quick Commerce Advantage?
Pee Safe’s overall financial performance provides useful context for its quick-commerce ambitions.
According to Inc42’s financial data, the company generated ₹82.5 Cr in revenue in FY25, up approximately 44% from ₹57.3 Cr in FY24. It reported a net loss of around ₹4 Cr in FY25.
Kumar said the company’s revenue grew by approximately 60% in FY26, although the financial statements were still being audited at the time of the conversation.
For FY27, he expects revenue growth to exceed 100%. The quick commerce business forms a major part of that ambition.
According to Kumar, Pee Safe’s quick commerce revenue reached an annualised run rate of ₹150 Cr in September 2026. The figure represents the annualised pace of sales at that point, rather than revenue recognised over a completed financial year.
In January 2026, Pee Safe also secured $32 Mn in a Series C round led by OrbiMed, comprising a combination of primary capital and secondary share sales. Its investor base has also included Alkemi Venture Partners and Venture Catalysts.
The funding is intended to support expansion across offline retail, quick commerce, ecommerce and brand marketing.
However, pursuing growth across multiple channels will also require Pee Safe to manage inventory investments, advertising expenditure and competition from both established consumer companies and emerging brands.
Private labels are another potential challenge.
As quick-commerce platforms expand their own product portfolios, they could compete more directly with brands selling through their marketplaces.
Kumar believes Pee Safe’s position in intimate and feminine hygiene offers some protection because consumers place considerable importance on trust when purchasing these products.
“Private labels can be threatening when you don’t have high defensibility. A platform building a private label in women’s hygiene faces a high trust deficit as it takes years to build, and Pee Safe has a head start on that,” he said.
That confidence will be tested as competition increases and platforms develop their own capabilities in categories currently served by third-party brands.
Pee Safe is also looking beyond quick commerce for its next phase of expansion.
While offline retail already contributes a quarter of domestic revenue, the company intends to deepen its presence in the channel. Kumar also sees scope to improve its performance on traditional ecommerce, where he believes the brand remains underrepresented.
The strategy is to expand the categories already demonstrating traction and capture a larger share of those markets, rather than relying exclusively on new product launches.
For Pee Safe, quick commerce has evolved from a difficult distribution experiment into a major revenue contributor. But its experience also shows that getting listed on a platform is only a starting point.
The harder work lies in making products consistently available, matching assortments to buying behaviour and ensuring that the cost of selling does not exceed the value of the demand a brand captures.
Whether Pee Safe can preserve that balance as it expands across categories and geographies will determine how much of its next phase of growth quick commerce can profitably support.
[Edited By Shishir Parasher]

However, 17 workers of the sugar mills remained missing, prompting residents to take to the streets and block traffic on the Indus Highway in protest.
Residents staged a protest at Paroa Adda, blocking the main Indus Highway to demand the safe recovery of the missing workers.
Police said an operation was underway to recover the abducted persons and that several teams had been formed for the purpose.
The incident has triggered fear and panic in the area, while the families of the missing workers remain deeply distressed over the fate of their loved ones.

items.author: Asif Mehmood
items.content:
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) on Wednesday expressed concern over the alleged murder of 15-year-old Waseem Abbas in Multan and the subsequent death of the primary suspect in an alleged police encounter, calling for an independent and transparent investigation into the case.
The suspect, Tauqeer Nazir, had allegedly chased Abbas in his car after a dispute over work and run him over in a private housing society in Multan on October 19. He was arrested and handed over to police on a four-day physical remand by a judicial magistrate the following day. Later today, police said the suspect fled custody and was then killed by his accomplices when a police party tried to re-arrest him.
According to the HRCP, Abbas was reportedly chased and run over by his employer. The subsequent death of the suspect in an alleged police encounter has raised serious questions about the state’s approach to protecting human life and upholding legal safeguards.
The commission said extrajudicial killings violate the right to due process and deprive victims and their families of the opportunity to establish the truth and seek justice.
It added that the perception that such killings are an acceptable means of controlling crime suggests that vengeance without accountability is being prioritised over justice.
The HRCP called for an independent and transparent investigation into the case and urged the authorities to bring an end to extrajudicial killings in all forms.
Bonded Labour Liberation Front seeks probe into orphanages
Separately, the Bonded Labour Liberation Front Pakistan demanded an investigation into Abbas's death and action against unregistered orphanages allegedly involved in the exploitation of children.
Read: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in CCD encounter
According to a press release issued by the organisation’s president, Syeda Ghulam Fatima Gilani, Abbas was living at an orphanage in Multan and had been sent to work at a workshop, where he died after being run over by a vehicle. The organisation termed the incident a killing rather than an accident and called for legal action against those responsible.
The organisation alleged that more than 52 unregistered orphanages across Punjab were sending children to brick kilns and workshops for labour. It also accused the relevant labour officer in Multan and an official of the Child Protection and Welfare Bureau (CPWB) of negligence and demanded action against them.
The organisation called for strict action against unregistered orphanages and registered institutions involved in child exploitation, monthly surprise inspections of all orphanages, and the creation of an online record of children residing in these facilities.
It also urged the Lahore High Court to take notice of the incident.
“Wasim should have been in school, not at a workshop,” Gilani said, warning that the organisation would approach the High Court if no action was taken within seven days.
The case
The first information report (FIR), registered on Monday named Nazir and Amjad Ali as suspects and invoked Sections 302 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code, relating to murder and acts done by several persons in furtherance of their common intention. It alleged that the two men pursued Abbas in a car and deliberately ran him over, causing fatal head injuries.
According to the FIR, Sub-Inspector Liaquat Ali Bhatti was on patrol with police personnel in Royal Orchard when a man identified as Mukhtiar Ahmed approached them at around 4:35pm. Mukhtiar told police that his cousin, Abbas, had been working as an electrician for the suspects and that they had allegedly subjected him to violence and threatened to kill him. The report stated that Abbas had fled to a neighbouring street to escape the alleged abuse, while the two suspects pursued him in a vehicle. Police said they saw Abbas running in fear, followed by a Honda vehicle bearing registration number BVE-474.
The FIR alleged that the suspects ran the vehicle over Abbas with the intention of killing him. His head struck a pillar at the gate of house 3-A, crushing his skull and causing severe injuries. He died at the scene.
Two residents, Saqlain Raza and Syed Naseem Abbas, were named as witnesses in the FIR. According to the report, they told police that Abbas had passed by shortly before the incident, saying that the suspects wanted to kill him and that he was running to save his life.
The FIR further stated that the vehicle stopped after the incident and the suspects attempted to flee. Nazir was apprehended at the scene, while Ali escaped. Police took the vehicle into custody as evidence.
Mukhtiar told police that Abbas wanted to leave the job because of the alleged violence and feared for his safety. The FIR alleged that the suspects pursued him over his decision to leave and acted in concert to kill him.

items.author: Amiya Johar
items.content:
Jio Platforms’ $3.2 billion IPO was reportedly fully subscribed within around 100 minutes of opening on Wednesday (21 October), as investors rushed to take part in India’s largest share sale.
Sources told Reuters institutional investors covered their allocated portion within 10 minutes of bidding opening, although demand from retail investors was slower. Around a third of the shares are reserved for retail buyers.
“It’s the fastest in the history of India,” a source said.
Reliance Industries’ telecoms unit is offering 270 million shares priced at between INR1,065 ($11.28) and INR1,119 apiece, with the offer closing on Friday (23 October). The IPO values the business at up to $108.3 billion and marks the first public offering from billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance conglomerate in two decades.
The company plans to use most of the IPO proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm, its telecoms subsidiary, with the remainder earmarked for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditure.
Jio Platforms reported a profit of around $3.2 billion on revenue of $15.5 billion in the year to March.
The offering also comes despite a weak domestic equity market, after the country’s Nifty 50 benchmark index of 50 leading Indian companies slumped this year.
However, Indian wealth management firm SMIFS Limited noted “the long-term outlook for Jio Platforms Limited remains highly favourable, driven by sustained growth in India’s digital economy”.
According to the company, Jio Platforms will “benefit from rising 5G adoption, increasing smartphone penetration, accelerating broadband penetration, growing enterprise digitalisation and expanding demand for cloud and AI-enabled services”.
Jio’s telecoms business has more than 500 million subscribers, making it the world’s second largest telecoms operator in a single country after China Mobile. It disrupted India’s telecoms market after launching in 2016 with low-cost data plans, putting pressure on rivals Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
However, the company continues to face regulatory uncertainty and growing competition in satellite connectivity, as billionaire Elon Musk’s Starlink prepares to enter India’s market.

items.author: Staff
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
PKR 100,000 is a line many buyers hesitate to cross. Spend less and you expect compromises, spend more and you expect everything. The TECNO POVA Curve 2 5G, launched in Pakistan on October 15 at PKR 99,999, sits just under that line, and TECNO’s pitch is that it asks for no compromises: a 5G processor, an 8000mAh battery and what it calls the slimmest design among phones with a battery that size.
Here is what the phone offers, in the order most buyers care about, and what to weigh before you decide.
Performance and 5G: fast now, fast later
The phone runs on a MediaTek Dimensity 7100 5G processor, with 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. At this price, the question is less how fast it is on day one and more whether it stays that way. TECNO says it holds 90 minutes of smooth Free Fire at 60fps, helped by Ice Cooling 3.0, and that it is TÜV Rheinland certified to stay lag-free for six years. The software promise backs that up, with 2 Android version updates and 3 years of security patches.
Battery: the reason to look twice
Battery is where the POVA Curve 2 5G aims hardest. Its 8000mAh cell is meant to take you two days between charges, with more than 15 days of standby, according to TECNO. When you do need a charger, 45W fast charging takes it from empty to full in 82 minutes, and 10W reverse charging lets it power other devices.
The part buyers tend to overlook is longevity. TECNO says the battery is built for 2,000 cycles, which it describes as six years of safe use, so it shouldn’t need replacing in the time you’re likely to own the phone.
Design: the slimmest 8000mAh phone
At 7.42mm and 195g, TECNO says the POVA Curve 2 5G is the slimmest phone among those with an 8000mAh battery. That matters because a big battery usually means a bulky phone, and this one is meant to slip into a pocket and sit comfortably in the hand.
The look is inspired by interstellar spaceships, with bold, flowing lines and a minimalist finish, in Melting Silver, Mystic Purple or Storm Titanium. Corning Gorilla Glass 7i and SGS-certified 1.5m drop resistance cover everyday knocks.
Display: smooth, bright and responsive
The 6.78-inch curved AMOLED display runs at 144Hz, so scrolling and games stay smooth, and peak brightness of up to 4,500 nits keeps it readable outdoors. A 2160Hz touch sampling rate keeps touch responsive, and anti-mistouch means wet or oily hands shouldn’t cost you a tap.
The camera and extras
The camera isn’t the headline here. It’s a 50MP primary camera, a 2MP macro camera and a 13MP front camera, backed by AI tools including AI Eraser 2.0 and AI Flare Remover. The Ella voice assistant adds call translation and WhatsApp summaries, and FreeLink 2.0 keeps calls and messages going between phones within 1.5km without network coverage. If photography is your top priority, compare samples before you buy.
Price and who it suits
The POVA Curve 2 5G is available across Pakistan in 8GB RAM + 256GB ROM at PKR 99,999. It suits people who use their phone hard and are tired of chasing a charger: gamers, heavy multitaskers and anyone whose day runs longer than a typical battery.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent ‌website operators scrambling to protect their systems.
Developers of the PHP programming language said Tuesday they had identified two critical vulnerabilities, and urged users to update their sites as soon as a fix was released. They said around 1345 GMT on Wednesday that a new version fixing the vulnerabilities was live.
But with reports that hackers were exploiting the flaws to break into websites, government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland were among those that took sites offline ahead of ​the fix as a precaution.
PHP underpins large parts of the internet, raising concerns that a significant number of websites could be vulnerable to attack.
"PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, ​Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under ⁠the hood," cybersecurity company Huntress said in a blog post.
Read: US judge orders Saudi engineer held in OpenAI case
Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer of Web and cloud security firm Cloudflare, said that attacks were emerging and Cloudflare was updating its ​firewall rules as a stopgap measure.
"We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. This is a STOPGAP only. Patch as soon as PHP releases the update," he ​said on X.
Wordfence, a security plugin that protects WordPress websites, said all WordPress sites run on a PHP-installed server. It warned that automatic updates would not apply the fix and advised site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their sites.
Cybersecurity agencies in Europe, Australia, Japan and Britain have urged PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied. The Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying ​it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities.
Officials have said that all PHP versions from PHP 5 onward could be affected, although PHP has not yet disclosed which versions are ​vulnerable.
Critical software
PHP is a programming language used to run websites. When a visitor loads a page, a server running PHP assembles the content and sends it to the browser. It is free, open-source software maintained by ‌volunteers.
It is also ⁠among the most widely used software on the internet. PHP runs roughly 75% of websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs. It is the engine behind WordPress, which powers about 43% of all websites, from blogs and small business pages to government portals, online stores and news sites.
Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, said: "We don't comment on the details of security issues, but our team is prepared and has been working with the PHP security team to ensure a smooth update."
Security experts said the vulnerabilities could potentially open the door to millions of servers because so ​many websites rely on the same underlying software. ​Rather than target victims individually, attackers could scan ⁠the internet for systems running vulnerable versions of PHP.
Read more: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
AI-assisted hacking campaigns, which have proliferated in recent weeks, could magnify the threat, said Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King's College London.
"The scale is huge," Olejnik said. "And with AI, exploitation may happen instantly, on a large scale."
The risk is particularly ​acute for small websites run by individuals or organisations with limited technical resources, often on shared hosting services where customers do not directly ​manage the underlying servers. Security ⁠experts said such sites could take longer to patch and remain exposed well after fixes become available.
Mass outages
In the Netherlands, several organisations followed the example of the National Cyber Security Centre and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national soccer association KNVB, the websites of the country's five largest political parties and several hospital websites.
Danish municipal IT company Kombit said it had shut down several ⁠services, including ​the national school communication platform, a spokesperson told Reuters.
Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider ​Valtori said government public network services had been taken offline "as a precautionary measure."
France's Interior Ministry said it had temporarily taken local government administrative websites offline while awaiting a security fix.
The US cybersecurity agency CISA did not respond to emails seeking comment.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Zomato and Blinkit parent Eternal has unveiled Dark, a privacy-focused AI platform that founder Deepinder Goyal hopes to launch globally within 2026.
In Eternal’s Q2 FY27 shareholder letter, Goyal said the platform is aimed at power users, including founders, researchers, scientists, enterprises, and governments, who want to keep their conversations and research private.
Dark has been in internal use for a few months, he said, adding that its privacy features had encouraged him to share more information and explore questions he would hesitate to ask other AI assistants.
The platform uses fine-tuned frontier open-weight models running on Eternal’s own infrastructure. Unlike building a model from scratch, this approach involves adapting existing models whose trained parameters are available for developers to use and modify.
According to Goyal, Dark uses end-to-end encryption, alongside an encrypted memory management layer controlled by users, to retain context across sessions.
“We cannot read your conversations, even if we are forced to,” he said.
He positioned Dark around concerns that users’ interactions with mainstream AI assistants could be retained or accessed by others, discouraging them from sharing sensitive information.
He argued that disabling the use of conversations for model training does not, by itself, address questions around data retention, legal holds, human reviews, or third-party logging.
Eternal’s AI Ambitions
Goyal said concerns around data retention, human reviews, legal holds and third-party logging on mainstream AI platforms could limit the extent to which people use AI for sensitive or commercially valuable work.
He argued that founders, researchers and scientists may hesitate to share breakthrough ideas with AI tools over fears that their information could be accessed by others. Similarly, individuals may avoid asking AI assistants sensitive questions about their health, finances or relationships because of privacy concerns.
Dark aims to address these concerns by combining data privacy with what Eternal describes as high-quality AI responses. The company said it has fine-tuned its models to deliver answers that prioritise truth over user approval, adding that benchmark results would be disclosed later.
Goyal also highlighted the potential risks associated with AI companies retaining user conversations, questioning whether such data could eventually be used to influence consumer behaviour or shape users’ beliefs.
However, not many details about the platform are available yet. “Dark will launch globally, hopefully within 2026,” Goyal said in the letter.
With Dark, Eternal has doubled down on its strategy to commercialise AI capabilities developed for its own operations. In February last year, it launched AI-native customer support platform Nugget after building it as an internal tool over three years to handle millions of customer support interactions per month across Zomato, Blinkit and Hyperpure.
Nugget offers businesses conversational chatbots and co-pilots, alongside voice AI, image classification and workflow automation to businesses.
These disclosures came as Eternal reported a 92% surge in its net profit to ₹125 Cr in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27), from ₹65 Cr in the previous year’s quarter. On a sequential basis, profit rose 36% from ₹92 Cr.
Operating revenue for the quarter zoomed 78% YoY and 19% QoQ to ₹24,138 Cr. Including other income of ₹351 Cr, total income stood at ₹24,489 Cr.
District Faces Higher Risk From Agentic Commerce
Apart from outlining its own AI ambitions, Eternal also raised concerns about the impact of agentic commerce on its group companies. Notably, it said its going-out vertical District faces the highest potential disruption from AI agents as they could bypass the platform to discover restaurants, book tables and purchase event tickets, reducing the platform’s role as an intermediary.
Goyal classified District as being in the medium-to-high risk zone, warning that AI agents could weaken content-led competitive advantages, including reviews, ratings and curated listings, by synthesising information from across the internet. However, he believes competition could increasingly favour platforms with stronger execution capabilities.
Meanwhile, he said that Zomato and Blinkit are relatively insulated from agentic commerce because their businesses rely on complex fulfillment infrastructure rather than discovery alone.
According to consumer surveys cited by Goyal, over 65% of Zomato app openings are exploratory, with users browsing an average of 12 menus and more than 100 food images before ordering. He argued that food discovery is an enjoyable activity that conversational AI may not easily replace.
While repeat orders and restocking could shift to AI agents, Eternal said reordered carts account for only a low-single-digit share of activity on both Zomato and Blinkit. It also believes in-app AI assistants could cater to these use cases.
More importantly, food delivery and quick commerce require real-time coordination between restaurants, delivery partners, inventory systems, pickers and dispatch operations. He argued that agents could initiate transactions, but the platforms managing fulfillment would remain responsible for delivering orders and resolving issues.
This comes as consumer companies are increasingly exploring agent-led shopping and payments. In February 2026, Razorpay and NPCI demonstrated agentic payments through Anthropic’s Claude, enabling users in a pilot to order food and groceries from platforms including Zomato, Swiggy and Zepto within AI conversations.
Meanwhile, Meesho has developed Vaani, a voice-first, multi-agent commerce system designed to help users discover and compare products conversationally.

items.content:
OpenAI said on Wednesday it was expanding advertising on ChatGPT to Pakistan and 25 additional countries, bringing the total number of markets where ads are available to 89, as the artificial intelligence company seeks to grow revenue ahead of a potential initial public offering.
The company said in August that its advertising business had reached an annualised revenue run rate of $1 billion.
OpenAI began testing ads on ChatGPT's Free and Go plans in the United States earlier this year. More than 100,000 advertisers have since run campaigns on the platform, the company said.
Read: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
The latest expansion includes 14 additional Latin American countries, including Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru, following earlier launches in Mexico and Brazil, it outlined, adding that advertising was also launching in markets across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia, including Nigeria, South Africa, Serbia, Ukraine, Cambodia, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
Advertisers can access ChatGPT ads in the new markets through technology partners or use a self-service option through the company's Ads Manager platform.
The company said ads will appear only on ChatGPT's Free and Go subscription plans, while Plus, Pro and Enterprise subscriptions will remain ad-free.
In September, OpenAI introduced artificial intelligence-powered tools for advertisers and began testing business-sponsored agents with select US advertisers, as it expands its advertising capabilities on the platform.
