items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Qualcomm has rejected reports claiming that its upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset is facing overheating problems. The company says recent claims about thermal issues are inaccurate and has defended the progress of its next-generation flagship processor.
The controversy began after a South Korean media report suggested that Samsung was facing problems with the chipset during internal testing. According to the report, the processor was running too hot and experiencing thermal throttling, which reduces performance to control temperatures.
The report also claimed that Samsung was considering using Exynos chipsets across its Galaxy S27 series next year instead of relying on Qualcomm’s processors. It suggested that the Exynos 2700 was performing better in thermal tests.
Qualcomm Denies Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 Overheating Reports – What’s the Issue
Qualcomm’s Chief Marketing Officer responded to the reports in a discussion on X, calling the claims inaccurate. The company said it remains confident in its next-generation flagship platform and continues to work with smartphone manufacturers to deliver premium user experiences.
The executive also clarified that the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 does not have any widespread thermal issues. He suggested that reports based on internal testing could be misleading because smartphone manufacturers adjust chipset performance and power consumption according to their devices and intended use cases.
These adjustments can affect how a processor performs under different workloads. As a result, test results from one device or testing environment may not reflect the performance of every smartphone using the same chipset.
Powerful Mobile Chips Face Cooling Challenges
Although Qualcomm has dismissed the claims, questions about heat management in powerful smartphone processors remain relevant. Modern mobile chipsets offer increasingly high performance and can handle demanding games and other intensive tasks.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series reportedly features two prime CPU cores running at up to 5.0GHz and six performance cores clocked at up to 4.0GHz. Such high clock speeds can increase power consumption and heat production, placing additional demands on smartphone cooling systems.
Unlike desktop computers, most smartphones rely on compact cooling solutions and do not have active fans. Manufacturers must therefore balance processing power, energy efficiency, and temperature control within a limited space.
See Also: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 vs Dimensity 9600 Pro: Benchmarks and Specs Compared
Sustained Performance Remains a Concern
High peak performance does not always translate into consistent performance over long periods. When a chipset reaches its thermal limits, it may reduce its clock speeds to control temperatures. This process, known as thermal throttling, can affect performance during extended gaming sessions or other demanding workloads.
Previous flagship smartphones have also shown performance drops during stress tests, highlighting the challenges of maintaining peak processing speeds over time. However, such results do not necessarily mean that a device will overheat during everyday activities.
For now, independent testing of smartphones powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 will be needed to determine how the chipset performs under sustained workloads.
Qualcomm has denied the reports of widespread overheating, but the actual thermal performance of the new processor will become clearer when commercial devices undergo real-world testing.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan is set to become the first country in the world to sign the Digital and AI Compact, marking a significant step in the country’s efforts to promote artificial intelligence (AI), digital inclusion, and equal access to technology.
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja has departed for South Korea on an official visit to represent Pakistan at the Global AI and Digital Summit 2026.
During the summit, the minister will participate in the AI and Digital Ministerial Meeting, where participants will discuss priorities related to the development of artificial intelligence, digital inclusion, and equal access to technology in Pakistan.
Pakistan Set to Become First Country to Sign Digital and AI Compact
Shaza Fatima is also expected to hold an important bilateral meeting with Google Vice President Wilson L. White. The meeting will focus on potential cooperation in digital technology and artificial intelligence.
The federal minister will present Pakistan’s future roadmap during a session on the Digital and AI Compact. She is also scheduled to meet World Bank Vice President Ousmane Diagana to discuss areas of mutual interest and cooperation.

The summit will bring together participants to discuss how artificial intelligence can support economic growth, create employment opportunities, and improve access to digital services.
Pakistan’s expected participation in the Digital and AI Compact reflects its efforts to strengthen its position in the global digital economy. The initiative could also open new opportunities for international cooperation in AI development, digital infrastructure, and technology access.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Dalal Street emerged as a founder’s paradise in 2025, with 18 Indian startups listing on the bourses and collectively mopping up a record ₹41,248 Cr from the public markets.
The surge was driven by a combination of macroeconomic tailwinds and regulatory support. While robust GDP growth projections helped revive investor appetite, SEBI’s reforms played a key role. Measures such as simplified DRHP filings reduced red tape, while more flexible ESOP rules allowed founders to retain meaningful ownership.
Retail investors also fuelled the frenzy as demat accounts crossed the 20 Cr mark. The OFS component dominated public issues last year, providing liquidity to the early backers of the new-age tech companies. Post-listing performance also followed the usual curve, with investors rewarding companies that prioritised profits, sustainable growth and governance over hype.
“⁠Besides the readiness that startups showed in their unit economics, there is also an increase in the founders committing to their businesses for next couple of decades and grow their businesses by adding adjacent profit pools – something that the public markets reward handsomely,” said Ashish Kumar, cofounder and general partner at Fundamentum Partnership.
Building on the momentum, fifteen new-age tech companies have already made their D-Street debut so far this year. Of these, ESDS Software Solution, Klassroom, RentoMojo, SEDEMAC, Kissht, LEAP India and Shiprocket made a bumper debut on the bourses.
Nevertheless, the IPO pipeline remains strong. Twenty seven startups have already filed their DRHPs with SEBI, while over 25 are in various stages of finalising their IPO plans. Unicorns like OYO, Razorpay and Zetwerk alone could raise over ₹34,000 Cr in 2026, making it one of the biggest years for startup IPOs.
However, recalibration is likely to define 2026 as investors are expected to prioritise strong fundamentals, profitability and low cash burn when backing new-age tech companies.
“IPO-bound startups in 2026 will be increasingly defined by their ability to demonstrate predictable cash flows, sustainable unit economics, and operational discipline rather than headline growth alone. Public market investors will place greater emphasis on governance, capital efficiency and long-term value creation, favouring companies that balance scale with financial prudence,” Orios Venture Partners’ managing partner Rehan Yar Khan told Inc42.
There are other challenges as well. Average retail subscription levels are moderating, while foreign institutional investors (FIIs) are pulling back in droves, reflecting caution amid geopolitical tensions and muted secondary market performance. The ongoing conflict in West Asia has further complicated the situation.
Yet, the overall outlook remains bullish for new-age tech IPOs. Maturing business models, deeper domestic capital pools and an evolving regulatory framework favouring transparency position India as a leading startup IPO hub.
With much on the anvil, we have compiled a list of Indian new-age tech companies eyeing a Dalal Street debut later this year. But before we dive into the list, here are the latest developments from India’s IPO landscape:
Latest Updates:
Burma Burma’s parent Hunger Pangs has filed its DRHP with SEBI for an IPO, which will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹150 Cr and an OFS of up to 2.8 Cr shares
Markets regulator SEBI has greenlit gym chain Cult.fit’s IPO, which consists of a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹950 Cr and an OFS of up to 17.9 Cr shares
Defence tech company Tonbo Imaging’s ₹852 Cr IPO was oversubscribed 7.78X at the end of the second day of bidding
