items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over the death of the veteran journalist and diplomat, Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, saying that the late statesman devoted his life to national service.
Ambassador Cole died at the age of 86.
President Tinubu, in his tribute titled “Farewell to Ambassador Dele Cole, distinguished diplomat, journalist and public servant,” said the late veteran journalist brought distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.
The tribute read: “I received with profound sadness the news of the passing of Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, a distinguished diplomat, journalist, politician, and public servant, who died at 86.
“Ambassador Cole devoted his life to national service, bringing distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.
“His career reflected the enduring value of dialogue, tact, mutual respect and the pursuit of shared interests in advancing national development and international cooperation.
“His contributions to Nigeria’s media landscape were particularly notable. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he upheld the vital role of the press in holding public officials accountable, speaking truth to power, and strengthening democratic governance. His legacy in journalism and public life remains an enduring part of our national story.
“At 86, Ambassador Dele Cole witnessed defining moments in Nigeria’s history and contributed to the nation’s development through his work in the media, diplomacy and public service. His life stands as a testament to the value of experience, principled engagement and commitment to the public good.
“As we mourn his passing, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, professional associates and all whose lives he touched. I pray that memories of his remarkable life will bring them comfort and strength at this difficult time.
“May Almighty God grant Ambassador Cole eternal rest and give his family and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this profound loss.”

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Nigeria’s full economic recovery depends entirely on sustaining the bold reform policies initiated by President Bola Tinubu.
Wike said this on Saturday, at the Rainbow Coalition’s stakeholders’ consultation in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers.
He said that only the continuation of the current administration’s economic direction could permanently pull the country back from the brink of collapse.
He noted that the hard economic choices being implemented presently were necessary remedies to salvage a system that was virtually “dead” when Tinubu took office.
“Only the continuation of the economic reforms initiated by the Tinubu government can bring this country back from the economic comatose it was in before this present administration took over,” he said.
He said that the presidential candidate of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Abubakar Atiku and his vice, Rotimi Amaechi, had nothing to offer to Nigerians.
The minister urged residents of the state not to surrender the country’s progress to “career politicians” and “political opportunists” whom he likened to “chronic pool betters” who repeatedly gamble with public trust.
According to him, supporting politicians who have made decades-long pursuits for power would mean diverting national funds to recoup lost campaign expenses rather than consolidating economic gains.
Wike further said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, would not make any meaningful difference if elected, stressing that Tinubu was the person who had shown true commitment.
Reaffirming that leadership must be judged by past governance records, the former Rivers governor challenged his predecessor to account for major capital allocations in Rivers.
Explaining the political strategy behind the cross-party Rainbow Coalition movement, he said that delivering economic recovery required total alignment between the executive and the national assembly.
He urged voters to support Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates vying for the Senate and House of Representatives seats in the area to ensure legislative cooperation for the president’s economic policy agenda.
He also called on party leaders and community mobilisers to prepare for an overwhelming turnout on election day.
“I want total mobilisation on Jan. 16, 2027. Everybody must be mobilised. Make sure we vote and win decisively to protect our collective future,” he said.
In his remarks, the Executive Chairman of the council, Dr Chukwu Shedrack, commended Wike for his historic development projects in the council, including road construction, hospital upgrades, and human capital investments.
Shedrack highlighted several local governance achievements which he said aligned with the FCT minister’s leadership model.
Reaffirming the council’s political commitment to the Tinubu administration’s economic recovery drive, he pledged a complete block vote for the APC across all elective positions come 2027.
“We are fully mobilised, ward by ward and unit by unit. Come the 2027 general elections, our people will deliver 100 per cent. From president to national assembly and house of assembly, no vote will drop,” Shedrack assured. (NAN)
The post Nigeria’s economy needs continuation of Tinubu’s reforms – Wike appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Hadiza Yusuf
Two suspected bandits have been killed by local hunters, while ₦10 million paid as ransom for a kidnapped man has been recovered in Falgore Forest, Doguwa Local Government Area of Kano State.
This was contained in a statement signed by CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Police Public Relations Officer, on Saturday.
According to the statement, the kidnapped victim, identified as 45-year-old Kabiru Aliyu of Falgore Village, was released unharmed after the suspects collected the ransom
The incident occurred at about midnight on Saturday, when three suspected bandits allegedly emerged from Falgore Forest to collect the money demanded for Aliyu’s release.
According to the statement, the victim was kidnapped on September 11, 2026, and had spent several days in captivity before his release.
The police said that shortly after collecting the ₦10 million ransom and releasing the victim, the suspects were ambushed by local hunters known as Yan Bula while returning to their hideout in Falgore Forest.
“During the ambush, two of the suspected bandits were neutralised, while the third suspect escaped with injuries. The entire ransom sum of ₦10 million was recovered intact from the neutralised suspects,” the statement said.
The command said preliminary investigations had identified one of the suspects killed as Dogo Isah, a commercial motorcycle rider from Maigwanda Village in Kubau Local Government Area of Kaduna State.
The police said the suspects were believed to have come from Maigwanda Village before the incident.
The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the Yan Bula hunters for their efforts in supporting security operations in the area.
Bakori said the hunters’ activities continued to complement the police operation against kidnapping, banditry and other violent crimes in the state under Operation Kukan Kura.
Following the incident, the commissioner directed the Area Commander, Divisional Police Officers and tactical teams operating in the area to immediately search the forest and surrounding communities for the fleeing suspect.
He also directed the teams to intensify efforts to arrest the suspect and recover any weapons used by the group.
The police further disclosed that the rescued victim had been debriefed, medically examined and reunited with his family.
The command assured residents of its commitment to protecting lives and property.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
A former Caretaker Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area of Benue state, Mr. Inalegwu Adakonye, has defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), alongside other political stakeholders and their supporters from the APC, African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Zenith Labour Party (ZLP).
The defection featured several prominent political figures from Adoka and Ugboju communities in Otukpo council.
Among prominent politicians who weekend in Otukpo joined the PDP with the former chairman of Otukpo were Adoga Edache, popularly known as Ebo, from the ADC; Emmanuel Akoche of the ZLP; Garuba Sule of the APC; and Mr. John Ojonye, ADC Chairman of Ugboju Ehaji Ward, alongside other party members and supporters.
Explaining his decision to return to the PDP, Adakonye said the party’s ideology of inclusiveness and collective participation informed his choice, arguing that its approach to politics differed from that of the APC.
He said “the PDP treats its members as one family and offer a platform where everyone can participate. And I am confident that the party is best positioned to rescue Benue state from bad governance.”
Adakonye, who led APC members from Adoka and Ugboju into the PDP, also cited the emergence of Dr. Oyije Ogbenjuwa as the party’s deputy governorship candidate as a factor behind their decision.
He said they could not afford to remain outside the political movement of their brother and friend, who he expressed confidence would soon become the deputy governor of the state.
The defectors also cited the PDP’s people-oriented ideology, leadership and prospects in forthcoming elections as reasons for abandoning their former parties for the opposition platform.
Receiving the new members were the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Dr. Ogbenjuwa; the Otukpo Local Government PDP Chairman, Godwin Ochapa; the party’s House of Assembly candidate for Otukpo/Akpa, Johnson Egli; its candidate for Adoka/Ugboju, Gabriel Olofu; and the Senior Legislative Aide to the Senate President, Chief George Alli.
Speaking on behalf of the party, Ogbenjuwa welcomed the defectors and assured them of “equal opportunities and full integration into the party’s activities.”
He described their decision to join the PDP “as evidence of the party’s growing acceptability across Benue South Senatorial District, and your support will further strengthen our political base ahead of future elections.”
The new members, in turn, pledged their loyalty and commitment to working for the success of the PDP at all levels.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, WTO, has recalled how her investigation into an alleged $2.4bn fuel subsidy fraud in Nigeria led her mother’s kidnapping.
Read Also: Okonjo-Iweala’s mother, 82, kidnapped
Okonjo-Iweala narrated her experience in an interview with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua. She said the kidnappers’ demands were that she resigns as the Minister of Finance and leave the country.
On how the ordeal began, she said her office noticed a sharp increase in subsidy claims, so she began to probe.
Her words: “So I went to the president and said, look, something is going on here. Could we audit the accounts? And he said, yes, go ahead.
“And we found about $2.4 billion worth of fraud. So we refused to pay.”
That was when they took her mother. Okonjo-Iweala said the five-day ordeal was among the most painful periods of her life.
“I was told (by the kidnappers) that for her to be released, I should resign and leave the country.
“She was held in the middle of a forest, and one night she escaped. She’s still alive. She’s 96 now.”
“It was a terrible, terrible five-day ordeal. I think the worst in my life,” she said.
Okonjo-Iweala said initially she felt paralysed by fear and considered resigning. She added that that the experience left her with a sense of guilt that she still carries.
“I never dreamt my parents could ever be touched in this way, that people would be that evil,” she said.
On her father’s reaction at the time, she said: “He said, ‘We don’t give in to blackmail’. And he said, ‘You’ve got to carry on. You’ve got to go to work’.”
Okonjo-Iweala served as Minister of Finance under President Goodluck Jonathan. Her mother, Kamene Okonjo, was kidnapped from her home in Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, in December 2012. Read the kidnap story HERE.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
…Zulum’s support instrumental to military success – COAS
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri
Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has called on the military to immediately commence a coordinated offensive operation, Operation Lake Sanity, to dislodge insurgents from the shores and islands of Lake Chad.
Governor Zulum made the call on Saturday when he received the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, on a courtesy visit at the new Council Chamber, Government House, Maiduguri.
The governor commended the Nigerian Army for improvements in the security situation in the state and also requested stronger military deployments in strategic locations, including Kareto, Baga, and the Sabon Gari–Wajiroko axis, to protect communities, secure waterways, and support the reopening of the Damboa–Biu road.
“The recent attacks on some communities in northern Borno are a result of the presence of insurgents along the shores of Lake Chad. We cannot achieve complete peace without undertaking major military operations in that area,” Zulum said.
The governor acknowledged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s support for the proposed operation and the coordination among the service chiefs; however, he urged the military authorities to accelerate preparations.
“I understand that the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has provided the necessary support for the operation. I urge you to hasten the process so that the insurgents threatening northern Borno can be dislodged,” he stated.
He called for strengthening the amphibious command in Baga to clear waterways, stressing that holding those positions would be essential to sustaining the operation’s gains.
On the Gubio–Damasak corridor, Zulum appealed for the speedy establishment of a military formation in Kareto, and around Sabon Gari and Wajiroko in Damboa Local Government Area to support the restoration of vehicular movement between Damboa and Biu.
Governor Babagana Zulum thanked the Chief of Army Staff for training about 1,000 forest guards, who he said had completed their training and were deployed to the state.
Zulum emphasised the need to consolidate military successes through reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement, commending the Army’s support for re-establishing the Mairari community and preparing for military formations and community resettlement in Maiwa, Koshobe and Ala.
“Military operations must be followed by stabilisation measures, including reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement. Borno State Government will provide the support required by the Nigerian Army to fortify these locations,” he pledged.
He also expressed appreciation for additional battalions deployed across the two sectors, noting that the reinforcements were helping to strengthen security and stabilise affected areas.
“Notwithstanding the recent attacks in some parts of Borno State, there has been tremendous improvement in our security situation. I commend the officers and men of Operation Hadin Kai and urge them to sustain this momentum,” Zulum announced.
The Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, commended Governor Babagana Umara Zulum for his sustained support to the Nigerian Army, describing it as instrumental to the successes recorded against insurgency.
“I must put on record that the support of the Executive Governor of Borno State has been phenomenal in the successes we have recorded here in Borno State. For that, we say a very big thank you, sir,” the COAS said.
The Army Chief explained that his visit to troops of Operation Hadin Kai was part of a routine assessment of their operations, to encourage commanders, and to appreciate the resilience of personnel confronting insurgency in the Northeast.
He reaffirmed their mandate to restore normalcy and create an enabling environment for socio-economic activities, assuring that challenges presented by commanders would receive prompt attention.
The courtesy visit was attended by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, member representing Marte, Monguno, Nganzai federal constituency, Hon. Bukar Talba, Secretary to the State Government, Commissioners, Special Advisers and other senior military and heads of security establishment in the state. End

Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has commissioned a 1MW Solar Inter-connected Mini-Grid Project in Talasse, headquarters of Balanga Local Government Area of the State.
The project, commissioned on Saturday, is expected to provide reliable, affordable and sustainable electricity to over 6,000 households and businesses, unlocking new opportunities for economic growth, job creation and improved living standards in the long-neglected community.
Speaking at the commissioning ceremony in Talasse, Governor Yahaya said the project, which was flagged off on November 6, 2025, has moved from promise to reality in less than a year.
He noted that lack of electricity had for over 17 years constrained economic opportunities for farmers, artisans, traders and entrepreneurs in Talasse who relied on expensive alternative energy sources.

“Electricity is not merely a social amenity; it is a fundamental driver of modern economic development. With this commissioning, small businesses can now operate more productively, artisans can expand, farmers can add value to their produce, and our youths can acquire digital skills,” he said.
Governor Yahaya said the project aligned with the Federal Government’s electricity sector reforms under the Electricity Act 2023, signed by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.
He said Gombe has keyed into the reform through its own Electricity Law, the establishment of the Gombe State Electricity Regulatory Commission and the Gombe Electricity Company Limited.
He stressed that sustainability will depend on effective management and responsible use, urging operators to maintain high standards of transparency and service delivery.
To complement the power supply, he said the state government will provide productive-use equipment at favourable prices, including modular rice milling machines, electric multi-flour grinding machines and groundnut oil processing machines to boost agro-processing and create jobs for women and youths.
The governor announced that construction of 4MW solar mini-grids will soon be flagged off in Akko, Dukku, Funakaye and Kaltungo LGAs, “while mini-grid projects in Filiya and Gelengu have reached 90 percent completion.
According to him, a total of 80 communities across the state are targeted under the rural electrification programme.
He commended President Tinubu, the Minister of Power, Mr Joseph Tegbe; the Rural Electrification Agency led by Engr. Abba Aliyu; the World Bank and technical partner, MIDS Dynamic, for their support.
Governor Yahaya also thanked traditional rulers and the people of Talasse for their cooperation, urging them to protect the facility against vandalism, theft and illegal connections.
He said, “Support the operators by observing the necessary safety guidelines and fulfilling your obligations as responsible consumers. The sustainability of this investment is essential to ensuring that its benefits endure for generations yet unborn.”

By Kingsley Omonobi
Former President Dr Goodluck Jonathan and Africa’s wealthiest man, Aliko Dangote, on Saturday called for greater investment in job creation and social development as part of efforts to tackle terrorism and other forms of insecurity in Nigeria.
This is as Jonathan called for a revisit of the Almajiri education system, which he pioneered during his administration to halt the tendency of vulnerable youths being recruited for criminal activities, noting that the Great Green Wall project introduced to keep youths gainfully employed in agriculture should also be revisited.
The duo spoke at the public presentation of the book, “Beyond the Bullets: Policing Terrorism in a Democratic System”, written by a former Inspector-General of Police, IGP Mohammed Abubakar.
Represented by his former Chief of Staff, Chief Mike Oghiadomhe, Jonathan said the Almajiri schools programme was designed to equip young people with skills beyond religious education and enable them to contribute to national development.
“My administration engaged in the establishment of Almajiri schools, aimed at providing skills to millions of youth population beyond religious education only,” he said.
Jonathan disclosed that the initiative was intended to help young people earn a living while reducing the number of youths available for recruitment into violent crime.
He also said the Great Green Wall project had the potential to address desertification, support agriculture and create employment.
“We also engaged in the Great Green Wall project, which, apart from arresting desertification and making more fertile land available for crop farming and animal husbandry, had the potential of providing employment for hundreds of thousands,” he said.
While urging the government to revisit both programmes, he added, “I therefore use this opportunity to call on government to revisit and review these programmes.”
He said terrorism is a national and global challenge that required sustained commitment and cooperation across successive administrations.
His words, “The fight against terrorism is not the responsibility of one administration or the other. It is a continuing national and global challenge that requires sustained commitment, institutional learning, and cooperation across successive governments and generations.
In his remarks, Alhaji Aliko Dangote called on the government and private sector to work together to create jobs and stimulate economic growth, arguing that military force alone could not eliminate terrorism.
“If you don’t create jobs, it’s difficult to fight terrorism and get it out of the way,” he said.
He noted that entrepreneurs had a responsibility to partner with the government by investing in businesses that could generate employment and prosperity.
“On our own side as entrepreneurs, we have to partner with the government, create jobs, create growth, and also prosperity, and that will help when they are also fighting with force,” he said.
Dangote disclosed that combining economic opportunities with security operations could help Nigeria overcome terrorism, banditry and other forms of violent crime.
“If you use these two things, we will get rid of terrorism, banditry, and the rest,” he said.
He cited the economic cost of the conflict in the Northeast, saying a UNICEF report put the cumulative national economic loss at about $100bn since the conflict began.
“But personally, I believe when you look at the agricultural side of the country and other things, this is more than $100 billion by far.
While urging Nigerians to support efforts to address insecurity rather than leave the responsibility to the government alone, he said, “Fighting terrorism is not only for the government alone; it’s our collective responsibility.”
“What we need to do is to join hands with the government in fighting this menace, because it is a collective responsibility on all of us.”
In his remarks, IGP MD Abubakar said the fight against terrorism must not undermine democratic principles, human rights and the rule of law.
Abubakar said the central message of his book was that the fight against terrorism should combine effective security operations with fairness, accountability and respect for human dignity.
“This book insists on a vital point that I learned in service. Fighting terrorism should never mean treating the whole community as suspects.
He warned that excessive use of power could damage the relationship between security agencies and the communities they were meant to protect.
“When fear becomes policy, discrimination becomes security.
He stressed that democratic institutions, including the courts, legislature, media and civil society, should not be regarded as obstacles to national security.
“They are the ground rails that prevent security from becoming domination,” he said.
According to him, “Effective counterterrorism required coordination among security agencies, intelligence gathering, accountability and respect for the law.
“Democracies must answer violence with process.
He disclosed that justice remained central to democratic security, insisting that investigations must be credible, evidence tested and victims heard.
He added that governments needed coordination, security agencies required adequate capability and funding, communities needed trust, courts needed evidence, and citizens deserved transparency.
Dignitaries present at the occasion include Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State and Mr Peter Obi, former governor of Anambra State; Dr Bukola Saraki, former Senate President; Inspector General of Police IGP Olatunji Disu; Senator Ireti Kingibe; and Gen Aliyu Gusau, former National Security Adviser, among others.

items.content:
Political Economist,  Prof. Pat Utomi, says he cannot guarantee that embattled professor Anthony Kila has never made mistakes but to suggest that he has never gone to school is spectacularly unfair to his personality.
Utomi made this known on his verified Facebook page in Lagos on Saturday, saying that Kila is a good man.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that Kila is currently at the centre of a major scandal regarding his academic credentials.
In October, an investigative report published by Premium Times revealed that Kila allegedly falsified all of his higher education qualifications, including his bachelor’s, master’s, doctorate (PhD) degrees, and his rank as a professor.
Utomi, reacting to the online claim, said that there was no evidence to support the claim that Anthony Kila (popularly known as “Prof Kila”) had never gone to school.
“I know Anthony Kila. I became aware of all the trending discussions about his career rather late.
“I have never had any reason to ask about his certificates or letters of appointment, so I cannot claim to have those details.
“However, if he has never gone to school, then those who have must ask for a refund.
“We watched the cyber mob bully Jason Arday, the youngest Black professor ever appointed at Cambridge, to his early death.
“Incidentally, I first met Anthony Kila in the city of Cambridge, England, in 2006, when I was beginning a run for the office of President of Nigeria.”
Utomi said that among those in the mob that sought to lynch Arday were white professors, who had been pardoned for mistakes of a far worse nature.
He said he did not know who might be going after Kila in a country where many people confer academic and non-academic titles on themselves, while the media, through its status-conferring function, elevates them to celebrity status.
He,  however, said that this does not seem normal, saying he could empathise because he has had a similar experience.
Utomi said: “Years ago, when a journalist tried to suggest that my stay at Volkswagen Nigeria had something to do with its demise, I offered ₦12 million to anyone who could produce a shred of evidence to support that claim. Fifteen years on, no one has come forward to claim the bounty.
“When I became the first professor of Pan-African (Pan-Atlantic) parent of the Lagos Business School, someone at UNILAG went, “…huh, until he found out that the evaluating team was led by the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan.”
“If professors like Adele Jinadu in Political Science and Joe Umo at UNILAG had not met me in graduate school abroad and interacted with my Head of Department, Elinor Lin Ostrom, who went on to become the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economics, someone may have written something demeaning about my education.
“Kila is a smart and good man. I cannot guarantee he has not made mistakes but to suggest he has not gone to school is spectacularly stupid.” (NAN)

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Hansi Flick’s dominant Barcelona routed 10-man Real Betis 5-2 on Saturday to return five points clear at the top of La Liga.
Teenage winger Lamine Yamal scored a brilliant goal for the Spanish champions, with Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and Dani Olmo also finding the net at La Cartuja stadium in Seville.
Betis, third, had Facundo Bernal sent off for a headbutt on Yamal early in the second half of a pulsating clash.
Barca set a new club record for victories at the start of a league campaign and equalled the all-time record of nine, set by Real Madrid in the 1968/69 season.
Flick’s side boast 11 wins from 11 games across all competitions.
“Once again the team has shown its attacking potential, but it’s also true we’re giving quite a bit away, and that’s probably where the improvement has to come from too,” Rodri told DAZN.
Earlier Atletico, second, snatched a late 1-0 win at Espanyol and are five points behind Barca, while Betis are eight points adrift of the leaders and Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla on Sunday.
Betis rested several players, including key midfielder Isco, ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Feyenoord.
Manuel Pellegrini’s side still gave Barca a stern test, after the Catalan giants went ahead through a sensational Yamal strike in the 10th minute.
The 19-year-old turned sharply on the edge of the box to escape Bernal and then exquisitely curled into the top corner.
“(It was) an incredible goal, we’ve got used to him doing this lately, I have to say,” added Rodri.
“In the end, players like that make the difference. But I try to focus on the other things he brings… (like) hard work, a lot of solidarity with the team, understanding the game and where he could find space.”
– Defensive flaws –
Despite their irresistible attacking play, Barca’s clear weakness under Flick has been their defence and Betis were level before the half-hour mark.
A corner came all the way through the box and was recycled by Pablo Fornals, who crossed for Valentin Gomez to head home, getting in front of Barca defender Xavi Espart.
Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri put Barca back in front with a header from a corner, before Giovani Lo Celso thought he had equalised in spectacular fashion for the hosts.
However the Argentine midfielder’s long-range goal was ruled out for a handball by Cucho Hernandez earlier in the move, much to Betis’ chagrin.
Jesus extended Barca’s lead six minutes into the second half from Yamal’s cut-back, moments after having another goal ruled out for offside.
Ez Abde immediately pulled one back for Betis during a wild spell, and in the aftermath they were reduced to 10 men when Bernal was sent off for a headbutt on Yamal, who was booked for his part in a confrontation between several players from both sides.
Barca added their fourth when Pau Cubarsi nodded the ball across to Garcia to pounce from close range.
It was the eighth time this season Flick’s free-scoring side have scored four goals or more in a match.
The coach brought Raphinha on as a substitute after the Brazilian missed the previous two matches with an injury problem, taking off Yamal to prevent a potential further card and suspension for the Clasico next weekend.
First comes the matter of a visit to the French capital on Tuesday to face reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain, which promises to be a thrilling match.
Substitute Olmo finished the match off with a neat finish from the edge of the box as Betis backed off to allow Barca’s attention to turn to Europe.
Betis defender Hector Bellerin said there were a “couple of unfair decisions” that went against his side but he was pleased with the team’s efforts against his former club.
“Facing a team like this, with this quality, we stood up to them until the final minutes,” Bellerin told DAZN.
“We showed that with 11 players we’re able to compete against the best.”

items.content:
By Shina Abubakar, OSOGBO
President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that Nigeria’s greatest asset is not the mineral deposit beneath its soil but the creative youth population with there resilience and abundant talent.
Read Also: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal
Tinubu said this at the flag off construction of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Centre for Youth Empowerment and Inter-Cultural Dialogue at the Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife Osun State at the weekend.
The President was represented by the Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hazmat, said the event transcend a mere celebration but a national statement and deliberate investment in the aspiration of Nigeria’s young population.
While describing that the establishment of the centre as timely and strategic, he said the centre offer opportunity to develop a structured platform through which young Nigerians can acquire relevant skills, transform ideas into enterprises, access mentorship.
His words, “Today is more than a ceremonial occasion. It is a statement of national purpose. It represents an investment in the aspirations of our young people, a commitment to the unity of our country, and a recognition that Nigeria’s greatest resource is not merely what lies beneath its soil, but the talent, creativity, resilience and enterprise of its people.”
“The establishment of this Centre is therefore timely and strategic. It offers an opportunity to develop a structured platform through which young Nigerians can acquire relevant skills, transform ideas into enterprises, access mentorship, engage with industry and international partners, and contribute to national development.
He emphasised that the centre’s success should be measured by the opportunities it creates for young people and the lives it transforms.
“The true value of this Centre will ultimately be determined not by the magnificence of its buildings, but by the quality of the opportunities it creates and the lives it transforms,” he stated.
He also called for partnerships among universities, industries, government, investors and international development institutions to connect young people with economic opportunities and help transform their ideas into viable enterprises.
He also highlighted the importance of mutual respect and understanding among people from different ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds, with the aim of promoting national unity, peaceful coexistence and social cohesion.
“Our expectation should be that, in the years ahead, this institution will be known not merely as a centre of learning, but as a centre of transformation—one that produces capable leaders, responsible citizens, innovative entrepreneurs and globally competitive professionals.
“The Centre should provide a meeting point for universities, industry, government, investors, civil society and international development institutions,” the President said.
In his welcome address, the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simeon Bamire said the centre was conceived as a response to challenges confronting young people, including unemployment, limited access to skills development, unequal economic opportunities and social exclusion. 
He said the initiative would provide a sustainable platform for equipping young people with practical competencies, promoting enterprise and innovation, and connecting talent with meaningful opportunities.
According to him, the centre would serve as an internationally recognised platform where young people from Nigeria, Africa and other parts of the world could learn, collaborate, innovate and develop solutions to shared challenges. 
“Its programmes would promote entrepreneurship, digital technology, leadership, creative enterprise and peacebuilding, while encouraging cooperation across cultural and national boundaries”, he added.
The proposed centre will feature an international conference and dialogue complex, a digital innovation and learning duplex, an entrepreneurship and incubation hub, a scholars and creators lodge, a culture exhibition and community engagement centre, as well as administrative, research and support infrastructure.
The project is expected to promote human capital development, employment and enterprise growth, peace, inclusion and social cohesion. It is also intended to provide networking opportunities and support research and policy development.
The project is expected to provide young people with opportunities to learn, collaborate, innovate and engage across cultural boundaries. January was mentioned as a target for commissioning the building, although the year was not specified in the information obtained.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
Luis Diaz hit a hat-trick as Bayern Munich pummelled a listless RB Leipzig 6-1 at home on Saturday to climb to the top of the Bundesliga table.
Borussia Dortmund had edged ahead of Freiburg into top spot after their earlier draw at Union Berlin, but Bayern responded in typically ruthless fashion to take the summit.
The dominant display was Bayern’s best performance of the season and will boost their confidence days out from Wednesday’s home Champions League clash with English champions Arsenal.
Diaz had faced criticism after four league games without a goal but the Colombian sparked to life to terrorise Leipzig defender Lukas Klostermann down the left.
In his 100th Bundesliga match, Harry Kane scored a goal and laid on two assists as he pulled the strings from deep while Aleksandar Pavlovic and Michael Olise also got on the scoresheet.
Confined to his chair with a hip complaint, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany produced a masterclass against opposite number Martin Demichelis, his former Manchester City teammate.
Bayern have now won their past three games against Leipzig by a combined scoreline of 17-1.
Bayern had drawn their past two matches, a rare run of middling form for the German giants, but shook off the funk early, with Diaz, Pavlovic and Olise putting the hosts in control before half-time.
Diaz scored either side of a Kane tap-in after the break, with the England captain withdrawn before the hour mark ahead of old rivals Arsenal’s visit.
Leipzig’s Andrija Maksimovic got on the board with a late late consolation in stoppage time.
Dortmund draw in Berlin
Dortmund missed a chance to stay ahead of Bayern after being held to a scoreless draw at Union Berlin.
After starting the season strongly with six wins in a row in all competitions, Dortmund have stalled of late, drawing two and losing one of their last three matches.
“We simply have to get better in attack. Right now, it’s just not good enough,” Dortmund’s Waldemar Anton told Sky.
Serhou Guirassy had a golden chance to snatch all three points for his side at the end of a match of few opportunities, but headed just wide with 11 minutes remaining to cap a poor game up front for the Dortmund striker.
It was the first draw between the two sides in their history, with each of their previous 16 clashes in all competitions producing a winner.
Compounding Dortmund’s woes was a serious-looking ankle injury to substitute midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas, who was helped from the pitch just eight minutes after coming on.
“Let’s hope it’s not too serious. He’s not feeling great right now,” Dortmund sporting director Ole Book told reporters.
Stuttgart suffered a blow ahead of Tuesday’s home Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid, going down 1-0 at Hamburg after an 88th-minute Miro Muheim goal.
Stuttgart are languishing in 13th in the Bundesliga with two wins and four defeats but have impressed in Europe this season to sit in fourth spot in the 36-team Champions League table after two matches.
Elsewhere, promoted Elversberg continued their impressive debut season in the top flight, winning 4-3 at home to Augsburg.
Lukas Petkov, Lasse Guenther, Maximilian Rohr and Frederik Schmahl got on the scoresheet as Elversberg, from the smallest town to ever host a Bundesliga side, climbed to sixth in the table.
Niclas Fuellkrug scored for the fifth straight Bundesliga match as his brace helped Werder Bremen come from two goals down to draw 2-2 at home against Paderborn.
The Germany striker returned to Bremen on loan after an unhappy spell at West Ham but now has seven goals in seven games in all competitions.
A first-half goal for Phillip Tietz was enough for Mainz to win 1-0 at Schalke and climb to fifth in the standings.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
The captain of a flydubai flight whose co-pilot attacked him with an axe in an alleged bid to bring down the plane said one thought kept running through his head as the harrowing ordeal unfolded: “You can’t die like this.”
Read Also: ‘I could not let all those people die’ — Indian pilot recounts flydubai ordeal
Indian pilot Smit Machchhar recounted the “traumatic” experience to Sky News Arabia in his first interview since the incident late last month in which he, passengers and other crew members were credited with averting disaster on the Tel Aviv-bound flight.
With his head and one hand bandaged and glasses perched on his nose, Machchhar spoke from his hospital bed in the UAE.
“My vision was restricted to a few inches,” said the pilot, describing the effect of being struck in the back of the head with an emergency axe by his co-pilot, who had positioned himself behind Machchhar’s seat.
At first thinking that a part of the airplane’s ceiling had come loose, he then received several more blows and was wounded in the hand as he tried to shield himself.
Machchhar recalled struggling to open the cockpit door so another pilot who was travelling on board could get inside.
“So I was screaming his name and I was trying, because the switch that was very close to me to open the door, I was trying to just get help in,” he said.
“But I remember being able to open the door,” he went on, only for it to shut again.
“And at that point, I felt all the blood, you know, everything rushing down, my energy, everything, I was just, I was barely staying in consciousness.”
“Soon after that, that was the time when I heard the engine sounds going down. And then immediately after that I felt the aircraft going into a dive.”
According to findings released by the Emirati attorney general, Machchhar’s 29-year-old Omani co-pilot had planned to use the plane to carry out a suicide attack on the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, inspired by the September 11, 2001 attacks in New York.
He claimed to have acted alone, something investigators are still working to verify.
The prosecutor found that the other pilot on board, having seen the cockpit door open and close “in an unusual manner”, entered the flight deck and with the help of another crew member and passengers, subdued the co-pilot and regained control of the aircraft.
The jet, which plunged violently during the fray, was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
Machchhar said the way his colleague was able to intervene and safely land the plane was “commendable”.
“It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die.”

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
Israeli settlers on Saturday attacked a convoy of European diplomats and beat up a visiting French mayor, in a new escalation of violence during the Palestinian olive harvest, witnesses and diplomats told AFP.
The 78-year-old mayor said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France, kicked him and hit him with iron bars as he joined Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank alongside the top French and Belgian representatives in Jerusalem and Polish diplomats.
“I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, told AFP after he was attacked.
“The whole world needs to know what’s happening,” he said. “For me, I’ll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here.”
Baudoux, who was wearing a sash with the French tricolour, was seen collapsed on the side of the car after the attack but he did not need hospital care.
The attack came just one day after settlers beat an American photographer for The Washington Post, who was in moderate condition with broken vertebrae on Saturday.
Israel’s foreign ministry condemned the attack on the diplomats and Israeli police promised to open an investigation.
But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, days away from an election in which he is seeking to shore up support from the far-right, instead alleged a “smear” campaign against settlers.
Netanyahu said the diplomats should have coordinated their movements with the Israeli military and pointed out that Baudoux is a communist known for supporting the Palestinian cause.
“We urge caution before drawing conclusions” about the attacks, Netanyahu’s office said in a statement.
His main rival in October 27 elections, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, strongly criticised Netanyahu over the violence, saying it was “burning away the little legitimacy the State of Israel still possesses”.
The attacks are “Jewish terrorism, under the auspices of the Israeli government”, Eisenkot said.
Belgium called for an end to “impunity for violent settlers” after the latest attack.
Attacks on cultural symbol
Baudoux, the mayor, said he had come to the town of Taybeh, a Christian stronghold, along with his local pastor from France to sign a goodwill agreement.
He was attacked just as he joined the harvest as a symbolic gesture with the Palestinians, for whom olives are an important cultural symbol.
Extremist Israelis have issued calls to stop the Palestinians’ harvest after months of growing attacks in which settlers have stolen land and property. There has also been violence against Israelis, with a Palestinian shooting dead a settler last month.
Bashar Fawadleh, a priest in Taybeh, said settlers had already attacked the harvest and snatched olives before beating the mayor.
“One person was hit in the head and needed stitches. They also beat up an older lady in her 70s after insulting her with very bad words,” the pastor told AFP.
The West Bank violence has shocked much of the world, with Britain leading economic sanctions that in turn caused Netanyahu to voice outrage.
Netanyahu had also sought to throw doubt on the circumstances behind the beating Friday of the photographer, Heidi Levine, suggesting that Palestinians and “far-left” activists caused trouble.
But President Isaac Herzog, who holds a mostly symbolic role, took the initiative Saturday to call Levine in the hospital, calling the attack “outrageous and shocking” and saying it weighed on his conscience.
Israel Gantz, head of an umbrella settler group, blamed the recent incidents on “groups of provocateurs and terrorists” and implicitly acknowledged some Israelis’ responsibility, saying that they caused harm to the settlers’ cause.
Settlers earlier this month also beat up AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh as he covered the olive harvest tensions, fracturing several of his ribs.
Netanyahu’s government has ramped up approval of West Bank settlements, which are illegal under international law.
Some 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank, which Israel seized in 1967, alongside three million Palestinians.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi
Vice President Kashim Shettima has said he fears divisions within the ruling All Progressives Congress APC more than he fears the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Shettima spoke on Saturday in Abuja when he unveiled the campaign head office of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a northern coalition backing the Tinubu/Shettima ticket, and formally inaugurated its campaign structure.
“Honestly, I am not afraid of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP. I am not afraid of a diminished Peter Obi. But I am more afraid of internal contradictions within our household. If we unite as a people, as a family, we will conquer,” he said.
He warned northern leaders against pursuing the presidential race at the expense of their governors. “There is no point in championing the cause of the presidential election and then undermining the governor in the gubernatorial election. Honestly, it will not go down well with the system,” he said.
“Let’s rally round our governors. Let’s rally round our members of the National Assembly. Let’s rally round President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and see to the victory in the next round of elections,” he added.
The Vice President said the North had already made its choice. “By now, I believe the North has spoken. We have spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction. From Adamawa to Zamfara, from Borno to Niger, we have spoken,” he said.
He told the gathering that the poll is close. “In less than 100 days, Nigerians will return to the polls. Democracy requires us to seek their confidence again, with humility about the work outstanding and conviction about the cause we have chosen,” he said.
On Atiku Abubakar, Shettima urged party members to take him on respectfully. “Go and perform. Go and defeat Baba Atiku. Defeat him respectfully,” he said.
He said the party had the structure to contest every polling unit. “There are 176,845 polling units across the country. The APC, from ward to local government levels, has 361,045 officials. What it means is that we can match every polling unit two to two,” he said.
Shettima said appointees must prove their local strength. “Politics is still local,” he said, adding that he had asked the Borno State governor to compile a list of all political appointees from the state to local government level. “Let him account for his performance at his polling unit, at his ward unit and in his local government,” he said.
On the party’s standing in the North, he said, “Out of 19 states in the North, 18 are in the APC.” He said 15 of the 18 members of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) from Kano in the House of Representatives have crossed to the APC, adding: “The governor is with the APC.”
The Vice President acknowledged that many families are struggling. “Every household struggling to make ends meet reminds us how much remains to be done,” he said. “We lose our hearing when applause becomes our only source of information.”
Defending the administration’s economic record, he said Tinubu inherited a weak economy. “When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu assumed the mantle of leadership in this country, what we had in our foreign reserves was a country with 3.9 billion dollars, barely enough to import oil for one month. And our Ways and Means expenditure was over N27 trillion.
“Nigeria was on the road to Caracas. The economy was teetering on the brink of collapse. He literally saved the nation,” Shettima said.
He added that “for the first time in nearly 18 years, our foreign reserves are in the neighbourhood of 58.9 billion dollars.
He assured that the North has nothing to fear about a Tinubu second term.
“For the North, we have absolutely nothing to fear in a Tinubu second term. He has the North at heart,” he said.
National Chairman of the APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, moved a motion at the event for the President’s return and asked the audience to affirm it.
“Today is a time for us to renew a mandate that was largely supported by the North, and the North again will largely support the return of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a second term,” Yilwatda said.
He cited the President’s projects in the region, including the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano and Kano-Maiduguri roads. “Those two roads alone are over 900 kilometres, more than the 700 kilometres of Lagos Road,” he said.
The Director General of A4A and former Jigawa State governor, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, said the new campaign headquarters is at No. 4 Port Harcourt Street, Area 11, Garki, Abuja, and described it as “the biggest campaign office anywhere in the country.”
“Let it be understood that this building is more than just a campaign office. It is a message. It says that Arewa is serious,” Badaru said.
He said the group would run “a campaign that is disciplined, peaceful and issue-based,” taking its message to markets, farms, campuses, mosques and churches.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
EU pledges €20m defence support to Nigerian military
By Kingsley Omonobi
ABUJA — Nigeria is expecting the delivery of 10 attack helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other military equipment to strengthen its capacity to tackle emerging security threats, the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), has said.
Musa disclosed this when he received the European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), Gautier Mignot, and his delegation at Ship House, Abuja.
The meeting focused on bilateral defence agreements, including a review of security cooperation between Nigeria and the EU, as well as a proposed €20 million assistance package for the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the European Peace Facility.
In a statement by Leah Katung-Babatunde, Special Assistant on Media to the Minister, Mignot commended Nigeria’s defence leadership and invited Musa to a meeting of defence ministers in Brussels later in the year.
The minister said the shrinking of the Lake Chad Basin, on which more than 50 million people depend, remained a potential source of instability.
He added that denying terrorists access to their strongholds on islands in Lake Chad remained a key operational priority for the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF).
Musa thanked the EU for its continued support for Nigeria and assured the ambassador of President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to protecting lives and property and promoting national development.
He said relative peace was gradually returning to parts of the country through the efforts of the Armed Forces and other security agencies.
However, he acknowledged that kidnapping along major highways and attacks on isolated communities persisted, adding that security agencies were working to address the threats.
On the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme, the minister stressed that its implementation should prioritise victims of the conflict, including affected military personnel.
Mignot disclosed that an EU technical delegation would visit Abuja in November to agree on the details for delivering the proposed assistance.
He also commended a recent conference of former and serving MNJTF force commanders, which was attended by representatives of the African Union and the Lake Chad Basin Commission.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Chinese AI company DeepSeek has released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, an updated version of its Flash model with improvements in coding, agentic tasks, speed, and output efficiency.
The model is available through DeepSeek’s website, app, and API. The company has also published its weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope.
DeepSeek says the update delivers better benchmark performance than its predecessor while completing tasks faster and generating shorter responses. The company describes this as a Pareto improvement in the balance between performance and cost.
New Training Method
For end-to-end software development, DeepSeek uses a post-training method called reinforcement learning with self-feedback, or RLSF.
The technique allows the model to use its own confidence scores or generated critiques as reward signals rather than relying on human evaluators or external reward models.
DeepSeek says this improves the model’s ability to build complete projects from scratch, covering tasks including game development, 3D modeling, and design work.
The model can also create compact animated explainer videos.
DeepSeek tuned V4.1-Flash-1017 for development environments including DeepSeek Harness, Tencent CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy. The company recommends DeepSeek Harness version v0.2.1-rc.1 or newer.
Smaller Model Beats Larger Rivals
According to DeepSeek’s own benchmarks, V4.1-Flash-1017 improves over the previous V4.1-Flash across every tested category.
The company also claims the smaller model outperforms larger systems including Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 in several coding and AI agent benchmarks.
On the DeepSWE benchmark, V4.1-Flash-1017 reached a top score of 77.0% at an average cost of just under $0.20 per task.
At its low setting, the model still scored above 72% while costing around $0.10 per task.
Its predecessor reached 74.2% but cost roughly $0.50 per run.
DeepSeek’s chart places models including GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Claude Opus 5 at between roughly $2 and more than $10 per task, while showing lower accuracy than V4.1-Flash-1017.
Independent benchmarks are not yet available, and real-world developer assessments of code quality may differ from benchmark results.
Search Engine Opened to Developers
Alongside the new model, DeepSeek is opening its internal web search technology to outside developers for the first time.
The new Search and Fetch APIs use DeepSeek’s own search engine, which the company says already handles hundreds of millions of queries per day worldwide.
Each endpoint costs $0.75 per 1,000 calls.
DeepSeek API users can access the tools for free through server-side integrations in DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and Codex until October 31, 2026, at 4:00 PM UTC.
China Could Restrict Open-Weight Models
The release comes as the Chinese government reportedly considers tighter controls on publishing open-weight AI models and other key AI technologies.
Under the reported proposal, whether a model ranks among the 10 most capable systems could be one factor in determining whether additional restrictions apply.
That could complicate deeper reliance on Chinese open-weight models if tighter export or publication rules are introduced.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
A dinosaur fossil that remained largely unnoticed in a museum collection for nearly a century has been identified as a previously unknown meat-eating species with large curved claws.
The dinosaur, named Invictibellatrix amberina, lived in what is now Britain around 120 million years ago and was roughly the size of a large tiger.
Researchers led by University College London (UCL) studied the fossil, which was originally found on the Isle of Wight. Their findings were published in Royal Society Open Science.
First Known European Megaraptoran
The researchers identified Invictibellatrix as the first known European member of the megaraptorans, a poorly understood group of two-legged carnivorous dinosaurs related to tyrannosaurs.
Unlike Tyrannosaurus rex, which relied heavily on its powerful jaws, megaraptorans had narrower heads, muscular arms, and large curved claws that they likely used to capture prey.
Some members of the group later evolved into enormous apex predators comparable in size to the largest tyrannosaurs.
Invictibellatrix, however, was one of the earliest and smallest known megaraptorans.
Its name translates to “unconquered female warrior,” referring to the group’s later rise as major predators.
Fossil Had Been in Museum Collection Since 1924
The discovery came from a fragment at the back of the dinosaur’s skull that entered the Natural History Museum’s collection in 1924.
The specimen remained largely overlooked for almost 100 years before researchers examined it in detail.
Lead author Dr. Cassius Morrison of UCL Earth Sciences estimated that the dinosaur measured around three to four meters long and stood slightly more than 1.5 meters tall.
It likely had feathers and claws measuring roughly 10cm to 20cm.
Researchers believe it preyed on small dinosaurs, mammals, and lizards, occupying a role in its ecosystem comparable to that of a modern hyena.
Could Have Been Dangerous to Human-Sized Prey
Morrison said that, although humans never lived alongside the dinosaur, a human-sized animal would have been suitable prey for Invictibellatrix.
He argued that the smaller predator could theoretically have posed more of a direct threat to humans than a T. rex, which would likely have considered a human too small to be worthwhile prey.
The comparison was used to illustrate the dinosaur’s likely hunting behavior rather than suggest humans ever encountered it.
Major Gap in Megaraptoran History Filled
Megaraptoran fossils are rare, leaving scientists uncertain about where the group originated and how it spread across the ancient world.
One theory proposes that megaraptorans first evolved in Asia, moved through Europe and later reached Gondwana, which included modern-day Africa, South America and Antarctica.
Until now, no megaraptoran fossils had been identified in Europe.
Co-author and UCL PhD student Charlie Scherer said the discovery provides the first evidence that megaraptorans were present in Europe and supports the idea that they reached Gondwana through this route rather than moving between islands farther south.
CT Scans Helped
Researchers used computed tomography scans to study the skull fragment without damaging it.
The scans allowed them to create a detailed 3D reconstruction of the fossil and digitally examine the space that once contained the dinosaur’s brain.
The team compared its anatomy with skulls and braincases from tyrannosaurs, spinosaurs, raptors, and other meat-eating dinosaurs.
Several unusual features helped distinguish it from known species, including an oval opening where the spinal cord connected to the brain and a distinctive hourglass-shaped crest.
Computer-based comparisons also repeatedly placed the fossil within the megaraptoran group.
Megaraptorans Later Became Giant Predators
The researchers also studied how megaraptorans spread and evolved over millions of years.
Their models combined fossil evidence, evolutionary relationships, ancient geography and prehistoric climate conditions.
The findings suggest megaraptorans were widely distributed during the Early Cretaceous but later disappeared from Laurasia, the northern landmass containing much of present-day North America, Europe and Asia.
In Gondwana, however, some evolved into enormous predators with curved claws reaching around 35cm.
One example, Maip macrothorax from present-day Argentina, is estimated to have reached nine to 10 meters in length and weighed about as much as an elephant.
Researchers do not know exactly why megaraptorans disappeared from northern regions. Climate changes, environmental shifts and competition with other large predators, including tyrannosaurs, may have played a role.
Fossil Was Collected by an Amateur Paleontologist
The fossil was originally collected by amateur paleontologist Reginald Walter Tooley near the base of a cliff on the southwestern coast of the Isle of Wight.
Tooley collected more than 1,000 fossils, which later became part of the Natural History Museum’s collection.
Professor Paul Barrett, the study’s senior author from the Natural History Museum, said the discovery shows that historically collected museum specimens can still contain important scientific finds even after decades of study.
The species name amberina refers both to amber found in the rocks where the fossil originated and to the female given name.
Researchers said the genus name was also intended to offer encouragement to people facing bullying, discrimination, victimization and oppression.
The discovery shows that even fossils collected generations ago can still reveal previously unknown species and provide new information about how prehistoric animals evolved and spread across the world.

Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) fell 0.4% during the outgoing week, shedding 670 points, as persistent geopolitical tensions, elevated crude oil prices and concerns over a possible rate hike dampened investor sentiment.

On Wednesday, the market tentatively rebounded amid geopolitical uncertainty, with the benchmark index gaining 641 points (+0.39%) to close at 165,418, reclaiming the psychological level of 165,000. Positive momentum continued on the second last day of the trading week as the PSX held ground above 166k. The index gained 769 points (+0.46%) and closed at 166,186. The market concluded the week with a range-bound session, modestly rising by 234 points (+0.14%) at 166,420.
"The KSE-100 declined marginally by 0.4% week-on-week to 166,419 points, shedding 670 points, primarily due to persistent geopolitical uncertainty," said Arif Habib Limited (AHL) in its weekly report.
Among major economic data, Pakistan's trade deficit widened 5% year-on-year (YoY) and 7% month-on-month (MoM) to $3.53 billion in September 2026 as exports increased 18% YoY and 17% MoM to $2.96 billion, while imports grew 11% YoY and MoM to $6.49 billion. During 1QFY27, the trade deficit expanded 15% YoY to $10.77 billion, with exports rising 11% to $8.45 billion, while imports increased 13% to $19.21 billion.
AHL mentioned that the government raised Rs685.5 billion in T-bills' auction against the target of Rs550 billion, with cut-off yields inching up 0.5 basis point in three-month and 12-month tenors, while declining 5.1 basis points in the one-month and 17.9 basis points in the six-month tenor. The largest amount of Rs310.1 billion was raised via three-month papers.
The PSX recorded its highest-ever monthly addition of 25,280 new investor accounts in September, bringing total UINs to a record 656k, up 55% YoY from 423k in September 2025, reflecting growing investor confidence and broader participation in Pakistan's capital market.
Pakistan's gross Roshan Digital Account (RDA) inflows reached $14,157 million as of Sept'26. Out of the total received funds, $2,146 million has been repatriated while $8,937 million has been utilised locally. With this, the net repatriable liability stood at $3,074 million.
Oil production declined 1.7% WoW to 62.5k barrels per day, mainly due to lower flows from northern fields, while gas production decreased slightly by 0.2% WoW to 2,992 mmcfd, driven by lower production from Uch, Nashpa and Sharf.
Auto sales (cars, LCVs, vans and jeeps) decreased 3% MoM to 15.1k units during Sept'26, reflecting a decline of 12% YoY, while cumulative sales during 1QFY27 increased 19% YoY to reach 50.5k units.
Pakistan recorded a current account deficit of $356 million in September, compared to a surplus of $133 million in September last year and a deficit of $73 million in Aug'26, taking cumulative deficit for 1QFY27 to $874 million, up from $755 million in the same period of last year. Among petroleum prices, motor spirit recorded a 2.1% WoW decline to Rs390.23/litre, while high-speed diesel rose 0.3% to Rs396.96/litre, AHL added.
Topline's weekly review noted that the KSE-100 index continued its downward trajectory, declining 0.4% WoW, primarily driven by elevated crude oil prices amid US-Iran geopolitical tensions and expectations of a potential policy rate hike by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) at its upcoming monetary policy meeting to contain inflationary pressures.
Key developments during the outgoing week included: (1) automobile sales, as reported by PAMA, totalled 15,104 units in September 2026, down 12% YoY and 3% MoM; (2) the Large-Scale Manufacturing (LSM) Index increased 0.7% YoY in August 2026 but declined 5% MoM; (3) the current account recorded a deficit of $356 million in September 2026, widening from $73 million in August 2026; and (4) Pakistan's Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) rose to 108.93 in September from 107.92 in August. Average daily traded volume and value during the week stood at 449 million shares and Rs18 billion, respectively, Topline said.

Next year, the focus in Hong Kong's equity capital markets is expected to shift away from pure hardware, toward Chinese artificial intelligence models and application developers, he said.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
India's food safety authority has named officials of Reliance retail and consumer units and of Eternal's Blinkit and Hyperpure units, including Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa, in a probe over expired food products that have allegedly re-entered the food supply chain, according to case documents reviewed by Reuters.
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) of Maharashtra state, home to Mumbai, has led a crackdown on food safety under its chief Tukaram Mundhe, 51, including shutting down some of Mumbai's most popular eateries as well as outlets of Domino's and Pizza Hut for poor hygiene. The state agency has also suspended the permit of a McDonald's outlet.
The latest case, which has led to a police complaint by the food safety authority, involves large retail and quick-commerce companies, which sell products to millions of households in the world's most populous country.
Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration, according to the documents reviewed by Reuters, said its officials visited some warehouses of Reliance Retail, Reliance Consumer and Zomato Hyperpure, and that company officials could not provide verifiable proof that disposal of expired food was actually carried out by their contractors.
"The disposal agencies... do not destroy the stock," the case document alleged.
In the case of a Zomato Hyperpure warehouse, a company representative named a contractor as its disposal agency which FDA officials could not trace, according to the documents.
Reliance and Blinkit did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
"Any attempt to divert expired, damaged or consumer-rejected food products meant for destruction back into the market is a serious matter that demands strict scrutiny and accountability," Maharashtra's FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe told Reuters.
"No company, brand, business or individual is above the law when it comes to food safety."
India's intensifying crackdown
Reliance Retail and Reliance Consumer are part of billionaire Mukesh Ambani's business group. Zomato's Hyperpure is a unit of Eternal that also runs food delivery service Zomato and quick commerce business Blinkit.
The FDA probe said it found a pattern where large retail and quick commerce distribution warehouses handed over expired and customer-rejected packages of food to contractors who passed the food to unlicensed sorting yards. These sorting yards then separated out saleable-looking packets, which eventually reached other retailers and the consumer market, according to case documents from the probe.
"The chain thus runs from company warehouse to disposal agency, unlicensed yard, broker, retailer and consumer."
The Maharashtra FDA on Thursday suspended the licences of five establishments in the state – three Reliance and two Eternal entities, the case documents said.
Enforcement of food safety laws has traditionally been weak in India and the recent round of extensive crackdowns has garnered large-scale public support.
In August, Indian authorities raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo, Nestle, Coca-Cola and Unilever, so they could be exported to other countries.
Ban on added sugars in infant foods proposed
India's food safety regulator on Saturday proposed a ban on adding sucrose and fructose to food products for infants up to six months of age, tightening rules on added sugars in infant nutrition products.
Under existing rules, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant nutrition products, while sucrose and fructose can be added when required, subject to prescribed limits, the regulator said.
The move comes amid an intensifying food safety crackdown in India, where regulators have forced local eateries and branded restaurants to suspend operations, while a push for front-of-pack warning labels has rattled the country's more than $100 billion packaged food industry.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said the proposed measure aims to reduce infants' exposure to added sugars and address health risks linked to childhood obesity.
The existing regulations set nutritional composition, quality and safety standards for infant nutrition products intended for children from birth to 24 months of age, it said.
Activists and officials have long raised concerns about rising obesity rates, particularly among children. India had 180 million overweight or obese adults in 2021, a figure projected to reach 450 million by 2050, according to a study published in the medical journal The Lancet.
The FSSAI and some state regulators have intensified checks on food safety in recent months, releasing regular public updates including photos and videos of raids that have drawn widespread attention online.
In August, the FSSAI proposed a red hexagonal stamp on labels of food products high in any two or more nutrients of concern such as sugar, salt or saturated fat, but tightened the proposal after a public outcry, saying a warning would now be required if even one nutrient exceeds the prescribed level.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Competition Commission of Pakistan (CCP) has developed an artificial intelligence-powered system to uncover concealed patterns of cartelisation in Pakistan's public procurement market, where an estimated $60 billion is spent annually on goods, works and services.
The Bid-Rigging Detection System (BRDS) is designed to screen large volumes of procurement data and flag suspicious bidding patterns for investigation. Its development assumes particular significance as public procurement is estimated to account for approximately 15-20% of Pakistan's gross domestic product.
Historically, fragmented procurement data and the absence of automated links with corporate ownership records have constrained the systematic detection of sophisticated practices such as bid rotation, cover-bidding and participation by related companies across multiple tenders. BRDS seeks to shift detection from a largely complaint-driven and manual process towards proactive, systematic and data-led market surveillance, says a CCP statement issued on Saturday.
The initiative has also gained international recognition, with BRDS featuring in the Computational Antitrust Worldwide: Fifth Cross-Agency Report, published by Stanford Computational Antitrust. The report brings together first-hand accounts from 30 competition authorities and examines how computational tools are enabling regulators to undertake enforcement work that would otherwise be difficult – or impossible – through conventional methods.
BRDS has reached an advanced stage of development and pre-deployment preparation. Understandings have been reached with the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority, provincial procurement authorities and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan to facilitate its implementation and the institutional coordination required for effective data integration.
CCP Chairman Farid Ahmad Tarar said procurement worth trillions of rupees could not be effectively monitored solely through complaints and the manual examination of individual tenders. He said BRDS would enable the commission to identify complex and concealed bidding patterns across large datasets and direct its investigative resources towards the highest-risk cases.
He emphasised that alerts generated by the system would serve as investigative leads rather than determinations of wrongdoing. Each alert will require independent verification, evidence gathering and legal assessment under the Competition Act, 2010.
"CCP's contribution to the Stanford report also sets out practical lessons for competition authorities in developing economies, emphasising machine-readable data, inter-agency cooperation, controlled testing and legal defensibility," the statement said.
