items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Samsung has reportedly found overheating and sustained-performance problems with Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 during internal testing, prompting Qualcomm to push back against the claims.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is Qualcomm’s first 2nm chipset, but South Korean outlet Sedaily reports that Samsung is still seeing thermal issues despite the move to a more advanced manufacturing process and Qualcomm’s new packaging design.
Samsung has reportedly shared its findings with Qualcomm and asked the company to address the overheating problems this month.
Throttling Under Heavy Loads
According to the report, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 experiences throttling during demanding workloads, causing its clock speeds to fall when high performance is sustained for extended periods.
However, the report did not provide any figures or detailed results from Samsung’s internal testing, making it difficult to independently assess the claims.
Qualcomm has already adopted Offset PoP packaging for the chipset to improve thermal performance. Instead of placing the DRAM directly above the main silicon, the design shifts it slightly and allows a heatsink to sit above it.
An earlier test showed a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 reference device taking around 15 minutes to reach its maximum temperature threshold, more than twice as long as devices powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5.
“Claims Are 100% NOT Accurate”
Qualcomm Chief Marketing Officer Don McGuire responded to the controversy on X, saying the overheating claims were “100% NOT accurate.”
In a reply, McGuire said smartphone manufacturers are constantly tuning their platforms as products move toward launch.
That could mean Samsung’s internal testing allowed the chip to operate at its maximum power limit, potentially causing thermal throttling.
However, McGuire’s post specifically referred to the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, rather than the higher-end Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 at the center of the original report.
The omission leaves some uncertainty over whether his comments apply specifically to the Extreme version or only to the standard chip.
Extreme Version Can Run at Higher Power
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 share several similarities, but the Extreme version can be tuned to reach its advertised 5.00GHz clock speed by operating at a higher power limit.
Qualcomm has pursued higher clock speeds and the latest manufacturing processes to improve single-core and multi-core benchmark performance.
However, higher power limits can also increase heat output, meaning additional performance can come with a thermal trade-off.
Samsung Could Turn to Exynos 2700
Samsung has another option if Qualcomm cannot address the reported issues.
The company is developing the Exynos 2700, which is expected to use Samsung’s improved SF2P 2nm manufacturing process and could potentially appear in the Galaxy S27 Ultra.
The original report suggested that continued problems with Qualcomm’s chip could give Samsung more reason to use its own processor.
However, the lack of detailed internal test results has also raised questions about whether the reports could be helping build expectations around the Exynos 2700.
South Korean media have previously promoted Samsung’s Exynos chips, including the Exynos 2600, before they later fell behind competing processors in several benchmarks.
Apple’s Different Approach
The report also contrasts Qualcomm’s strategy with Apple’s approach to the A20 Pro.
Apple’s 2nm chip focuses not only on the manufacturing process but also on architectural improvements.
Paired with the vapor chamber inside the iPhone 18 Pro Max, the A20 Pro reportedly allows the phone to run cooler than Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5-powered Android gaming phones equipped with dedicated cooling fans.
For now, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 overheating claims remain unverified because Samsung’s internal test data has not been made public.
Qualcomm has disputed reports of systemic thermal problems, but questions remain because McGuire’s public response referred specifically to the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 rather than clearly naming the Extreme model.

items.content:
The Punjab Livestock and Dairy Development Department has announced that it will begin distributing free cows and buffaloes among selected widowed and divorced women in South Punjab from October 21, 2026.
According to the latest departmental announcement, women who applied under the Chief Minister’s Livestock Asset Transfer Scheme can now check whether they have been selected through the official online portal.
The initiative aims to provide livestock to deserving rural women, allowing them to generate income through dairy farming and livestock rearing.
The Punjab government conducted electronic balloting for the second phase of the scheme on October 14. The Punjab Information Technology Board (PITB) reported that 3,380 women would receive free livestock under the program.
The second phase has an estimated budget of Rs. 3 billion. The government will distribute animals among eligible women following verification and selection.
How to Check Punjab Free Livestock Scheme Selection Status
Women who previously applied for the program can check their selection status through the official Livestock Asset Transfer Portal. Applicants must visit the website and enter their CNIC number in the designated field.
They must then enter the CAPTCHA code displayed on the screen and select the submit option to check their details. The latest announcement specifically directs successful applicants to use the portal to check their selection information.
The notice concerns the distribution of livestock to previously selected beneficiaries. It does not announce a new application period.
Who Is Eligible for the Free Livestock Scheme?
The Punjab government’s livestock scheme targets widowed and divorced women living in rural areas of South Punjab. Applicants must be 55 years old or younger, possess a valid CNIC, and have a mobile SIM registered in their own name.
Women who received livestock under any government scheme during the previous five years are not eligible.
The program covers 13 districts of South Punjab, including Multan, Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Layyah, Lodhran, Khanewal, and Vehari.
The government verifies applications before selecting beneficiaries through electronic balloting.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Listed home services major Urban Company’s board approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr yesterday, seeking to shore up its war chest at a critical juncture.
On one hand, Urban Company’s instant home services business, InstaHelp, is facing stiff competition. Fighting rivals Snabbit and Pronto for a slice of the market has turned out to be an expensive affair, with spending on InstaHelp contributing to Urban Company’s widening losses.
At the same time, the company is looking to expand its product lineup under the Native brand by entering the residential air conditioner market. Meanwhile, its bread and butter consumer services continue to generate stable results.
Urban Company’s financials reflect these pressures. The company reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹144 Cr in Q2 FY27, driven by a ₹174 Cr investment in InstaHelp. Excluding InstaHelp, it reported an adjusted EBITDA profit of ₹30 Cr.
During the quarter, consolidated revenue from operations grew 41.4% YoY to ₹537.3 Cr, while total expenses increased 61.5% to ₹745.7 Cr. Consequently, the company’s consolidated net loss more than tripled to ₹182.5 Cr from ₹59.3 Cr in the year-ago period.
However, the management maintains that Urban Company can meet its profitability targets without the proposed fundraise Yet, the management has rejected the suggestion that the fundraise is necessary to offset InstaHelp’s impact on its financials.
How Badly Does Urban Company Need The Cash?
Urban Company has positioned the proposed ₹2,500 Cr fundraise as a means to bolster its balance sheet and provide greater flexibility to invest across its businesses.
“Our ambition is to go beyond being just a home services company and eventually become the trusted home platform for Indian consumers – almost the operating system for the Indian home. So given that ambition, we want the strategic flexibility over the next few years to invest in all our areas of business,” CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal told analysts during the company’s Q2 FY27 earnings call.
The company also plans to deploy the capital towards growth opportunities, including acquisitions. While no acquisition deals have been finalised till now, the management is evaluating opportunities that could help Urban Company consolidate its position in an existing market or enter a new category.
Bhal added that the company would take an opportunistic approach to international markets and Native. However, an acquisition in InstaHelp would be “highly unlikely”.
“If at all we do an M&A, it would be to add on categories that we don’t operate in today where we feel that the decision of build versus buy may be tilting in favour of buy,” he noted.
Urban Company has guided for adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 Cr in adjusted EBITDA profit by FY31. The management maintained that its current financial position, even without raising additional capital, is sufficient to meet these targets.
However, Bhal acknowledged that the company’s existing balance sheet limits its financial flexibility, given InstaHelp’s losses.
While the management maintains that the company can meet its profitability targets without additional capital, the proposed fundraise would provide it with greater room to invest in growth and respond to changing market conditions.
In particular, Urban Company is facing intense competition in the emerging quick home services segment. For instance, after Urban Company disclosed that InstaHelp completed 6.2 Mn orders in Q2, Snabbit’s founder Aayush Agarwal claimed that the startup had served 6.45 Mn orders during the period.
Diving Into A New Market
While it faces intense competition in the quick home services market, Urban Company is simultaneously looking to expand into a new category.
Alongside approving the fundraise proposal, its board proposed exploring residential air conditioners as a new business under its consumer appliances brand Native, whose portfolio currently comprises water purifiers and smart locks.
“We’ve now operated in the segment of air conditioning servicing and repair for close to 11-12 years, ever since the inception of the company. And there’s a lot of data and knowledge that we have gathered on what are the consumer pain points and what are some of the unmet needs of the consumers. Based on those data points and our own understanding of the market and the unmet needs, we have been quietly working on creating an innovative cutting-edge product,” Bhal told analysts on the call.
The company is yet to disclose further details, including a commercial launch timeline. Notably, Inc42 reported last year about Urban Company’s potential foray into AC business.
Bhal said the first one to two years in the new market would focus on learning and gathering customer feedback. He also noted that Urban Company’s app would be the sole distribution channel for its ACs.
The CEO emphasised a “calibrated and measured” approach to capital allocation, adding that Native has a clear path to profitability that should not be affected by the new venture.
For context, Native’s net transaction value (NTV) grew 35.4% YoY in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue rose 40% to ₹105 Cr. The segment remained loss-making on an adjusted EBITDA basis, reporting a loss of ₹9 Cr. However, loss as a percentage of NTV declined to 6.8% from 9% a year ago.
Urban Company’s platform sees 10X as many AC servicing, repair, and installation orders as water purifier orders, giving it a larger existing customer base for AC-related services. This provides a potential channel to market Native’s ACs, although service demand does not necessarily translate into appliance sales.
With InstaHelp facing stiff competition and Native preparing to enter a new product category, Urban Company is pursuing multiple growth opportunities even as its losses widen. The proposed fundraise would provide additional capital to support these plans, although the management maintains that the company can achieve its stated profitability targets without it.
The post Decoding Urban Company’s ₹2,500 Cr Fundraise Proposal appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
The Punjab Transport and Masstransit Department, in collaboration with the Punjab Information Technology Board (PITB), has shared the application process for the T-Cash Card, allowing commuters to pay public transport fares without using cash.
According to the latest announcement, residents can apply through the e-Transit Punjab mobile application, official online portal, or helpline 1762.
The rechargeable smart card supports cashless fare payments on Punjab’s Metrobus, Orange Line Metro Train, Speedo Bus, and Electro Bus services, along with other integrated public transport systems.
The card also offers debit card functionality for eligible financial transactions, subject to the issuing bank’s conditions.
Who Can Apply for the Punjab T-Cash Card?
Residents who use public transport in Punjab can apply for the T-Cash Card. According to the Punjab Mass Transit Authority, applicants must be at least 18 years old and possess a valid CNIC.
The application process also involves identity verification through NADRA and compliance with the relevant banking requirements. Minors can use a parent or guardian’s card under the authority’s published guidelines.
How to Apply for the T-Cash Card Online
The Punjab government has provided three application channels for commuters.
Apply Through the e-Transit Punjab App
Applicants can download the official e-Transit Punjab app on their mobile phones and open the T-Cash Card application service.
They must register or sign in, provide their personal and identification information, and complete the application according to the app’s instructions.
After submitting their details, applicants can follow the available verification, payment, and card issuance procedures.
Apply Through the Official Web Portal
Commuters can also apply through the e-Transit Punjab Web Portal. First-time users must register an account, while existing users can sign in using their registered credentials.
Applicants must select the T-Cash Card service, complete the required information, and submit their applications. The portal also allows users to check their application status.
Apply Through Helpline 1762
The government has introduced 1762 as the T-Cash Card assistance helpline. Applicants who cannot complete their registration online can call the number for guidance.
A customer service representative can assist them with the application process and related queries.
Punjab T-Cash Card Fee and Delivery Charges
The Punjab Mass Transit Authority lists the following charges for issuing a T-Cash Card.
Fee Category
Amount
Card Issuance Fee
Rs. 130
Delivery Charges
Rs. 130
Service Charges
Rs. 15
Total Listed Charges
Rs. 275
How to Recharge Your Punjab T-Cash Card
The Punjab IT Board’s latest announcement states that commuters can recharge their T-Cash Cards through the Bank of Punjab (BOP) mobile banking app or through Interbank Funds Transfer (IBFT) using a supported banking application.
The announcement specifically clarifies that card recharges should not be made through the e-Transit Punjab app. Cardholders should follow their bank’s payment instructions and verify their account or card details before transferring funds.
For applications, card tracking, and further assistance, commuters can visit the official e-Transit Punjab portal or contact 1762.
The post How to Apply for Punjab T-Cash Card Online appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Peshawar has released a list of Class 9 students for the distribution of free Chromebooks under the Prime Minister’s Digital Pakistan Initiative.
According to an official notification issued, the board has already forwarded the details of eligible students who appeared in the SSC Annual-I Examination 2026 to the Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC), Islamabad.
BISE Peshawar has directed the heads of affiliated government schools to check the published student lists and verify the academic and personal records of their students.
The initiative aims to provide digital learning devices to students in public-sector educational institutions.
Eligibility Criteria for Free Chromebooks
The Chromebook distribution process covers eligible Class 9 students from public-sector schools affiliated with BISE Peshawar.
According to the eligibility information circulated with the announcement, students who obtained 424 or more marks in the Science group and 315 or more marks in the Arts group have been identified for consideration.
However, BISE Peshawar’s official notification does not independently specify these marks as universal eligibility cutoffs. Schools should therefore check the board’s published list before confirming a student’s eligibility.
The board has uploaded the list of students on its official website, allowing school administrations to check the relevant records.
Final allocation remains subject to verification and the requirements of the Chromebook distribution program.
How Schools Can Verify Students for Free Chromebooks
BISE Peshawar has instructed the principals and heads of affiliated public-sector schools to review the official list of eligible students.
School heads must complete the prescribed verification form with accurate information, including the student’s name, B-Form number, examination roll number, board registration number, academic marks, and institution details.
Schools must provide the student’s marksheet and an attested copy of their B-Form. They must also submit an attested copy of the parent or guardian’s CNIC.
The student and parent or guardian must sign the form. The principal must then verify, sign, and stamp it.
The board instructed schools to submit the signed hard copies directly to the following address:
Office of the Director Equivalence, Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC), Plot No. 25, Street No. 38, G-10/4, Islamabad.
School heads must also inform the Director of Research and Development, BISE Peshawar, about the submission.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
Pakistan has accepted an invitation to participate in the Sultan Azlan Shah Hockey Tournament, scheduled to take place in Malaysia in November 2026.
Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) President Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani said the tournament would provide national players with valuable international experience and help improve their skills and performance.
Meanwhile, the PHF has also confirmed that Pakistan will host Canada’s hockey team for a bilateral series in Islamabad from February 8 to 21, 2027.
Wani welcomed the upcoming visit, calling it an important step toward reviving international hockey in Pakistan and strengthening sporting relations between the two countries.
The federation will work with the Ministry of Inter-Provincial Coordination and relevant authorities to arrange accommodation, transportation, sports facilities, and security for the visiting team.
The series will also provide players and officials from both countries with opportunities to gain international experience and exchange knowledge.
Pakistan’s Under-21 hockey team is currently in Malaysia to participate in the Sultan of Johor Cup.
The PHF is also working on a development plan for the Under-18, Under-21, senior men’s, and women’s teams, focusing on better coaching, training facilities, and international exposure.
The federation also plans to improve financial incentives and support for players while creating more opportunities for young talent to join the senior national team.
Wani said efforts would continue to bring international hockey competitions back to Pakistan and improve the performance of national players.

items.author: Rilwan Muhammad
items.content:
The Association of Mobile Phones and Allied Products Traders of Nigeria (AMPAT) has demanded a 90-day suspension of fees imposed on imported mobile phones, warning that the policy could force shops to close and threaten millions of jobs across the country.
The association said traders were being charged about N670 for each small phone and nearly N4,000 for bigger devices, raising concerns over the impact on businesses and consumers, particularly low-income earners who depend on affordable and refurbished phones.
Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, the association’s Kano State Chairman, Jamilu Bala Gama, who spoke on behalf of the National President, Sani Tasiu Ibrahim, said the traders supported efforts to register phones to curb counterfeiting and the use of stolen devices.
However, he faulted the implementation of the policy, demanding that the authorities disclose the legal basis for the charges and identify the private company receiving the fees.
‘It’s far better when a northerner rules’, Davido&#8217;s aide picks Atiku over Tinubu
FG taking steps against Schools Increasing Examination Fees — WAEC
“We support the registration of phones. We want fake phones out of this country. We want stolen phones to become useless. We want criminals to have nowhere to hide.
“But there is another thing happening that nobody is talking about, and that is why we are here today,” he said.
Gama said the charges could significantly increase the cost of low-priced phones, citing the example of a device sold for N10,000 that could attract a fee of nearly N4,000 before reaching the market.
He questioned the legality and transparency of the charges, saying the association had yet to be shown the law authorising them or the official fee schedule.
“Where is that money going? To a private company. Which company? Nobody knows. Under what law? Nobody has seen it. We have asked. They have not shown us,” he said.
The association warned that the policy could affect businesses throughout the mobile phone supply chain, including retailers, technicians, repairers, transporters and apprentices who depend on the trade for their livelihoods.
According to Gama, phone traders contribute billions of naira to the economy through customs duties, taxes and commercial transactions, while investing in shops, warehouses, vehicles and distribution networks across the country.
He expressed concern that increased operating costs could force small businesses to shut down and leave young people who depend on apprenticeships and phone repairs without sources of income.
“If this policy is implemented as it is, it is those millions of youths — our young people, our apprentices, our boys and girls who have just learnt a trade and opened their first small shop — who will lose their jobs,” he said.
The traders outlined five demands, including a 90-day suspension of the fees and phone-blocking measures to allow consultations with stakeholders; publication of the legal provisions and fee schedule; engagement with traders before implementation; provision of an appeal mechanism for phone users whose devices are wrongly blocked; and strict adherence to the rule of law.
Gama also called on the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) to ensure that the policy complied with the Nigerian Communications Act and the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
He said phone owners needed a clear channel to challenge wrongful blocking, particularly where devices were affected by errors or legitimate repairs.
The association disclosed that it had written to the NCC, petitioned the Senate and House of Representatives, and approached the Kano State governor over its concerns.
While insisting that it was not opposed to measures aimed at eliminating fake and stolen phones, AMPAT urged the Federal Government and the National Assembly to review the implementation to prevent unintended economic consequences.
“A policy that is meant to fight fake phones should not destroy the people who sell genuine ones. That is all we are saying,” Gama said.
He appealed to the Federal Government, the National Assembly and the Kano State Government to engage the traders and find a solution that would protect consumers and businesses while achieving the policy’s security objectives.
The NCC and the private company alleged to be receiving the fees were not represented in the statement, and their responses to the traders’ allegations were not included.

items.author: Hope Abah
items.content:
The Federal Government has been urged to integrate comprehensive climate change education into Nigeria’s national school curriculum to equip students with practical skills to tackle flooding, drought, rising temperatures and other environmental threats.
Executive Director of Climate and Green World Foundation (CGWF), Dr. Ike Anosike, who made the call in Makurdi during sensitisation lectures carried out some secondary schools, noted that the country’s education system must prepare children and young people to understand climate risks and build resilient communities.
Anosike said climate change had far-reaching implications for public health, agriculture, food security, water resources, biodiversity and livelihoods, stressing the need for urgent action to prepare learners for its growing effects.
He said the Nigeria’s education system must respond to the growing threat by ensuring that climate change education goes beyond theoretical lessons to provide learners with practical knowledge and skills for addressing environmental challenges.
‘It’s far better when a northerner rules’, Davido&#8217;s aide picks Atiku over Tinubu
Pantami’s Challenger Hamma Saleh Resigns from PDP, Joins APC
He advocated a comprehensive, age-appropriate and action-oriented curriculum covering climate science, the effects of climate change on Nigerian communities, adaptation strategies, renewable energy, environmental protection and sustainable agriculture.
The environmental expert noted that students should be taught about climate-related disasters, including flooding, drought, desertification, coastal erosion and rising temperatures, as well as their implications for food production, public health and community safety.
He also called for lessons on disaster risk reduction, early warning systems, climate justice, environmental rights and Nigeria’s climate policies to help learners understand the responsibilities of governments, businesses, communities and individuals in tackling climate change.
Anosike added that climate education should also equip students with practical skills in waste management, recycling, tree planting, forest conservation, energy efficiency and sustainable consumption.
He further stressed that schools should encourage environmental clubs, school gardens, tree-planting exercises, waste reduction initiatives and climate awareness campaigns to translate classroom learning into practical environmental action.
The CGWF boss further led his team, teachers and students to plant trees in some schools, including Christ Anglican College, High Level in Makurdi, while emphasising the need for climate change education to be integrated across relevant subjects.
Anosike also urged support for appropriate learning materials, teacher training, practical activities and community engagement with curriculum that should reflect local environmental realities.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Pakistan extended the closure of its airspace to Indian aircraft for another month, with the restriction remaining in place until November 24, the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) said on Saturday.
“Pakistan’s airspace will remain closed to Indian aircraft until November 24,” the PAA said in a new Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), making it the 19th consecutive month of the closure.
The restriction applies to all civil and military aircraft of Indian-registered airlines, the notice says. The authority added that under the extended restriction, no Indian-registered aircraft can use Pakistan's airspace, even if the aircraft has been taken on lease.
Read: Iran war deals double blow to Indian airlines already hit by Pakistan airspace ban
PAA issued the new NOTAM on the government’s directions.
Earlier, the PAA extended the restriction on Indian aircraft using its airspace until October 23.
Pakistan has kept its airspace closed to Indian aircraft since April 2025, when tensions between Islamabad and New Delhi sharply escalated after an attack in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir’s Pahalgam.
The attack killed 26 people; India immediately blamed Pakistan for the incident. Pakistan, however, categorically rejected the blame and offered to support a neutral investigation.
In response, India undertook a series of hostile actions the day after the incident. On April 23, 2025, it suspended the 65-year-old Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), cancelling visas for Pakistani citizens, closing the Wagah-Attari border crossing, ordering the shutdown of the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi, and reducing diplomatic staff at each other's embassies.
Tensions further escalated in May, when missile strikes hit six cities in Punjab and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), destroying a mosque and killing dozens of civilians, including women, children, and the elderly.
Read More: Air India feels the heat of Pak airspace ban
In response, Pakistan’s armed forces shot down Indian warplanes, including three Rafale jets. India then targeted several Pakistani airbases with missile strikes. In retaliation, Pakistan launched Operation Bunyanum Marsoos, damaging Indian military installations, including missile storage sites, airbases, and other strategic targets.
On May 10, 2025, United States President Donald Trump announced that a ceasefire had been reached following intense diplomatic efforts. Minutes later, the agreement was confirmed separately by Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and the Indian foreign secretary.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Fewer than half of the 67 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage advanced this week despite a broader market recovery. While 31 stocks gained between 0.03% and 17.63%, 36 declined, with losses reaching 18.43%.
Snapdeal parent AceVector was the biggest loser, falling 18.43% to ₹24.97, about 12% below its listing price.
Market intelligence platform Tracxn followed, declining 8.26% to ₹31.78. IndiQube and Veefin lost more than 7% each.
ixigo, EaseMyTrip, Swiggy, and Fractal touched fresh 52-week lows, while Nazara, Zelio, and E2E Networks hit fresh 52-week highs this week.
NSE SME-listed Yudiz led gains, surging 17.63% to ₹24.35, although it remained over 85% below its listing price. Nazara, ideaForge, DevX, and FirstCry were among the other gainers.
The combined market capitalisation of the 67 companies increased by $5.84 Bn to $160.55 Bn from $154.71 Bn at the end of the previous week.
Now, let’s take a look at the key developments at the new-age tech companies this week.
E2E Networks Swings To Profit
E2E Networks posted a consolidated net profit of ₹72.7 Cr in Q2 FY27 against a ₹13.5 Cr loss a year earlier. Operating revenue jumped 411% to ₹223.8 Cr from ₹43.8 Cr.
Separately, it paid fines of ₹10,000 each, plus GST, to NSE and BSE for failing to provide prior intimation of its August 31 board meeting. The cloud infrastructure company said it would strengthen compliance monitoring to prevent recurrence.
NCLT Dismisses Globalbees Insolvency Plea
The NCLT dismissed an insolvency application against FirstCry subsidiary Globalbees filed by Ashutosh Garg, Paritosh Garg, and Manju Agarwal over an alleged ₹64.92 Cr claim, plus 18% annual interest.
Separately, Globalbees extended the deadline for its ₹5.69 Cr sale of its entire 51.54% stake in textile brand Mush to November 30. The buyers are existing shareholder Nihar Gosalia and Vaishvik Brahmbhatt.
Fairfax Proposes Go Digit Stake Transfer
Fairfax proposed transferring its interests in Go Digit General Insurance and Go Digit Life Insurance to IDBI Bank. Separately, Fairfax India Holdings also proposed transferring its entire IIFL Capital Services stake to the lender.
The proposals follow the selection of a wholly owned Fairfax Financial subsidiary to acquire a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank for approximately ₹52,878 Cr. The transfers would expand IDBI’s insurance and investment services presence, subject to requisite approvals.
Lenskart Faces Customs Demand
Lenskart received an order during the week demanding ₹6.59 Cr in differential customs duty and ₹6.58 Cr in penalty, totalling ₹13.17 Cr, plus unquantified interest.
The authority reclassified certain imported optical eyeframes with clip-ons. The company said it considers the order contestable and plans to appeal.
First Games’ GST Demand Reduced
Paytm joint venture First Games Technology received a ₹703.66 Cr GST demand for April 2018 to March 2023, down from ₹5,712 Cr proposed in an April 2025 show-cause notice.
An equivalent penalty and applicable interest are additional. First Games is evaluating its statutory options.
BlackBuck Restructures Loads Business
BlackBuck approved transferring its loads business to wholly owned subsidiary BlackBuck Transport Services through a slump sale to improve operational efficiency.
The business generated ₹88.74 Cr in FY26 revenue, equivalent to 12.6% of BlackBuck’s standalone total income, and had net worth of ₹98.8 Lakh.
Aequs’ Amalgamation Proposal Rejected
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs’ regional director of South Western Region rejected Aequs’ amalgamation with wholly owned subsidiaries AeroStructures Manufacturing India, Aequs Engineered Plastics, and Aequs Force Consumer Products.
The order cited non-compliance with Section 233 of the Companies Act: shareholder approval representing 88.9% of total share value against the required 90%, uncertain delivery of postal ballot notices, pending labour cases, and missing BSE and NSE no-objection certificates.
Aequs is considering refiling or seeking approval under Section 232.
With that, here’s a look at the performance of the broader market this week.
IT Leads Market Recovery
The Sensex gained 3.11% to 74,729.27 this week, while the Nifty 50 rose 2.78% to 23,146.15. IT led sectoral gains at 11.72%, although participation beyond large-cap stocks remained muted.
Geojit Investments’ research head Vinod Nair attributed the recovery to improving rupee sentiment, softer crude prices, easing bond yields, and strong quarterly business updates. The IMF’s higher growth forecasts for India for FY27 and FY28 also supported sentiment.
Investors tracked RBI’s measures to manage public-sector oil marketing companies’ dollar demand and tighten rupee-linked forex derivatives rules. Effective October 16, banks’ minimum daily CRR maintenance rose to 99% of the prescribed requirement from 90%.
Inflationary pressures, elevated crude oil prices, and continued foreign investor outflows remained concerns for the market. FIIs remained net sellers for the ninth consecutive week, although their net selling moderated to ₹8,991 Cr from ₹30,294 Cr in the previous week. However, they turned net buyers yesterday, with net purchases of ₹1,166 Cr.
DIIs remained net buyers for the ninth straight week, investing ₹7,813 Cr. Month-to-date purchases of ₹48,168 Cr nearly offset FII selling of ₹48,769 Cr, according to Bajaj Broking.
Investors will track September infrastructure output, October flash PMI readings, and the minutes of RBI’s monetary policy committee meeting. Earnings of major lenders will also be in focus, alongside results from Infosys, Swiggy, Eternal, Dr Reddy’s Laboratories, and Tata Motors.
Nair said sustaining the recovery would require earnings growth beyond IT, with financials, consumption, and industrials’ revenue and margins under scrutiny.
Now, let’s take a deeper look at the performance of Nazara Technologies and Groww this week:
Nazara Gains Amid Leadership Changes
Nazara gained 10.02% to ₹416.80 amid a reshuffle that saw founder Nitish Mittersain move from MD to a non-executive role.
The company’s board approved CaratLane founder Mithun Sacheti’s five-year appointment as whole-time director, designated executive director, subject to shareholder approval. Arun Agrawal, former global CFO of Ness Digital Engineering, will succeed outgoing CFO Rakesh Shah. Whole-time director Rohit Sharma will step down from January 1, 2027.
The changes follow the $303 Mn acquisition of Spanish gaming companies Bluetile Games and BestPlay Systems and a ₹733.5 Cr preferential fundraise to finance it.
On the financial front, Nazara posted a ₹82.5 Cr loss in Q1 FY27, with operating revenue falling 14% YoY to ₹428.8 Cr. Bluetile’s EBITDA remained flat despite 54% revenue growth amid higher user acquisition costs.
Groww Gains Despite Flat Sequential Revenue
Groww gained 4.34% to close the week ₹200.70 after its Q2 FY27 net profit rose 54% YoY to ₹724.7 Cr and operating revenue increased 47.4% YoY to ₹1,501.5 Cr.
Sequentially, revenue was almost unchanged and profit fell 1.4% from ₹735 Cr. EBITDA slipped to ₹969 Cr from ₹971 Cr in the preceding June quarter.
Growth in margin trading and commodity derivatives offset a 14.3% QoQ decline in equity derivatives revenue. The company attributed the decline in equity derivatives revenue to adjustments following the closing auction system’s (CAS) introduction.
Expenses rose 28.5% YoY to ₹555.9 Cr, reflecting higher technology costs, AI-linked and other compute cost inflation, and ₹13 Cr in client reimbursements following a third-party market infrastructure institution’s operational issue.
Groww AMC’s assets under management rose 145% YoY to ₹7,179 Cr, although it posted a ₹8.3 Cr quarterly loss.
Separately, brokerage Jefferies reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating on Groww following SEBI’s changes to the CAS framework.
The revised rules include a shorter cash-market auction window and changes to the settlement-price calculation for index derivatives on expiry days. The updated framework is scheduled to be effective December 7, 2026.
Jefferies expects lower expiry-day volatility and regulatory uncertainty to benefit brokers more than exchanges, whose premium turnover has already recovered to pre-CAS levels.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Flipkart-owned travel platform Cleartrip’s net loss widened 28.1% YoY to ₹805 Cr in FY26 from ₹628.4 Cr in FY25, as its expenses continued to outpace revenue growth.
The online travel aggregator’s operating revenue grew 20.8% to ₹198.3 Cr during the year from ₹164.1 Cr in the previous fiscal. Including other income, Cleartrip reported total income of around ₹241.3 Cr, compared with ₹366.7 Cr in FY25. Other income declined 34.2% YoY to ₹43 Cr.
Meanwhile, spending on cashbacks and discounts rose 47.5% to ₹897.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹608.2 Cr a year earlier, outpacing top line growth.
Cleartrip generated ₹702.2 Cr from service charges and ₹378.4 Cr from commissions and incentives before accounting for cashbacks and discounts, taking the combined figure to around ₹1,095.7 Cr. These figures should be distinguished from the operating revenue reported in its financial statements.
Founded in 2006 by Hrush Bhatt, Matthew Spacie and Stuart Crighton, Cleartrip enables users to book flights, hotels, trains, buses and local activities through its website and app. Ecommerce major Flipkart acquired the company in 2021.
Cleartrip’s accumulated losses rose to ₹3,828 Cr as of March 31, 2026, from ₹3,023 Cr a year earlier. Its negative net worth also widened to ₹3,066 Cr from ₹2,262 Cr in FY25.
In its financial statements, the company said its ability to continue as a going concern depended on the success of its operations and its ability to secure funding. However, it added that its holding company, Flipkart Internet Private Limited, had provided a commitment and letter of financial support.
During FY26, Cleartrip borrowed ₹3,964 Cr from Flipkart Internet and repaid ₹3,653 Cr. Interest on these loans stood at ₹130.4 Cr for the year.
The widening loss comes as Cleartrip seeks to reduce its reliance on discounts and diversify beyond flight bookings. In July 2026, the company said it was targeting operational break-even by the end of FY27. Its plans include growing its hotels, trains and buses businesses and increasing revenue from ancillary services.
The company has also seen leadership changes in recent years. Anuj Rathi, who joined as CBO, stepped down in June 2025, less than a year after his appointment, to launch his venture, profound.me.
He was succeeded by former Flipkart executive Manjari Singhal, who previously led the ecommerce company’s beauty, FMCG and general merchandise businesses as vice-president and business head.
Before Rathi’s departure, long-standing CEO Ayyappan Rajagopal resigned from Cleartrip in August 2024 to launch quick-commerce startup FirstClub.
Where Did Cleartrip Spend?
Cleartrip’s total expenses increased 21.9% YoY to ₹1,045.9 Cr in FY26 from ₹858.2 Cr in FY25. Against operating revenue of ₹198.3 Cr, this translated into expenditure of ₹5.27 for every rupee earned from operations.
Advertisement & Sales Promotion: Cleartrip’s spending on advertising and sales promotion rose 30.9% YoY to ₹133.8 Cr in FY26 from ₹102.2 Cr a year earlier.
Employee Benefit Expenses: Employee costs increased 7.8% to ₹258.1 Cr from ₹239.4 Cr in FY25.
Payment Gateway Charges: Payment processing expenses rose 40% YoY to ₹110.1 Cr from ₹78.7 Cr.
Commission & Brokerage: Expenses under this head increased 33.2% YoY to ₹171.5 Cr from ₹128.8 Cr in FY25.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Clashes broke out between police and protesters in cities across France on Saturday as tens ​of thousands of people angered by rising costs and declining public services took to the streets in some of the country's most violent protests in years.
The ‌Interior Ministry said 272 people had been arrested by mid-afternoon after violent incidents involving hooded individuals, including in Paris, Marseille in the south, Toulouse in the southwest, Angers in the west and Lyon in east-central France.
The protesters said most people were protesting peacefully and put much of the violence down to troublemakers who had set out to cause damage and clash with the police.
The ministry said, however, that violence ​was increasing, and that there had been "confrontations with law enforcement, looting or attempted looting of shops, attacks on and damage to public buildings". It blamed the ​unrest on what it described as the "ultra-left".
In some parts of Paris, police occasionally fired tear gas rounds as they retreated in the face ⁠of mostly young protesters, many of whom were dressed in black and wore hoodies, masks and goggles to protect against tear gas.
Read: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released a day after detention
Some tourists at a fashionable department store near the ​Paris opera were seen spluttering when they were caught in clouds of tear gas, and shops nearby were hastily shuttered. Windows of many shops and restaurants in the capital were ​smashed, and cars and trash cans were set on fire.
In Lyon, protesters torched the tourist office.
In Marseille, the mayor said the town hall had been vandalised and that additional police were being sent to the city following talks with the government.
In protests partly inspired by those in France, several hundred mostly young people also protested in Brussels on Saturday, and some clashed with police. Belgian student groups have said they ​are protesting against rising education costs and reforms they fear will make higher education less accessible.
Albania also faced more protests on Saturday, with police firing what appeared to be ​rubber bullets at protesters during a fifth day of mass student demonstrations calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to step down.
Police response under scrutiny
The protests in France began last month at high schools ‌in Paris' ⁠poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards.
Read more: Greta Thunberg joins French teens on new day of school protests
"We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh, because the price of fuel is too high, because high school pupils are being violently attacked and hurt all over the country just for trying to protest and ask for more teachers and decent learning conditions," said Lola, a 19-year-old protester in Paris.
A large police presence had been deployed in central Paris, especially near landmarks such as ​the Champs-Elysees and the Arc de Triomphe, ​which were excluded from the routes of ⁠two authorised demonstrations.
Protesters in high-visibility vests blocked streets, recalling the Yellow Vest movement that marked President Emmanuel Macron's previous term in office.
Macron, who urged calm on Friday, is entering the final stretch of his presidency, facing a fragmented political landscape and growing pressure over the economy.
France's ​efforts to reduce public debt have failed to reassure investors, pushing government borrowing costs to their highest levels in more than two ​decades.
Police tactics have drawn ⁠criticism following a series of injuries among demonstrators, including a teenager who lost a hand after picking up a stun grenade. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said more than 900 police officers had also been injured in previous protests.
The police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen allegations of police violence. France suspended the use of stun grenades during the student demonstrations, but Interior Minister Laurent ⁠Nunez said ​they could be used on Saturday.
The Yellow Vest movement emerged in 2018 in opposition to diesel taxes before ​expanding into a wider protest against living costs and inequality. The movement subsided after Macron announced billions of euros in tax cuts.

items.author: Fiaz Mehmood
items.content:
An Islamabad anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday summoned the Islamabad inspector general of police (IGP) for the November 3 hearing of a post-arrest bail petition filed by Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha and issued show-cause notices to the superintendent of police (SP) and a deputy superintendent of police (DSP) over the investigating officer’s repeated absence and failure to produce the case record.
The ATC was convening a hearing of a post-arrest bail petition filed by Imaan and Hadi in a case involving protests and interference in official duties in Islamabad.
The court also warned that the concerned officers could face proceedings leading to imprisonment if the record was not presented at the next hearing.
Judge Abul Hasanat Muhammad Zulqarnain heard the bail petitions of Imaan and Hadi. Their lawyers, Raja Ali Azad and Eimal Khan Mandokhail, appeared before the court, while Special Public Prosecutor Raja Naveed Hussain was also present during the hearing.
Read: Ministry of Law issues notification for jail trial for Imaan, Hadi
During the case proceedings, the court grilled the prosecutor about the investigating officer’s absence, asking where he was and why he was not present. The court’s reader informed the judge that the IO had gone to Gilgit-Baltistan and had not yet returned.
The court subsequently summoned the SP investigation.
Islamabad Bar Council Vice Chairman Advocate Asif Irfan told the court that it was not helpless and yet it had been unable to summon the case record.
During the hearing, Advocate Azad stressed that the bail petition had been filed on October 29 and the court had issued notices, but proceedings could not move forward because of the IO’s long absence. He said that in several similar cases, when the IO was unavailable, another police official brought the record to court.
“How long would the court wait for the record?” he asked.
He then presented arguments before the judge and reminded the court about its own order that the suspects' physical remand was not required and all the charges against his clients were bailable.
He further highlighted that section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had also been added to the case and urged the court to decide the matter in accordance with the law.
During the hearing, the lawyers also referred to judicial policy, citing that bail petitions should be decided within four to five days. They said the delay was creating the impression that the accused would first be convicted in the trial of another case and then the bail petition would be decided. They stressed that the impression needed to be dispelled.
Read more: Imaan, Hadi boycott proceedings as ATC records witness statements
Advocate Aleem Abbasi urged the court to exercise its powers and decide the matter on merit.
He said the legal fraternity stood with the judiciary for its independence and warned that if the courts did not exercise their powers, everything would be taken away.
“Lawyers raise slogans for justice but are unable to secure justice for their own children,” he said, urging the court to decide the case according to its conscience.
During the case hearing, Advocate Zafar Khokhar also asserted that the lawyers would present their arguments and leave, but the situation would not create a favourable impression of the judiciary. He asked which rules and laws allow the IO to take the case record on a vacation with him.
In response, Judge Zulqarnain said the SP and DSP could be sent to jail if the case record was not produced and issued show-cause notices to both officers. He also summoned the Islamabad IGP for the next hearing.
The hearing was then adjourned until November 3.
Separately, the court ordered the discharge of workers arrested in connection with the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf long march from the cases registered against them.
It also granted bail to Jammu Kashmir Democratic Party Chairperson and Advocate Nabeela Irshad against surety bonds of Rs5,000.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that Egypt would take any measures necessary to defend Saudi Arabia if asked, ​amid escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom, and parliament announced ‌an emergency session on Sunday.
"It is inconceivable that we would allow Saudi Arabia, its security or stability to be harmed," Sisi said at a graduation ceremony ​at the Egyptian Military Academy. He said Egypt was not seeking ​to attack anyone, but was prepared to act in ⁠defence.
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport and the ​state oil giant Saudi Aramco, amid renewed fighting with the Saudi-backed forces of ​the internationally recognised government following the collapse of a truce.
Read: Iran offers help to end Saudi-Houthi conflict through dialogue
Sisi said Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin ​Salman, who visited Sisi on September 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited, ​to discuss issues including security and navigation in the Red Sea.
"I know this requires ‌the ⁠approval of the Egyptian parliament, and I ask that an emergency session be held so that it can give us that authorisation if we are asked," Sisi said.
Shortly after he spoke, parliament said it would ​hold a plenary ​session at 1pm (1000 GMT) on Sunday in response to the request, though it did not disclose the agenda.
Egypt and ​Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi ​Arabia and ⁠other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of Islamist president Mohamed ⁠Morsi ​in 2013.
Egypt also joined the Saudi-led coalition ​that intervened in 2015 to support the Yemeni government against the Houthis.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Instakart Services, the Flipkart-owned logistics company behind Ekart, nearly broke even in the fiscal year ending March 2026 (FY26). Its loss narrowed 98.3% to ₹26 Cr in the fiscal under review, compared to ₹1,508 Cr in FY25.
The brand’s revenue from contracts with customers fell 4.2% to ₹13,194 Cr in FY26, from ₹13,779 Cr in the previous fiscal year. In this, Flipkart itself contributed ₹9,112 Cr, or about 69% of the total operating revenue.
Operationally, logistics, transportation and shipping contributed the most share, approximately 50% to ₹6,419 Cr in the reported year. Revenue from this vertical plunged 39.5% YoY.
Ekart also generates revenue from collection services and warehousing services. Collection services income fell 68% to ₹510 Cr, while warehousing services income rose 44% to ₹2,212 Cr.
Including finance and other income of ₹418 Cr, Instakart’s total income fell 3.9% to ₹13,612 Cr in the year under review.
Founded in 2009 by Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal as an in-house logistics entity within Flipkart, Ekart was spun off as a separate entity in 2016 to support the fulfillment services not only for Flipkart and Myntra but also for D2C brands, online sellers and retailers.
As of last year, the company claimed to be operating more than 7,000 trucks running daily across the length and breadth of the country, 70 fulfilment centres, 80 sortation facilities and 3500 delivery hubs to ensure timely delivery across 14,000 pin codes.
Earlier in July, Ekart opened its pan-India logistics network to MSMEs, D2C brands, FMCG companies, and enterprises, allowing external businesses to access the logistics infrastructure used by Flipkart.
The logistics arm has already operationalised more than 300 franchise outlets across Surat, Mumbai, Delhi, and Bengaluru, and had plans to expand the network to over 1,000 outlets by the end of 2026.
Magnifying Ekart’s Spending
Ekart’s total expenses for the fiscal dipped by 13% YoY to ₹13,638 Cr in the year under review, while its costs stood at ₹15,673 Cr in FY25. Here is a closer look at where Ekart spent the highest:
Freight, Handling and Servicing Expenses: The spending under this head fell by 17.1% to ₹9,191 Cr in FY25 from ₹11,093 Cr in the previous financial year. Of the overall expenditure, freight costs comprised 67.4%.
Employee Benefit Expenses: Employee costs, which include salaries, provident fund, gratuity, among others, shrunk by 24.9% to ₹958 Cr from ₹1,275 Cr in FY25. Further, it accounted for 7% of the overall expenses in FY26.
Depreciation And Amortisation Expense: These costs increased by 5% to ₹1,456 Cr from ₹1,387 Cr in FY25.

items.author: Ahtesham Khan
items.content:
The federal government on Saturday formally notified the establishment of the 48-member Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) across 12 districts of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) as the governor consolidated his rule in the province.
The federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in K-P on October 11 under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, which suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and transferred executive authority to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. On October 15, a joint session of the Parliament adopted two separate resolutions ratifying the presidential proclamations imposing a state of emergency and governor's rule for two months in K-P amid opposition uproar.
Through the first resolution, the joint sitting approved the proclamation of emergency issued by President Asif Ali Zardari under the second proviso to Article 232(1) of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. The approval was granted in accordance with Article 232(7) of the Constitution.
The official notification named 48 members drawn from the tribal and adjacent districts, with Shaukatullah Khan of the Tarkani tribe from Bajaur district appointed as chairman and Malik Khan Marjan of the Wazir tribe from North Waziristan named vice chairman.
https://x.com/fkkundi/status/2111474785368858728?s=20
According to the government, the move was intended to give local communities a direct role in developmental decision-making as well as ensure closer oversight of regional development projects.
The Area Development Secretariat (ADS) outlined that the entire nomination process had been completed through extensive consultations with local jirgas (assemblies of tribal elders), held with the full cooperation of the respective district administrations.
Read: K-P is rich in minerals; we will 'extract and sell them', says Kundi
The secretariat said deputy commissioners across all 12 districts facilitated the jirgas, during which communities identified “preferred and influential tribal elders” through consensus.
Officials explained that the names emerging from the jirgas underwent careful initial scrutiny and processing by the additional chief secretary and administrator of the ADS. The refined list was then forwarded to the K-P chief secretary, who examined it and forwarded the names to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
The governor subsequently sent the final list to the federal government for formal approval.
Once the process had been completed, the federal government issued the official notification through the Cabinet Division.
The notified council members represent a broad cross-section of the region’s major tribes.
From Bajaur, the Tarkani tribe was represented by Shaukatullah Khan, Shahabuddin Khan, Malik Sultan Zeb and Haji Lali Shah. Mohmand district was represented by Malik Fayyaz Khan of the Khadikhel Khozi, Malik Nadir Manan of the Bazai and Malik Sahib Khan Amber of the Utman Khel. In Khyber, five Afridi elders — Malik Abdul Razzaq, Malik Izzatullah, Malik Salahuddin, Malik Zahir Shah and Sherin Khan — served on the council.
Kurram’s representation included Munir Hussain Bangash of the Bangash tribe, Malik Abdul Wali Khan of the Ali Sherzai, and Malik Zameen Hussain, Syed Wali Syed Mian and Ehsanullah Ehsan of the Turi tribe.
Furthermore, Orakzai nominated Lal Man Shah of the Ali Khel, Syed Fakhar Abbas of the Syed tribe and Faizullah of the Mashti. North Waziristan was represented by Malik Khan Marjan, Malik Nasrullah and Malik Haji Sher Muhammad of the Wazir tribe, along with Mufti Misbahullah Khan of the Dawar and Malik Habib Khan of the Dawar Darpa Khel. Malik Khan Marjan also discharged the duties of vice chairman.
Read more: Parliament's joint session endorses K-P emergency, governor's rule amid opposition uproar
For the ARDC, Upper South Waziristan nominated Saleh Shah of the Qureshi Mehsud, Malik Irfanuddin Ahmed Burki of the Burki tribe, and Malik Muhammad Roman Mehsud and Malik Ramtal Khan of the Mehsud tribe. South Waziristan Lower was represented by Malik Alauddin Wazir, Malik Jameel Toji Khel and Malik Moinuddin Wazir of the Wazir tribe, together with Malik Sardar Abbas of the Suleman Khel.
Bannu was represented by Baz Muhammad Khan and Maulana Abdul Ghaffar Qureshi of the Bannuchi tribe, and Malik Sherin and Malik Ehsan Khan of the Wazir tribe.
Dera Ismail Khan’s members were Abdul Haleem of the Qasuria, Sardar Aghaz Khan of the Gandapur, Sardar Ibad Khan of the Sherani and Qaiser Khan Advocate of the Mian Khel, who represented their respective areas.
From Tank, Nawabzada Abdul Wahab of the Kati Khel, Abdullah Nangial of the Mehsud and Irfanullah Kundi of the Kundi tribe were nominated. Finally, Lakki Marwat was represented by Maulana Umar Ashrafi of the Bettani tribe and Malik Idris Khan, Najeebullah Khan and Rehmatullah, alias Matti, of the Marwat tribe.
The governance strategy
Following the federal cabinet’s approval and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s advice, President Asif Ali Zardari invoked Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, imposing emergency measures and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P). The move transferred executive authority from the provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. All these measures were then ratified during the individual as well as joint sessions of the parliament held in mid-October.
The federal government subsequently formed an 11-member advisory council to oversee administrative affairs and ordered the immediate establishment of the ADS in 12 designated districts: Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, Upper South Waziristan and Lower South Waziristan. The ADS was set to operate under the supervision of the ARDC, in coordination with federal and provincial authorities, security forces and law enforcement agencies.
Also Read: Explainer: What are the ARDC and ADS, and what are their roles and objectives?
Council members were to be nominated based on population and tribal representation, with appointments to be officially notified by the federal government. The ARDC would elect its chairman and vice chairman, meet every 15 days, and convene whenever required. Its members would also serve on district coordination committees to strengthen cooperation between local representatives and administrative institutions.
The council would also identify development projects based on local needs, public demands and ground realities, submitting recommendations to the federal government.
It will also review law and order, recommend measures to counter terrorism and illegal activities, and propose improvements in governance, public safety and basic services. The arrangement aims to strengthen local representation, improve institutional coordination and ensure more effective delivery of development and security initiatives.

items.content: Financial markets are showing signs of increasing stress in funding the global artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom, with borrowing risks rising for companies involved in building AI infrastructure, according to a Jefferies research report.The report highlighted a sharp increase in credit risk indicators for companies such as Oracle and CoreWeave, raising concerns over whether financial markets will continue to support the massive investments required for AI expansion.In its GREED & fear research report titled "K-shaped stresses, AI tremors and the Houthis," Jefferies' Christopher Wood said investors should closely monitor borrowing conditions as companies continue to spend heavily on AI infrastructure.The report said investors need to remain "laser focused on credit spreads for any evidence that the market is no longer willing to fund the ongoing AI capex boom".Credit spreads are indicators of the risk associated with lending to companies. A rise in these spreads generally signals that investors are demanding greater compensation for taking on credit risk.According to the report, Oracle's five-year credit default swap (CDS) spread increased from 186 basis points on September 11 to 288 basis points, while CoreWeave's spread surged from 749 basis points to 1,118 basis points during the same period."These are the highest levels seen so far since the AI capex cycle got underway in early 2023," the report noted.It also highlighted that the yield on CoreWeave's bond maturing in 2032 had reached 14.8 per cent, indicating elevated financing costs for the company.The development is significant as expanding AI infrastructure requires substantial investments in data centres, computing capacity and related technology. Higher borrowing costs could make financing such projects more challenging, particularly for companies dependent on external funding.However, the report does not suggest that funding for AI projects has stopped. Instead, it identifies rising credit risk as an early warning sign that investors should monitor.Jefferies also highlighted the possibility of slowing earnings growth among AI-related companies. Citing a separate research report titled "Diversifying Beyond AI," published on October 13, it said consensus earnings growth for global AI stocks is expected to moderate from around 100 per cent in 2026 to 30 per cent in 2027 and 22 per cent in 2028.The report noted that global AI stocks trade at 23 times forward earnings, compared with 13 times for non-AI stocks, reflecting a considerable valuation gap.The findings suggest that although investment in AI remains substantial, rising financing risks and expectations of slower earnings growth could increase pressure on companies to justify their spending.

items.content: The global race to expand artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities could increasingly be determined by which companies can secure enough electricity, financing and data-centre infrastructure to operate advanced chips, rather than simply by their ability to acquire the latest technology, according to a Morgan Stanley research report.The assessment comes as rapid investment in AI infrastructure threatens to outpace the availability of electricity, raising concerns that smaller companies could struggle to compete with financially stronger technology giants.In its equity research report titled "What Does the Power Shortfall Mean for Semis?", Morgan Stanley estimated that US data-centre developers could face a 32-gigawatt (GW) power shortfall through 2028, even after accounting for additional power-generation solutions. This represents around 34 per cent of projected power requirements.The report said, "Nvidia confirmed our thesis that there is not enough power to meet demand, and there are more semiconductors being built than there are places to put them."The findings suggest that expanding chip production alone may not be enough to sustain the AI boom unless companies can also secure electricity, suitable land and operational data centres.Morgan Stanley said access to electricity was increasingly favouring large companies with strong financial backing and predictable revenues."We believe we're in an environment where data center energization is being concentrated across a handful of large, credit-worthy players," the report stated.It added that companies with strong credit support and large power requirements were securing electricity more quickly, potentially leaving smaller developers at a disadvantage.The research estimated that major technology companies and specialist cloud providers could account for approximately 94 per cent of global data-centre capacity additions in 2026, followed by 64 per cent in 2027 and 57 per cent in 2028."We believe this could potentially 'squeeze out' or put pressure on other players over time," Morgan Stanley said.The constraints could also affect semiconductor manufacturers if data centres are unable to install the chips they have ordered."If there's chip capacity expected to come online that cannot be deployed at data centers, we could see customers push out delivery or start canceling orders," the report warned.However, Morgan Stanley expects Nvidia and Broadcom to meet their 2027 forecasts, citing their visibility into customer demand and infrastructure availability. It sees greater risks for suppliers of memory chips, optical equipment and other supporting components if deployment slows.The report also indicated that the infrastructure challenge could persist beyond 2028, with the projected cumulative US data-centre power shortfall potentially widening to 68 GW by 2029.The shortage could encourage technology companies to expand computing infrastructure outside the United States, including in Asian markets such as India.Morgan Stanley's Asia data-centre team estimates that 14 GW of demand from US hyperscalers could shift to Asia through 2030, although the report does not specify India's share."While we expect international expansion to continue, we don't see it as a solution to the US power problem," the report said.The findings underline a growing challenge for the AI industry: technological advances and spending on chips may not translate into additional computing capacity unless electricity supply and supporting infrastructure expand at a similar pace.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday, a ‌day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief.
Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), rose to prominence this year when a weeks-long ​sit-in contributed to India's education minister resigning.
CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was ​released after he agreed to certain conditions. Singh gave no details of the ⁠terms.
Dipke's youth-led group, opposition parties and student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief ​Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya ​Janata Party (BJP).
Read: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Dipke ahead of protest
More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning ​legitimate electoral processes.
Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained ​on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday.
"Please, spare the people ‌of ⁠India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.
Student groups call for more protest action
Dipke was detained on Friday as ​he stepped out of a ​house in central ⁠Delhi, with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument.
Read more: From theatre to streets, Gen Z protester Neha Bora a new face of India's youth unrest
Dipke had called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders ​detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating ​at a protest ⁠site in violation of a ban.
Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.
Student groups called for more protest action on Saturday.
The movement, which was mobilised by the ⁠youth and ​joined by many opposition parties, has emerged as one of ​the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and the BJP in the prime minister's 12 years in power.

items.title: Ufone achieves global recognition at Dragons of Asia 2026
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pak Telecom Mobile Limited (PTML), through its brand Ufone 5G, has won two awards at the Dragons of Asia Awards 2026, including a Gold Dragon in the hotly contested ‘Best in Media’ category for its ‘Super 5’ campaign, and a Black Dragon in the ‘Marketing Discipline’ category for ‘Babar Azam’s Lost Phone’ campaign. Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pak Telecom Mobile Limited (PTML), through its brand Ufone 5G, has won two awards at the Dragons of Asia Awards 2026, including a Gold Dragon in the hotly contested ‘Best in Media’ category for its ‘Super 5’ campaign, and a Black Dragon in the ‘Marketing Discipline’ category for ‘Babar Azam’s Lost Phone’ campaign. Ufone was the only telecom brand from Pakistan to win a Gold at the prestigious awards.
The Dragons of Asia recognize excellence in results-driven marketing communications across the region, and celebrate campaigns that combine strategic insight, creative thinking and effective execution. Ufone’s double win underscores its ability to translate consumer insights into compelling brand experiences that resonate with audiences.
Built around Ufone’s Super 5 package, which enables customers to share data, calls and SMS with four friends or family members, the Gold-winning campaign brought together comedian and television host Tabish Hashmi and former Pakistan cricket stars Younis Khan, Shoaib Malik, Abdul Razzaq and Saeed Ajmal, all members of Pakistan’s 2009 ICC T20 World Cup-winning squad.
Launched in February 2026, the campaign sparked public curiosity through teaser videos on social media in which the cricketing legends hinted at a mysterious “selection”, prompting speculation about a possible return to the game. The eventual reveal through the ad campaign turned the premise on its head by showing the players competing for a place in Tabish Hashmi’s own Super 5 group. The campaign ran across Pakistani television channels and digital platforms, attracted coverage from multiple digital media outlets, and garnered millions of views online.
The Black Dragon-winning ‘Babar Azam’s Lost Phone’ campaign promoted Ufone’s Weekly Grand Offer. Launched in February 2025, it began with cricketer Babar Azam announcing on social media that he had lost his phone and contacts. The reveal showed this to be part of a Ufone campaign, with Babar searching for his phone alongside fans before presenting the offer. The campaign immediately became a fan favorite, piqued international interest, and garnered over 10 million views. Both campaigns sparked instant, organic conversation on social media, as audiences speculated, reacted, and shared, giving each campaign momentum from the first day.
Commenting on the achievement, Syed Atif Raza, Chief Commercial Officer, PTML, said,
“We wanted our campaigns to be something people would talk about, not just watch. Our approach is to understand consumer behavior, challenge conventional thinking and back ideas that stand out. Having this work recognized at the Dragons of Asia is a proud moment for us, and it is encouraging to see locally developed ideas earn international recognition. It strengthens our ambition to take our work beyond Pakistan’s borders. I commend the Brands and Media teams, and our agency partners, whose strategic thinking, creativity and execution brought these ideas to life.”
The double win reflects Ufone’s continued focus on marketing excellence and on campaigns that are as creative as they are effective, and stand to show how a clear consumer insight, told with humor and cultural relevance, can turn a product offer into a story audience choose to watch and share.
