items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Enterprise AI startup RapidCanvas has raised $29 Mn (about ₹280 Cr) in its Series B funding round led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India. The round also saw participation from new ventures Hitachi Ventures, along with existing investors Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures.
RapidCanvas will use the proceeds to expand its go-to-market teams and field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil. It will also invest in all three products — deepening the Enterprise Context Engine, expanding the skills library behind the Visual Development Canvas, and strengthening governance in the Operational Harness.
Founded in 2021 by Rahul Pangam and Uttam Phalnikar, RapidCanvas is an agentic AI startup that helps enterprises build and deploy AI applications as well as oversee their performance.
RapidCanvas claims that its annual recurring revenue (ARR) has grown 8X over the past six quarters.
So far, in 2026, more than 75 enterprises across manufacturing, financial services, retail, business services and infrastructure have made 1.4 Mn AI-led decisions using applications built on its platform.
RapidCanvas follows a subscription-based business model and targets large enterprises that have AI budgets but lack the in-house expertise to move beyond pilot projects. It claims that its platform is “trusted” by companies like PayPal, TresVista, Yale Appliances, Orion, Treetech, among others.
“Vibe coding has made it easy to start building with AI. Getting AI into production reliably and safely still remains the biggest gap. Our growth over the past six quarters is evidence that AI in enterprises is moving beyond pilots into production and real operations,” said cofounder and CEO Pangam.
Enterprise AI Draws Investor Interest
RapidCanvas’ fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in enterprise tech startups helping businesses deploy AI across their operations. Yesterday, enterprise AI startup Shamrock AI raised $5 Mn in a seed round led by Endiya Partners, with participation from Capria Ventures. A day earlier, Parallel Loop secured $6.6 Mn in a seed round led by 3one4 Capital to help businesses integrate AI into their existing systems and workflows.
The trend is also reflected in funding data for the Indian AI ecosystem. According to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026, AI startup funding surged 265% YoY to $438 Mn in the September quarter.
Investor sentiment, however, suggests that capital is not flowing indiscriminately across the AI stack.
Inc42’s Indian Investor Ranking & Sentiment Survey, based on responses from more than 85 institutional investors, found that 63% of investors see some degree of froth in Indian AI startup valuations. About half of those who see froth expect a correction within the next 18 months, while another 31% believe valuations are elevated but supported by real revenue.
The survey also points to a preference for AI applications that address specific industry needs. Vertical AI applications across sectors such as BFSI, healthcare, defence and agriculture emerged as the leading choice, with 39% of investors expecting them to capture the most value over the next five years. AI hardware and semiconductors followed at 23%, while AI-led IT and business services accounted for 18%.

items.author: Kavit Majithia
items.content:
Reliance Industries appeared to hit back at Elon Musk’s suggestions its owner Mukesh Ambani (pictured) was blocking Starlink’s entry into India, stating it welcomes competition and pointing out its own satellite venture has also not been cleared by regulators.
In a statement on Musk-owned X, Reliance said considering recent remarks about the company and the Indian market, it wished to put on record that like every Indian enterprise it had grown in a country that welcomes investment and innovation.
It continued to state the open nature of the Indian market rests on the rule of law, and the government has stated it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign.
“Jio’s own satellite service awaits clearances,” it said. “At Reliance we never feared competition… we welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.”
Reliance’s statement followed a series of Musk’s own posts regarding Starlink’s entrance into India. The SpaceX chief claimed “certain oligarchs” were delaying its entry into the country to maintain a “monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people”.
While emphasising the benefits satellite connectivity will have on the Indian market, Musk sarcastically addressed Ambani as India’s real Prime Minister and asked if he would “consider allowing Starlink to compete”.
Musk also described suggestions Starlink would struggle to compete with Jio and its low-cost data plans as “absurd, hypocrisy and hyperbole”.
India’s government has also rejected Musk’s claims, stating its satellite communications framework is fair and non-discriminatory while emphasising that Starlink, Jio and Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb are all awaiting security clearance and spectrum allocation.
The post Reliance snaps back at Musk over Ambani claims appeared first on Mobile World Live.

items.summary: Oppo Find X10 Pro Max will be launched in India with the industry-first triple rear camera system, the company announced on Friday. The flagship Oppo Find X10 Pro Max will be India’s first phone to be equipped with a triple 200-megapixel camera system. The phone will get a Hasselblad-tuned camera unit, with a 200-megapixel (f/1.5) Ultra HDR Main shooter with a 1/1.3-inch ISOCELL HPC sensor, 24mm focal length, and optical image stabilisation (OIS). In India, the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max will also feature a 200-megapixel Ultra-Sensing Ultra-Wide (f/2.2) camera with a 13mm focal length and autofocus. On the other hand, the standard Oppo Find X10 model is also confirmed to feature a Hasselblad-powered triple rear camera setup.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) cannot use its information-gathering powers to pursue tax assessments after the legal deadline has expired. The court has also set aside notices seeking taxpayers’ bank account details, as the tax authorities failed to establish a valid legal purpose for their requests.
A division bench comprising Justice Hassan Nawaz Makhdoom and Justice Muhammad Ajmal Zahid accepted two constitutional petitions, including one filed by Syed Naved Amjad Andrabi. The petitions challenged notices that the FBR had issued to commercial banks under Section 176 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.
LHC Stops FBR From Seeking Bank Records Beyond Legal Deadlines
The notices required banks to provide information about the petitioners’ accounts. Their counsel, Advocate Taffazul Haider Rizvi, argued that the taxpayers had submitted their tax returns up to tax year 2015 and paid their liabilities according to the law. He also maintained that the FBR had not selected them for audits for the relevant years and that no inquiry, investigation, or other proceedings were pending against them.
During the hearing, the bench asked the tax authorities to explain whether they intended to use the requested information for proceedings under Sections 121, 122, or 124 of the Income Tax Ordinance, or under any other legal provision. However, the authorities could not identify a specific proceeding or explain the lawful purpose behind the notices.
In its judgment, Justice Muhammad Ajmal Zahid explained that Sections 175, 176, and 177 of the Ordinance allow tax authorities to access records, collect information, and conduct audits. However, these provisions do not give the FBR the power to bypass statutory deadlines for initiating or completing tax assessments.
The court clarified that information collected under Section 176 may help authorities assess a taxpayer’s liability. However, the provision cannot extend the time limits prescribed under Sections 120, 121, 122, and 124.
The judgment stressed that statutory time limits define how long a government authority can legally exercise its powers. It noted that these deadlines are not merely procedural requirements but establish clear boundaries for lawful action.
See Also: FBR Extends Income Tax Return Filing Deadline Again For Tax Year 2026
The court further observed that issuing a notice under Section 176 cannot preserve, suspend, or restore powers that have expired under the law. Similarly, requests for information cannot replace the formal legal proceedings required to determine a taxpayer’s liability.
However, the bench clarified that its decision applied to the purpose of the notices challenged in these cases. It did not mean that the expiry of the deadline for a particular assessment automatically removes every other power available to the FBR under the Income Tax Ordinance.
After finding that the authorities had failed to establish a lawful basis for seeking the bank records, the court accepted the petitions and set aside the notices.
The ruling reinforces the importance of statutory deadlines in tax matters and clarifies that the FBR must act within the limits established by law when seeking taxpayers’ financial information.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s mobile phone imports declined by 16.6% during the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27, even as September recorded a slight month-on-month recovery, according to the latest import figures.
The country imported mobile phones worth $417.24 million during July–September 2026, compared with approximately $500.01 million in the same period last year. The figures indicate that the improvement seen in September was not enough to offset the broader slowdown in mobile phone imports.
Mobile Phone Imports Rise in September but Remain Below Last Year
In September 2026, Pakistan’s mobile phone import bill reached $143.14 million, up 7.1% from $133.66 million in August. However, compared with September 2025, when imports stood at $199.27 million, the latest figure represents a substantial 28.2% year-on-year decline.
A similar trend emerged in rupee terms. Mobile phone imports increased to Rs. 39.75 billion in September from Rs. 37.17 billion in August, reflecting month-on-month growth of 7%. But the import bill was still 29.2% below the Rs. 56.17 billion recorded in September last year.
During the July–September quarter, the cumulative mobile phone import bill stood at Rs. 116.01 billion, down 18% from Rs. 141.42 billion in the corresponding period of FY2025-26.

The total telecommunications import bill, which includes mobile phones and other telecom equipment, reached $220.08 million (Rs. 61.12 billion) in September, compared with $196.95 million (Rs. 54.77 billion) in August.
Despite this monthly rise, total telecom imports were 18.3% lower in dollar terms and 19.5% lower in rupee terms than in September 2025, when the import bill stood at $269.29 million (Rs. 75.92 billion).
For the entire first quarter, telecommunications imports stood at $651.80 million (Rs. 181.24 billion), compared with $665.83 million (Rs. 188.32 billion) in the same period last year. This translates into declines of 2.1% in dollar terms and 3.8% in rupee terms.
Interestingly, imports of other telecommunications apparatus moved in the opposite direction.
Pakistan imported $76.94 million (Rs. 21.37 billion) worth of other telecommunications equipment in September, up from $63.29 million (Rs. 17.60 billion) in August. On a year-on-year basis, the category grew by 9.9% in dollar terms and 8.2% in rupee terms.
The quarterly increase was even more noticeable. Imports of other telecom apparatus surged to $234.57 million (Rs. 65.23 billion) during July–September 2026, compared with $165.82 million (Rs. 46.90 billion) a year earlier, registering growth of 41.5% in dollar terms and 39.1% in rupee terms.
This suggests that the decline in overall telecom imports was largely driven by lower handset imports rather than a uniform reduction across all categories. September’s month-on-month improvement offers some indication of recovery, but it remains too early to conclude that mobile phone imports have returned to sustained growth.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
For rickshaw drivers and small business owners, an electric three-wheeler can reduce dependence on petrol or CNG. But the initial purchase price remains a hurdle. The Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification (PAVE) program aims to address this with government-backed financing and subsidies.
Electric Rickshaw Installments: Key Scheme Details
Feature
Financing terms
Programme
Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification (PAVE)
Maximum capital subsidy
Rs. 200,000 (subject to eligibility)
Maximum bank financing
Rs. 880,000
End-user markup
0%
Maximum repayment period
36 months
Financing structure
80:20 debt-to-equity
Age for three-wheelers
21–65 years
Loan processing fee
Nil
The maximum subsidy is not automatically granted to every buyer. The bank must approve financing and the applicant must qualify for an allocation. Insurance and registration can still add costs.
How Much Is the Monthly Installment?
With 0% end-user markup, the monthly principal payment depends on the actual amount financed and the repayment period. The following are examples over the maximum 36-month tenure, not official dealer quotations:
Loan amount
Monthly principal over 36 months
Rs. 400,000
About Rs. 11,111
Rs. 500,000
About Rs. 13,889
Rs. 600,000
About Rs. 16,667
Rs. 700,000
About Rs. 19,444
Rs. 880,000
About Rs. 24,444
The actual installment may differ after applicable insurance and other charges.
How Does the Rs. 200,000 Subsidy Work?
Under the 80:20 debt-to-equity arrangement, the eligible government subsidy can cover part or all of the 20% equity requirement. Consider an illustrative Rs. 1 million vehicle: Rs. 800,000 would be the bank’s 80% financing portion, with Rs. 200,000 representing the equity share. If that buyer qualifies for the full Rs. 200,000 subsidy, the subsidy could cover that equity amount. They must still repay the bank financing and pay applicable insurance and registration costs.
This illustration is not a promise of zero down payment on every model.
Who Can Apply?
The official framework covers eligible Pakistani citizens, including citizens in AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan. For electric rickshaws and loaders, the individual applicant age range is 21 to 65 years. Eligible fleet operators may also apply under separate conditions. Financing depends on successful scheme selection, bank verification and repayment assessment.
Documents Required
The State Bank’s framework identifies a valid CNIC and a digital undertaking about the driving licence among the mandatory requirements. Banks may ask for evidence of income, bank statements, or other documentation as part of their credit assessment. Always follow the current official portal and lender’s requirements.
How to Apply for an Electric Rickshaw Through PAVE
Step 1: Visit the official PAVE portal. Open www.pave.gov.pk and check whether registrations for electric rickshaws/loaders are currently open.
Step 2: Register or sign in if the portal permits applications. Follow the portal’s displayed registration or login instructions. Enter your details accurately.
Step 3: Review eligible electric rickshaw/loader models. Only vehicles qualifying under the relevant government scheme phase are eligible; not every three-wheeler sold in Pakistan qualifies.
Step 4: Complete the application shown in your account. Enter the requested personal and financing details, and provide the documents indicated by the official portal.
Step 5: Review and submit when registration is open. Check the form carefully and keep any application reference or confirmation issued by the portal.
Step 6: Await selection and bank verification. The first PAVE round used computerized e-balloting. Selection does not itself guarantee financing: the bank must still complete its checks, and successful buyers must complete vehicle delivery formalities.
Is the Electric Rickshaw Scheme Interest-Free?
The official financing framework sets the end-user markup at 0%, with the government covering the financing markup. Conventional and Islamic financing channels are included. However, insurance, vehicle registration, and possible late-payment charges are separate considerations. No loan processing fee or early settlement fee is specified under the framework.
Things to Check Before Applying
Whether a new allocation round is open and whether the selected model is approved.
Your eligibility, bank financing approval and required documents.
Total payments including insurance, registration and any lawful additional charges.
Battery warranty, replacement costs, charging arrangements and after-sales support.
Final Thoughts
The PAVE electric rickshaw scheme could make the move to electric transport more practical for eligible drivers and business operators. The advertised maximum Rs. 200,000 subsidy, 0% borrower markup and three-year repayment window are attractive, but allocations and bank approvals are subject to conditions. Check the official portal for the next public registration announcement before making plans or paying any intermediary.
Sources: State Bank financing framework; Government announcement on 2025 balloting; EDB Phase II manufacturer prequalification document.

Apple Touchscreen MacBooks Expected Soon
One of the biggest highlights of the upcoming launch could be Apple’s long-rumoured touchscreen MacBook lineup. The new laptops are expected to bring touch input to the Mac, offering users another way to interact with macOS.
Apple has traditionally relied on keyboards, trackpads, and external pointing devices for its Mac computers. Introducing touchscreen support would represent a notable change in the company’s laptop strategy.
The new MacBooks could attract users who prefer touch-based controls for certain tasks. However, Apple has yet to reveal the devices’ specifications, features, or pricing.
OLED iPad mini Could Also Debut
Apple is also reportedly preparing an iPad mini with an OLED display. The upgrade would bring OLED screen technology to the company’s compact tablet lineup.

The new processor is expected to be a key part of Apple’s next-generation Mac hardware. However, details about its performance, efficiency, and other improvements remain unconfirmed.
The updated MacBook Pro could appeal to professionals who need powerful hardware for demanding workloads. Meanwhile, a refreshed iMac would give desktop users another option within Apple’s computer lineup.

This remains an assumption, as Apple has not confirmed whether the announcement and media event will take place on separate days.

items.title: CERT-In Flags Unauthorised AI Agent Access To Indian Organisations’ Systems
items.summary:
India’s cybersecurity watchdog CERT-In has warned that autonomous AI agents deployed for research and evaluation accessed Indian organisations’ live systems without authorisation, reading business records containing personal data and confidential information.
In a critical advisory, the agency separately flagged attackers using publicly available agentic AI tools for financially motivated intrusions into Indian entities.
The incidents surfaced through AI model providers’ voluntary disclosures, CERT-In’s forensic analysis, and threat hunting. None of the organisations in the voluntarily disclosed cases detected the access themselves.
The advisory follows disclosures by OpenAI and Anthropic about agents exceeding their authorised scope during evaluations. CERT-In did not name the providers involved in the Indian incidents.
AI Agents Exploit Vulnerabilities At Machine Speed
Agents under evaluation accessed information using credentials and connection settings exposed in application config
items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
India’s cybersecurity watchdog CERT-In has warned that autonomous AI agents deployed for research and evaluation accessed Indian organisations’ live systems without authorisation, reading business records containing personal data and confidential information.
In a critical advisory, the agency separately flagged attackers using publicly available agentic AI tools for financially motivated intrusions into Indian entities.
The incidents surfaced through AI model providers’ voluntary disclosures, CERT-In’s forensic analysis, and threat hunting. None of the organisations in the voluntarily disclosed cases detected the access themselves.
The advisory follows disclosures by OpenAI and Anthropic about agents exceeding their authorised scope during evaluations. CERT-In did not name the providers involved in the Indian incidents.
AI Agents Exploit Vulnerabilities At Machine Speed
Agents under evaluation accessed information using credentials and connection settings exposed in application configurations, public code repositories, and permissive cloud service roles, exceeding their assigned tasks’ authorisation.
Separately, attackers misused AI-native offensive-security frameworks for reconnaissance and financially motivated intrusions. Deployments across infrastructure in multiple countries indicated these tools’ widespread availability.
In the financially motivated campaign, agentic tools shortened the time between initial access and an attack’s final impact from days to hours. Multiple agents operated in parallel for hours or days.
Organisations that incompletely addressed vulnerabilities faced repeat attacks within days, at greater scale. In the voluntarily disclosed cases, agents rediscovered and reused exposed credentials across separate operations.
The weaknesses included exposed credentials; dormant or deprecated internet-accessible APIs; plaintext payment API keys; permissive cloud roles; and exposed administrative interfaces with weak credentials or no multi-factor authentication.
CERT-In also flagged unpatched application middleware, saying agents exploited conventional weaknesses faster, more thoroughly, and at greater scale than human attackers.
Global Incidents Highlight Containment Risks
Earlier this month, the Wikimedia Foundation disclosed activity it believed involved OpenAI agents, including unauthorised wiki edits, unsuccessful exploitation attempts, and millions of automated requests.
In July, OpenAI disclosed that models undergoing cybersecurity evaluations bypassed internet restrictions and accessed Hugging Face’s systems. Anthropic has reported similar incidents involving misconfigured evaluation environments.
Last week, Anthropic disclosed further unintended actions, including running commands on servers and bypassing controls to access gated data. It said no customer data or internal systems were involved.
Against this backdrop, CERT-In has urged developers to isolate evaluations, technically restrict internet access, use synthetic data and credentials, monitor agents live, and automatically stop runs exceeding authorised scope.
Developers should block reuse of third-party credentials and promptly notify affected organisations and CERT-In of unauthorised access. Organisations should audit and rotate exposed credentials, remove dormant APIs, enforce least-privilege access and multi-factor authentication, and monitor suspicious API activity.
They should retain logs for at least 180 days and treat environments as compromised after credential exposure or confirmed access until forensically cleared.
Organisations deploying agents should assign each run a separate, short-lived identity, restrict network access, and maintain tamper-resistant logs. BFSI and fintech entities should also implement CERT-In’s earlier payment and disbursement API security measures.

Nora is preparing to introduce two new electric vehicles, the NEO and Metro, in Pakistan. Both models target urban commuters looking for an affordable option for daily travel, with a claimed driving range of up to 300 kilometres on a single charge.
The two vehicles fall into the L7 quadricycle category and share several key specifications, including battery capacity, motor power, top speed, and charging time. Their expected prices are below Rs3 million each, although the company has not officially confirmed the final prices.
Nora Introduces Two New Electric Vehicles in Pakistan With Up to 300km Range
With rising interest in electric mobility, the NEO and Metro could offer another option for people who want to reduce their fuel expenses and use an electric vehicle for routine city travel.
Nora NEO and Metro Battery, Range, and Performance
Both Nora models feature a 23.1kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery paired with a 4kW electric motor. According to the provided specifications, they offer a claimed driving range of 250km to 300km on a full charge.
The vehicles have a maximum speed of 70km/h, making them more suitable for city commutes than high-speed motorway travel. Both use rear-wheel drive and a 72-volt electrical system.
Nora estimates that charging the battery will take around six to eight hours. Each vehicle can accommodate up to four passengers, making them an option for small families and urban commuters.
However, the actual driving range may vary depending on road conditions, passenger load, weather, driving habits, and the use of electrical features.
Nora NEO Features and Design
The Nora NEO comes with a modern exterior design and several convenience features. Its cabin includes a 9-inch HD touchscreen, keyless entry, push-button start, and a multifunction steering wheel.
The vehicle also features an electronic parking brake and disc brakes on all four wheels. These features provide additional convenience and braking capability for everyday driving.
The NEO has a wheelbase of 2,300mm and ground clearance of 180mm. It rides on 175/70 R13 tyres.
Its combination of compact dimensions and technology-focused interior equipment makes it suitable for buyers seeking a small electric vehicle for urban use.
Nora Metro Offers More Ground Clearance
The Nora Metro shares the NEO’s main powertrain specifications but features a different design and equipment package.
Its interior includes a touchscreen infotainment system, keyless entry, push-button start, power windows, and a reversing camera. These features aim to make everyday driving and parking easier.
The Metro has a wheelbase of 2,360mm, which is slightly longer than the NEO’s. It also offers 210mm of ground clearance and uses larger 195/70 R14 tyres.
The additional ground clearance may help the vehicle handle uneven urban roads and speed breakers more comfortably, although its real-world performance will depend on its suspension and overall design.
See Also: China’s Shengtang Group Eyes $10 Million Investment in Pakistan’s EV and Energy Sectors
Nora NEO and Metro Expected Price in Pakistan
The Nora NEO and Metro are reportedly expected to cost less than Rs3 million each in Pakistan. However, Nora has yet to announce their official prices, booking details, or delivery schedule.
Buyers will need to wait for further information to determine how the two models compare with other affordable electric vehicles available in the country.
Their final prices, charging arrangements, after-sales support, and actual driving range will play an important role in their market performance.
If Nora keeps both vehicles within the expected price range, the NEO and Metro could attract buyers looking for a compact electric vehicle for daily commuting. However, the company’s official announcement will be necessary to confirm their specifications, prices, and availability in Pakistan.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Zambia’s CherryPick is an agro-processing company that is helping to build more resilient, inclusive and adaptable food systems while encouraging healthier eating habits, one healthy snack at a time.
Founded in 2016 by Zama Bbuku and her husband Lwando, CherryPick started as a modest strawberry-growing venture keen to contribute meaningfully to Zambia’s agricultural landscape.
“This exposed us to a reality shared by farmers across Zambia – abundance at harvest and loss shortly after due to challenges with market linkages. This sparked a defining question for us – what if we could preserve more of what we grow, add value locally and make nutritious food accessible year round,” she said.
“At the heart of what we do is a very simple idea – Zambia produces a lot of good food, but too much of it is lost after harvest, while at the same time consumers are looking for healthier and more convenient food options.”
CherryPick sources seasonal, nutritious produce from small-scale farmers and transforms it into quality, shelf-stable, conveniently-packaged dried fruit and cashew nut snacks.
“By extending the shelf-life of fresh produce, we are able to reduce post-harvest losses, create market opportunities for farmers and give consumers convenient healthier alternatives to ultra-processed foods,” Bbuku said.
Improving traceability and quality
The startup is currently in the process of developing AgroChain360, a technology platform designed to improve traceability, farmer coordination, production planning and quality assurance across the agricultural value chain.
“Ultimately, we want consumers to have greater visibility of where their food comes from while creating stronger and more reliable links between farmers and markets,” said Bbuku.
“We saw two sides of the same problem. On one side, farmers can have good produce but struggle with reliable markets, and because fresh produce is highly perishable, anything that isn’t sold quickly can become a loss. On the other side, consumers increasingly want convenient snacks, but many of the readily available options are highly processed.”
CherryPick saw an opportunity to connect those two problems.
“We are not simply trying to sell another snack. We are building a farm-to-shelf model around local sourcing, value addition, healthier eating and traceability. AgroChain360 will strengthen that differentiation by helping us build greater transparency and coordination into the supply chain,” said Bbuku.
Finding support to grow
Cherry-Pick has been grown through a combination of founder investment, business revenues and grant funding.
“One of our most important milestones has been our participation in the Standard Chartered Women in Tech programme implemented by BongoHive, through which we received both funding and business support. We have received three grants since inception, which has helped us expand our operations.”
This refers to the Standard Chartered Foundation’s Women in Tech Accelerator, implemented by BongoHive in Zambia, with support from Village Capital. The program is part of a multi-region initiative which supports impact-creating, tech-enabled, women-led startups in building thriving businesses across Africa, the Middle East, and Pakistan.
“Other important milestones have included obtaining our ZABS certification, expanding our retail presence, building partnerships within Zambia’s entrepreneurship ecosystem, and continuing to grow our production capacity despite operating in a very challenging environment,” Bbuku said.
Building traction
“We have built up a lot of traction over the years with uptake and growth increasing year-on-year by over 60 per cent. The response has been highly encouraging, particularly as more consumers become conscious of what they eat and look for convenient but healthier alternatives.”
The business has grown through a combination of retail sales, direct customers, corporate orders and partnerships.
“One of the things that has encouraged us most is repeat consumption. When somebody tries the product and comes back for it, that tells us we are not simply benefiting from curiosity around a new product, we are building something people genuinely want,” said Bbuku.
“We have also learnt that building a food brand takes time. It involves educating consumers, getting them to try something different and then consistently delivering the quality that makes them come back.”
Expanding beyond Zambia
CherryPick’s ambition goes beyond Zambia.
“We believe the challenges we are addressing such as post-harvest losses, fragmented agricultural value chains and growing demand for healthier foods, are shared across many African markets,” said Bbuku.
“Our longer-term plan is therefore to expand our product distribution into regional and export markets while also scaling AgroChain360. We want Cherry-Pick to demonstrate that African agricultural businesses can create value locally and build products and systems capable of competing beyond their home markets.”
Bbuku’s background is not in the food business, but rather the ICT regulatory space, where much of her work involved licensing, regulation, stakeholder engagement and understanding how businesses operate within structured environments. Entrepreneurship came from a desire to build something of her own, but also something that could solve a real problem.
“The journey has definitely not been a straight line. We started small and have had to learn almost every aspect of the business along the way – from production and packaging to certification, getting products onto retail shelves, managing cash flow and building a brand. We’ve also had to navigate challenges such as load shedding, access to equipment, sourcing consistently and finding the right markets for our products,” she said.
“For me personally, entrepreneurship has been a journey of resilience. I have had to learn that you don’t need to have everything figured out before you start. You build, you make mistakes, you adjust, and you keep going.”

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has extended the deadline for filing income tax returns for tax year 2026 to October 31. The extension gives taxpayers an additional 16 days to submit their returns and pay any applicable taxes.
The FBR announced the decision through a notification shared on its official X account. The board said it had extended the deadline under Section 214A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, following requests from trade bodies and tax bar associations.
FBR Extends Income Tax Return Filing Deadline Again For Tax Year 2026
The extension applies to taxpayers who were originally required to file their returns by September 30, 2026, and whose deadline had already been extended to October 15.
The FBR had previously moved the deadline from September 30 to October 15. However, business organisations and tax professionals continued to request more time to complete the filing process.
Trade Bodies Seek More Time for Tax Filing
Several business groups and tax professionals called for another extension, citing delays in the availability of tax return forms and heavy traffic on the FBR’s online filing system.
Atif Ikram Sheikh, president of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI), had formally requested the government to extend the deadline to October 31. He said additional time would help businesses, traders, and other taxpayers complete their returns.
The Karachi Tax Bar Association (KTBA) also raised concerns about problems affecting the filing process. In a five-page letter to the Member Inland Revenue (Operations), the association highlighted delays in issuing draft notifications and technical issues with the FBR’s IRIS portal.
These difficulties created challenges for taxpayers and tax professionals trying to submit returns before the deadline.
Income Tax Returns Increase by 34.38%
Despite the reported challenges, the number of income tax returns filed has increased significantly compared with the same period last year.
According to official data available until October 14, taxpayers had submitted 6.71 million returns, compared with 4.99 million during the corresponding period last year. This represents an increase of 34.38%.
By September 30, the FBR had received 5.76 million returns, up from 3.98 million during the same period last year. The figures showed an increase of approximately 45%.
The total tax paid alongside returns reached Rs66.81 billion by October 14. This was around 14.61% higher than the Rs58.29 billion collected during the corresponding period last year.
See Also: FBR Introduces New Tax Rules for Non-Resident Social Media Influencers
Non-Salaried Taxpayers Lead Growth
Returns filed by non-salaried individuals recorded particularly strong growth. This category includes traders, shopkeepers, professionals, and self-employed people.
The number of returns filed by non-salaried taxpayers increased by 46.35%, rising from 3.04 million last year to 4.45 million by October 14, 2026.
Meanwhile, salaried individuals filed 2.18 million returns, compared with 1.88 million during the same period last year. This represents an increase of 16.16%.
The latest extension gives eligible taxpayers more time to address filing difficulties and complete their tax obligations.
Taxpayers covered by the FBR’s notification should submit their returns by October 31, 2026, to meet the revised deadline.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
RedMagic has officially launched the RedMagic 12 Pro+ in China, introducing a new gaming smartphone with a 185Hz display, an advanced RGB liquid-cooling system, and powerful hardware. The device targets mobile gamers who want smooth gameplay, improved thermal management, and high-end performance.
RedMagic 12 Pro+ is Now Official – Check Out its Specs, Price and Availability
The smartphone runs on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, paired with RedMagic’s in-house RedCore R5 gaming chip. It offers up to 16GB of LPDDR5T RAM and 1TB of UFS 4.1 Pro storage. These specifications aim to deliver fast performance for demanding games and other intensive tasks.
RedMagic 12 Pro+ Features a 185Hz AMOLED Display
The RedMagic 12 Pro+ features a 6.85-inch AMOLED display with a resolution of 1216 x 2688 pixels. The company describes it as the industry’s first 185Hz under-display “true full-screen” display, designed to provide a more immersive viewing and gaming experience.
The screen reaches 1,900 nits in high-brightness mode and up to 5,000 nits at peak brightness. Gorilla Glass 7i protects the display, while its 0.96mm bezels and 96.3% screen-to-body ratio give the phone a nearly uninterrupted front design.
RedMagic has also integrated a ninth-generation 16MP selfie camera beneath the display in collaboration with BOE. This design removes the need for a visible camera cutout. An ultrasonic fingerprint reader is also included.
On the rear, the phone carries a 50MP primary camera with optical image stabilisation (OIS) and 8K video recording support. A 50MP ultrawide camera completes the rear camera setup.
Advanced RGB Liquid-Cooling System
One of the main highlights of the RedMagic 12 Pro+ is its RGB liquid-cooling system. The lighting sits around the circular cooling module on the back and can respond to in-game activity, adding a customisable visual element for gaming enthusiasts.
The phone uses a dual-loop liquid-cooling design that surrounds both the processor and battery. According to RedMagic, its micro-pump is 85% more powerful than the one used in the previous RedMagic 11 Pro+, while consuming as little as 20mW of power.
The cooling system works alongside a built-in fan that can reach speeds of up to 25,500 RPM. The fan carries an IPX8 rating, while the overall thermal setup combines graphene materials, a vapour chamber, and liquid metal. RedMagic describes this arrangement as a five-layer thermal system designed to manage heat during demanding gaming sessions.
Gaming Features and Large Battery
The dedicated RedCore R5 chip supports ray tracing, 2K upscaling, and frame interpolation of up to 185Hz in compatible games. These features are intended to improve visual quality and deliver smoother gameplay.
RedMagic has also upgraded its PC Emulator, allowing users to sign in to Steam and play games from their PC libraries on the smartphone. However, compatibility depends on the individual game.
The device packs an 8,400mAh battery with support for 120W wired charging and 80W wireless charging. It also supports bypass charging, which can power the phone directly during gaming, and 22.5W reverse wired charging for compatible devices.
Design, Software, and Connectivity
The RedMagic 12 Pro+ measures 8.55mm in thickness and weighs 223 grams. Gorilla Glass 7i protects both the front and back, while the phone carries IP68 and IP69 ratings for dust and water resistance.
It runs RedMagic OS 12 based on Android 17 and includes dual stereo speakers with Dolby Atmos, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and 700Hz capacitive shoulder triggers for gaming controls.
Other features include an X-axis linear motor, NFC, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, an infrared blaster, and a USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-C port with DisplayPort output.
RedMagic 12 Pro+ Price and Availability
RedMagic has announced three standard configurations for the Chinese market. The 12GB RAM and 256GB storage model costs CNY 6,999, approximately $980. The 16GB RAM and 512GB storage variant costs CNY 7,999, or around $1,120, while the top-end 16GB RAM and 1TB storage version is priced at CNY 8,999, approximately $1,260.
The smartphone will be available in Nightfreeze and Subzero colour options, while the Skyfrost variant will arrive later this year.
The company has also announced a Golden Saga edition featuring a forged carbon design, 24GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage. Further details about this special edition will be revealed later.
For international buyers, RedMagic has confirmed that the device will launch globally under the name RedMagic 12 Pro. The company will announce its global specifications, pricing, and availability on November 3.
With its high-refresh-rate display, advanced cooling hardware, large battery, and dedicated gaming features, the RedMagic 12 Pro+ aims to strengthen the company’s position in the premium gaming smartphone market.
The post RedMagic 12 Pro+ is Now Official – Check Out its Specs, Price and Availability appeared first on PhoneWorld.

items.content:
‘May the seeds of national security take root and sprout in the hearts of the pupils…’
Originally published on Global Voices
Hong Kong police launch an AI-powered national security education platform for the city’s pupils during a ceremony on October 6, 2026. Photo: HKPF, via Facebook. Used with permission.
This article was originally published by Hong Kong Free Press on October 13, 2026. The following version is republished on Global Voices under a content partnership agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” You can support this coverage by donating here.
Hong Kong police have launched an artificial intelligence-powered national security education platform for young students.
The NSmarties AI Interactive Platform was officially launched on October 6, 2026, at a ceremony at Precious Blood Primary School in Ap Lei Chau, with about 700 pupils attending, police said in a Facebook post:
【 NSmarties童心護港AI互動平台 • 正式啟動 】
國家安全，由童心出發！
由警務處國家安全處主辦的「NSmarties童心護港AI互動平台」今日（6日）於海怡寶血小學正式啟動！ 警務處處長周一鳴、警務處副處長（國家安全）江學禮、寶血會總會長區綺雯修女等一眾嘉賓，聯同約700位同學一同見證這個重要時刻。
啟動禮圓滿結束，標誌着國安教育以創新科技走進校園的新里程！ 願國安種子在同學心裏生根發芽，茁壯成長！
[ NSmarties: Children’s Hearts Protect Hong Kong AI Interactive Platform • Officially Launched ]
National security begins with the hearts of children!
Organized by the National Security Department of the Hong Kong Police Force, the ‘NSmarties: Children’s Hearts Protect Hong Kong AI Interactive Platform’ was officially launched today (6th) at Sea View Precious Blood Primary School! Distinguished guests, including Commissioner of Police Joe Chow Yat-ming, Deputy Commissioner of Police (National Security) Kelvin Kong Hok-lai, and Sister Au Yee-man, President of the Precious Blood Society, joined some 700 pupils in witnessing this momentous occasion.
The successful launch ceremony marks a new milestone in bringing national security education into schools through innovative technology! May the seeds of national security take root and sprout in the hearts of the pupils, and grow strong!
The platform, jointly developed by police and Hong Kong Qianfan Technology, lets students generate personalized stories centered on China’s “holistic approach to national security” — a framework pushed by Chinese President Xi Jinping that covers areas from politics and the economy to ecology and technology.
It also features the voices of Chow and security chief Chris Tang, who explain the city’s national security laws and security information.
The ceremony marked a “milestone” in bringing national security education into the city’s schools through innovative technologies, police said.
The NSmarties platform was first unveiled on National Security Education Day in April, but it was not fully launched to the public at that time.
Hong Kong has strengthened national security education alongside a crackdown since Beijing imposed a national security law in 2020 following the 2019 protests and unrest.
Beijing inserted national security legislation directly into Hong Kong’s mini-constitution in June 2020 following a year of pro-democracy protests and unrest. It criminalized subversion, secession, collusion with foreign forces and terrorist acts — broadly defined to include disruption to transport and other infrastructure. The move gave police sweeping new powers and led to hundreds of arrests amid new legal precedents, while dozens of civil society groups disappeared. The authorities say it restored stability and peace to the city, rejecting criticism from trade partners, the UN and NGOs.
Written by Hong Kong Free Press

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Shopify’s India Checkout Bet
Shopify is preparing to bring Shop Pay to India. Setting up a direct clash with domestic rivals like GoKwik and Razorpay, the Canada-based SaaS giant aims to disrupt the local checkout market on the back of its existing merchant network.
Shop Pay’s India Launch: Shopify plans to launch the offering in the country by Q1 2027. The company is in talks with multiple payment orchestration platforms to integrate payment service providers. In India, Shop Pay will likely sit alongside Shopify Checkout as an optional accelerated experience.
For context, Shop Pay allows customers to save payment, shipping and contact information, enabling faster purchases across participating stores.
The Distribution Edge: What works for Shop Pay in India is Shopify’s existing base of Indian merchants. Since many Indian D2C brands already build their online storefronts on Shopify, the company benefits from deep merchant integration, a ready distribution pipeline and strong global brand equity. This gives Shop Pay a direct route into the checkout layer.
Navigating Competition: Shop Pay enters a crowded Indian checkout market populated by established players like GoKwik, Shopflo, Razorpay, Shiprocket and Cashfree Payments. These domestic rivals offer specialised, India-centric capabilities like returns management, shopper engagement and advertising. These may turn out to be a tough nut to crack for Shopify.
The Ultimate Test: Shop Pay’s success in India will eventually depend on whether its native integration platform can outperform local checkout rivals on pricing, conversion and localised features. To win, Shopify must prove that Shop Pay can deliver higher net margins and lower overall operational costs than entrenched domestic alternatives.
As Shopify gears up to launch Shop Pay in India, can the SaaS giant turn its brand equity and distribution advantage into a meaningful Indian checkout business? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Zetwerk IPO Day 1
The B2B manufacturing startup’s public issue was subscribed just 23% on the first day of bidding, receiving bids for 4.17 Cr shares against 18.51 Cr shares on offer. The public offer saw the highest interest from QIBs, followed by retail investors and NIIs.
Zetwerk’s ₹5,000 Cr IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹2,830 Cr and an OFS component of up to 14.45 Cr shares. At the upper end of its ₹143-₹151 IPO price band, the issue values the company at around ₹25,583 Cr.
Separately, Tonbo Imaging’s IPO was oversubscribed 4X at the end of the first day, receiving bidding for 3.4 Cr shares against 85.3 Lakh shares on offer. The defence tech startup’s issue consists entirely of an OFS of up to 1.2 Cr shares worth ₹852 Cr.
JFS’ Profit Halves In Q2
Jio Financial Services’ consolidated net profit declined 51% YoY to ₹340.4 Cr in Q2 FY27. This came despite operating revenue zooming 73% to ₹1,699.3 Cr in the quarter under review.
The company attributed the decline in profits to higher expenditure and the absence of dividend income during the quarter. Total expenses jumped 167% YoY to ₹1,166.1 Cr in the quarter ended September 2026.
On the operational front, JFS’ NBFC arm, Jio Credit, had ₹37,320 Cr in AUM at the end of September 2026, while its digital payments vertical clocked a total payment value of ₹14,682 Cr in the quarter. The JioFinance App also reached 3.2 Cr unique users in Q2.
Origin Bags $20 Mn
The physical AI startup has raised around ₹190 Cr in a strategic round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures to build its fleet of robots, support pilots in the US and Europe, and experiment with new use cases.
Founded in 2025, Origin is developing modular autonomous robots for the construction sector. Its robots can handle tasks such as drywall finishing, painting, taping, and drilling. The startup plans to deploy 150 bots by 2027-end.
Origin operates in the broader Indian deeptech sector, which continues to draw investor attention on the back of regulatory push, subsidies, a thriving talent pool and growing demand. The sector raised $290 Mn in Q3 2026, up 176% YoY.
Go Digit’s New Home
Canadian investor Fairfax Financial Holdings has proposed transferring its 49% stake in the listed insurtech company to IDBI Bank. The proposed restructuring will make the bank the holding company for the insurance business.
This will allow IDBI Bank to distribute insurance products through Digit Insurance. However, the transaction will still require clearance from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI).
The proposals come after the Centre allowed Fairfax Financial to pick up a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank. Under its bid, Fairfax would acquire the controlling stake for approximately ₹52,878 Cr ($5.6 Bn), at ₹81 per share.
Udaan’s FY26 Turnaround
The B2B ecommerce unicorn managed to narrow its net losses by 19.4% YoY to ₹851.5 Cr in FY26. Udaan attributed the improving bottom line to operating revenue growing nearly 13% YoY to ₹5,134 Cr, tighter execution and EBITDA burn declining about 70%.
Despite improving operational metrics, concerns remain over Udaan’s ability to continue as a going concern. At the end of FY26, current liabilities exceeded current assets by ₹1,391 Cr, while total liabilities exceeded total assets by ₹790.9 Cr.
Going forward, Udaan said that it is targeting sustained profitability and a public listing, which is targeted for early 2028. To get there, it must sustain revenue growth, keep narrowing losses, complete its debt restructuring and improve cash flows.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How Ubiqedge Is Giving Industrial Equipment An AIoT Brain
Regulators today expect factories to monitor water extraction, emissions and other metrics in real time. But most of this tracking equipment was never designed to be connected. To solve this, Ubiqedge is building an AIoT layer that automates compliance and operations.
A Full-Stack Approach: Founded in 2024, Ubiqedge combines hardware and software to help OEMs and system integrators upgrade conventional equipment. The platform is designed to deliver monitoring and automation without asking factories to replace their existing machinery.
The Dual Combo: Its flagship hardware offering, KLEON, connects to industrial equipment, reads sensor data and then transmits it to the cloud. Its SAMASTH software then turns this data into live dashboards, historical records, alerts and compliance reports. For example, KLEON can capture groundwater flow-meter readings, while SAMASTH tracks consumption and can automatically shut off a borewell pump once the extraction limit is reached.
The Business Model: Rather than selling directly to factories, Ubiqedge partners with OEMs and system integrators, who bundle the startup’s technology with their equipment. The startup currently serves smart water management, solar monitoring, smart concrete and air-quality use cases. It closed FY26 with a revenue of about ₹7 Cr and cash-positive operations.
Growing Steadily: Backed by Piper Serica, the startup claims to have so far served more than 100 direct customers, 8,000+ end users and roughly 30,000 devices deployed through its partner network. The startup now plans to expand into the Middle East. So, can Ubiqedge make industrial AIoT simple enough to move beyond pilots?

From Oracle and TCS to Paytm and Flipkart, layoffs have hit across the board in 2026. But here’s the statistic that stands out: 18 out of 32 companies in our list cited AI as a reason for layoffs. Read on to know more…

items.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has directed the State Public Works Corporation (LSPWC) to commence immediate road reconstruction and rehabilitation across the state, taking advantage of the dry season to address deteriorating infrastructure.
The General Manager of LSPWC, Engr. Tokunbo Ajanaku, disclosed this on Thursday during an inspection tour of ongoing projects, assuring residents of improved road networks as weather conditions become more favourable for construction work.
Ajanaku said Oshodi-Isolo Local Government Area was a major focus of the exercise, with reconstruction underway on Godwin Omonuwa Road, Taiwo Street, Salamotu Street, Peter Agah Street and Ibeh Street.
He said the projects were undertaken at the governor’s direction to address infrastructure deficits and improve connectivity within communities.
“These roads are important links within the Oshodi-Isolo axis, serving residents, traders, business owners and other road users daily.
“Their reconstruction will not only improve mobility but also reduce transportation costs, enhance road safety, boost commercial activities and create a more conducive environment for businesses and residents,” Ajanaku said.
He added that the inspection covered other ongoing rehabilitation projects across the state, including Ogunnusi Road in Ojodu Local Council Development Area (LCDA), Awolowo Way in Ikeja Local Government Area, Lanre Awolokun Road and Idowu Olaitan Street in Shomolu, as well as Idimu-Ikotun Road in Alimosho.
According to him, heavy rainfall often limits asphalt laying, but the corporation maintained emergency palliative interventions during the rainy season to keep critical roads motorable.
He said the agency was now shifting towards more comprehensive and durable repairs with the return of dry weather.
Ajanaku added that much of the maintenance and asphalt-laying work was being carried out at night, under appropriate safety measures, to minimise traffic congestion across the metropolis.
He appealed to residents to be patient, explaining that road repairs were prioritised based on road conditions, traffic volume and the urgency of intervention.
The general manager said the corporation would progressively extend its operations to other parts of the state.
He also urged residents to protect public infrastructure by avoiding practices that contribute to road deterioration, including dumping refuse in drainage channels, spilling petroleum products and discharging wastewater onto roads.
“Our roads are our collective heritage. Government has the responsibility to provide and maintain them, but citizens also have a duty to protect them. Road preservation must therefore be a shared responsibility,” Ajanaku said.

items.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu
The Tinubu Support Group (TSG) in the Southeast, led by former All Progressives Congress (APC) National Auditor, Sir Paul Chukwuma, on Thursday held a rally in Awka, Anambra State, to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.
At the rally, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, urged voters in the zone to support APC candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections.
Chukwuma, a former governorship candidate in Anambra State, and the APC senatorial candidate for Anambra Central, Uche Ekwunife, also urged voters to support Tinubu and other candidates of the party.
They expressed confidence that the APC would secure substantial votes across the five Southeast states, arguing that Tinubu’s actions and policies had earned him support in the region.
However, some APC leaders in Anambra State reportedly expressed dissatisfaction with what they described as the party’s national leadership relying on the strength of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) to secure votes for Tinubu in the state.
The APC state secretary, Sir Obiora Okpala, said the party should be adequately recognised in political arrangements in Anambra, given its status as the ruling party at the national level and a major political stakeholder in the state.
He argued that the APC should be carried along in the process, rather than APGA being given what he described as undue advantage over the party in Anambra.

items.content:
By Chioma Obinna
The Coalition of Civil Society Action for Education for All (CSACEFA), Lagos State Chapter, has called for increased investment in girls’ education, stronger child protection measures and coordinated efforts to end child marriage and ensure that girls have access to quality education.
The coalition made the call at its Lagos Education Summit and International Day of the Girl Child 2026, held at the State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB) Hall, Maryland, Lagos, with the theme, “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights.”
Speaking at the event, CSACEFA Lagos Coordinator, Stella Olubunmi Francis, said every child deserved access to quality education, irrespective of gender or personal circumstances.
Francis expressed concern over the stigma and discrimination faced by pregnant schoolgirls, urging stakeholders to create opportunities for them to continue their education.
“There is a lot of stigma and shame, but these children should not be denied education because of their pregnancies. We need to create more opportunities for them to continue their education,” she said.
Representing the Executive Chairman of SUBEB, Dr Akeem Babatunde Shittu, the Board Secretary, Lamidi Akeem, reaffirmed the Lagos State Government’s commitment to children’s rights and basic education.
“The Lagos State Government has already domesticated the Child Rights Act. Every government agency saddled with responsibilities concerning children, particularly SUBEB, has a role to play,” Akeem said.
He acknowledged the contribution of civil society organisations and development partners to efforts aimed at bringing out-of-school children back into the education system.
In her keynote address, a lawyer and member of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) Nigeria, Mrs Olubola Afolabi, called for stronger child protection mechanisms, legal accountability and improved access to education to tackle child marriage.
“Why does child marriage happen? What happens to the girls? These are the questions I want us to ask ourselves,” Afolabi said, urging stakeholders to confront the factors responsible for the practice and its consequences for girls.
CSACEFA Lagos Provost and Founder of LEADIN AFRICA, Margaret ChiChi Nkire, said the summit was organised to strengthen gender-responsive education financing and inclusive budgeting in Lagos State and Nigeria.
During a panel session she moderated, participants called for rights-based education policies, the removal of hidden charges that undermine free education and improved support for pregnant, married and parenting girls to remain in school or return without discrimination.
“We hope that beyond this summit, we will have better coordination among stakeholders. We have Plan International, Save the Children, the British Council, SUBEB, the National Human Rights Commission and other stakeholders here today,” Nkire said.
Representing Plan International Nigeria, Aishatu Usman Bukar stressed the need for adequate and sustainable education funding, gender-responsive budgeting and measures to remove financial barriers facing girls and vulnerable households.
A student participant, Esther Matthew, said the summit had broadened her understanding of the opportunities available to girls beyond marriage.
“I have learnt that being a girl child is not only about marriage. A girl can stand on her own, become a business owner and achieve whatever she wants in the future,” Matthew said.
She also pledged to act on the message, “See Something, Say Something,” by intervening where possible when she encountered situations threatening children’s safety and reporting cases beyond her capacity to a teacher or another trusted adult.
The summit featured discussions on child marriage, inclusive education and sustainable financing, alongside cultural dance and spoken-word performances celebrating the girl child.
Other participants included representatives of Save the Children International Nigeria, the National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools, Child Protection Network Lagos, the National Youth Council of Nigeria, mothers’ associations and School-Based Management Committees.
The stakeholders called for stronger collaboration among government agencies, civil society organisations, development partners, schools and communities to protect girls’ rights and ensure that poverty, pregnancy, early marriage and discrimination do not deprive them of education.
The post CSACEFA seeks end to child marriage, demands more investment in girls’ education appeared first on Vanguard News.

Financial service giant Goldman Sachs has sold 53.4 Lakh shares of foodtech giant Eternal in a major block deal worth ₹168.7 Cr.
According to NSE data, the investment bank, via its entity Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, sold the shares at ₹316 apiece to rake in the amount. The investor offloaded the stake at a discount of more than 2.6% to the stock’s last closing price on Thursday.
The shares that flooded the market were lapped up by Bank of America, via its affiliate BofA Securities Europe, for ₹168.7 Cr.
This is the second block witnessed by Eternal in the past two months. In early September, French financial services giant BNP Paribas and US-based hedge fund Millennium Management together sold over 9.9 Cr shares of the listed foodtech giant for a sum of ₹3,264.8 Cr.
This latest block deal comes as investors continue to be bullish on Eternal. Shares of the foodtech giant have surged nearly 10% in the past three months, and are up 16.2% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis.
The uptick in Eternal’s shares has come on the back of strong financial performance by the startup despite intensifying competition in the quick commerce space and the entry of new players like Rapido’s Ownly, Flipkart and Swish. What has been powering the stock’s rise is Eternal’s quick commerce arm Blinkit, which continues to dominate the instant delivery market.
On the financial front, Eternal reported a consolidated net profit of ₹92 Cr in Q1 FY27, up nearly 3.7X from ₹25 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, operating revenue surged 182% YoY and 17% QoQ to ₹20,211 Cr during the quarter under review.
Shares of Eternal closed Thursday’s trading session 2.77% higher at ₹324.35 on the BSE.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said on Thursday that the Federal Government (FG) had no plan to increase electricity tariffs.
Tegbe said this in Ibadan while flagging off the 17.7MW hybrid solar mini-grid project, with a 17.74MW Battery Energy Storage System for communities in Oyo State.
The minister described reports of a planned tariff hike circulating on social media as misinformation and urged Nigerians to disregard it.
“I want to say this clearly and without ambiguity: there is no plan to increase electricity tariffs.
“What we are planning is a power sector that works round the clock,” he said.
He said the FG’s commitment to regular power supply starts with having three Energy Zones: the Lagos-Ogun corridor, Abuja-Kaduna-Kano corridor, and the Benin-Enugu-Port Harcourt corridor.
He explained that the 17.7MW project would serve communities across Akinyele, Ido, Ibadan North, Egbeda and Lagelu Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Oyo State.
According to him, the interconnected mini-grid would improve supply to homes and businesses, reduce dependence on generators and create better conditions for investment and jobs in the beneficiary communities.
Tegbe commended President Bola Tinubu for his leadership under the Renewed Hope Agenda and appreciated the Olubadan of Ibadanland for his support.
He also thanked the Rural Electrification Agency (REA), Paras Energy, the World Bank, Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company (IBEDC) and the Oyo State Government for their contributions.
He said the FG plans to build and improve the national grid across the eastern, western and central corridors to ensure stability and extend the 24/7 power vision to every part of Nigeria.
Mr Deolu Ijose, the Managing Director (MD)/Chief Executive Officer (CEO), IBEDC, said the new mini-grid project would provide electricity to 22,597 customers across five communities.
Ijose said the project, developed by Paras Energy and Natural Resources Development Limited, would provide 17.7MWp solar PV generation with battery storage to Bola, Jiboye, Molade-Adelubi, Ogo-Oluwa, and Sooko-Elega clusters.
According to him, IBEDC’s existing distribution infrastructure will be used to integrate and deliver electricity generated by Paras Energy.
He said that this model would show how DisCos and private developers could collaborate to improve access.
Ijose added that the project builds on IBEDC’s previous innovative interventions such as the Mokoloki Mini-Grid in Ogun and the recently commissioned Oke-Oyi mini-grid in Kwara.
He then urged the host communities to protect the infrastructure.
The MD/CEO of REA, Abba Abubakar-Aliyu, said the project details are: 1.8 megawatts in Bola, Akinyele LGA and 3.5 megawatts in Jiboye, Ido LGA.
Others are 6.9 megawatts in Molade, Ibadan North LGA; 3.6 megawatts in Ogo Oluwa, Egbeda LGA, and 1.9 megawatts in Sooko, Lagelu LGA.
Earlier, the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, lauded the minister for including rural and underserved communities in various power reform projects.
He urged the Oyo State Government to speed up work and complete its ongoing hybrid power project before 2027 for residents to start enjoying regular power supply.
Earlier, Gov. Seyi Makinde, represented by the state Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Prof. Dahud Shangodoyin, said the government would continue to pursue practical electricity interventions across the state.
He noted that the state government’s Hybrid Independent Power Project, meant to serve the state’s secretariat and other strategic public facilities, has a plant capacity of 11 MW.
He recalled that the 5 MW phase was commissioned in 2024.
“Our wide agenda includes solar power for public facilities, rural electrification, mini-grids, as well as private sector-led generation and distribution.
“Therefore, no single technology can meet every need,” said Makinde.
He charged the developer and implementing institutions to maintain clear construction and commissioning mindsets, and comply with applicable licenses and technical standards. (NAN)
The post No plan to increase electricity tariffs – FG insists appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman
Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has rejected suggestions that the arrest of politician Alhaji Wakiil Goni Mama, popularly known as Mai Salati, was politically motivated, insisting that the military has nothing to do with politics.
Buni spoke on Thursday during the swearing-in of commissioners and chairmen of the 17 local government areas in Damaturu, where he disclosed that he had directed the chairman of Geidam Local Government Area to follow up on the case with military authorities and community elders.
The governor’s remarks come amid allegations in some quarters that he was behind Mai Salati’s arrest and had used the military to target the politician over political differences.
Dismissing the insinuations, Buni said he has no history of opposition bullying, insisting that threatening political opponents was inconsistent with his principles.
“I reached out to the Geidam chairman, instructed him to follow up on the case with the military commander and other elders on the case and report back to me,” the governor said.
“It is not in my principle to threaten opposition,” he added.
Buni also maintained that the military should not be drawn into partisan political disputes, insisting that Mai Salati’s case was not political.
It could be recalled that troops of the Nigerian Army’s Operation Hadin Kai reportedly arrested Mai Salati in early October over allegations of providing logistics support to suspected members of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), a faction of the Boko Haram insurgency operating in the North-East.
Reports published by TheCable and other media organisations on October 8 and 9 said the arrest followed an alleged attempt by the politician to bribe soldiers to secure the release of suspects arrested in Kanamma, Yobe State, over suspected terrorist logistics activities.
According to the reports, the suspects were being processed for further investigation when Mai Salati allegedly intervened to secure their release by offering money to military personnel.
The soldiers reportedly rejected the alleged inducement and arrested him instead, with security sources saying he and other suspects were subsequently moved from Damaturu to Maiduguri for further investigation.
The arrest generated political controversy, with reports highlighting speculation that it might be connected to Mai Salati’s reported defection from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to the African Democratic Congress (ADC).
Security sources cited in the initial reports rejected the suggestion that the operation was politically motivated, maintaining that it concerned allegations of terrorism-related logistics and an attempt to interfere with the detention of suspects.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
A shooting has left “multiple victims” at an elementary school in the northwestern US state of Oregon, police said Thursday, adding that the shooter is dead.
“We don’t have confirmation yet who shot the suspect. It may have been a bystander. At this time, we have multiple victims,” said Sheila Miller, a spokesperson at the Bend Police Department, in a press conference.
The Bend-La Pine School District said in a statement on social media that the Silver Rail Elementary School was under lockdown.
An updated post later said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.
Miller said that officers were alerted to respond to a critical scene at 1:00 pm local time, and that police were on the scene approximately two minutes later.
“Seconds later, we received word over the radio that the suspect in this incident was down,” she said.
Miller said medics had taken at least two people to a local hospital, adding that “we do not know their status.”
The school is more than 100 miles (160 kilometers) southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.
The United States, where firearms are readily available, is a frequent scene of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.
The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on April 16, 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.
There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the United States so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot.
AFP

items.title: Meta unveils new ‘open’ AI model to rival Chinese competition
items.summary:
Meta on Thursday launched a new open-weight AI model which it claims rivals, and in some cases outperforms, similar products from leading Chinese developers.
Muse Spark Open “is the most capable US open-weight model to date,” Meta’s chief of AI Alexandr Wang wrote on X.
Unlike with so-called closed models — such as Anthropic’s Claude or OpenAI’s ChatGPT — developers can download the parameters, or weights, of an open-weight model and then customize it.
Chinese developers have emerged as dominant players in the open-weight market for AI models over the past couple of years.
Alibaba’s Qwen, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 and Z.ai’s GLM models have been considered open-weight frontrunners globally, but Meta claims its new open model now competes on a similar level.

“Built for coding and agentic work,” Muse Spark Open “excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning,” Meta said in a blogpost, adding that “strong safeguards” have been integrated into the new model.
Muse Spark Open is also “optimized” to run on Apple’s advanced M5 Ultra chips, Meta said, signaling an unusual partnership between the two tech giants.
Meta boss Mark Zuckerberg wrote on X that the new model “runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work” with Apple and its new CEO John Ternus.
Ternus, who took over as Apple’s chief from Tim Cook in September, responded that it is “amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open’s caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!”
Muse Spark Open still requires significant computing power, though.
Users can run the model on two Mac Studios with M5 Ultra chips to create a “supercomputer” on their own desktop, Meta said.
The launch comes just days after Meta announced its newest closed model.
On Monday, the company unveiled two new “frontier” models called Wonder and Wonder Full, which the company claimed rival the most advanced versions of ChatGPT and Claude.
Meta’s AI efforts were initially focused on open models, but more recently Zuckerberg has pushed the company to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.
Meta launched its Spark model in April, marking a departure from its open-source model known as Llama, which lagged behind the rest of the industry.
AFP

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
Viral footage circulating online appears to show sealed iPhone boxes and luxury perfume packs floating in the Strait of Hormuz after a container ship was struck, caught fire and sank this week, turning a shipping attack into an unlikely consumer-tech story.
The Singapore-flagged vessel GFS Pride went down near Oman’s Musandam peninsula after what Singapore’s Maritime and Port Authority described as an unknown projectile strike that damaged the ship and started a fire. All 21 crew members were evacuated and no injuries were reported.
&&&&&&&
Clips shared widely on social media appear to show Apple iPhone boxes and perfume packs bobbing in the water, with small boats moving among scattered containers. Major outlets that carried the footage, including India Today, said they could not independently verify where or when the clips were filmed, or confirm that the phones were part of the ship’s cargo. AI-generated images claiming to show thousands of iPhones in the water were also shared around the same time.
What Officials Say Happened
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said a ship hit a naval mine while using what it called an unauthorised route through the strait. Singapore and other maritime reports said the vessel was hit by an unidentified projectile. A second Singapore-flagged ship, GFS Giselle, was also hit around the same period, suffered hull damage, and reached a safe anchorage with its crew.
Pakistan’s Hydrographer warned mariners that GFS Pride had sunk about four nautical miles north-west of Ras al-Sheikh Masud. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported multiple projectile strikes on commercial vessels in the strait this week.
Why The Strait Matters
The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for global oil and gas trade. Shipping there has faced repeated attacks since the wider Iran conflict began earlier this year, and the waterway has at times been effectively closed or tightly restricted. The viral iPhone clips do not change the maritime facts: a freighter sank, its crew survived, and commercial traffic through one of the world’s most important sea lanes remains under threat.
Source: BBC (Singapore Maritime and Port Authority)
