items.author: olufemiajasa
items.content:
The Court of Appeal in Abuja on Tuesday returned the case files in two appeals arising from a N101 million defamation judgment in favour of two operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) to the Presiding Judge for reassignment.
The appeals were filed by the Incorporated Trustees of the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) and by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Ogundare. The High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) awarded the damages in May.
The panel had earlier heard the first appeal and reserved judgment. It later vacated that order, ruling that the two appeals, which emanated from one judgment, should be heard together for a composite judgment.
The development was the second setback in the matter. Last week, proceedings in Ogundare’s appeal were halted midway.
Before the panel vacated its order, a brief drama played out when SERAP’s lead counsel, Tayo Oyetibo, SAN, told the court that an application was pending for certain persons to be joined as amici curiae (friends of the court).
Prof Olarewaju Fagbohun, SAN, a former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos, rose to address the panel.
He said he appeared for the Columbia Global Freedom of Expression Initiative of Columbia University and for the United Nations Special Rapporteurs on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and of association, and to freedom of opinion and expression.
He said the application, filed on October 12 under Order 6 Rule 1 of the Court of Appeal Rules 2021 and Section 6(6)(a) of the 1999 Constitution, sought leave to participate in the appeal.
“We’re seeking the leave of this Hon court to participate in this appeal and assist the court with independent submissions,” he said.
He added that the proposed brief would offer independent legal analysis and relevant comparative and international jurisprudence.
The panel’s lead judge, Justice Danlami Senchi, was unimpressed. “Did the court invite you? Let’s be serious. This is the kind of image we create that is not good for us. We didn’t invite you. On behalf of whom?” he asked.
He added: “I said earlier that we are not here to speak long grammar or waste the court’s time. We didn’t seek for any assistance.”
Fagbohun replied: “We are not adversarial. We’re actually trying to assist this court.”
Justice Senchi said every matter is decided on its merits and that an outsider could be heard only if its interests would be injured. “But you’re not a party in the lower court and in this court,” he said, asking the professor to withdraw the application “so that we can make progress.”
Fagbohun withdrew the application and apologised to the court. The judge commended him: “Your juniors here will be happy for that.”
Mojirayo Ogunlana, who appeared for the Southern African Litigation Centre, also withdrew her application to be admitted as amicus curiae.
The panel then turned to Ogundare’s appeal, the same one that stalled last Friday.
Midway into the hearing of an application for enlargement of time by the appellant’s counsel, Oluwatosin Adesoye, the court voiced displeasure with his presentation, saying he “should have sought the counsel of your seniors.”
“Look at the way and manner you couched your prayers. We can’t grant this. You have to withdraw and refile it,” Justice Senchi said. “This is a court of record. You’re before the Court of Appeal.”
The judge then announced: “We are sending this case file back for reassignment.”
In its appeal, SERAP argues that the judgment was legally and procedurally flawed. Its Appellant’s Brief of Argument, filed by Oyetibo, raises 24 grounds challenging the finding of liability, the damages and the consequential orders.
The group says the central question is whether the claimants proved by credible evidence that the publications referred to them.
“The publications did not name the respondents, and the descriptions relied upon were general physical descriptions which did not, without more, identify the particular individuals who brought the action,” SERAP said.
The publications followed SERAP’s call on President Bola Tinubu to investigate alleged corruption at the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and reverse fuel price increases. SERAP had alleged that DSS officers entered its Abuja office without proper notice, describing two of them as “a tall, large, dark-skinned woman” and “a slim, dark-skinned man.”
SERAP argues that neither publication identified the claimants by name, rank, designation, office or photograph. It adds that the claimants called no independent witness to show that an ordinary member of the public read the publications and understood them to refer to the two officers.
“No independent witness was called to establish the alleged identification, while the social-media reactions relied upon by the respondents were not tendered in evidence,” the group said.
SERAP also accuses the trial court of supplying the missing identification link by relying, among other things, on its own observation of the claimants’ physical appearance during proceedings.
“The issue was whether the publications identified the respondents when they were published, not whether the respondents happened to fit the descriptions when they appeared before the Court,” it said.
The group further describes the ₦100 million damages as excessive and unsupported by sufficient evidence. It says the trial court relied on claims that the publications affected the officers “mentally and psychologically” and had “gone viral,” without evidence of the extent of publication or of specific professional, financial or reputational injury.

items.content:
Healthcare workers at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Abeokuta, Ogun State, have begun a three-day warning strike following the alleged stabbing of a medical laboratory scientist, Lawal Toheeb Olasunkanmi, by a patient’s relative.
Olasunkanmi was reportedly attacked on Sunday night while on duty at the hospital.
A video shared on X showed the medical laboratory scientist bleeding from his nose as the alleged assailant threatened him.
The incident prompted members of the hospital’s Joint Action Committee, comprising nurses, medical laboratory scientists and other non-academic staff, to commence the industrial action on Monday.
In a notice issued on Monday, the committee condemned the attack and demanded measures to ensure the safety of healthcare workers within the facility.
“On behalf of the leadership and entire members of our union, we write to express our profound displeasure, outrage, and deep concern over the unfortunate and unacceptable incident in which one of our colleagues (mr Lawal Toheeb Olasunkanmi), a Medical Laboratory Scientist, was stabbed by a patient’s relative last night within our Centre,” the notice read.
The committee described the incident as an assault on the dignity, safety and welfare of healthcare professionals, insisting that violence against workers providing essential medical services should not be tolerated.
It said hospitals should be safe environments for both patients and healthcare workers, adding that disagreements over medical services could not justify physical attacks.
“No healthcare worker deserves to be threatened, assaulted, or stabbed in the course of providing care. Disagreement, frustration, or dissatisfaction with any service rendered in the hospital cannot justify violence under any circumstance,” the union said.
The committee further described the attack as a collective concern for the hospital’s workforce, warning that workers could not remain silent while their safety was threatened.
It called on the hospital management to formally report the incident to the appropriate law enforcement authorities and ensure that the alleged assailant was investigated and prosecuted in accordance with the law.
The unions also warned against attempts to conceal or downplay the incident or resolve it in a manner that would undermine accountability.
They demanded prompt and comprehensive medical treatment for Olasunkanmi, psychological support where necessary, and institutional assistance throughout his recovery.
Meanwhile, the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, has called on the Nigeria Police Force to immediately arrest and prosecute the suspect allegedly involved in the attack.
In a statement issued on Tuesday by Ado Bako, Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Salako described the incident as “barbaric and unacceptable”.
“No grief, frustration or dissatisfaction with care can justify violence against a health worker performing his lawful duties,” the minister said.
Salako also urged the striking healthcare workers to return to their duties in the interest of patients and the wider public.
He called on the hospital management to ensure that the injured worker received appropriate medical attention and support, while strengthening security arrangements in line with Federal Government directives.
The minister also extended his condolences to the family of the deceased patient and advised members of the public to channel complaints about hospital services through appropriate formal procedures.

items.content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
The National Pension Commission is targeting Nigeria’s informal sector to secure the participation of the nation’s largest group of workers in the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS).
The Director-General of Pencom, Ms. Omolola Oloworaran, who spoke at the 2026 National Pension Commission Media Conference in Abuja, yesterday, said that with the informal sector accounting for about 92 percent of the nation’s workforce, it must be included in the pension reform for it to be considered successful.
She spoke on the theme, “From Reform To Reality, Renewed Hope, Pension Security for Nigerians”.
The D-G said that her team was giving the Personal Pension Plan for the informal sector a very strong push to enable them benefit from the various programmes targeting pensioners in the country.
According to her, PenCom has engaged accredited pension agents targeting workers in the informal sector and that the commission was in the process on accrediting more agents for the same purpose.
She said that the agents were taking the Personal Pension Plan to markets, motor parks, farms and workshops to enroll traders, artisans, farmers and transport workers.
Tinubu most Pro-Pensioners President
Ms. Oloworaran said President Bola Tinubu was laying the foundation for a sustainable social security in the country through enhanced welfare for retirees with increased pensions and the free health to be launched at the end of this month.
The Pencom boss described President Tinubu as, “the most pro-retiree president, going by the achievements recorded so far in the pension industry.
“From the very beginning of pensions in the country to all the reforms that have happened, he is the most pro-worker, most pro-retiree President we have seen in the history of Nigeria,” she said.
Ms. Oloworaran said that the administration had settled N758 billion inherited pension obligations (with nearly one million pensioners benefiting from the payment), introduced new benefits, accelerated payment of retirement benefits and improved pension security for workers and retirees.
She said that for the first time in 21 years, pensions of 2,116 retirees of the defunct Nigerian Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) were reviewed, citing an example of a particular pensioner on N18, 000 monthly, now receiving N206,000.
“Twenty-one years of waiting was answered in a single decision,” she said.
According to her, retirement benefits that previously took up to 21 months to approve are now approved within 48 hours for federal government workers.
The D-G said that two additional initiatives would be unveiled during the National Pension Week scheduled for October 26 to October 30.
She said that one of them was “PenCare,” a retiree healthcare programme that would provide eligible low-income retirees with essential healthcare at no cost during its pilot phase. The pilot stage would cover 30,000 retirees.

items.content:
The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has described the inclusion of opposition figures in the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign council as “indiscipline and rascality”.
Olawepo-Hashim made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he reacted to the inclusion of opposition figures like Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke and Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo in the APC campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Asked whether the move reflected political maturity or political survival, the Accord Party candidate dismissed both interpretations, describing it instead as a lack of discipline.
“No, this is simply indiscipline and rascality,” he said.
Olawepo-Hashim also argued that Adeleke’s participation in the APC campaign council would not automatically translate into support for President Bola Tinubu among voters in Osun State.
He said the governor’s electoral victory did not give him the power to determine how the people of the state would vote in the presidential election.
“Governor Adeleke, the fact that he won his election cannot compel the people of Osun State to vote for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.
To support his argument, Olawepo-Hashim recalled the 2011 general election, when he said voters in Osun State did not follow the political direction of then Lagos State Governor, Bola Tinubu, after the latter allegedly backed the Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate, Goodluck Jonathan, instead of the Action Congress of Nigeria’s presidential candidate, Nuhu Ribadu.
He said Osun voters supported Ribadu despite the reported political arrangement, arguing that the state’s electorate had a history of making independent political choices.
“Osun people are incredibly honourable people, what we call Omoluabi in the Yoruba parlance; they are ideological; they have great history, they are not conquered people, they do what they believe,” he said.
The Accord Party candidate maintained that Adeleke’s current political alignment would not prevent his party from seeking votes in Osun State during the presidential election.
“I still believe that regardless of what Governor Adeleke is doing, Osun people are still going to vote for Accord Party at the presidential election,” he said.

The Pakistan Army on Tuesday conducted a successful test launch of the hypersonic ballistic missile Fatah-2 extended range, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement, adding that the weapon system was equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.
"It is capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating the enemy's missile defence systems due to its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features. Fatah-2 ER, with its extended range, will further enhance the army's reach and capability of engaging deep targets," said the military's media wing.
The launch was witnessed by the commander of the Army Rocket Force Command (Comd ARFC), senior officers from the Pakistan Army and committed scientists and engineers, the ISPR said, adding that the ARFC commander "appreciated the dedication and technical prowess of scientists and engineers."
The statement also noted that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, along with service chiefs, congratulated the scientists and engineers on the successful test launch.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the successful test launch, stating that the scientists and engineers of the Pakistan Army had achieved a commendable feat. He added that the test was a significant development in the defence sector.
Last week, an indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-4 ground-launched cruise missile was successfully test launched. The weapon system was equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids and could engage targets at extended ranges with "high precision and lethality," the ISPR had said.
The test also validated additional "technical parameters" of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability, it added.
In September 2025, the Pakistan Army had successfully conducted a training launch of its newly developed Fatah-4 at a range of 750 kilometres. The Fatah-4 is designed to evade enemy missile defence systems due to its terrain-hugging capabilities, ensuring high precision when engaging targets. The missile's features enhance its lethality and survivability, boosting the effectiveness of Pakistan's conventional missile systems.

By Adegboyega Adeleye
The Super Falcons of Nigeria secured a resounding 5-0 victory over Comoros at the Remo Stars stadium, Ikenne on Tuesday to seal a 7-0 aggregate win and reach the third round of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games qualifiers.
A four-goal second-half surge sent interim coach Augustine Eguavoen-led side into the third round of the Olympics qualifiers, completing a 7–0 aggregate victory over Comoros. Inter Milan forward Toni Payne and Cruz Azul striker Uchenna Kanu both scored twice, with Christy Ucheibe also adding a penalty in Tuesday’s dominant performance over the Southern Africans ladies in Ikenne.
Payne opened the scoring in the 41st minute after Kanu pounced on a mistake by the Comoros goalkeeper and squared the ball for her to finish. Nigeria led 1–0 at half-time, but lost captain Rasheedat Ajibade to an ankle injury. She was stretchered off in tears and replaced by Folashade Ijamilusi, who had an impressive show with two assists.
Kanu doubled the lead in the 58th minute, heading in an Ijamilusi cross. Five minutes later, substitute Blessing Okpe dribbled past two defenders and laid the ball off for Payne, who scored her second.
Ijamilusi delivered again in the 66th minute, crossing for Kanu to head home her second goal of the night. Okpe then won a penalty after being fouled in the area, and Ucheibe converted calmly in the 71st minute. Introduced for Gift Monday at half-time, Okpe finished with an assist and the run that led to the penalty. Nigeria kept clean sheets in both legs of the tie, giving interim coach Augustine Eguavoen an emphatic result as the team advances to the next round.
The Super Falcons will face Morocco in the third round of the Olympics qualifier scheduled for March 2027, where victory in the two-legged tie will bring the dream of a fifth Olympics participation closer for Nigeria’s female national team

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
ABUJA– PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has asked the Judiciary to dismantle procedural loopholes and flawed prosecution tactics that allow offenders to escape justice, warning that no well-connected individual should be able to manipulate technicalities to evade the law.
The President spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the annual EFCC/NJI Capacity Building Workshop for Judges and Justices. He was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima.
Tinubu urged the judiciary to interrogate existing statutory frameworks in view of emerging financial crimes.
“Probe prosecution strategies, dismantle outdated precedents, and seal procedural gaps that politically exposed persons and organised crime actors exploit to delay or frustrate trial,” he stated.
He demanded an aggressive overhaul of the justice system to ensure that no well-connected individual can manipulate technicalities to evade the full, crushing weight of the law.
The President, who was represented by the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, warned that financial and economic crimes pose an existential threat to Nigeria, adding that corruption has no respect for status and spares no arm of government.
He said framing the anti-corruption campaign as purely an executive agenda is a fundamental error because compromised public services equally affect the executive, legislature, judiciary, and ordinary citizens.
“Corruption is a battle for the nation’s collective survival. We must no longer permit legal pyrotechnics and procedural pedantry to shelter criminality. The Bench is not merely a mechanical arbiter of rules, but an active guardian of moral order and social equity.
“Law is, by design, an instrument of social engineering; it must invariably prioritise the public good over narrow, selfish interests shielded by technical manoeuvres. Our courts must embody the spirit, and not just the arid letter, of the law,” Tinubu said.
He maintained that there will be no meaningful progress in uprooting graft “without an independent, progressive, and reform-minded Bench.”
Digital-age crimes
Tinubu commended the EFCC for convening the 8th edition of the Judges and Justices Workshop, themed “Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Financial Crimes in a Digital Age.”
He described the workshop as timely and necessary in fostering the institutional cohesion required to confront corruption’s changing architecture in Nigeria.
“My Lords, we confront a rapidly shifting criminal landscape. Technology has amplified the audacity and reach of illicit actors, ushering in sophisticated crimes driven by destructive ingenuity. The rise of blockchain technology and artificial intelligence has introduced unprecedented layers of complexity to traditional illicit activities.
“Because these modern crimes constantly mutate, law enforcement and judicial authorities must continuously build capacity to adapt and respond effectively,” he added.
The President urged the judiciary to adapt to shifting dynamics of financial crime, stressing that realigning the nation’s investigative and prosecutorial strategies is critical to preventing institutional obsolescence.
Tinubu said the country was already on the right trajectory, citing the EFCC’s recent momentum in tackling cryptocurrency fraud and recovering virtual assets.
“The EFCC’s recent momentum in tackling cryptocurrency fraud and its commendable strides in recovering virtual assets are highly reassuring. The agency has recovered billions of naira in cryptocurrency investment-related fraud cases.
“In 2025, the agency secured the forfeiture of $22,417.91 (Twenty-Two Thousand, Four Hundred and Seventeen Dollars, Ninety-One Cents) worth of Bitcoin; 1,001,301.87 USDT (One Million, One Thousand, Three Hundred and One USDT and Eighty-Seven Cents) in digital assets; and US$5.6 million linked to the CBEX scheme, while 192 foreigners arrested for cyber-terrorism and cryptocurrency fraud were successfully prosecuted and deported afterwards,” he said.
He said the EFCC’s actions show an agency that is proactive, forward-looking and resolved not to be outpaced by technological innovation, while the judiciary must complement law enforcement by rapidly upscaling its capacity.
Tinubu acknowledged the Chief Justice of Nigeria’s efforts in reforming the judiciary and pledged the full support of the executive to ensure the judiciary is adequately equipped for justice delivery in the digital age.
Earlier, Chief Justice of Nigeria, Hon. Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, said the 8th edition of the event reflects the commitment of the NJI and EFCC to sustain efforts aimed at addressing challenges confronting stakeholders in Nigeria’s justice system.
She said the trend in technology has impacted how digital evidence is obtained and recorded, noting that effective administration of criminal justice in the digital era requires firm and disciplined case management, which capacity-building programmes such as the EFCC and NJI collaboration aim to strengthen.
The CJN noted that sustained judicial education and capacity development in the justice sector was yielding positive results, with improved conduct of judicial officers, especially judges, in case management and the dispensation of justice in recent years.
Senate Committee Chairman on Anti-Corruption and Financial Crimes, Sen. Emmanuel Udende, said the timing of the workshop was apt given the increasing sophistication of financial crimes and corruption, particularly cases involving politically exposed persons, which directly impact timely case management and the dispensation of justice.
He assured stakeholders that the National Assembly remained committed to supporting the enhancement of the war against corruption and financial crimes in Nigeria through proactive legislation.
Minister of Justice and Attorney General of the Federation, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, represented by the Director of Public Prosecution, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo, urged synergy among stakeholders in addressing emerging challenges in Nigeria’s fight against corruption, stating that one arm of government alone could not effectively address the problem.
He urged judicial officers, especially judges and lawyers, to leverage opportunities provided during the workshop to enhance their capacities to make investigation more thorough and prosecution more diligent.
In his welcome address, Administrator of the National Judicial Institute, Justice Babatunde Adejumo, said the collaboration between the EFCC and the NJI in enhancing the capacity of judicial officers has become an integral part of government’s efforts to frontally tackle the dynamics and scale of financial crimes in the digital age.
He said the presence of the Vice President at the event was a practical demonstration of the commitment of the Tinubu administration to boost Nigeria’s war against corruption.
Executive Chairman of the EFCC, Mr Ola Olukoyede, said the event was a national imperative that has become an important component of the annual programme of both the EFCC and the NJI.
He said the commission under his leadership was reform-minded and has recorded unprecedented convictions as well as financial recoveries over the past three years, assuring transparent and judicious handling of recovered money and property.
Olukoyede also regretted the impact of advanced technology on financial crimes and other forms of corruption, noting that digital innovation was fast outpacing legal instruments and provisions for prosecution.
The post Tinubu to Judiciary: Seal loopholes criminals exploit to escape justice appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
The Senate on Tuesday passed for second reading a bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and strengthen support for survivors during plenary.
The bill, sponsored by Sen. Asuquo Ekpenyong (Cross River South) seeks to establish a legal and institutional framework for suicide prevention, treatment and support for people experiencing psychological distress.
Leading the debate for the bill, Ekpenyong said Nigeria’s existing laws presented conflicting approaches to attempted suicide, with mental health legislation recognising it as a psychiatric emergency while criminal laws prescribed punishment.
“At the heart of this bill is a simple question: when a Nigerian survives a suicide attempt, should the first response of the state be prosecution or protection?” he asked.
According to him, the National Mental Health Act recognises attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate intervention, while Sections 327 of the Criminal Code and 231 of the Penal Code exposes survivors to criminal punishment.
Ekpenyong said the bill would resolve the contradiction by prioritising prevention, treatment and the preservation of life.
He argued that criminalisation could discourage people experiencing suicidal thoughts from seeking help and cause families to conceal suicide attempts for fear of stigma or prosecution.
According to him, such practices can delay intervention and undermine reliable data collection, weakening national suicide-prevention efforts.
The senator said decriminalising attempted suicide would neither legalise nor encourage suicide, adding that the bill focused on protecting survivors and ensuring access to timely medical care.
He said the proposed legislation would establish coordinated prevention services, including crisis helplines, referral pathways and follow-up support for people who survived suicide attempts.
Ekpenyong added that the bill would strengthen public education and train healthcare workers, law-enforcement personnel, teachers and emergency responders to recognise warning signs and connect at-risk individuals with appropriate services.
He said families affected by suicide or attempted suicide would also require access to psychosocial support, while improved data collection and research would help the government develop effective prevention policies.
The senator said the bill would provide an institutional and funding framework for implementing suicide-prevention services, stressing that decriminalisation without accessible care would be incomplete.
He added that the committee stage would allow lawmakers to harmonise the proposed legislation with the Criminal Code, Penal Code, National Mental Health Act and relevant state laws.
Other lawmakers who took turns to support the bill argued that attempted suicide should be treated primarily as a mental health concern requiring professional care rather than criminal punishment.
They said that people experiencing severe emotional distress needed medical attention and support, adding that detention or imprisonment would not address the underlying causes of their conditions.
They stressed that suicide prevention required coordinated action involving healthcare professionals, educational institutions, families, law enforcement agencies and relevant government institutions.
The proposed legislation, according to them, will provide an opportunity for public consultation and professional contributions before the Senate takes further legislative action.
Senate President Godswill Akpabio subsequently put the bill to a voice vote, and it was passed for second reading, and thereafter referred the bill to the committee on health and Judiciary, human rights and legal matters

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Gov. Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers remains an integral and active part of the ruling political team.
Wike stated this during a media chat in Abuja on Tuesday, dismissing insinuations that Gov. Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers has been sidelined in the political architecture of the state.
According to him, the governor remains an integral and active part of the ruling political team.
Addressing questions about Fubara’s current status and quiet disposition, Wike maintained that the governor’s perceived silence does not equate to exclusion or unhappiness.
“Fubara has not been pushed aside. If you know him, he’s been a very quiet person.
“He is fully a member of the Rainbow Coalition and fully playing his part in efforts to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027,” he said.
The minister revealed that the governor recently hosted a crucial, high-level strategic meeting at his residence attended by key stakeholders, underscoring his active involvement in the state’s political direction.
“Do you know what it takes to hold a meeting in his house? For everybody to be there?
“What matters most to Gov. Fubara is ensuring that his political family retains its influence and power moving forward,” he said.
Speaking as the campaign coordinator for Rivers, Wike said lists of campaign committee members have been duly submitted, with Fubara slated to serve as one of the primary leaders.
Reflecting on past political tensions in the state, Wike blamed external actors and ungrateful elements, including certain opposition governors for trying to drive a wedge between him and Fubara for political mileage.
He, however, noted that despite external attempts to exploit the situation, mutual forgiveness and reconciliation have prevailed.
Wike also touched on speculation regarding Fubara’s future political trajectory after his tenure, including potential federal appointments.
While noting that he does not possess the constitutional prerogative to nominate ministers, Wike maintained an optimistic outlook on the governor’s standing.
Wike reiterated that speculations regarding friction between him and the governor are unfounded, stressing that both leaders were actively working together to safeguard the state’s political stability.
He explained that the Rainbow Coalition in River was engineered to unite different political factions across party lines—including members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and other groups.
He added that the goal was to champion a unified agenda under Tinubu and avoid destructive litigations that previously plagued the state.
When pressed on how offices and candidacies were being shared among coalition members, Wike defended the strategy as a display of high-level political ingenuity that respects the peculiarities of different areas while maintaining team solidarity.
“When you talk about politicians that agree to form an umbrella, the umbrella does not mean that all the candidates will be one party.
“We look at the peculiarities of areas, and say, listen, all of us are together and all of us are supporters of Mr President,” he said.

items.title: After flood disasters, Nepal needs clear numbers on aid and a reconstruction plan

items.author: Susmita Aryal
items.content:
Nepali communities live in the shadow of natural hazards, where uncertainty and fear are daily realities
Originally published on Global Voices
Settlements across the Tadi River, Devighat in Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal on October 7, 2026. Used with permission.
Forty-six days later, just when Nepal was trying to recover from the Bhotekoshi flash flood, which struck the Nepal–Tibet border regions, affecting Rasuwa and Nuwakot, another landslide-induced flood hit Chumnubri, Gorkha, on October 11, 2026. This latest disaster has added to the wounds of communities who live in the shadow of natural hazards, where uncertainty and fear are daily realities.
Read more: The day after the central Nepal flood
The climate-related disaster in Nuwakot has devastated a once-popular tourist landscape, destroying its natural beauty and economic opportunities, with settlements heartbreakingly reduced to rubble and vital infrastructure, including roads, bridges and hydro-power facilities, washed away. The full death toll remains officially unconfirmed.
Survivors still come to search for their belongings in Devighatm, Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal on October 7, 2026. Used with permission.
But an uncomfortable truth lies behind the devastation: The human cost of such disasters often goes ignored. Behind the statistics are stories of broken dreams, lost livelihoods, buried memories. There are families trying to stay alive without their loved ones, communities faced with an uncertain future, and countless people trying to make lives reconnect and rebuild from what little is left.
Read more: Nepal floods: Reporter’s diary, August 27, 2026
The task of rebuilding is huge. The damage is not only to homes, roads and bridges, but also to farms and local businesses. Kyodo News reports via AP that 7,500 homes were damaged or completely destroyed, with costs of recovery hitting USD 4.77 billion. The government has now moved from emergency relief to rehabilitation and reconstruction and has also acknowledged the risks posed by possible glacial outburst floods (GLOFs) and other hazards. The destruction of bridges and transport links has made surviving communities vulnerable and slowed reconstruction, exposing residents to further risk.
Buildings left standing, and homes left empty in the Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal on October 7, 2026. Used with permission.
To this end, joint efforts are underway to rebuild damaged infrastructure and restore vital services. But pledged assistance is not the same as money that has actually been received and delivered to affected communities. Nepal’s Ministry of Finance’s foreign assistance tracker shows that Nepal has received USD 24.89 million in disaster relief funds. Such tracking can help bring transparency to the collection and distribution of aid. The Prime Minister's Office separately reported that USD 50.47 million of assistance (cash, materials, and teams) had been pledged.
No formal update has been given on the implementation of longer-term reconstruction plans. Most of the aid is still going to meet immediate needs like medical aid, food, and temporary shelters, such as tents.
What are houses without their people called? Photo featuring reporter Susmita Aryal. Photo from Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot District via Maya Devi Aryal on October 7, 2026. Used with permission.
Many affected communities remain far from rebuilt infrastructure and restored livelihoods. India, China, the United States, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are providing assistance, and the Asian Development Bank and other international financial institutions have committed funds. Yet recovery is likely to progress unevenly. The challenge for affected communities is not just to rebuild what was lost but to restore livelihoods, public services and a sense of security in the face of recurring environmental hazards.
In the following photo essay, Global Voices highlights how Nepali citizens are still affected by the disaster. All photos were taken by Susmita Aryal in Bidur Municipality, Nuwakot District on October 7, 2026.
Tara Devi Tamang and others waiting for relief and basic needs provided at the Bidur Municipality Office, Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal. Used with permission
Daily essentials scattered around the community in Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal. Used with permission.
A half-destroyed shelter once used to be a home. Photo from Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal. Used with permission.
Somebody’s whole world reduced to rubble. Image from Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot District via Susmita Aryal. Used with permission.
A viral house broken window pane weaponized for an emergency flight. Image from Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot District via Susmita Aryal. Used with permission.
Nothing is left of a riverside home in Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal. Used with permission.
A helmet sits alone without its rider. Image from Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot District via Susmita Aryal. Used with permission.
Written by Susmita Aryal

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Lagos State on Tuesday met  with security agencies, political parties and other stakeholders to strengthen collaboration and ensure peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections.
Speaking  at the stakeholders’ meeting in Lagos, Prof Ayobami Salami,  Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), said the meeting also aimed at mobilising public support for effective implementation of the commission’s electoral plans.
Salami said the commission was intensifying preparations in logistics, personnel deployment, election security, voter education and accessibility.
He said INEC had moved from strategic planning to active operational implementation, with nine of the 14 scheduled milestones for the 2027 elections already accomplished as of Oct. 6.
“At the national level, the Register of Voters currently stands at approximately 103 million.
“Preparations are also advancing in critical areas, including the procurement and delivery of 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, software upgrades, battery optimisation and biometric calibration.
“Similarly, extensive logistical arrangements are being made for the deployment of over 100,000 vehicles and 4,000 boats nationwide,” he said.
The REC added that recruitment of approximately 1.4 million election personnel through the INECPRES portal was ongoing, with the application window scheduled to close on Nov. 18.
He said Lagos, with 7,488,633 registered voters, remained strategically important to the electoral process, requiring meticulous planning and coordinated deployment of resources across its 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs).
According to him, the state has 245 Registration Areas and 13,325 Polling Units, making effective logistics and inter-agency cooperation essential to the successful conduct of the elections.
Salami said the commission was taking account of Lagos’ peculiar challenges, including traffic congestion, densely populated communities, commercial activities, difficult-to-access settlements and riverine locations.
“Beyond these figures are the distinctive operational realities of Lagos: a large and mobile population, densely populated urban communities, extensive commercial activities, traffic challenges, some difficult-to-access settlements and riverine locations.
“These peculiarities demand careful planning and solutions tailored to the circumstances of individual communities.
“Our commitment is to ensure that these challenges are anticipated and addressed through timely, coordinated and effective operational arrangements,” he said.
He said preparations included transportation planning, timely deployment of election materials, activation of Registration Area Centres (RACs) and assessment of the readiness of election personnel and facilities.
The REC added that INEC was strengthening internal coordination and monitoring mechanisms to identify potential operational challenges early and address them before they affected election activities.
He said the commission would also provide assistive materials, including Braille ballot guides, EC30 PWD posters and magnifying glasses, where applicable, to promote participation by persons with disabilities.
Salami urged organisations representing persons with disabilities to continue engaging with the commission and providing recommendations to improve accessibility and inclusion.
On election security, he said INEC would continue working with relevant security agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), led by the Nigeria Police Force, to identify and mitigate potential electoral risks.
“Our collective priority is to safeguard voters, election personnel, observers, electoral materials and facilities throughout the electoral process.
“Particular attention will be given to prevention of electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying, ballot snatching and other unlawful activities capable of undermining the credibility of elections.
“In collaboration with relevant law enforcement and anti-corruption agencies, appropriate preventive and enforcement measures will be pursued in accordance with the law,” he said.
The REC called on political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their activities responsibly, respect electoral laws and avoid actions capable of disrupting public peace.
He stressed that political competition should not be used to justify violence, intimidation or other unlawful conduct, adding that protecting citizens’ right to participate freely in elections was a shared responsibility.
Salami also raised concerns about misinformation, disinformation and the misuse of artificial intelligence to circulate manipulated images, fabricated reports, synthetic audio and video recordings, deepfakes and voice clones.
He urged political actors, media practitioners, civil society organisations and members of the public to verify election-related information through authorised INEC communication channels before sharing it.
The REC reiterated that the collation and declaration of election results must follow established legal procedures and be undertaken only by duly authorised electoral officials.
He said unverified figures and speculative reports should not be presented as official results, warning that false information could generate confusion, heighten political tensions and undermine public confidence in the electoral process.
Salami emphasised that the successful conduct of the elections required the commitment of all stakeholders, noting that INEC could not achieve the objective of credible elections acting alone.
“Political parties have a great responsibility to promote peaceful competition, respect electoral regulations and encourage responsible conduct among their members and supporters.
“Security agencies must continue to provide a safe and enabling environment for electoral activities.
“Traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, and community institutions remain important partners in promoting civic responsibility, peaceful coexistence and public participation,” he said.
He also urged civil society organisations to intensify voter education and public enlightenment, while calling on the media to uphold accuracy, fairness and professionalism in reporting electoral activities.
The REC appealed to stakeholders to encourage registered voters to verify their details on the Register of Voters, collect their Permanent Voter Cards, when available, and obtain electoral information from authorised sources.
He said INEC remained committed to professionalism, transparency, inclusivity and effective implementation of its constitutional responsibilities as preparations for the 2027 General Elections gathered momentum.
“Our objective is clear: to ensure that every stage of the electoral process is properly planned, effectively implemented and conducted in a manner that strengthens public confidence in the Commission and the integrity of elections.
“With your continued cooperation, constructive engagement and shared commitment, I am confident that Lagos State can contribute significantly to the successful conduct of a peaceful, credible, transparent and inclusive General Elections,” he said.

items.author: Urowayino Jeremiah
items.content:
THE Delta State Government has commenced an emergency free comprehensive medical and surgical outreach to residents of Odidi Federated Communities along the Trans-Forcados Pipeline in Warri South-West Local Government Area, following the oil spill that has affected the communities.
The State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Joseph Onojaeme, who led the medical team, said the initiative was in compliance with the directive Governor Sheriff Oborevwori.
He noted that the outreach would carry out multidisciplinary interventions, including surgeries, eye checks, dental care, laboratory investigations, medical outpatient care and others.
The Commissioner commended the people of Odidi Federated Communities for the peaceful manner they had conducted themselves since the oil spill occurred.
He appealed to residents to cooperate with the medical team, stressing that all drugs, mosquito nets and treatments being administered were completely free.
Onojaeme highlighted the Governor’s keen interest in the well-being of Deltans, which said, had led to the construction and renovation of primary health care facilities across the state, as well as increased funding for these facilities.
He assured that the government would continue to ensure that healthcare is easily accessible to all Deltans.
Speaking on behalf of the Odidi Federated Communities, a community leader, Mr. Faith Mamamu, commended the Delta State Government for its prompt response to the oil spill crisis, which he said has disrupted the economic life of the communities.
He said the people of Odidi were deeply grateful for the Governor’s concern and swift intervention.
Beneficiaries of the outreach who spoke also commended Governor Oborevwori for his prompt response and for the free drugs and care provided to them, expressing appreciation that the government had come to their aid at a difficult time.
Recall that Governor Oborevwori, on October 6, 2026, directed the Commissioner for Health to immediately deploy medical personnel to the affected communities to assess residents and determine the health implications of the pollution.

items.content:
Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman has urged parliamentary party leaders and lawmakers to legislate to withdraw the government's authority to set the petroleum levy, arguing that parliament's delegation of this power weakens its constitutional role.
He has also called for a united political response to rising inflation and warned that governor's rule and the imposition of emergency measures in 12 districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa could deepen the province's political crisis.
In a letter to the heads and members of parliamentary parties, Hafiz Naeem said the petroleum levy was affecting multiple sectors of the economy, including food, agriculture, transport and industry.
He urged all parliamentary parties to rise above their political affiliations and work together to provide the public with relief from inflation.
The JI chief argued that the revenue shortfall resulting from a reduction in the petroleum levy could be offset by curbing unnecessary government expenditure and eliminating financial irregularities.
He called on political parties to devise a joint strategy to ease the burden of inflation on the public and abolish the levy.
Expressing concern over the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Hafiz Naeem said the province was already facing uncertainty. The imposition of governor's rule and the declaration of an emergency in 12 districts, he warned, could further aggravate the political crisis.
He called on all political parties to unite to protect the constitutional and democratic order in K-P, stressing that the province's problems should be resolved in accordance with the Constitution, the law and democratic principles.
In his letter, the JI emir urged parliamentary parties to rise above their political differences and play a collective role in securing the abolition of the petroleum levy, reducing inflation and safeguarding the democratic system.

items.author: Hasnaat Malik
items.content:
The Supreme Court held that the principle of life expectancy cannot be applied to commute the death sentence of a man convicted of murdering a young woman because she had refused to marry him, declaring that the killing constituted a grave and aggravated offence with no mitigating circumstances.
A three-member bench, led by Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, dismissed the convict's review petition seeking to convert his death sentence to life imprisonment on the ground that he had spent 14 years in jail.
In a nine-page judgment authored by Justice Kakar, the court said the murder of an innocent woman solely because she declined a marriage proposal was an act that could not be justified by wounded pride, customary practices or claims of honour.
"It is a matter of profound shame to the conscience of any civilised society when a man fails to gain a woman's affection and responds to her refusal with violence instead of acceptance," the judgment said, adding that marriage was a mutual and voluntary covenant requiring the free consent of both parties.
The court observed that patriarchal systems often treated men as having an exclusive right to choose a woman, demand her hand in marriage and assert possession over her, irrespective of her wishes.
It said a woman exercised her fundamental right when she rejected a suitor, but men operating under a patriarchal mindset sometimes perceived such a refusal as an affront to their "honour". This attitude, the judgment noted, could lead to stalking, home invasions, acid attacks and femicide.
The bench said the case provided an opportunity to examine ego-driven customs and violence against women, particularly whether a woman's refusal to marry could constitute a mitigating circumstance in a murder case.
The court rejected that proposition, observing that treating a woman's lawful refusal as "provocation" or a mitigating factor was an absurd argument because no person had the right to deprive another of life merely for declining a marriage proposal.
"Accepting such an argument would constitute judicial endorsement of the notion that a woman's will is subordinate to a man's preference," the judgment stated.
The court emphasised that a woman's consent to marriage could not be treated as irrelevant in a male-dominated society. It said such a mindset was irreconcilable with Islam, which requires a woman's free assent as a prerequisite for a valid nikah.
Every adult, whether male or female, is equally entitled to decide whether, when and with whom to marry, the judgment said. This right is inherent and does not depend on permission or approval from a person's family, tribe or society.
"There is no excuse for such behaviour, regardless of whether it is committed in the name of honour, custom, injured pride, or emotions," the court observed.
The judgment also referred to Pakistan's obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW).
Article 16 of the convention requires states to ensure that women have the same right as men freely to choose a spouse and to enter into marriage only with their free and full consent.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Planning Ahsan Iqbal on Tuesday stressed that poverty alleviation, human resource development and improved social indicators must remain top national priorities to transform Pakistan into a sustainable and competitive economy.
Addressing an international conference on Pakistan's Vision for Inclusive and Resilient Economic Transformation, Iqbal said it was imperative to ensure that the benefits of development reached every citizen and region, with equitable access to economic opportunities.
He noted that poverty was not merely a lack of income but also limited access to education, healthcare, nutrition and decent employment.
Expressing concern over the rising poverty rate and weak social indicators in Pakistan, he stressed that addressing these fundamental challenges was essential for sustainable national development.
Iqbal observed around 25 million children were out of school in Pakistan, while the rate of child stunting stood at approximately 40 per cent. Without improvements in education, healthcare and nutrition, he said, Pakistan could not compete effectively in the global economy.
He termed early childhood development, quality education and investment in human resources fundamental to future economic growth.
The minister said the government's focus was not limited to assessing poverty levels; rather, its ultimate objective was to lift people out of poverty and enable them to achieve self-sufficiency. He said the government was intensifying and accelerating its efforts while mobilising all relevant stakeholders to achieve this goal.
He said sustainable poverty alleviation required more than financial assistance or the provision of productive assets to deserving families, adding they also needed skills, business capital, access to markets and reliable livelihood opportunities.
He emphasised women's economic empowerment, employment opportunities for young people and the role of universities in promoting the development of local communities.
Iqbal said the government intended to link poverty alleviation initiatives with evidence-based policymaking, measurable outcomes and effective monitoring to ensure stable incomes, savings, improved nutrition and a better quality of life.
Calling for prosperous districts to become partners in the development of underdeveloped areas, the minister stressed promoting self-reliance and mutual support. He pointed out that 11 of Pakistan's 20 poorest districts were located in Balochistan.
He said resources and capabilities must be pooled to extend the benefits of development to every region and reduce regional inequalities.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday emphasised the need to complement efforts to curb irregular migration with practical opportunities for "safe, orderly and regular migration" during a meeting with European Union (EU) Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner.
The meeting focused on strengthening Pakistan-EU cooperation in the areas of migration and mobility, one of the eight pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan 2019, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said in a press release.
Welcoming Commissioner Brunner on his first visit to Pakistan, the prime minister highlighted Pakistan's sustained efforts to curb irregular migration and combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking through legislative reforms, institutional strengthening, effective enforcement, and international cooperation.
The premier underscored the importance Pakistan attached to its partnership with the EU and reaffirmed its commitment to further strengthening cooperation across all pillars of the Pak-EU Strategic Engagement Plan.
He noted that expanding legal pathways for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals would help meet the labour-market needs of European countries while reducing the vulnerability of prospective migrants to smuggling networks.
Brunner appreciated the measures taken and the cooperation extended by the government of Pakistan. He expressed confidence that these efforts would contribute positively to the expansion of legal migration pathways and the promotion of mutually beneficial labour mobility between Pakistan and the EU.
NAFSC
Terming agriculture as the backbone of the national economy, the prime minister noted that the sector has the potential to steer Pakistan's economy on the path of development in a short span of time.
He made the remarks while chairing the first meeting of the National Agriculture and Food Security Council (NAFSC).
The premier observed that the livestock sector also possessed vast potential to increase national exports and the government was taking steps to increase Pakistan's halal meat exports.
He said the federal government would provide all kinds of cooperation to the provinces for agricultural development, adding that providing farmers with low-cost fertilizer, quality seeds, modern machinery and equipment and technical capabilities for the better use of water was a top priority.
The prime minister expressed his satisfaction at the availability of wheat to meet domestic requirements and warned that no leniency would be shown to those hoarding wheat.
He stressed that ensuring a fair price for farmers' crops, especially small and medium-scale farmers, is a priority, adding that it was necessary to determine the correct price of wheat before sowing so that farmers received appropriate compensation for their hard work.
"We want farmers to get the right price for wheat and consumers to avail of affordable wheat. The decision regarding the price of wheat will be made in consultation with the provinces," he said.
During the meeting, the prime minister lauded Punjab chief minister for taking commendable steps such as farmers' development, aquaculture, shrimp farming, and providing direct subsidies to farmers through the Kissan Card.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has launched the second edition of its Banking on Equality Policy to narrow the gender gap in financial inclusion and improve women’s access to banking services.
The Banking on Equality Policy 2026 sets new targets for banks to increase women’s representation in the workforce, expand digital banking access, and provide more financing to women-owned businesses.
Under the policy, banks are encouraged to introduce simplified digital accounts for women, promote digital payments for women-led businesses, and develop financing products for female entrepreneurs. The policy also calls for alternative credit assessment methods to help women who lack formal credit histories or conventional collateral.
SBP has also asked banks to set targets for hiring women, reaching female customers, and increasing women’s representation among branchless banking agents. Banks are encouraged to provide daycare facilities for working mothers and introduce career development policies to help women move into leadership positions.
The new policy builds on the first edition introduced in 2021. During its implementation, Pakistan’s gender gap in financial inclusion narrowed from 39 percent in 2021 to 29 percent in 2025.
Banks also hired more than 17,500 women during this period, while women’s share of the banking workforce increased from 13 percent to 17 percent. Banks have also established dedicated teams to develop financial products and services for women.
SBP will monitor implementation through quarterly data reporting, regular evaluations, and mystery shopping exercises.
The policy supports Pakistan’s National Financial Inclusion Strategy target of reducing the gender gap in financial inclusion to 25 percent by 2028. It also aims to improve women’s financial literacy and support their participation in entrepreneurship.
SBP said the policy was finalized after consultations with local and international stakeholders.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) has digitized 99 percent of payments at its service centres across Pakistan to make digital payments easier and accessible.
The progress was discussed at a meeting chaired by Minister of State for Railways and Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani at the Finance Division on October 13, 2026. Officials reviewed progress on digital payments and discussed targets for the next phase of the initiative.
The number of merchants accepting digital payments increased fourfold during the last fiscal year. Passport centres have also been enabled to accept digital payments.
Around 75 percent of payments across the federal government’s centralized and self-accounting entities are now accepted digitally, according to the meeting’s briefing.
Participants reviewed three key indicators to measure progress: the number of active and unique digital payment users, the annual number of digital transactions, and the number of merchants accepting digital payments.
The committee decided to review the definitions of active app users, active merchants and unique digital payment users to ensure the figures accurately reflect usage and avoid double counting.
Kayani also asked private sector representatives to prepare recommendations on tax policy changes that could support the expansion of digital payments.
The minister said the Cashless Pakistan initiative aims to make payments more convenient, improve transparency and bring more economic activity into the documented economy.
He stressed the need for reliable data to track progress.
The government said it would continue working with regulators, banks, fintech companies and other businesses to expand digital payments and improve financial inclusion.
Representatives from the Finance Division, State Bank of Pakistan, Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, NADRA and Pakistan Digital Authority attended the meeting.
Private sector participants included representatives of the Pakistan Banking Association, Easypaisa, JazzCash, Bank Alfalah, JS Bank and Karandaaz Pakistan.

items.author: Amiya Johar
items.content:
The GSMA board outlined the industry’s connectivity priorities, calling for action on smartphone affordability, online scams and network investment while backing closer international cooperation on future 6G standards.
Following a board meeting in New Delhi, India, the industry association stated that although 97% of the global population live within mobile broadband coverage, 3.4 billion people remain unconnected to mobile internet. The cost of devices remains a significant barrier, with an entry-level internet-enabled handset equivalent to 44% of average monthly income for the poorest 20% of people in low- and middle-income countries.
The GSMA highlighted potential measures to improve affordability including financing schemes, targeted tax cuts and closer cooperation between device makers and memory suppliers.
It also identified scams and fraud as a growing threat, warning that although the mobile industry continues to strengthen network detection and cyber defence tools, “no single sector can tackle the threat alone”. The GSMA noted AI-generated content and deepfakes further add to risks for consumers, public trust and government objectives, calling on the industry to “join forces to counter scams with practical solutions”.
Sustained investment
The GSMA also highlighted the need for network investment and supportive policy to accelerate connectivity growth. It found mobile technologies and services generated $6 trillion in economic value in 2025, equivalent to 6.4% of global GDP. This figure is forecast to reach $11.3 trillion by 2030.
In addition, operators are projected to invest $1.2 trillion in capital expenditure between 2025 and 2030 to expand and upgrade networks, with 57% of mobile connections expected to use 5G by the end of the decade.
GSMA director general Vivek Badrinath said the sector’s next priority must be to translate 5G expansion into “meaningful value”, ensuring more people can participate in the digital economy. “This will require sustained investment, enabling policy and collaboration across the wider ecosystem,” he stressed.
Looking ahead, the industry association reiterated its support for global standards and harmonised spectrum as 6G development continues. It highlighted countries representing more than 80% of the world’s population support mobile use of the upper 6GHz band, which could provide the 200MHz to 400MHz channel bandwidths expected to be needed for 6G.
GSMA chair Gopal Vittal said that “by working through global standards and collaborating across markets, we can accelerate innovation, strengthen trust and resilience” as the industry develops the next generation of connectivity.
The post GSMA puts 6G, AI threats, digital inclusion in focus appeared first on Mobile World Live.

items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
Profits of Pakistan’s top 20 listed textile companies rose 11 percent year-on-year to Rs. 51.9 billion in fiscal year 2026, driven by lower finance costs and a decline in effective tax rates, according to Topline Securities.
The companies generated combined sales of Rs. 1.4 trillion, equivalent to around $5 billion, largely unchanged from the previous year. The 20 companies account for 83 percent of the total market capitalization of the selected listed textile sector.
The effective tax rate of the companies fell to 33.2 percent in FY26 from 37.1 percent a year earlier, mainly due to reversals of deferred tax liabilities following changes in the future super tax treatment of exporters.
Meanwhile, finance costs declined 19 percent year-on-year to Rs. 54.5 billion, which Topline attributed primarily to lower financing rates and reduced borrowings under the Export Finance Scheme.
Gross margins remained stable at 13.1 percent, while gross profit and sales declined 0.2 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively.
Pakistan’s textile exports reached a record $17.6 billion in FY26, up 2 percent year-on-year, accounting for 57 percent of the country’s total goods exports. Value-added textile exports increased 3 percent to $13 billion. Interloop, Sapphire Textile Mills and Nishat Mills were the three largest contributors to the listed sector’s profits, collectively accounting for 48 percent of total earnings.
Interloop’s consolidated profit rose 129 percent to Rs. 12.7 billion, supported by improved gross margins, lower finance costs and a sharp increase in other income. Its sales grew 5 percent to Rs. 187.7 billion.
Sapphire Textile Mills’ unconsolidated profit increased 73 percent to Rs. 6.8 billion, despite a 13 percent decline in sales to Rs. 81.2 billion. The improvement was driven primarily by higher other income, lower finance costs and a reduced effective tax rate.
In contrast, Nishat Mills’ unconsolidated profit fell 9 percent to Rs. 5.5 billion, mainly due to lower dividend income and a contraction in gross margins. Its sales increased 2 percent to Rs. 181.6 billion.
Looking ahead, Topline expects measures announced in the FY27 budget and lower financing costs to support textile sector profitability. Companies are also shifting towards renewable energy and other lower-cost energy sources to manage energy expenses and remain competitive.
However, high energy costs remain a key near-term challenge. Uncertainty over Pakistan’s GSP+ status and a potential slowdown in major developed economies, including the United States and European countries, also pose risks to the sector’s outlook.

items.title: Govt Delays Cost Pakistan $132 Billion
items.summary:
Pakistan suffered an estimated economic loss of $132 billion in 2023, equivalent to 39 percent of its gross domestic product (GDP), due to administrative friction, according to a document by the Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA).
The document identifies administrative inefficiencies and fragmented institutional processes as major obstacles to the country’s economic performance, highlighting the need to reduce procedural barriers and improve coordination among government institutions.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan has called for reform of the international financial architecture to keep pace with fragmentation disrupting trade and investment, climate shocks eroding development gains, restrictive financial conditions and widening financing gaps, as it prepares to take over as chair of the G-24 grouping of developing nations.
Speaking as First Vice-Chair of the G-24 at the Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors' Meeting on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb outlined three priorities for the grouping: restoring development as the central objective of the international financial system, making the Bretton Woods institutions more representative and responsive, and building a development-oriented architecture.
He stressed that reform must ensure timely support for countries undertaking difficult reforms while confronting external shocks beyond their control, and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment as incoming chair to strengthening the G-24's collective influence so that the Global South's voice translates into concrete outcomes. Appreciating Nigeria's leadership, he underscored cooperation among members and institutional partners to advance a more representative, resilient and development-centred economic order.
At investor roundtables organised by Jefferies International and Barclays, the minister, accompanied by Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal and State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad, highlighted improving fiscal and external balances, consecutive primary surpluses, stronger reserves, rating upgrades and renewed access to capital markets. Discussions covered the IMF-supported programme, debt management and financing instruments including Sukuk, further Panda bond issuance and tokenisation, alongside privatisation, tax-base broadening, agricultural income tax, digital enforcement and federal-provincial fiscal coordination.
He pointed to a strong pipeline of initial public offerings (IPOs) and foreign investor interest in electricity distribution companies, as well as airport outsourcing. Responding to questions, the delegation addressed regional geopolitical risks, energy security and liquefied natural gas (LNG) obligations, alongside economic engagement with the United States and Saudi Arabia.
On funding diversification, the minister told Nikkei Asia that Pakistan will continue to "diversify its funding sources," hinting at more yuan-based bonds and possible yen-denominated samurai bonds. He said the recent Panda bond would not be a "one-time issuance" and that Pakistan intends to "keep going back and be a repeat issuer," given China is the "second largest and deepest capital market in the world." Samurai bonds "would make sense" and are "something which we should think through," he said, adding, "We need to do more homework." He said Pakistan does not want to increase the quantum of its external debt.
Pakistan issued its first Panda bond worth 1.75 billion yuan ($261 million) in mid-May as part of a 7.2 billion yuan programme, with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) providing partial guarantees. On a panel on mitigating sovereign risks in market-access countries, the minister outlined fiscal consolidation, lower inflation and rebuilt reserves, with debt management measures to lower financing costs, extend maturities and reduce rollover risks. He said renewed market access supports a strategy to improve the external debt profile without increasing its overall size, and stressed national ownership of taxation, energy, state-owned enterprise and pension reforms.
In a meeting with Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) Chief Executive Officer Sultan Abdulrahman Al-Marshad, discussions covered trade and investment, private-sector engagement, the bilateral investment protection agreement and refinery upgrades. He noted satisfactory progress on SFD-supported projects, discussed a fresh project pipeline and sought continued support within the fund's mandate.
Talks with International Finance Corporation (IFC) Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Central Asia Imad Fakhoury covered small-business financing, entrepreneurship, capital markets, and green and digital bonds. He reaffirmed commitment to Reko Diq and appreciated IFC's financing leadership. Mining infrastructure and value addition, affordable housing, agricultural storage and cold chains, and public-private partnerships in water services and advanced electricity metering were also discussed. On population, the minister stressed the urgency of addressing rapid growth and its implications for health, education and employment, citing Indonesia, Bangladesh and Iran. He outlined a National Population Council led by the prime minister, emphasising women's education, workforce participation and engagement with religious leaders on birth spacing, and pointed to freelancing, IT-enabled services and digital skills as ways to expand youth earnings and exports.
A meeting with Mashreq Bank's senior management covered digital banking, financial inclusion, offshore service operations, digital accounts for overseas Pakistanis and collaboration on tokenisation, blockchain and digital assets within Pakistan's evolving regulatory framework. The minister also said the National Tariff Policy would not be compromised, calling it "not only about the auto industry – it's about industries in general," and referred to a revamped auto policy targeting 30% electric vehicles among new sales by 2030. He noted that ASEAN reduced tariffs in the late 1990s to generate various upsides, adding, "This can very much be a Southeast Asia moment for Pakistan."
Pakistan, an IMF member since 1950, is in its 25th arrangement and owed the fund about $10.5 billion as of Monday. The minister said the programme's structural reform agenda would lead to sustainability, and that Pakistan would graduate once "the rest of the world becomes convinced that we don't need the lender of last resort."

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Rising government bond yields are making it much harder for major developed economies to stabilise debt burdens, with countries including France, the US and Britain facing growing fiscal challenges, credit rating agency Fitch said on Tuesday.
In a report, Fitch said benchmark 10-year government bond yields in the world's 10 largest developed economies had risen by an average of 81 basis points so far this year. That would contribute to a nearly $4 trillion increase in overall developed-market government debt, taking it above $75 trillion, or $68.5 trillion across the top 10 economies.
IMF warns on AI, debt, ME war
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday flagged significant growth and financial stability risks from a potential ending of the AI investment boom, growing debt levels and a prolonged Middle East conflict.
The IMF forecast global growth at 3.1% for 2026, a slight uptick from a 3.0% forecast in July as still-strong AI infrastructure investment offset higher oil prices caused by the war in the Middle East.
The latest World Economic Outlook report, released in Bangkok during the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank, also predicts 3.4% growth in 2027, but that is based on assumptions that the Strait of Hormuz reopens by March and shipping conditions return to the pre-war situation by October 2027.
A more protracted war that kept oil prices above $130 through the first quarter of 2027 would cut growth next year by half a percentage point, the IMF said.
In another downside scenario, the IMF said that a steep drop in AI investment could lead to a sharp fall in asset prices, ultimately cutting global GDP by 1.1% by 2028, including a 1.8% drop in US output.
It would also lead to reduced trade, IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro said. Trade in AI goods grew 29% between 2023 and 2025, more than triple the 8.3% growth rate of global trade over the same period. Without the AI trade, overall growth in trade would have been only 4.6%, she said.
The debt vulnerabilities of many developing economies are a "major barrier" to inclusive growth, said Nigerian Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele, who chairs the Group of 24 developing nations, warning that member governments were increasingly contending with mounting debt burdens.
Oyedele said estimates showed that developing countries were paying $500 billion more for their debt than developed countries, even as they contend with growing deficits.
"France, Germany, the US all need to do fiscal consolidation, but they're moving in the opposite direction," said Josh Lipsky, vice president of international economics at the Atlantic Council.

He stressed that timely investment in skills development would prepare Pakistani youth for emerging employment opportunities. "Pakistan missed important opportunities during earlier phases of the global automobile revolution, but we cannot afford to miss the electric vehicle revolution," he remarked.
The adviser said the government's forthcoming Auto Policy, expected in the coming weeks, would place particular emphasis on EVs. Work was also underway on a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy, he added. He said the transition could reduce the country's oil import bill and create opportunities for local value addition.
He directed the Engineering Development Board (EDB) to engage with the EU delegation and explore practical areas of cooperation.
The EU delegation expressed interest in exploring cooperation.
