items.author: Bismah Malik
items.content:
For close to two years, Bhavish Aggarwal has been stuck between a rock and a hard place. All to keep Ola Electric and his other ventures going without giving up control of the company he built.
Between November 2024 and March 2025, Aggarwal pledged Ola Electric shares to raise debt for Krutrim Data Centre, the AI infrastructure and services company that he founded in 2023.
Then in December 2025, he sold part of his stake in Ola Electric to repay the ₹260 Cr loan that covered the pledge and release the encumbered shares, selling 3.93% of his holding in the company.
At the time, Ola Electric said repaying the loan meant the company should operate with zero pledge overhang. But ten months later, another pledge is here.
On 30 September, Aggarwal pledged 20 Cr Ola Electric shares, or 4.32% of the company, against non-convertible debentures (NCDs) issued by Krutrim Data Centre.
CTL Trusteeship holds the pledge on behalf of the debenture holders.
Neither the filings nor Ola have disclosed how much Krutrim Data Centre is raising through these debentures.
What is clear is that this is a bigger pledge than before — 20 Cr shares (4.32%) against 17.3 Cr shares (3.93%) that secured a ₹260 Cr loan in the previous instance.
Ola Electric said that the pledge is solely meant to fund his subscription to the company’s upcoming ₹1,000 Cr rights issue, and that no shares are being sold, and that Aggarwal will invest on the same terms as every other shareholder
Shriram Subramanian, founder of advisory firm InGovern Research, said that the EV firm scores poorly on what investors call the “say-do” ratio: how often a company does what it says. The situation around the pledges highlights this.
He added that investors will read a founder pledging, clearing and pledging again as a sign of stress for the promoter or the promoter’s group entities, “and that may not be a good sign.”
Especially after Ola raised ₹780 Cr through a qualified institutional placement (QIP) in June 2026. Four months later, it is asking shareholders for more.
Ola Electric’s Cash Problem
One thing we need to point out: Ola Electric’s rights issue is coming on the heels of the improved operating metrics. Market share rose from 5.1% in Q4 FY26 to 8.4% in Q1 FY27, but short of the 15–20% it targeted for 2026.
But in the same quarter, rival Ather delivered 83,173 scooters, more than twice Ola’s 39,192, while posting a lower loss.
Ola’s dealership rollout is still under way, and its gigafactory has not yet reached its 6 GWh target. Both are drags on its bottom line.
In Q1 FY27, Ola Electric reported revenue of ₹455 Cr, down 45% from a year earlier and below its own guidance of ₹500–550 Cr. Its net loss narrowed to ₹336 Cr, the lowest in seven quarters, but free cash flow was still negative at about ₹351 Cr.
At that rate, the ₹780 Cr raised in June covers roughly two quarters of cash burn. The rights issue, approved by the board on 28 September, would add up to ₹1,000 Cr.
According to the draft letter of offer, about ₹350 Cr will go towards repaying or prepaying borrowings and ₹400 Cr towards organic growth. Of the money earmarked so far, nearly half goes to paying down debt.
These are partly paid shares, which means investors pay in installments. The issue price, entitlement ratio and payment schedule are yet to be announced.
The Idea Behind Pledging Instead Of Selling
A rights issue is offered only to existing shareholders, in proportion to what they already own. Aggarwal still holds roughly 26.2% of Ola Electric shareholding.
If he sits out this rights issue and does not buy in, his stake and therefore his control will shrink.
According to the legal experts we spoke to, Agarwal also cannot simply borrow debt from Ola Electric. Section 67(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 bars a public company from giving financial assistance, directly or indirectly, through a loan, guarantee or security, for anyone to buy or subscribe to its own shares.
Selling shares to invest in the rights issue would be counterproductive to Aggarwal’s goal of maintaining his stake in the company, so pledging shares is the only option on the table
The money comes through Krutrim Data Centre, which, as a company, can issue debentures in a way an individual cannot. Aggarwal has used this route before, with the same company and the same kind of pledge.
What has changed since is his priority.
In December, he faced a similar choice and went the other way.
With the stock near a record low at that time and his pledged shares closer to a margin call, he sold part of his stake to repay the loan and release the pledged shares.
A margin call on pledged shares would have meant that Aggarwal would have had to deposit funds or securities to cover for the dropping market value of the pledged collateral.
Aggarwal avoided this eventuality by selling a portion of his stake in December 2025, but now he is looking at pledging shares to protect his stake. For now at least, it would seem that retaining his control on Ola Electric matters more than any overhang from the pledge.
The Krutrim Link
The current shares pledged by Agarwal aim to secure debt on behalf of Krutrim Data Centre. That also puts a private company’s balance sheet directly behind a listed company’s shares.
If, for instance, Krutrim Data Centre struggles to repay these NCDs, the pledged Ola Electric shares are exposed, and could be sold by the lender group, even if Ola Electric has recovered financially.
InGovern Research’s Subramanian said that if Krutrim’s debt goes bad and the lender enforces the pledge, it could sell the shares, which would weigh on the stock.
He called this an extreme scenario, but said the risk alone is an overhang: public investors will keep watching whether Krutrim is able to pay back the debt. But the lender has to give reasonable notice, sell, and return any surplus, and Aggarwal can redeem the shares until then.
It is also not clear how the money raised by Krutrim reaches Agarwal, whether as a loan, an advance or in some other form, or whether all of it is meant for the rights issue.
That route of funds transfer from Krutrim to Agarwal also matters, according to VPS Law Associates’s VP Singh.
He says that under Section 185 of the Companies Act, a straight loan from Krutrim to Agarwal is not applicable, however it could be a likely scenario of Krutrim repaying some loan it already owes to Agarwal or Krutrim directly subscribing to Ola Electric rights issue through entitlements Aggarwal renounces in its favour.
For Ola Electric itself, this would not be a related-party question. “A transaction only between Krutrim and Aggarwal does not automatically become an Ola Electric related-party transaction. That will kick in when Ola Electric or its subsidiaries deal with a related party,” Singh added.
In the scenario that the lenders decided to enforce the pledge, Ola Electric’s board would have no say. “The shares are the promoter’s property and freely transferable; the company’s obligation is only confined to disclosure,” Singh said.
Can Falling Stock Trigger A Crisis?
A pledge is a loan secured by shares, and the value of that security moves with the stock price. That is exactly what makes it a double-edged arrangement.
At around ₹37 a share, the 20 Cr pledged shares by Agarwal are worth roughly ₹740 Cr.
Brokerages like Citi have set a target price of ₹26 for the next 12 months, indicating that investors should sell.
Lenders in a pledge arrangement typically respond to a price fall by asking the borrower to pledge more shares. If the promoter cannot provide them, lenders can sell the pledged shares in the market.
That is likely to result in a runaway effect where the price is pushed down further, triggering the call for more shares or more funds to cover the pledge.
Subramanian elaborated, but he stressed that this is an extreme scenario. “If Ola’s stock keeps falling, the value of the pledged shares drops against the margin the lender requires. So more and more shares would have to be pledged. Either the promoter pledges more shares to hold the margin, or investors sell their shares to recover some money, which adds to the downward spiral,”
Ola Electric’s investors have already seen a version of this. When Aggarwal sold shares in December to clear his earlier pledge, the stock fell 11% in two days and came close to its record low.
Ola Electric’s stock has fallen about 30% over the past year and trades at less than half its IPO price of ₹76.
While legally, there is no law that bars Agarwal from pledging the shares in a listed firm to secure debt for his private company, the cost he and Ola Electric pay is of credibility. The share entitlements to key shareholders and the schedule of funds payments will all be keenly watched out for.
After that, the question is purely operational in nature. Ola needs to bring its quarterly cash burn down before the money from the QIP and the rights issue runs out.
If Ola Electric needs to raise money again, Agarwal will face the same choice between selling and borrowing, and the cycle will begin anew.

FirstCry’s Swara Baby Products Gets SEBI Nod For ₹1,000 Cr IPO: The Brainbees Solutions subsidiary has secured the markets regulator’s approval for its proposed ₹1,000 Cr public issue.
AITMC Files Updated DRHP: The agri-drone company has filed its UDRHP for a fresh issue of up to 3.5 Cr shares, about ten months after receiving SEBI’s nod. It reported a ₹13.4 Cr profit in FY26 on revenue of ₹106.8 Cr.
StockGro Parent Files Confidential DRHP: AssetGro Fintech is targeting an IPO of up to ₹2,500 Cr, including an ₹800 Cr fresh issue, even as StockGro raises $10.4 Mn in a Series B led by BITKRAFT Ventures.
That’s all for this week.
Bismah Malik

The auction will be conducted on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on October 13, 2026 (Tuesday). The Government Stock up to ten per cent of the notified amount of the sale of each stock will be allotted to eligible individuals and institutions, subject to a maximum limit of one per cent of its notified amount for a single bid per stock as per the ‘Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility’. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on October 13, 2026 (Tuesday). The competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:30 A.M. and non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:00 A.M.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team may be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD Auction Team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids would be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form obtainable from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
The yield per cent per annum or the price as the case may be, expected by the bidder should be expressed up to two decimal points. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid at same/different rates of yield or prices in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system. However, the aggregate amount of bids submitted by a bidder should not exceed the notified amount for each State.
The Reserve Bank of India will determine the maximum yield / minimum price at which bids will be accepted. Stock will be issued for a minimum nominal amount of ₹10,000.00 and in multiples of ₹10,000.00 thereafter.
The results of the auction will be announced on October 13, 2026 (Tuesday) and payment by successful bidders will be made during banking hours on October 14, 2026 (Wednesday) at Mumbai and at respective Regional Offices of RBI.
The new State Government Stocks will bear interest at the rates determined by RBI at the auctions. For the new stock, interest will be paid half yearly on April 14 and October 14 of each year till maturity. For the re-issued Government Stock, interest will be paid at the rate as determined on the date of original issue of Government Stock and will be paid on half yearly basis till maturity. The Stocks will be governed by the provisions of the Government Securities Act, 2006 and the Government Securities Regulations, 2007.
The investment in State Government Stocks will be reckoned as an eligible investment in Government Securities by banks for the purpose of Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. The stocks will qualify for the ready forward facility.

The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions specified in the General Notification F.No.4(2)-B(W&M)/2018 dated March 26, 2025, issued by Government of India, as amended from time to time. State Governments, Union Territories with legislature, eligible Provident Funds in India, designated Foreign Central Banks and any person or institution specified by the Bank in this regard can participate on non-competitive basis, the allocation for which will be outside the notified amount. Individuals can also participate on non-competitive basis, as retail investors. For retail investors, the allocation will be restricted to a maximum of 5 percent of the notified amount. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
The auction will be Price based using multiple price method. Bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India’s Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber system) on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, during the below given timings:
Category of Bids Timing
Competitive 10:30 am - 11:30 am
Non-Competitive 10:30 am - 11:00 am
Results will be announced on the day of the auction.
Payment by successful bidders will have to be made on Thursday, October 15, 2026.
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids would be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190), before the auction timing ends, in the prescribed form. The form can be downloaded from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx). items.content:
Today the Reserve Bank of India placed on its website a Working Paper titled, “Data Gaps in State-Level Inflation: An Assessment for the Covid Period” under the Reserve Bank of India Working Paper Series1. The paper is co-authored by Purnima Shaw and R. K. Sinha.
The collection and compilation of official statistics was affected during the outbreak of Covid-19 pandemic due to the resulting restrictions across the world. In India, imputed price indices for the official inflation were released at the aggregate level for the months of April and May 2020. However, the State-wise official inflation figures remain unavailable for four of the pandemic months viz., April and May 2020 and April and May 2021.
In this context, this paper uses RBI’s Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH) granular data to derive State-wise CPI-U inflation estimates for these four pandemic months. The paper describes the importance of IESH, which continued to be conducted bimonthly and disseminated during the pandemic months. Using the distributions of centre-wise urban consumers’ inflation perceptions, three months ahead inflation expectations, and past State-wise realised CPI-U inflation figures, the paper derives estimates for the State-wise official inflation pertaining to the specified Covid months. These State-wise inflation estimates when aggregated, closely follow the all-India official CPI inflation series.
State-wise inflation data are crucial in the current inflation targeting regime, and therefore, providing estimates for the specific months (for which the official CPI data remains unpublished) can be potentially useful for future research involving State-level inflation time-series data.
(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/1298
1 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the RBI Working Papers series in March 2011. These papers present research in progress of the staff members of the RBI and at times also those of external co-authors, when the research is jointly undertaken. They are disseminated to elicit comments and further debate. The views expressed in these papers are those of the authors and not necessarily those of the institution(s) to which they belong. Comments and observations may please be forwarded to the authors. Citation and use of such papers should take into account its provisional character.

items.content:
EVs Power Cleantech Funding Boom
India’s cleantech story accelerated in Q3 2026. The quarter saw the sector nearly triple its funding volume on the back of big-ticket electric mobility rounds and rising deal activity. So, what’s pulling investors towards the sector and can the momentum extend beyond EVs?
The Cleantech Boom: As per Inc42 data, Indian cleantech startups raised a record $433 Mn in Q3 2026, nearly 3X from $118 Mn in the year-ago quarter. Although funding remained heavily concentrated in one segment, the sector’s broader momentum was evident: deal count rose 44% YoY to 23, while average cheque size zoomed to $19 Mn from $7 Mn in Q3 2025.
The EV Concentration: Within cleantech, electric mobility dominated funding charts in Q3. Just three EV startups – River, Yulu and Ultraviolette – raised a combined $298 Mn, nearly 69% of the sector’s total haul in the quarter. The concentration highlights the sector’s over-dependence on a small group of well-funded ventures.
Decoding The Boom: Cleantech funding surged as investors shifted their focus from climate narratives to commercially-viable businesses solving real problems. Electric mobility led the charge, supported by rising EV registrations, stronger consumer demand and improving PMF. What also helped was rising component localisation and growing investor confidence.
The Road Ahead: Experts believe that the sector’s long-term outlook will depend on broadening investment beyond EVs to other emerging areas such as energy storage, grid tech and green hydrogen. They also see deeper localisation improving margins and reducing supply chain risks. As such, unit economics and a clear path to sustainable revenues will be a key focus area for backers going forward.
As investor conviction expanded across the cleantech ecosystem in Q3, why did capital remain tightly locked within a handful of EV players? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
The AI Safety Drill
OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI giants are rehearsing how they would respond to a catastrophic incident involving AI. The companies are set to engage with US lawmakers as experts believe a major AI incident could happen within 12 months.
The planning comes as AI companies look to avoid a serious failure, which could prompt sweeping public backlash, new restrictions and scrutiny of industry leaders. The fear is that a major AI incident could impact internet infrastructure or financial systems.
The safety drill comes as LLMs find software vulnerabilities and coordinate agents. In the past few months, both OpenAI and Anthropic have reported several instances, where their agents bypassed safeguards and accessed real-world infrastructure.
Weekly Startup Funding Tanks
Indian startups managed to raise a cumulative $123 Mn last week, down 47% from $234 Mn in the preceding week. However, deal count more than doubled week-on-week to 25. DailyObjects and Lumio emerged as the most funded startups last week.
Ecommerce dominated the funding charts last week, raising $63.9 Mn across nine deals. Fintech ranked second with $24 Mn in funding, followed by advanced hardware and technology at $10 Mn.
Early-stage funding trends remained strong as pre-seed and seed-stage startups collectively bagged $12.5 Mn across nine deals. 3one4 Capital and Fireside Ventures emerged as the most active investors, backing two startups each.
Mixed Week For Startup Stocks
Of the 66 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 36 gained in the range of 0.1% to nearly 25% last week. The remaining 30 fell in the range of 0.23% to 13.93%. MobiKwik and PW emerged as the biggest gainers, while Yudiz and Zappfresh shed the most.
The combined market capitalisation of 67 new-age tech stocks, including the recently listed AceVector, stood at $154.71 Bn at the end of last week compared to $153.61 Bn for 66 companies in the preceding week.
Going forward, investors will be tracking inflation data, crude oil prices, progress in Iran-US negotiations and global bond yields for market cues next week.
Nat Habit Bags ₹142 Cr
The D2C personal care brand has raised around $14.7 Mn in its Series C round led by Trident Growth Partners to expand its distribution network, product portfolio and manufacturing capabilities.
Founded in 2019, Nat Habit sells Ayurveda-based personal care products, including hair oils, masks, scrubs, and face creams. Having served 60 Lakh customers so far, the D2C brand currently claims to clocking ₹330 Cr in annualised gross revenue.
The funding comes amid growing investor interest in the homegrown ayurvedic wellness segment, which is being driven by growing demand for traditional formulas, the rise of quick commerce, premiumisation and multi-functional products.
India’s Listed Startup Tracker
India is home to over 70 listed new-age tech companies, with a combined market capitalisation of $173 Bn. Of this, 18 startups went public in 2025 and another 15 have already crossed the milestone this year so far.
Together, these listed startups boast a combined revenue of $26 Bn. A majority of these new-age tech companies, nearly 74%, are profitable, while the remaining posted a cumulative loss of $932 Mn in FY26.
Delhi NCR is home to the largest number of listed startups. On the sectoral front, fintech and ecommerce account for the biggest chunk of listed new-age tech companies.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Turning Agri-Waste Into Steel Industry’s Next Big Power Bet
India’s steel industry still runs largely on coal, while millions of tonnes of agricultural waste goes waste every year. Climitra is connecting these two problems by converting waste biomass into industrial-grade biochar, offering industries a route to carbon removal.
Turning Waste Into Fuel: Founded in 2025, Climitra is building a vertically-integrated startup to convert biomass into bio-coal. It uses AI and geospatial intelligence to map and assess biomass availability, and then converts locally-sourced waste into fuel through a proprietary pyrolysis process.
A Coal Substitute: Climitra’s bio-coal is designed as a 1:1 replacement for fossil coal in steel-making, reducing the need for costly furnace retrofits. The startup claims that its output contains 75-85% fixed carbon, has a gross calorific value of 6,500–8,000 kcal/kg and can cut emissions by up to 90% compared with fossil coal.
Beyond Bio-Fuel: Climitra’s business model extends beyond bio-fuel. The startup is targeting both industrial decarbonisation and carbon removal, using its existing biomass supply chain. The startup claims it has already validated its bio-coal with Tata Steel, JSW Steel and AM/NS India.
Backed by InfoEdge Ventures, the startup is eyeing a piece of the Indian biomass briquette market, which is projected to become a $2.1 Bn opportunity by 2032. So, can Climitra turn agricultural waste into a lower-carbon fuel for its steel industry?

items.content:
“Care for the herd, and the herd will sustain the home”, this African proverb reflects the economic importance of livestock to families and communities.
As Nigerian veterinarians convene in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, this October for the annual conference of the Nigerian Veterinary Medical Association, the occasion provides an opportunity to reflect on more than a century of veterinary development in the country.
Since the establishment of the first Veterinary Department in Zaria in 1913, veterinary medicine has evolved into a vital component of Nigeria’s agricultural, public health and economic infrastructure. Through disease control, livestock development, food safety regulation and scientific research, the profession has made enduring contributions to national development.
Although often viewed primarily through the lens of animal healthcare, veterinary medicine has played a much broader role in safeguarding livelihoods, strengthening food security, facilitating trade and protecting public health. Its history mirrors the wider story of Nigeria’s agricultural transformation and institutional development over the past century.
Foundations of Veterinary Medicine in Nigeria
The roots of organised livestock administration in Nigeria predate colonial rule. In Northern Nigeria, livestock management was overseen through the institution of the Sarkin Shanu (Chief of Cattle), which supervised grazing areas (hurumi), stock routes (burtali), livestock markets (kara), slaughter facilities (kwata) and seasonal livestock movements. Revenue from the Jangali cattle tax, an important source of internally generated revenue levied mainly on pastoral cattle owners, supported livestock administration and governance across Northern Nigeria until its abolition by the federal government in 1975.
With the establishment of British colonial rule, these indigenous systems were retained and adapted through indirect administration. As livestock populations expanded and animal diseases increasingly threatened economic activity, the need for organised veterinary services became more pressing.
Modern veterinary administration formally began in 1913 with the establishment of the Veterinary Department in Zaria. Initially responsible for livestock census activities, disease surveillance and the control of infectious diseases, the department laid the foundation for what would become one of Nigeria’s most important agricultural institutions.
Following the amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria in 1914, F. R. Brandt was appointed the country’s first Chief Veterinary Officer and helped organise veterinary services on a more structured basis. A further milestone came in 1924 when veterinary laboratory and research activities were transferred from Zaria to Vom on the Jos Plateau. The favourable climate and strategic location made Vom an important centre for research, diagnostics and vaccine production. Over time, it evolved into the National Veterinary Research Institute (NVRI), Nigeria’s foremost veterinary research establishment.
Building a profession and supporting national development
The early years of veterinary practice were marked by formidable challenges. Rinderpest, commonly known as cattle plague, periodically devastated livestock populations across West Africa, while trypanosomosis transmitted by tsetse flies severely constrained livestock production in many parts of the country. Veterinary officers relied on surveillance, quarantine and treatment programmes to protect livestock and pastoral communities.
Their responsibilities extended beyond livestock diseases. Veterinary authorities also played important roles in controlling agricultural pests such as locusts, grasshoppers and Quelea birds, recognising the close relationship between animal health, crop production and food security.
Developing skilled personnel was equally important. The establishment of the Veterinary School in Vom in 1941 marked a turning point in veterinary education. Originally designed to train veterinary assistants and field personnel, the institution later became an important regional centre for veterinary training in Africa.
A significant milestone was achieved in 1954 when Dr Bukar Shu’aib graduated from the University of Liverpool, becoming the first Nigerian to obtain a university degree in veterinary medicine. His achievement symbolised the emergence of indigenous leadership within the profession.
The post-independence era brought rapid expansion. Governments invested in livestock development, while veterinary services became increasingly Nigerian-led. Programmes promoting access to water resources, grazing reserves, veterinary care and livestock markets helped strengthen pastoral production. The Northern Nigeria Grazing Reserve Programme emerged as one of the country’s major efforts to support livestock development and improve the management of pastoral resources.
At the same time, organised livestock enterprises gained prominence. Parastatal livestock establishments, dairy and breeding centres, and commercial production schemes were developed to improve productivity and strengthen domestic supplies of meat and milk. Notable examples included the Vom Dairy establishment, Shika Stock Farm, Mokwa Cattle Ranch, Raav Livestock Investigation and Breeding Centre, Obudu Cattle enterprise, Agege Dairy establishment, and the Western Livestock Company among others
Collectively, these developments transformed livestock production from largely traditional systems into an increasingly organised sector encompassing animal health, breeding, parastatal ranching, dairy and poultry production, pasture management, research and extension. They established the institutional foundations of modern livestock development and helped shape the veterinary and livestock administration that emerged with the creation of states in 1967.
Veterinary education also entered a transformative phase. The University of Ibadan established Nigeria’s first Faculty of Veterinary Medicine in 1963, followed by Ahmadu Bello University in 1964. These institutions laid the foundation for modern veterinary training and produced generations of professionals who have served in academia, research, government and private practice.
The profession’s regulatory framework matured alongside these developments. The Veterinary Surgeons Ordinance of 1952 provided statutory regulation for veterinary practice and laid the foundation for the Veterinary Council of Nigeria. Subsequent legislation and international professional standards strengthened the quality, ethics and credibility of veterinary practice in the country.
Landmark achievements in animal health
Among the profession’s most significant achievements was Nigeria’s contribution to the eradication of rinderpest. Veterinary officers travelled across vast and often difficult terrain, vaccinating livestock and implementing disease-control measures that ultimately eliminated one of history’s most devastating animal diseases.
Nigeria was officially recognised as free of rinderpest in 2005 and contributed to the global eradication of the disease in 2011. Rinderpest became the first animal disease ever eradicated worldwide and only the second disease, after smallpox, to achieve global eradication.
Another notable success came with the control of highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1). Following Africa’s first confirmed outbreak in Nigeria in 2006, veterinary authorities implemented surveillance programmes, laboratory diagnostics, biosecurity measures, strategic depopulation and compensation schemes. These efforts helped contain the disease, and by 2013 Nigeria had self-declared freedom from notifiable avian influenza.
The profession has also contributed significantly to public health through meat inspection, food-safety monitoring, abattoir supervision and the prevention of zoonotic diseases. These functions remain essential to protecting consumers and maintaining confidence in the food supply chain.
The profession today
Veterinary medicine has grown into a substantial national profession. Nigeria now has more than 13,000 veterinarians and an estimated 50,000 veterinary paraprofessionals serving across government institutions, universities, research centres, private practices and the livestock industry. The number of veterinary faculties has expanded to 17, producing graduates who contribute to animal health and public health both within Nigeria and internationally.
Yet significant challenges remain. Nigeria’s livestock population exceeds 900 million animals, including cattle, sheep, goats and poultry. Despite this vast resource base, many livestock producers still have limited access to veterinary services, diagnostic facilities, vaccines and quality-assured animal-health products.
At the same time, the disease landscape is becoming increasingly complex. Emerging and transboundary animal diseases, antimicrobial resistance, urbanisation, environmental degradation and climate change continue to pose significant threats to livestock production systems and public health.
Preparing for the next century
Meeting these challenges will require sustained investment in veterinary infrastructure, disease surveillance, laboratory networks, and emergency preparedness. The future will demand greater specialisation in epidemiology, food safety, public health, animal welfare, wildlife health, disease intelligence, and the application of artificial intelligence and digital technologies. Digital surveillance systems, geospatial tools, and data-driven decision-making are already transforming animal-health management worldwide and offer immense opportunities to strengthen disease control and livestock productivity in Nigeria.
Equally important is deeper collaboration between public and private veterinary services. While government institutions provide regulatory oversight and lead disease-control programmes, private practitioners deliver critical clinical services, biosecurity support, and technical expertise to livestock producers. Together, they form the backbone of a resilient and modern animal-health system.
As Nigeria enters its second century of veterinary medicine, the profession stands at a defining moment. The pioneers built the institutions, controlled devastating diseases, and laid the foundations for modern livestock development. The task now is to build on that legacy, embrace innovation, and prepare for the challenges of a rapidly changing world.
More than a century after veterinary services first took root in Zaria, the profession remains central to Nigeria’s prosperity, safeguarding animal and public health, securing food systems, supporting livelihoods, and driving economic growth. The iconic Veterinary Council of Nigeria headquarters in Maitama, Abuja, stands as a symbol of this remarkable journey, from humble beginnings to a modern, respected, and indispensable profession.
Hail Naija’s Animal Doctors: for over 100 years, they have protected the nation’s animals, safeguarded its people, secured its food supply, and helped build a stronger Nigeria.
 
Main is a former Chief Veterinary Officer of Nigeria and past VCN President

items.author: Baba Martins
items.content:
The police in Kano State yesterday blocked members of the ‘Tinubu Must Go’ (TMG) movement from accessing the venue of a planned meeting, sparking protests by the organisers and condemnation from Amnesty International Nigeria and other stakeholders.
The police blockade in Kano came about two weeks after the arrest and arraignment of five men in Maiduguri, Borno State, over the use of T-shirts bearing the inscription “Tinubu Must Go”, which triggered criticisms from human rights groups and opposition figures.
The men – Baba Aji Gremami, 44; Mustapha Abba Yemen, 28; Abbacha Mohammed Ali, 32; Adam Umar Gubio, 21; and Abdulhamid Mohammed, 21- were arrested on September 25, 2026, around the West End Roundabout area of Maiduguri.
They were subsequently arraigned before Chief Magistrate Court I in Maiduguri on charges of criminal conspiracy, inciting disturbance, disturbance of public peace and thuggery under Sections 60, 78, 79 and 392 of the Borno State Penal Code. They pleaded not guilty to the charges.
The police alleged that the defendants conspired to print and wear the T-shirts with the intention of causing a breach of public peace. The command later said officers found them with suspected cannabis, tablets, a shisha pot and other items during a routine patrol. The allegations have not been established in court.
The arrests drew condemnation from Amnesty International, which described the detention as arbitrary and called for the men’s release, arguing that peaceful political expression should not be criminalised.
Following their arraignment, the defendants’ lawyers applied for bail. The court subsequently granted bail to the five men, according to reports published on October 7. The substantive case has been scheduled for October 26, 2026.
 
TMG alleges rights violation
Earlier, members of the movement protested the police blockade, alleging that heavily armed security operatives prevented them from accessing a private event centre they had paid to use.
In a live video posted on his verified Facebook page on Sunday, October 11, Hikima said more than 10 mobile police vehicles had been stationed at the venue.
He described the gathering as an exercise of the group’s constitutional rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly, insisting that the organisers were not criminals and had no intention of causing trouble.
“Today, the 11th of October 2026, we gathered here in Kano State in order to exercise our fundamental human rights and to associate freely in order to exchange ideas and educate ourselves on the need to send away the administration of Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Nigeria,” Hikima said.
He accused the police of preventing the group from accessing the venue because of its opposition to the president’s administration.
The lawyer argued that the movement was entitled to assemble and exchange political opinions without obtaining police permission, citing Sections 39 and 40 of the 1999 Constitution, which provide for freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and association, respectively.
Hikima also rejected suggestions that the group needed police approval to hold its meeting, saying the organisers intended to conduct themselves peacefully and within the law.
He vowed that the movement would continue its activities despite the incident, including organising further demonstrations.
“The Court of Appeal decision stands. I do not need to inform any security agent to hold my rallies. Next time, we are going to protest; next time, we are going to demonstrate,” he said.
 
Police defend Kano blockade
Meanwhile, the Kano State Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, has defended the action, saying the command was concerned about public safety and needed to ascertain the nature of the gathering before providing security.
In an interview with an online platform, DCL Hausa, Bakori said he contacted one of the conveners, a lawyer, Abba Hikima, after seeing information about the planned meeting on social media.
“I saw it yesterday on social media that they are coming to hold a gathering. I called Barrister Hikima and asked him what was happening. He said it was a gathering they wanted to hold, and I said it was important that we were aware so that we could provide protection,” the commissioner said.
According to him, Hikima disclosed that about 700 people were expected to attend the gathering, prompting him to request a postponement to allow both parties to discuss security arrangements.
“He said 700 people would be coming into the state. I said the number was high and that he should postpone it and come so that we could discuss it. He said he would think about it and get back to me,” Bakori said.
The commissioner alleged that he later attempted to reach Hikima by telephone but the lawyer did not respond to his calls.
Bakori said the police needed to know the number of people attending such gatherings and the nature of the activities planned to ensure adequate security.
“We have to regulate. Who is coming? What type of event is he holding? We need to know,” he said.
He cited a recent incident in which the police allegedly intercepted arms from people who came to Sabon Gari in Kano under the guise of attending a political gathering.
He said the incident was still under investigation, adding that the command could not ignore security concerns when organisers announced plans to bring hundreds of people into the state.
Bakori, however, maintained that the police were not seeking to prevent the organisers from exercising their rights but wanted to ensure the safety of participants and other residents.
“It’s part of their right to bring people together and do whatever, and nobody will stop them. Legally, it is not compulsory, but we also have a mandate to ensure that nothing goes wrong for or against them,” he said.
He added that dialogue between the organisers and the police could have helped resolve the concerns surrounding the meeting.
“Where someone’s right stops is where another person’s right begins. It’s an easy thing that we will just come and discuss, so that they could be protected also,” the commissioner said.
Amnesty International condemns blockade
Meanwhile, Amnesty International Nigeria condemned the police action, describing the blockade as an unlawful restriction of the group’s rights.
In a statement, the human rights organisation said heavily armed police officers blocked both ends of the road leading to the venue of the TMG event.
“Amnesty International strongly condemns the unlawful and outrageous blocking of the venue of a ‘Tinubu-Must-Go’ event Today in Kano,” the organisation said.
It urged the Nigeria Police Force to desist from what it described as reckless violations of human rights, stressing that supporters of political candidates and parties had the right to organise peaceful activities.
“The duty of the police is to facilitate peaceful conduct of such political gatherings no matter the political party or candidate being supported or opposed,” the organisation said.
Amnesty International added that freedom of association and peaceful assembly was not exclusive to any political party or its supporters.
The organisation further described the incident as part of what it called a troubling pattern of police repression targeting opposition members in different parts of the country.
It warned that repeated attacks and intimidation against opposition supporters could make it more difficult for them to associate freely and organise public gatherings.
The incident has renewed debate over the balance between police responsibility for public safety and citizens’ constitutional rights to peaceful assembly, particularly as political activities begin to gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections.
 
APC using police to suppress dissent – ADC
The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has condemned the Kano State Police Command for disrupting the “Tinubu Must Go” rally in Kano.
While describing the action as “shameful, unconstitutional and a disturbing descent into authoritarianism”, the campaign council accused the police of violating Nigerians’ fundamental rights to peaceful assembly and freedom of expression, as guaranteed by the 1999 Constitution, as amended.
In a statement on Sunday, Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC campaign, Kola Ologbondiyan, said the rally, led by Barrister Abba Hikima and organised by concerned youths, was reportedly disrupted when police operatives barricaded The Avenue Event Centre and allegedly intimidated participants.
Despite the police action, the council said the youths demonstrated courage and determination by refusing to be silenced and insisting on making their voices heard.
The ADC-PCC expressed outrage over the reported arrest of the owner of The Avenue Event Centre for allegedly allowing the facility to be used for the gathering, describing the development as another “troubling indication of the APC-led government’s intolerance of dissent.”
The party questioned why a business owner should face arrest for making a facility available for a peaceful gathering.
“This is not democracy. This is tyranny. For how long will the APC continue to use the police to suppress dissenting voices?” Ologbondiyan queried.
He described as ironic a situation in which a government that claims to uphold democratic values appears threatened by citizens exercising their constitutional rights.
“The message from Kano is loud and clear: Nigerians are tired, hungry and angry. You can stop a rally and arrest a venue owner, but you cannot arrest hunger in the land. You cannot barricade the anger and frustration of over 200 million people,” he said.
Ologbondiyan argued that the government’s priorities were misplaced, insisting that the same determination displayed in disrupting the rally should instead be directed towards tackling insecurity, banditry and the crushing cost of living.
“If the APC government had deployed the same energy it used to stop a peaceful rally at The Avenue Event Centre to tackle insecurity, banditry and the excruciating cost of living, Nigeria would be a safer and more prosperous nation,” he added.
The council commended Barrister Abba Hikima and the youths who participated in the rally for their courage and determination to speak out despite the reported police intimidation.
It also called on the Inspector-General of Police and the Kano State Police Command to ensure the immediate and unconditional release of the event centre owner, if still in custody, and to desist from actions capable of turning the police into an instrument of political oppression.
The ADC-PCC further urged civil society organisations, human rights groups and the international community to pay close attention to what it described as a dangerous erosion of democratic freedoms in Nigeria.
“The right to protest is not a privilege granted by the police or the APC; it is a right guaranteed by the Constitution. No amount of intimidation will stop Nigerians from demanding change.
“The ADC stands firmly with Barrister Abba Hikima, the courageous youths of Kano and every Nigerian who has found the courage to say enough is enough,” the statement said.

items.content:
Enugu State Governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, has commended the Managing Director of Powell Homes and Shelters Ltd., Architect Chibuikem Onyekachi Emmanuel, describing him as a reference point for youths seeking to make an impact through enterprise.
The governor, represented by his deputy, Barrister Ifeanyi Ossai, spoke made the disclosure at the commissioning of Hosana Estate in Ibagwa Nike, Enugu East Local Government Area which calling for private-sector housing investments to complement government efforts to accelerate development across the state.
Ossai said the investment by the Enugu-born entrepreneur reflected the resilience and determination required to build a better state. He assured investors and residents of a secure environment for businesses and communities to thrive, a statement by the Firm has said.
He urged the developers to work closely with estate management for effective administration, and pledged continued infrastructure expansion
“On our part, we’ll keep expanding infrastructure and for all those we’ve not attended to, do not be disappointed, we’re already on that path and we’re progressing geometrically,” he said.
The Chairman of Enugu East Local Government Area, Beloved-Dan Anike, said the ongoing dualisation of the road had enhanced the area’s prospects as an emerging urban centre. He called the project a trailblazing move into a “future goldmine” and said housing projects like Hosana Estate could help address Nigeria’s housing deficit, particularly in Enugu.
The traditional ruler of Ibagwa Nike, Igwe Emma Ugwu, said the community welcomed genuine investments capable of contributing to its growth. He recalled assuring residents who made enquiries about the project that it was in line with the state’s development agenda.
He said Hosana Estate was designed as a planned, functional community around the needs of modern families. Facilities include internal roads, drainage, electricity infrastructure, recreational facilities, a synthetic football pitch and a children’s playground.
Emmanuel said the company would keep developing quality homes at affordable price points while exploring innovative financing models and strategic partnerships to widen access to homeownership.
He disclosed that Powell Homes and Shelters plans to expand its developments beyond Enugu to other parts of Nigeria where the need exists.

items.title: Once-hot AI trade leaves Korean stocks struggling for buyers
items.summary: South Korea spent much of this year as a poster child of the scorching global AI trade. items.content: South Korea spent much of this year as a poster child of the scorching global AI trade. Now, by almost every measure, the $4.3 trillion stock market is rapidly losing relevance with investors.Turnover has collapsed 70% from its peak in late May, foreigners are retreating at the fastest pace in Asia and local retail investors are also pulling back. The Kospi, the world’s best-performing major equities benchmark in the first half, has since lost 22% to be the worst in the second half while its AI-heavy Taiwanese and US peers set new highs.Behind the reversal is a market whose AI fortunes hinge disproportionately on Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc., the two memory-chip giants at the heart of the global AI supply chain. That concentration is now a liability as investors question the durability of memory chips’ boom cycle, while the brutal leverage-driven selloff in the summer has made some global funds hesitant to return.134880575“The biggest challenge I see for most investors — especially those who only recently got into Korea for the memory chip trade — is that the easy money in that theme has been made,” said Phillip Wool, head of portfolio management at Rayliant Global Advisors, adding his fund has been taking profit in Korean AI stocks and is now underweight SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics.The two chipmakers together account for over half of Kospi’s weighting and powered its ascent earlier this year. Foreign funds pulled $131 billion from Korean stocks this year, the most among major Asian markets, according to exchange data compiled by Bloomberg.Skepticism over memory chip demand was on full display when shares of Samsung, the world’s top producer of such semiconductors, fell Thursday despite a nearly nine-fold surge in quarterly operating profit.Read more: Wall Street Week Ahead: Bank earnings, CPI headline busy markets week as S&P 500 hovers near recordsKorea is now struggling to lure buyers, a problem amplified by the nearing completion of combined 55 trillion won ($41 billion) stock buybacks by Samsung and SK Hynix. Repurchases by the two chipmakers accounted for the bulk of the $23 billion worth of buy orders in the market last month, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co.“We have seen capital increasingly gravitate back toward US equities, contributing to ongoing foreign outflows from the Korean market,” said Richard Tang, head of research Hong Kong at Julius Baer.134880585Individual investors, a key force behind Kospi’s 100% rally in the first half, remain elusive following the July rout.Margin loans outstanding have hovered around 33 trillion won over the past month, after peaking at 38.6 trillion won in June, according to data from the Korea Financial Investment Association. Brokerage account balances — or investor deposits awaiting deployment — have also fallen to around 100 trillion won from a record of near 140 trillion won.Read more: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: What do Shah Rukh Khan and SIFs have in common? Radhika Gupta explains“The memory names in particular have become value names, cheap at current earnings,” said Jon Withaar, a portfolio manager at Pictet Asset Management in Singapore. “But retail and fast money hedge funds do not chase value or the concept ‘cheap’. They chase growth.”To be sure, the declines have opened up buying opportunities for some investors who see AI spending and memory chip profitability still holding up. Korea’s ongoing initiative to boost corporate value is also another draw. Thanks to earlier gains, Kospi is still among the best performers for 2026 overall.Yet for those less convinced, the competing Asian semiconductor hub of Taiwan is gaining favor due to its wider and deeper linkages across the AI supply chain and a more upbeat earnings outlook.Up 70% this year, the Taiex Index beat the Kospi by about 23 percentage points last quarter, the widest margin since the turn of the century. Taiwan’s stock gains are also more broad-based, with about 10% of the local gauge’s members having at least doubled in value this year. That compares to 4.7% for Kospi.“At this point in time, we prefer to express our tactical AI exposure through Taiwan equities, which offer a more complete technology hardware ecosystem and are supported by robust spending plans from major technology companies,” said Chun-Lai Wu, head of Asia Asset Allocation at UBS Global Wealth Management Chief Investment Office.

items.content:
By Innocent Anaba
Spokesman of the Dr Kasarachi Enyinna Michael Campaign Organisation, the National Democratic Congress, NDC, senatorial candidate for Abia South, Chief Emperor Ogbonna, has said there was need to have members of the party in the Senate and House of Representatives, to support Mr. Peter Obi if he wins the presidential election.
He also said that Michael represents a new era, as he has done so much for Abia South, where he lives and has companies operating in the area and that voting for him would ensure Obi has party members to support and pass his policies at the National Assembly.
Speaking weekend, he said: “Now, we all talk about Peter Obi. Everybody is talking about Peter Obi, that Peter Obi is the Ronaldo of Nigerian politics today. In fact, he is the most popular Nigerian today, as you know. Now, if Peter Obi becomes the President and we don’t have senators in the National Assembly or members of the House of Representatives, how will he perform? It is a normal thing. Assuming I am the President today and I am bringing reforms that would reduce the cost of governance, reforms that would stop corruption, first of all, I have to call my party men, and I will tell them, ‘Please, this is what I want.’ If NDC does not have a majority in the House and you voted for Peter Obi, you are wasting your time.
“Assuming the APC or other parties have the majority, they will just gang up and impeach him. It happened in Anambra State. They impeached Peter Obi in Anambra State as governor. Later, he went to court and got his mandate back.
“Now, in Nigeria, they may impeach him because his party may not have the majority.
“That is why we are telling Nigerians, be the grassroots. If you want a change, be the change yourself.”
On the senatorial candidate, Michael, he said: “For those of us who are young, we align with NDC and we brought out Dr. Michael, who is the right candidate for Abia South. Abia South is made up of Aba South, Aba North, Obingwa, Ugwunagbo, Ukwa West and Ukwa East.
“Now, we have looked at the political situation in Abia State. The person that has been there is Enyinnaya Abaribe. He has been there for a very long time. From being deputy governor, and he started talking about Otu Onu (one term), Later, he was elected to the Senate on the ground of Otu Onu. And he has been there for 20-something years. I am a voter in Abia South. I am a taxpayer too. I pay taxes, and I know that we need a change.
“So, that is why, for those of us who are young, we align with NDC and we brought out Michael, who is the senatorial candidate. For those who don’t know him, he is from Ogwe in Ukwa West.
“He is not only a giver; he is somebody who, when he looks at you, knows what your problem is. He is a true democrat. He is not a pompous person. If you see him, you will like him. Everybody likes him.
“He is an achiever. He is a technocrat. He has a company, Fintech, that operates in Abia State. His family has a house on Azikiwe Road. He grew up on Azikiwe Road, so he knows Aba very well. And he has companies operating here, operating in Abia. So, it is not as if he is a foreigner coming to run elections in Aba. He is somebody who has been consistent in promoting Aba’s welfare.
“We are looking for a way to get the country back, and it is very simple. We need people like Michael, who shall be a senator in the Federal Republic of Nigeria. We also need NDC House of Assembly and House of Representatives members, so that if the President wants to make a reform, there will be people from his party who will help him do it. That is why I advise Abia South: please, let us support Michael. He is an achiever, he is a young man, he is down to earth, and we need a paradigm change.

items.content:
…Charges FG to enforce 2021 Act, expand services
By Sola Ogundipe
Nigeria’s neglect of mental health is threatening social stability, weakening public trust and deepening despair among young people struggling with insecurity, and diminishing their confidence in the future, Professor Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, a leading psychiatrist, has warned.
Sheikh, a professor of psychiatry and psychopharmacology, at the Department of Psychiatry, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, called on the Federal Government to implement the National Mental Health Act 2021 and expand access to affordable care, particularly at the community level, warning that untreated psychological distress could weaken families, fracture communities and erode confidence in public institutions.
Speaking at the 4th Vanguard Mental Health Summit held at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, Sheikh said in a presentation titled “Mental Health as Social Capital: The Hidden Wealth of Nations” that mental wellbeing was fundamental to the trust, relationships and cooperation societies need to function.
He described mental health as one of the most neglected areas of healthcare, particularly in Africa and Nigeria, where inadequate investment has constrained access to services, especially community-based care.
“Nigeria faces a serious social capital crisis. We are a nation of about 230 million people, with a large youth population, yet our social indicators raise troubling questions about trust, cohesion and confidence in the future. Low trust in institutions and tensions between communities weaken the relationships that hold society together,” he said.
Sheikh identified insecurity, family breakdown, substance misuse and the growing desire among young Nigerians to leave the country as issues that must be understood beyond their immediate economic and social dimensions.
“When you live in survival mode, you cannot plan for tomorrow. The growing desire among young Nigerians to leave the country is not only an economic or migration issue. For some, it also reflects a loss of confidence in the future.
“Family breakdown and substance use, including the misuse of codeine and other psychoactive substances, must also be understood in context. They can reflect deeper psychological distress.”
He warned that prolonged exposure to violence and trauma could undermine the trust and social bonds needed to rebuild communities and sustain development.
“Consider a child who grows up in Kaduna witnessing killings and receiving no psychological support. That child may become an adult living with hypervigilance and deep mistrust. How will such an adult trust the state? How will that person nurture the next generation?” he asked.
According to Sheikh, the consequences of insecurity extend beyond deaths, displacement and property losses to include lasting psychological harm that can affect how survivors relate to others, engage with institutions and raise their families.
On the way forward, he said: “First, we must strengthen the mental health system and expand access to affordable, quality care, particularly at the community level. Second, we must implement the National Mental Health Act 2021 rather than allow its provisions to remain largely on paper. Third, we must ensure that attempted suicide is no longer treated as a criminal offence and that people in crisis receive appropriate care and support.”
Further, Sheikh stressed that mental health should be treated as a national and humanitarian priority, with services available close to where people live rather than concentrated in specialist facilities.
He also cautioned against viewing mental wellbeing solely through its economic benefits, noting that untreated mental health conditions could affect education, employment, productivity and quality of life, while access to care could produce benefits for individuals and society.
“The bridge between poverty and prosperity is not infrastructure alone, it requires mental health. The bridge between conflict and peace is not negotiation alone, it also requires trauma healing and reconciliation,” he said.
Explaining the relationship between mental health and social capital, Sheikh noted “Psychological wellbeing could help people build relationships, participate in community life and cooperate with others. In turn, supportive family ties, friendships and wider social networks could reduce loneliness, provide emotional support and help people cope with adversity.
“The relationship works both ways. Mental health can help generate social capital, while social capital can support mental wellbeing,” he said, adding that supportive relationships and access to opportunities were essential to ensuring that people could benefit from these connections.
“Without mental health, there is no sustainable social development. Without social capital, there is no development, and without development, there is no lasting prosperity,” he said.
The post Vanguard summit: Mental health neglect threatens Nigeria’s stability – Sheikh appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
Veteran playmaker Isco struck twice to help Real Betis climb back into third place in La Liga with a 5-2 win over Osasuna on Sunday.
The Andalucian side moved a point above Real Madrid, fourth, and level with second place Atletico Madrid, trailing leaders Barca by five points.
Manuel Pellegrini’s side claimed a sixth league win from eight matches with an exciting display of attacking football at La Cartuja stadium, where they are playing until their Benito Villamarin home is renovated, likely 2028.
Former Real Madrid midfielder Isco, 34, netted from the penalty spot after a foul on Rodrigo Riquelme, and Ez Abde doubled the hosts lead after half-an-hour with a cool finish.
Ante Budimir’s own goal gave Betis their third after half-time, before the Croatian striker netted at the correct and Raul Garcia added another to give Osasuna a fighting chance.
Isco capitalised on a loose ball in the box to grab his second and Jose Morante bagged a fifth in stoppage time to close out Betis’s big win.
“Football is never truly under control,” said Pellegrini after his side almost let their three-goal lead slip.
“As soon as the pace drops, the other team can pull level.”
The former Manchester City coach also praised Isco after his brace.
“He has spectacular quality and a maturity as a player that allows him to perform at whatever level he wants to,” added Pellegrini.
Elsewhere Valencia, 19th, earned a point in a 2-2 draw at Racing Santander under new coach Javier Aguirre.
Real Sociedad defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-2 in another entertaining battle.
The Basque side, sixth, eased into a three-goal lead Mario Soriano pulled one back for the visitors in San Sebastian to spark a Depor fight back.
They were given further encouragement when Real Sociedad’s Pablo Marin was sent off in the 66th minute for a foul on Nsongo Bil in the box and Yeremay Hernandez netted from the penalty spot.
Both teams finished with 10 men after Lorenzo Amatucci brought down Mikel Oyarzabal as the last man, and Depor could not find an equaliser.
On Saturday Liga leaders Barcelona beat Getafe 3-0 to prolong their perfect start to the season, with eight wins from eight league games.
Hansi Flick’s side are followed by second place Atletico Madrid, who snatched a late 2-1 win at Alaves, while Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid scraped a 1-0 victory over Villarreal despite Vinicius Junior’s red card for hair-pulling.

items.content:
By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA – President Bola Tinubu will on Tuesday flag off the reconstruction and dualisation of the 376km Lambata–Bida–Mokwa–Makera–Kontagora Federal Highway in Niger State, a project expected to improve transport links and boost agricultural and commercial activities across North-Central Nigeria.
For farmers struggling to move produce to markets, traders transporting goods and commuters travelling between communities, the highway could ease movement and open up economic opportunities, provided the project is delivered to the required standard.
In a statement by Dr Abiodun Essiet, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement for the North-Central region, the project was described as a major infrastructure initiative under Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.
The flag-off, scheduled for noon in Bida, is expected to attract the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago; and other federal and state government officials.
The statement said the highway would strengthen the movement of people, agricultural produce and commercial goods across the region.
“Beyond road construction, the project represents an investment in the economic connections that link farmers to markets, businesses to customers and communities to wider commercial opportunities,” it said.
Niger State’s agricultural economy stands to benefit from improved access to markets, while transport operators and businesses could gain from better road conditions, reduced journey delays and safer travel.
The project aligns with the Renewed Hope Agenda’s infrastructure priorities, which identify road development as a driver of economic growth and national development.
However, the statement did not disclose the contract sum, contractor, construction timetable or expected completion date.
It said the project’s success would ultimately depend on what is delivered to road users and host communities.
“The ultimate measure of the project’s success will be the delivery of a durable highway that improves transportation, strengthens economic connections and serves the needs of communities along the corridor,” the statement said.
The post Tinubu to flag off 376km Niger highway Tuesday appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor
President Bola Tinubu has challenged those seeking to lead Nigeria to explain the cost of their campaign promises, how they intend to implement them and whether they can sustain them.
Tinubu said every government commitment must be backed by a credible plan and be financially sustainable to avoid passing the burden to Nigerians and future generations.
The President stated this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, stressing that leaders must balance the need to provide immediate relief with the responsibility to protect the future of the country’s children.
“As President, I have a duty to provide relief today without compromising our children’s future.
“Every commitment must be sustainable and backed by a credible plan. That responsibility guides our decisions, including the difficult ones,” he said.
Tinubu added that political promises were easy to make when their costs could be deferred, leaving citizens and future generations to bear the consequences.
“Anyone seeking to lead Nigeria should be prepared to explain what their promises will cost, how they will deliver them, and whether they can sustain them.
“Promises are easy to make when the costs can be postponed, leaving Nigerians and future generations to pay the bill,” he said.
The President also referred to the stories of some Nigerians, including Blessing, Ada, Abigail and Kabir, saying their experiences demonstrated the impact of government investments on people’s daily lives.
He also acknowledged a request from Emmanuel, saying it reminded him of the work still required to expand access to essential services.
“Emmanuel, your request reminds me of the work still ahead. I know many more Nigerians like you are waiting for these services,” Tinubu said.
He stressed the need to continue expanding access to affordable transportation across the country, noting that the Federal Government would work with state governments to achieve the objective.
“Our responsibility is to keep expanding access until affordable transportation becomes a reality for more communities across our country.
“That is the work we will continue in collaboration with the States,” he added.
The post Tinubu to Aspirants: Don’t make promises you cannot fund appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
Says viral video is an old 2022 interview taken out of context
The media office of former Minister of Power, Chief Adebayo Adelabu, has dismissed a viral report claiming that he called on Nigerians to reject the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the allegation as false and misleading.
In a statement issued in October 2026, Adelabu’s media office said the video circulating on social media was an excerpt from an interview he granted in 2022, when he was the governorship candidate of the Accord Party in Oyo State.
It said Adelabu did not call on Nigerians to reject the APC, urging the public to disregard what it described as a deliberate attempt to misrepresent his position and create friction between him, President Bola Tinubu and the party’s leadership.
According to the statement, Adelabu had consistently maintained his loyalty to the APC and the President despite controversies surrounding the party’s governorship nomination process in Oyo State.
The former minister, who served under the APC-led Federal Government, reportedly left public office to pursue his governorship ambition in the state.
The statement alleged that the APC nomination process was marred by controversies, including the alleged imposition of a preferred aspirant and the failure to transparently release the primary election results.
It said Adelabu had nevertheless maintained that he had no intention of leaving the party and that his political ambition was not a do-or-die affair.
“His position has been consistent: loyalty does not preclude the demand for fairness, transparency and adherence to democratic principles,” the statement said.
It argued that Adelabu’s criticism of the party’s internal electoral process should not be interpreted as a call for Nigerians to reject the APC.
The media office explained that the 2022 interview reflected Adelabu’s view that political parties had disappointed Nigerians and that voters should focus on the credibility and character of individual candidates.
It added that the comments were made in the context of the political environment at the time and did not amount to opposition to the APC or Tinubu’s presidential ambition.
The statement also described Adelabu’s relationship with Tinubu as longstanding, saying it was based on mutual respect and trust.
It challenged those circulating the video to publish the full, unedited interview rather than selectively extracting portions of it.
The media office further claimed that Adelabu had not granted any media interview since the conclusion of the controversial APC governorship nomination process in Oyo State in which he made the alleged statement.
It urged APC members, the media and the public to verify information before sharing it, warning against the spread of unsubstantiated claims.
“Chief Adelabu remains committed to the APC, loyal to Mr President and supportive of the party’s broader political objectives,” the statement said.
The media office advised the public to rely on authentic statements from Adelabu or his authorised representatives.

He built his popularity through elaborate YouTube challenges, stunts and competitions before expanding into a business empire spanning entertainment, food, merchandise and technology.
His company, Beast Industries, oversees ventures including Feastables, Lunchly, analytics platform Viewstats, and toy and clothing licensing.
According to Forbes, his YouTube channels have more than 640 million subscribers and attract over five billion views annually.
MrBeast has also expanded into streaming with Beast Games on Amazon Prime Video, with its third season already in production at the time of the report.
In February 2026, Beast Industries acquired Step, a financial app designed to teach teenagers about investing and money management. Forbes also reported that the company had attracted venture investment at a valuation of $5 billion.

His production team of approximately 200 people creates digital shows that, according to Forbes, generate nearly 300 million views in a typical week.
Mann’s content reaches audiences in 13 languages, helping him build a global following across social media platforms.
He has also expanded beyond short-form digital entertainment. His partnership with the NFL saw him serve as the league’s “Chief Kindness Officer” for Super Bowl LX, while a deal with Fox Entertainment will see him produce 40 vertical dramas over 18 months.
His business model demonstrates how creators can build production companies capable of supplying content to traditional broadcasters and emerging digital platforms.

Total followers: 38.7 million | Average engagement: 0.22%
British entrepreneur and podcast host Steven Bartlett ranks third, with estimated earnings of $52 million.
Bartlett is best known for The Diary of a CEO, an interview podcast that grew from a project he started at his kitchen table into a major media brand.
According to Forbes, his holding company, Steven.com, is valued at $425 million and has interests spanning media, publishing, live events and investments.
His commercial partnerships include Spotify, LinkedIn and Adobe. He has also invested in technology companies Replit and Lovable.
Bartlett continues to expand his television profile through Dragons’ Den, the investment programme in which entrepreneurs pitch business ideas to potential investors.
His success illustrates how podcasting can develop into a wider business involving advertising, investments and entertainment.
4. Markiplier — $38 million
Total followers: 76.8 million | Average engagement: 0.21%
Mark Edward Fischbach, known professionally as Markiplier, occupies fourth place with estimated earnings of $38 million.
Initially known for gaming videos and online entertainment, Markiplier has moved into filmmaking, demonstrating how established creators can use their digital audiences to support projects outside social media.
His self-funded and self-produced feature film, Iron Lung, screened in approximately 3,000 theatres across North America and generated $50 million at the box office, according to Forbes.
The creator also negotiated a 50-50 revenue split with theatres, an arrangement that gave him a direct stake in the film’s theatrical performance.
Beyond filmmaking, Markiplier continues to host the podcasts Distractible and Go! My Favorite Sports Team.
5. Rhett & Link — $37 million
Total followers: 45.6 million | Average engagement: 0.12%
Comedy duo Rhett McLaughlin and Link Neal rank fifth, with combined estimated earnings of $37 million.
The childhood friends are best known for Good Mythical Morning, their long-running YouTube talk show featuring food challenges, product reviews, trivia and discussions about popular culture.
Forbes reports that the programme produces approximately 240 episodes annually and attracts nearly 20 million viewers.
The duo also operates the Mythical Kitchen channel, which features the Last Meal series hosted by Josh Scherer. Guests have included Tom Hanks, Gordon Ramsay and Ed Sheeran.
Their expansion into Tubi and publishing, including their fourth food book, Spaghetti Head & Chicken Fingers, further demonstrates their ability to turn a digital entertainment brand into multiple revenue streams.
6. Charli D’Amelio — $18 million
Total followers: 209.8 million | Average engagement: 11.59%
TikTok star Charli D’Amelio ranks sixth with estimated earnings of $18 million.
She rose to global prominence through dance videos on TikTok and has since expanded her career into theatre, fashion and other forms of entertainment.
Following her Broadway run in & Juliet, D’Amelio returned to posting dance content and YouTube vlogs while maintaining major fashion partnerships.
She serves as a Prada ambassador and has appeared in campaigns for Kate Spade.
Her position on the list highlights the commercial value of a highly engaged social media audience, particularly for creators whose influence translates into brand partnerships and opportunities beyond digital platforms.
7. Druski — $20 million
Total followers: 38.5 million | Average engagement: 13.77%
Comedian and internet personality Druski, whose real name is Drew Desbordes, ranks seventh with estimated earnings of $20 million.
He gained recognition through comedy sketches shared on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram before expanding into mainstream advertising and television.
His commercial appearances include campaigns for T-Mobile and Dunkin’, while his collaborations have brought him alongside entertainment figures such as Kevin Hart, Timothée Chalamet, Jeff Bridges and Zoe Saldaña.
Forbes also highlighted his role as host of the BET Awards in June.
Druski’s career illustrates how internet comedy can serve as a launchpad for opportunities in advertising, live entertainment and mainstream media.
8. IShowSpeed — $30 million
Total followers: 184 million | Average engagement: 0.39%
Popular streamer IShowSpeed ranks eighth with estimated earnings of $30 million.
The creator, whose real name is Darren Watkins Jr., initially gained attention through gaming videos featuring titles such as NBA 2K and Fortnite.
His popularity grew significantly after clips of his energetic reactions and gaming outbursts went viral on TikTok.
He later diversified into football-related content, collaborating with global stars including Cristiano Ronaldo, before expanding into travel livestreams and videos.
His projects include Speed Does America and Speed Does Africa. His commercial partnerships include Dick’s Sporting Goods, Beats by Dre and Doritos.
Forbes also highlighted his World Cup 2026 Tour with FIFA as part of his expansion into football-related entertainment and global travel content.
9. Mark Rober — $30 million
Total followers: 90.7 million | Average engagement: 0.23%
Former NASA engineer and science communicator Mark Rober ranks ninth, with estimated earnings of $30 million.
Rober is known for highly produced YouTube videos that explain scientific concepts through experiments, engineering projects and elaborate stunts.
His content includes projects designed to teach physics through roller coasters, explore scientific approaches to escaping Alcatraz and demonstrate robotics in collaboration with football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo.
According to Forbes, his team of approximately 100 people produces episodes that can cost seven figures to make.

His work combines education and entertainment while attracting commercial partnerships with companies including Rivian, Google and Disney.
